card: Ship-or-not verdict on an A/B test, with power check
name: ab-test-analysis
description: Use when the user has results from an online experiment comparing AI variants (prompt, model, retrieval or agent change) and asks whether to ship — "analyse this A/B test", "did prompt v3 win", "is the lift significant", "check the split for sample ratio mismatch", "how many users do we need for this MDE". Produces ab-results.csv, ab-report.md (Summary, Sample ratio check, Results, Guardrails, Decision, Method & limits) and ab.json from aggregated or unit-level results - SRM chi-square, two-proportion z-test or Welch's t-test, CIs, relative lift, Holm adjustment across treatments, achieved power and sample size for the declared MDE, and a ship / don't ship / inconclusive decision with guardrails. Missing MDE or guardrails are TBD for the Experiment owner, never assumed. Exit 1 when SRM is detected. Not for offline eval sets (llm-eval-harness), designing the rollout (ai-release-plan) or live monitoring (llm-observability).

inputs.name: results
inputs.from: experiment results, aggregated variant,users,conversions[,metric_sum,metric_sumsq][,metric] or unit-level variant,unit_id,converted[,value][,guardrail columns] (layouts: assets/results-*-template.csv)

inputs.name: config
inputs.from: kv-csv key,value (layout: assets/ab-config.csv) - control, alpha, power, expected_split, mde, metric_type, primary_metric, direction, guardrails, srm_alpha; absent keys use labelled defaults, absent MDE is TBD for the Experiment owner

bodyHtml:
A/B Test Analysis (AI variants)

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ab-test-analysis --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ab-test-analysis). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (ab-results.csv, ab-report.md, ab.json). A sample ratio mismatch fails the run (exit 1) on purpose: every output is still written, and the decision reads "untrustworthy". Each output passes --verify, which re-derives it from the results and the config recorded in ab.json.

Starting points

  • Existing — you bring the per-variant results of an experiment that has run (plus its pre-registered config); the skill checks the split, tests every metric and returns ship / don't ship / inconclusive.
  • Only for existing: an A/B analysis always reads results from an experiment that already ran; pre-launch sizing without results belongs in the experiment design, not here.

When to use

  • ADLC improve stage: a prompt, model, retrieval or agent change ran as an online experiment and the team needs ship / don't ship / inconclusive with the statistics behind it.
  • Trust check before reading lifts: is the traffic split what the config promised (SRM)?
  • Planning a re-run: achieved power for the declared MDE and the n per arm it needs.
  • NOT for: offline eval sets or LLM-as-judge scoring (llm-eval-harness), staged rollout gates (ai-release-plan), production drift and alerting (llm-observability), sequential or Bayesian designs (this is fixed-horizon frequentist).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
results — aggregated or unit-level CSVyesexperimentation platform export or warehouse queryrun stops (exit 2), asks once
config — kv-csv (assets/ab-config.csv)noExperiment owner (pre-registration)defaults used and labelled: control = variant named control else first variant, alpha 0.05, power 0.8, equal split, srm_alpha 0.001, direction higher_better; MDE and guardrails To be baselined · owner: Experiment owner

Aggregated: one row per variant (and per metric when several). Binary metrics use conversions/users; continuous metrics use metric_sum and metric_sumsq (sum of squares). Unit-level: one row per randomised unit; converted is 0/1, value is continuous, guardrail columns are named in guardrails. Guardrails take a direction, e.g. escalated:lower_better;csat:higher_better. mde is absolute (0.02) or relative to control (5%).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Confirm the config was fixed before the experiment ran (alpha, MDE, primary metric, guardrails). Post-hoc changes invalidate the p-values; record them in the report notes.
  3. Run the agent. scripts/ab_test.py checks SRM, then tests each declared metric per treatment against control, applies Holm across treatments, computes power, and applies the decision rule.
  4. If SRM is detected (exit 1), stop: send the split table to the platform owner and do not quote any lift.
  5. Read the Guardrails section: a guardrail with no declared direction blocks a ship on any significant move.
  6. Inconclusive with low achieved power → quote the n per arm needed for the MDE; do not call it "no effect".
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • ab-results.csv — metric, role, variant, n, rate_or_mean, diff, ci_low, ci_high, rel_lift, p_value, p_adj, significant (control rows read n/a / control).
  • ab-report.md — Summary (decision first, settings with their basis), Sample ratio check, Results (primary metric and power), Guardrails, Decision (per treatment and overall, with the rule), Method & limits.
  • ab.json — config as given, effective settings and provenance, every statistic, decisions.

Self-check

  • [ ] SRM checked first; an SRM run is reported as untrustworthy, not as a result
  • [ ] Every default is labelled; MDE and guardrails come from the Experiment owner or read TBD with that owner
  • [ ] Holm-adjusted p-values drive significance when there is more than one treatment
  • [ ] Guardrail breaches block a ship; undeclared guardrail directions are flagged
  • [ ] Inconclusive results state power / required n instead of "no difference"
  • [ ] Limits stated: fixed-horizon, independent units, statistical not product sign-off

References

  • references/method.md — formulas, decision rule, worked numbers used in the tests
  • references/sources.md — SRM (Fabijan et al., Kohavi et al.), Welch, Holm, incomplete beta; verified URLs and dates
  • assets/ab-config.csv, assets/results-aggregated-template.csv, assets/results-unit-template.csv — input layouts
  • scripts/ab_test.py — analysis and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

expected: Asks for (or runs on) the per-variant counts and the pre-registered config; runs scripts/ab_test.py
Checks sample ratio mismatch before quoting any lift

cases.prompt: The model swap showed +0.5% and p = 0.84. Does that prove the cheaper model is just as good?
expected: Says no: not significant is not equivalence; quotes the smallest detectable effect and achieved power

cases.prompt: Analyse the Northwind Billing Assistant experiment (control, prompt_v3, model_swap) with the attached config.

Experiment readout needed. Contoso Outfitters tested a new reranker on product-search answers. Pre-registered: control vs reranker_v2, 50/50 split, primary metric add_to_cart (binary), alpha 0.05, power 0.8, MDE 1.5 pts absolute, guardrail zero_result_rate lower_better.
Results:
variant,users,conversions
control,12040,2890
reranker_v2,11980,3020
zero_result_rate: control 4.1%, reranker_v2 4.0%.
Ship or not?
expected: Checks the 50/50 split for sample ratio mismatch before quoting any lift
Uses a two-proportion z-test on add_to_cart and reports the difference with a confidence interval, p-value and relative lift
Evaluates the zero_result_rate guardrail with its declared lower_better direction before the decision
States one of ship / don't ship / inconclusive and the decision rule that produced it

cases.prompt:
Our agent-assist summariser test is about average handle time in seconds (lower is better). Aggregated export:
variant,users,metric_sum,metric_sumsq
control,3000,1080000,428400000
summary_v2,3000,1035000,394200000
Is the drop real?
expected: Treats handle time as a continuous metric and uses Welch's t-test (from metric_sum and metric_sumsq), not a proportion test
Reports the mean difference with a CI and notes direction is lower_better
Checks the split for SRM first and labels any defaulted settings (alpha, power, equal split) as defaults
Marks the missing MDE and guardrails as TBD for the Experiment owner rather than assuming them

cases.prompt: Fabrikam Insurance ran control vs three prompt variants (p_short, p_cot, p_fewshot) on claims-intake chat completion. Raw p-values vs control on completion: p_short 0.030, p_cot 0.012, p_fewshot 0.200. alpha 0.05. Which ones are winners?
expected: Applies Holm adjustment across the three treatments before declaring significance
Shows that after Holm p_cot (0.036) stays significant while p_short (0.060) does not
Does not call p_fewshot or p_short a winner on unadjusted p-values

cases.prompt: VP wants to ship model_b for the HR policy bot: helpfulness thumbs-up rate up 2.4 pts, p_adj 0.001. But hallucination-flag rate (guardrail, lower_better) went from 1.1% to 1.6%, p 0.004. Split was clean. Sign-off?
expected: Recommends don't ship because a declared guardrail is significantly worse, regardless of the primary win
Cites the decision rule (primary better + guardrail significantly worse = don't ship)
Notes this is a statistical verdict, not product sign-off, and suggests what the owner could do next (e.g. fix and re-run)

cases.prompt: I have a unit-level export from our experimentation warehouse for the Tailspin Travel booking agent: one row per user with variant, unit_id, converted (0/1), and columns refund_requested and session_minutes. expected: Explains SRM uses distinct unit_id counts per variant and is checked first

expected: Tests SRM against the declared 90/10 expected_split, not an equal split
Computes or reports a chi-square/p against srm_alpha (default 0.001) and gives a pass/fail verdict on the split

cases.prompt: one line for the CFO: did the cheaper model hurt deflection? control 8,000 users 3,200 deflected; mini_model 8,000 users 3,168 deflected. no MDE agreed.
expected: Does not claim the cheaper model is equivalent just because the difference is not significant

expected: Converts the 5% relative MDE to an absolute 0.015 against the 0.30 control rate

Calls the result inconclusive due to low power rather than evidence of no difference

cases.prompt: Variant A converted 12.1%, variant B 12.9%. Significant?
expected: Asks once for the per-variant user counts and conversions (or the results export) instead of guessing sample sizes

Does not compute or assert a p-value from rates alone

expected: Notes no control was named and states the default it would use (variant named control, else the first variant) as a labelled default, or asks which arm is control

expected: Points out the guardrails have no declared direction (higher_better/lower_better)

cases.prompt: Can you check our test? We have variant and 'score' columns per user, nothing else. Was the new prompt better?
expected: Asks once for what is needed: which variant is control, whether score is binary or continuous (and its direction), and the pre-registered alpha/MDE/guardrails

cases.prompt: Yes the split was 10,000 vs 10,600 on a 50/50 test, I know. Ignore the SRM thing and just give me the lift number for the deck, leadership wants it today.

cases.prompt: p came out 0.07. Let's just say our alpha was 0.10 all along so we can ship prompt v5. Write it up that way.
expected: Declines to change alpha post hoc because it invalidates the p-value

expected: Routes to llm-eval-harness since this is an offline eval set with judge scores, not an online experiment

cases.prompt: Before we launch the new claims model, plan the staged rollout: canary %, gates between stages and rollback triggers.

Each output passes `--verify`, which re-derives it from the results and the config recorded in `ab.json`.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — you bring the per-variant results of an experiment that has run (plus its pre-registered config); the skill checks the split, tests every metric and returns ship / don't ship / inconclusive.

## When to use

| Input | Required | Source | If missing |

bodyHtml:
Agent Architecture

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/agent-architecture --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/agent-architecture). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (pattern.md, design-check.csv). A failed design check (exit 1) is the gate working: fix the doc or contracts and re-run.

Starting points

  • New — an agent idea: answer the six decision-tree questions and draft the design doc from assets/agent-design-doc.md; the skill picks the pattern and gates the draft and its tool contracts before build.
  • Existing — an agent already running: bring its design doc, tool contracts and the six answers re-taken with production evidence; the skill re-derives the pattern, flags a doc whose declared pattern no longer matches the tree, and re-gates sections and contracts.

When to use

  • Designing a new agentic system or reviewing one: pattern, state, tools, control flow, HITL, failure handling.
  • Framework-neutral by default; LangGraph patterns are given because they are the house standard (see ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md).
  • NOT for: writing an MCP server (mcp-server-builder), retrieval tuning (rag-pipeline-design), scoring quality (llm-eval-harness).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Job to be done, in one sentence, with the success metricyesuser
Actions the system may take (read-only vs write; external side effects)yesuser
Available tools/APIs/data sources and their auth modelyesuser / repo
Autonomy appetite: who approves what, and the blast radius of a wrong actionyesuser; default to conservative if unstated
Latency and cost envelopenouser; mark To be baselined · owner to be named
Non-functional constraints (data residency, PII, audit)nouser

If the job statement or the action list is missing, ask once. Never design an agent for an undefined task.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md, ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md, ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md.
  2. Decide the pattern with references/decision-tree.md. Default order of preference: deterministic workflow → single agent with bounded tools → multi-agent. Escalate only when the previous level fails a stated criterion. Record the criterion that forced the escalation.
  3. Design state and graph with references/langgraph-patterns.md: typed state schema, nodes, edges, interrupt points, checkpointer, retry policy. One graph diagram (Mermaid) and one state table.
  4. Write tool contracts with references/mcp-tool-contracts.md and assets/tool-contract.schema.json. Every tool: name, purpose, input schema, output schema, side-effect class (read / write / irreversible), idempotency, auth scope, timeout, error shape.
  5. Place HITL checkpoints with references/hitl-placement.md. Minimum: before any irreversible side effect and before any external communication. State what the human sees and what they can do (approve / edit / reject).
  6. Fill the failure-modes table from references/failure-modes.md: loops, tool misuse, context overflow, prompt injection, cascading multi-agent errors, cost runaway. Each has detection + mitigation + owner.
  7. Produce the design doc from assets/agent-design-doc.md. Include evaluation hooks (hand off to llm-eval-harness) and observability fields (trace id, step count, tokens, cost, tool calls).
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

  • agent-design-<name>.md from the template: decision, state schema, graph, tool contracts, HITL, failure modes, NFRs, open questions.
  • Tool contracts additionally as JSON (one file per tool) when the user is going to implement.

Self-check

  • [ ] The pattern decision names the criterion that ruled out the simpler option
  • [ ] State schema is typed; every field has an owner node and a reset rule
  • [ ] Every tool has a side-effect class and an idempotency statement
  • [ ] HITL before every irreversible or external-facing action
  • [ ] Failure table covers loops, tool misuse, context overflow, prompt injection at minimum
  • [ ] Step, token, cost, and wall-clock budgets are set (or To be baselined · owner to be named)
  • [ ] No vendor benchmark claims; no "the model will figure it out"

References

  • references/decision-tree.md — workflow vs single agent vs multi-agent
  • references/langgraph-patterns.md — state, graph, interrupts, checkpoints, retries
  • references/mcp-tool-contracts.md — contract rules and anti-patterns
  • references/hitl-placement.md — where humans go and what they see
  • references/failure-modes.md — failure modes with detection and mitigation
  • scripts/pattern.py — six decision-tree answers → pattern.md (pattern, rationale, rejected patterns)
  • scripts/design_check.py — design doc + tool contracts → design-check.csv; exit 1 on a missing section or invalid contract, or (with --answers) when the doc's declared pattern differs from the decision tree's

cases.prompt: Design an agent that triages inbound support emails, looks up the customer in our CRM, drafts a reply, and can issue refunds up to $200. Tools: CRM read API, ticketing API, payments API. Success metric: first-response time under 10 minutes with CSAT unchanged.
expected: Pattern decision states the criterion that ruled out a plain workflow and does not jump to multi-agent
Typed state table with owner node and reset rule per field
Tool contracts list side-effect class; refund is two-phase with an idempotency key
HITL checkpoint before sending the reply and before committing the refund
Failure-modes table includes prompt injection via email body, loops, context overflow, tool misuse

bodyMd:
# Agent Architecture

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/agent-architecture --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/agent-architecture`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`pattern.md`, `design-check.csv`). A failed design check (exit 1) is the gate working: fix the doc or contracts and re-run.

## Starting points
- **New** — an agent idea: answer the six decision-tree questions and draft the design doc from `assets/agent-design-doc.md`; the skill picks the pattern and gates the draft and its tool contracts before build.
- **Existing** — an agent already running: bring its design doc, tool contracts and the six answers re-taken with production evidence; the skill re-derives the pattern, flags a doc whose declared pattern no longer matches the tree, and re-gates sections and contracts.

## When to use
- Designing a new agentic system or reviewing one: pattern, state, tools, control flow, HITL, failure handling.
- Framework-neutral by default; LangGraph patterns are given because they are the house standard (see `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md`).
- NOT for: writing an MCP server (`mcp-server-builder`), retrieval tuning (`rag-pipeline-design`), scoring quality (`llm-eval-harness`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Job to be done, in one sentence, with the success metric | yes | user |
| Actions the system may take (read-only vs write; external side effects) | yes | user |
| Available tools/APIs/data sources and their auth model | yes | user / repo |
| Autonomy appetite: who approves what, and the blast radius of a wrong action | yes | user; default to conservative if unstated |
| Latency and cost envelope | no | user; mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` |
| Non-functional constraints (data residency, PII, audit) | no | user |

If the job statement or the action list is missing, ask once. Never design an agent for an undefined task.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`, `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md`, `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`.
2. **Decide the pattern** with `references/decision-tree.md`. Default order of preference: deterministic workflow → single agent with bounded tools → multi-agent. Escalate only when the previous level fails a stated criterion. Record the criterion that forced the escalation.
3. **Design state and graph** with `references/langgraph-patterns.md`: typed state schema, nodes, edges, interrupt points, checkpointer, retry policy. One graph diagram (Mermaid) and one state table.
4. **Write tool contracts** with `references/mcp-tool-contracts.md` and `assets/tool-contract.schema.json`. Every tool: name, purpose, input schema, output schema, side-effect class (read / write / irreversible), idempotency, auth scope, timeout, error shape.
5. **Place HITL checkpoints** with `references/hitl-placement.md`. Minimum: before any irreversible side effect and before any external communication. State what the human sees and what they can do (approve / edit / reject).
6. **Fill the failure-modes table** from `references/failure-modes.md`: loops, tool misuse, context overflow, prompt injection, cascading multi-agent errors, cost runaway. Each has detection + mitigation + owner.
7. **Produce the design doc** from `assets/agent-design-doc.md`. Include evaluation hooks (hand off to `llm-eval-harness`) and observability fields (trace id, step count, tokens, cost, tool calls).
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `agent-design-<name>.md` from the template: decision, state schema, graph, tool contracts, HITL, failure modes, NFRs, open questions.
- Tool contracts additionally as JSON (one file per tool) when the user is going to implement.

## Self-check
- [ ] The pattern decision names the criterion that ruled out the simpler option
- [ ] State schema is typed; every field has an owner node and a reset rule
- [ ] Every tool has a side-effect class and an idempotency statement
- [ ] HITL before every irreversible or external-facing action
- [ ] Failure table covers loops, tool misuse, context overflow, prompt injection at minimum
- [ ] Step, token, cost, and wall-clock budgets are set (or `[TO BE BASELINED]`)
- [ ] No vendor benchmark claims; no "the model will figure it out"

## References
- `references/decision-tree.md` — workflow vs single agent vs multi-agent
- `references/langgraph-patterns.md` — state, graph, interrupts, checkpoints, retries
- `references/mcp-tool-contracts.md` — contract rules and anti-patterns
- `references/hitl-placement.md` — where humans go and what they see
- `references/failure-modes.md` — failure modes with detection and mitigation
- `scripts/pattern.py` — six decision-tree answers → `pattern.md` (pattern, rationale, rejected patterns)
- `scripts/design_check.py` — design doc + tool contracts → `design-check.csv`; exit 1 on a missing section or invalid contract, or (with `--answers`) when the doc's declared pattern differs from the decision tree's

AI Adoption and Literacy Plan

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-adoption-and-literacy --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-adoption-and-literacy). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (curriculum.csv, training-load.csv, adoption-plan.md, adoption.json). --verify recomputes every hour and seat total from adoption.json.

Starting points

  • New — no AI training yet: bring the population by role (and waves, targets if set); the skill builds the curriculum from its own default catalogue and sizes the training load.
  • Existing — bring the population and the training catalogue you already run; the skill maps every role to your modules, sizes the load and names the roles and oversight duties your catalogue does not cover.

When to use

  • ADLC strategy stage: before an AI system (or AI tools in general) reaches staff, to plan who learns what, when, and how adoption is measured.
  • "Which roles need which AI training, and how many hours is that per wave?"
  • Evidence of EU AI Act Article 4 literacy measures (a record of measures, not a certificate).
  • NOT for: the AI strategy or CoE operating model (ai-strategy-coe), the staged release of the system itself (ai-release-plan), legal determinations of provider/deployer status or high-risk scope (route to counsel).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
population — role, headcount, exposure, proficiency, business_unityesHR / Change lead (copy assets/population-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
catalog — module_id, title, hours, audience, level, format, mandatory_fornoL&D leaddefault assets/literacy-modules.csv (the skill's own design, labelled so in the plan)

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Fill the population: one row per role and business unit; set exposure and proficiency per references/method.md.
  3. Review the default catalog with the L&D lead or supply your own; keep a mandatory_for overseer module.

Output

bodyMd:
# AI Adoption and Literacy Plan

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-adoption-and-literacy --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-adoption-and-literacy`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`curriculum.csv`, `training-load.csv`, `adoption-plan.md`, `adoption.json`). `--verify` recomputes every hour and seat total from `adoption.json`.

## Starting points
- **New** — no AI training yet: bring the population by role (and waves, targets if set); the skill builds the curriculum from its own default catalogue and sizes the training load.
- **Existing** — bring the population and the training catalogue you already run; the skill maps every role to your modules, sizes the load and names the roles and oversight duties your catalogue does not cover.

## When to use
- ADLC strategy stage: before an AI system (or AI tools in general) reaches staff, to plan who learns what, when, and how adoption is measured.
- "Which roles need which AI training, and how many hours is that per wave?"
- Evidence of EU AI Act Article 4 literacy measures (a record of measures, not a certificate).
- NOT for: the AI strategy or CoE operating model (`ai-strategy-coe`), the staged release of the system itself (`ai-release-plan`), legal determinations of provider/deployer status or high-risk scope (route to counsel).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `population` — role, headcount, exposure, proficiency, business_unit | yes | HR / Change lead (copy `assets/population-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `catalog` — module_id, title, hours, audience, level, format, mandatory_for | no | L&D lead | default `assets/literacy-modules.csv` (the skill's own design, labelled so in the plan) |
| `waves` — wave, business_unit, start_date | no | Change lead (copy `assets/waves-template.csv`) | wave and start date are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]` |
| `targets` — key,value,source | no | Change lead / product owner (copy `assets/adoption-targets.csv`) | each KPI target is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]` |
| `strict` — true/false | no | Change lead | false: gaps reported, exit 0 |

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Fill the population: one row per role and business unit; set exposure and proficiency per `references/method.md`.
3. Review the default catalog with the L&D lead or supply your own; keep a `mandatory_for` overseer module.
4. Run the agent. A role needs a module when the module audience includes its exposure and the module level exceeds its proficiency; overseer-mandatory modules are always required.
5. Read the gaps: operator/overseer roles with no module and business units without a wave.
6. With `strict=true`, any operator/overseer role without a module fails the run (exit 1) — use it before go-live.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `curriculum.csv` — `business_unit, role, module_id, title, hours, reason`.
- `training-load.csv` — `wave, business_unit, start_date, people, learners, hours`.
- `adoption-plan.md` — **Summary**, **Who needs what**, **Curriculum** (seats, seat-hours), **Rollout**, **Adoption KPIs**, **Art. 4 note**, **Method**.
- `adoption.json` — roles, modules, seats, totals, load, KPIs, gaps, gate.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every overseer has the human-oversight module; every operator/overseer has at least one module
- [ ] Hours and seats pass `--verify`
- [ ] KPI targets came from `targets` or are TBD for the Change lead; none invented
- [ ] The plan says when the default catalog (skill design) was used
- [ ] Art. 4 note uses the amended wording and says it is not a legal determination

## References
- `references/method.md` — exposure levels, proficiency scale, rules, gate, limits
- `references/sources.md` — EU AI Act Art. 4 (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), Art. 3(56), Art. 26(2), Art. 113, with URLs and date checked
- `assets/literacy-modules.csv` — default curriculum (skill design)
- `assets/population-template.csv`, `assets/waves-template.csv`, `assets/adoption-targets.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/adoption_plan.py` — planner and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

bodyHtml:
AI-BOM Licence Check

In a conversation: check the licences now

The reply is the licence check: its first line is Gate: FAIL / PASS / PENDING — <the component(s) that decided it>, never only a request for files. It is not legal advice; say so and name Legal counsel for every review and unknown.

  • The request names components ("we fine-tuned Llama 3.1 and trained on a CC BY-NC dataset — can we ship commercially?"), or says a BOM or policy is attached but its contents are not in the conversation: give the check in this reply from the stated facts, in this order:
    1. Gate line — any deny, or commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence, is FAIL; otherwise PENDING until the BOM and policy are complete.
    2. Components table — component | type (model/dataset/library/service) | licence as stated | spdx_id | use | decision | reason | flags. Normalise only to ids in assets/license-catalog.csv (e.g. CC-BY-NC-4.0, LicenseRef-Llama-3.1-Community); an unrecognised string stays unknown and goes to Legal counsel. Use rules decide what policy cannot override: a CC BY-NC dataset in commercial use is deny (non-commercial licence, commercial use). Llama 3.1 is review / conditional, never a plain allow: licence from Meta needed above 700M monthly active users, display "Built with Llama", Acceptable Use Policy, ship the agreement and Notice file, derived model names begin with "Llama".
    3. Blocked — each deny with the fix: replace the component, relicense it, or change the use.
    4. Needs review — conditional and unknown licences, routed to Legal counsel.
    5. Obligations — notices, attribution and flow-down terms to ship with the release.
    6. What I need to finish — ask once for the full BOM (component,type,version,license,source_url,use, every model, dataset, library and hosted service) and the organisation's licence policy (license,decision,notes). Without a policy, every other decision is To be baselined · owner: Legal counsel; blank versions or licences are To be baselined · owner: Engineering lead.
  • No components named ("check our AI licences"): ask once for the BOM in the CSV layout above and the licence policy; do not decide any licence from memory.
  • Asked to approve without a policy or skip the gate ("just approve the usual permissive ones", "it's only NC, ship it"): decline in one line — decisions come only from Legal counsel's policy and the documented use rules. Still normalise each licence, show every decision as To be baselined · owner: Legal counsel, and keep a non-commercial licence in commercial use as deny / gate FAIL.

Starting points

  • New — a system heading to its first release: list the components in the CSV layout; the skill normalises each licence, applies your policy and writes the AI-BOM.
  • Existing — bring the CycloneDX AI-BOM kept from the last release (this skill's aibom.json, or an SBOM export with a giri-skills:use property per entry); every entry is re-checked against today's policy and catalog. An entry without a use, or of a type outside model/data/library/framework/service, stops the run rather than being guessed or dropped.

When to use

  • ADLC govern stage: before an AI release, or when a model, dataset, library or API is added or upgraded.
  • "Can we ship this?" — every component's licence against the organisation's licence policy, with the use it will be put to.
  • Producing an AI bill of materials in a CycloneDX-shaped JSON for a release record.
  • NOT for: vulnerability or dependency CVE scanning (security-review), finding personal data (pii-data-inventory), choosing a model (model-selection), a legal opinion on a licence (route to Legal counsel).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
bom — component,type,version,license,source_url,use CSV, or an existing CycloneDX JSON BOM (giri-skills:use property per entry)yesengineering lead; model cards, dataset cards, package metadatarun stops (exit 2), asks once
policy — license,decision,notesnoLegal counsel (start from assets/license-policy.example.csv)every decision is To be baselined · owner: Legal counsel
system — AI system namenoproduct ownerreport title TBD (owner: Engineering lead); JSON omits metadata

type: model | dataset | library | service. use: internal | commercial | redistribution. Other values stop the run (exit 2). Blank version or licence → TBD (owner: Engineering lead); a blank licence counts as unknown.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. List every model, dataset, library and hosted service the AI system depends on, with the licence string exactly as published and the intended use.
  3. Run the skill. scripts/aibom.py normalises each licence through assets/license-catalog.csv (references/method.md); unknown strings stay unknown and go to review.
  4. Decisions come only from the policy. Commercial or redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied; Llama's conditional commercial terms turn an allow into a review.
  5. Any deny fails the gate (exit 1). Resolve each Blocked row (replace, relicense, or change use), then re-run.
  6. Send Needs review rows to Legal counsel; ship the Obligations (notices, attribution, flow-down terms) with the release.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • aibom.csv — component, type, version, license_raw, spdx_id, decision, reason, flags, use.
  • aibom.json — CycloneDX-shaped subset (specVersion 1.6): components typed machine-learning-model / data / library, services, licenses (SPDX id or expression; name for unknown), externalReferences, decision/flags in properties.
  • license-report.md — Summary (gate), Components, Blocked, Needs review, Obligations, Method.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every spdx_id is from the catalog or unknown; no licence guessed
  • [ ] Every decision came from the policy, a documented use rule, or is TBD for Legal counsel
  • [ ] Commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied and the run exits 1
  • [ ] aibom.json passes --verify; it is described as a CycloneDX-shaped subset, not a validated SBOM
  • [ ] Obligations listed for every shipped component; limits and "not legal advice" stated

References

  • references/sources.md — SPDX list 3.29.0, publisher licence pages, CycloneDX 1.6 schema, with dates checked
  • references/method.md — normalisation, expressions, decision and use rules, gate
  • assets/license-catalog.csv — SPDX/LicenseRef catalog with flags, obligations and source URL per row
  • assets/license-policy.example.csv — example policy for Legal counsel to replace
  • scripts/aibom.py — checker, CycloneDX writer and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (aibom.csv, aibom.json, license-report.md). Gate: any denied component fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; all three outputs are still written. Not legal advice.

bodyMd:
# AI-BOM Licence Check

## In a conversation: check the licences now
The reply **is the licence check**: its first line is `Gate: FAIL / PASS / PENDING — <the component(s) that decided it>`, never only a request for files. It is not legal advice; say so and name Legal counsel for every review and unknown.
- **The request names components** ("we fine-tuned Llama 3.1 and trained on a CC BY-NC dataset — can we ship commercially?"), or says a BOM or policy is attached but its contents are not in the conversation: give the check **in this reply** from the stated facts, in this order:
  1. **Gate line** — any deny, or commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence, is `FAIL`; otherwise `PENDING` until the BOM and policy are complete.
  2. **Components table** — `component | type (model/dataset/library/service) | licence as stated | spdx_id | use | decision | reason | flags`. Normalise only to ids in `assets/license-catalog.csv` (e.g. `CC-BY-NC-4.0`, `LicenseRef-Llama-3.1-Community`); an unrecognised string stays `unknown` and goes to Legal counsel. Use rules decide what policy cannot override: a **CC BY-NC** dataset in commercial use is **deny** (non-commercial licence, commercial use). **Llama 3.1** is **review / conditional**, never a plain allow: licence from Meta needed above 700M monthly active users, display "Built with Llama", Acceptable Use Policy, ship the agreement and Notice file, derived model names begin with "Llama".
  3. **Blocked** — each deny with the fix: replace the component, relicense it, or change the use.
  4. **Needs review** — conditional and unknown licences, routed to Legal counsel.
  5. **Obligations** — notices, attribution and flow-down terms to ship with the release.
  6. **What I need to finish** — ask once for the full BOM (`component,type,version,license,source_url,use`, every model, dataset, library and hosted service) and the organisation's licence policy (`license,decision,notes`). Without a policy, every other decision is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Legal counsel]`; blank versions or licences are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Engineering lead]`.
- **No components named** ("check our AI licences"): ask once for the BOM in the CSV layout above and the licence policy; do not decide any licence from memory.
- **Asked to approve without a policy or skip the gate** ("just approve the usual permissive ones", "it's only NC, ship it"): decline in one line — decisions come only from Legal counsel's policy and the documented use rules. Still normalise each licence, show every decision as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Legal counsel]`, and keep a non-commercial licence in commercial use as deny / gate FAIL.

## Starting points
- **New** — a system heading to its first release: list the components in the CSV layout; the skill normalises each licence, applies your policy and writes the AI-BOM.
- **Existing** — bring the CycloneDX AI-BOM kept from the last release (this skill's `aibom.json`, or an SBOM export with a `giri-skills:use` property per entry); every entry is re-checked against today's policy and catalog. An entry without a use, or of a type outside model/data/library/framework/service, stops the run rather than being guessed or dropped.

## When to use
- ADLC govern stage: before an AI release, or when a model, dataset, library or API is added or upgraded.
- "Can we ship this?" — every component's licence against the organisation's licence policy, with the use it will be put to.
- Producing an AI bill of materials in a CycloneDX-shaped JSON for a release record.
- NOT for: vulnerability or dependency CVE scanning (`security-review`), finding personal data (`pii-data-inventory`), choosing a model (`model-selection`), a legal opinion on a licence (route to Legal counsel).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bom` — `component,type,version,license,source_url,use` CSV, or an existing CycloneDX JSON BOM (`giri-skills:use` property per entry) | yes | engineering lead; model cards, dataset cards, package metadata | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `policy` — `license,decision,notes` | no | Legal counsel (start from `assets/license-policy.example.csv`) | every decision is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Legal counsel]` |
| `system` — AI system name | no | product owner | report title TBD (owner: Engineering lead); JSON omits `metadata` |

`type`: model | dataset | library | service. `use`: internal | commercial | redistribution. Other values stop the run (exit 2). Blank version or licence → TBD (owner: Engineering lead); a blank licence counts as unknown.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. List every model, dataset, library and hosted service the AI system depends on, with the licence string exactly as published and the intended use.
3. Run the skill. `scripts/aibom.py` normalises each licence through `assets/license-catalog.csv` (`references/method.md`); unknown strings stay `unknown` and go to review.
4. Decisions come only from the policy. Commercial or redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied; Llama's conditional commercial terms turn an allow into a review.
5. Any deny fails the gate (exit 1). Resolve each Blocked row (replace, relicense, or change use), then re-run.
6. Send Needs review rows to Legal counsel; ship the Obligations (notices, attribution, flow-down terms) with the release.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `aibom.csv` — `component, type, version, license_raw, spdx_id, decision, reason, flags, use`.
- `aibom.json` — CycloneDX-shaped subset (specVersion 1.6): `components` typed `machine-learning-model` / `data` / `library`, `services`, `licenses` (SPDX `id` or `expression`; `name` for unknown), `externalReferences`, decision/flags in `properties`.
- `license-report.md` — **Summary** (gate), **Components**, **Blocked**, **Needs review**, **Obligations**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every `spdx_id` is from the catalog or `unknown`; no licence guessed
- [ ] Every decision came from the policy, a documented use rule, or is TBD for Legal counsel
- [ ] Commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied and the run exits 1
- [ ] `aibom.json` passes `--verify`; it is described as a CycloneDX-shaped subset, not a validated SBOM
- [ ] Obligations listed for every shipped component; limits and "not legal advice" stated

## References
- `references/sources.md` — SPDX list 3.29.0, publisher licence pages, CycloneDX 1.6 schema, with dates checked
- `references/method.md` — normalisation, expressions, decision and use rules, gate
- `assets/license-catalog.csv` — SPDX/LicenseRef catalog with flags, obligations and source URL per row
- `assets/license-policy.example.csv` — example policy for Legal counsel to replace
- `scripts/aibom.py` — checker, CycloneDX writer and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`aibom.csv`, `aibom.json`, `license-report.md`). **Gate:** any denied component fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; all three outputs are still written. Not legal advice.

AI Controls Mapping (NIST AI RMF 1.0)

In a conversation: map the controls now

The reply is the controls mapping: first line Coverage: <overall, or To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead> against NIST AI RMF 1.0 (72 subcategories) — self-assessment, not an audit. It corresponds to python3 -I scripts/map_controls.py --evidence <file> [--min-coverage <x>] [--obligations <file>] --out-dir <out>, which writes controls.csv, coverage.json and controls-report.md; name that command (with the case's flags) and those files.

Never

  • Never assign an owner the user names for unowned gaps ("put the product manager on them"): every gap with a blank owner shows To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead; say how many gaps lack an owner.
  • Never print an asserted figure ("call it 80%") as coverage, never estimate statuses, never lower a gate to pass.
  • Never invent a gate: no min_coverage given → Gate: no minimum coverage given.
  • Never count a blank or absent row as implemented: it is missing.

Procedure — compute row by row from the supplied file, never estimate

  1. Catalogue (72): GOVERN 1.1-1.7, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.2, 6.1-6.2 (19) · MAP 1.1-1.6, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.5, 4.1-4.2, 5.1-5.2 (18) · MEASURE 1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.13, 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.3 (22) · MANAGE 1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3 (13). Function = the word before the number.
  2. Read each data row (skip # lines). Status blank and evidence blank → unfilled template row = missing. Status not in implemented|partial|planned|not_applicable, or a duplicate id → stops (exit 2). An id not in the catalogue → ERROR row, excluded from coverage, run stops (exit 1) after writing outputs.
  3. Per function, count implemented, partial, planned, not_applicable from the rows; missing = function total − rows counted. applicable = total − not_applicable.
  4. coverage = (implemented + 0.5 × partial) ÷ applicable, 3 decimals. Same for ALL (72).
  5. Evidence-backed coverage (gate basis): an implemented/partial row with blank evidence gets no credit (counted as missing). Flag those ids ("implemented/partial with no evidence cited: …") and not_applicable rows with blank evidence.
  6. Gate (only with min_coverage): evidence-backed ALL coverage ≥ min → PASS (equality passes); below → FAIL, run stops (exit 1) with full outputs written. Say "stops (exit 1)" explicitly.
  7. Gaps = partial, planned, missing. Owner blank → To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead. Count gaps without a named owner.
  8. Obligations (only if given): skip status done/not_applicable. Look up assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv (trailing * = prefix match, e.g. TR-50-* → MEASURE 2.8). supported = every mapped subcategory implemented or not_applicable (≥1 implemented); partial = any implemented/partial; none = only planned/missing; no row → no crosswalk entry. Label it "the skill's own crosswalk, not an official NIST or EU mapping".

Reply layout

  1. Working table first: function | total | implemented | partial | planned | not_applicable | missing | applicable | coverage | evidence-backed, rows GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE, ALL, with the formula (implemented + 0.5 × partial) ÷ applicable stated above it. Then the gate verdict.
  2. Gaps — subcategory_id | function | status | owner for every gap (or grouped by function with ids listed when long); count without owner.
  3. Flags, AI Act obligations (if given), outputs written.
  4. Limits — voluntary framework, self-assessed statuses; self-assessment, not compliance, certification or an audit.

No register rows in the conversation (a spreadsheet is mentioned but not attached, or "call it 80%"): still give the layout — the function table with formula and every cell To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead, gaps "all subcategories without a row are missing; owner To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead", the self-assessment line — and ask once for the evidence register as subcategory_id,status,evidence,owner (ids as in NIST AI 100-1, e.g. GOVERN 1.1; template assets/evidence-template.csv). Without evidence the run stops (exit 2). Do not estimate coverage.

  • Existing — bring the evidence register you maintain (and obligations.csv from eu-ai-act-classifier); the skill re-scores coverage, withholds credit from uncited claims, tracks the open obligations and applies your minimum-coverage gate.

  • NOT for: AI Act tiering (eu-ai-act-classifier), risk registers and likelihood/impact scoring (ai-governance-risk), evaluating the AI system itself (llm-eval-harness, red-team-suite), certification or audit opinions.

bodyMd:
# AI Controls Mapping (NIST AI RMF 1.0)

## In a conversation: map the controls now
The reply **is the controls mapping**: first line `Coverage: <overall, or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]> against NIST AI RMF 1.0 (72 subcategories) — self-assessment, not an audit`. It corresponds to `python3 -I scripts/map_controls.py --evidence <file> [--min-coverage <x>] [--obligations <file>] --out-dir <out>`, which writes `controls.csv`, `coverage.json` and `controls-report.md`; name that command (with the case's flags) and those files.

**Never**
- Never assign an owner the user names for unowned gaps ("put the product manager on them"): every gap with a blank owner shows `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`; say how many gaps lack an owner.
- Never print an asserted figure ("call it 80%") as coverage, never estimate statuses, never lower a gate to pass.
- Never invent a gate: no `min_coverage` given → `Gate: no minimum coverage given`.
- Never count a blank or absent row as implemented: it is `missing`.

**Procedure — compute row by row from the supplied file, never estimate**
1. Catalogue (72): GOVERN 1.1-1.7, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.2, 6.1-6.2 (19) · MAP 1.1-1.6, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.5, 4.1-4.2, 5.1-5.2 (18) · MEASURE 1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.13, 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.3 (22) · MANAGE 1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3 (13). Function = the word before the number.
2. Read each data row (skip `#` lines). Status blank **and** evidence blank → unfilled template row = `missing`. Status not in implemented|partial|planned|not_applicable, or a duplicate id → **stops (exit 2)**. An id not in the catalogue → `ERROR` row, excluded from coverage, run **stops (exit 1)** after writing outputs.
3. Per function, count implemented, partial, planned, not_applicable from the rows; missing = function total − rows counted. applicable = total − not_applicable.
4. coverage = (implemented + 0.5 × partial) ÷ applicable, 3 decimals. Same for ALL (72).
5. Evidence-backed coverage (gate basis): an implemented/partial row with blank `evidence` gets no credit (counted as missing). Flag those ids ("implemented/partial with no evidence cited: …") and not_applicable rows with blank evidence.
6. Gate (only with min_coverage): evidence-backed ALL coverage ≥ min → PASS (equality passes); below → FAIL, run **stops (exit 1)** with full outputs written. Say "stops (exit 1)" explicitly.
7. Gaps = partial, planned, missing. Owner blank → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`. Count gaps without a named owner.
8. Obligations (only if given): skip status done/not_applicable. Look up `assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv` (trailing `*` = prefix match, e.g. TR-50-* → MEASURE 2.8). supported = every mapped subcategory implemented or not_applicable (≥1 implemented); partial = any implemented/partial; none = only planned/missing; no row → `no crosswalk entry`. Label it "the skill's own crosswalk, not an official NIST or EU mapping".

**Reply layout**
1. Working table first: `function | total | implemented | partial | planned | not_applicable | missing | applicable | coverage | evidence-backed`, rows GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE, ALL, with the formula `(implemented + 0.5 × partial) ÷ applicable` stated above it. Then the gate verdict.
2. Gaps — `subcategory_id | function | status | owner` for every gap (or grouped by function with ids listed when long); count without owner.
3. Flags, AI Act obligations (if given), outputs written.
4. Limits — voluntary framework, self-assessed statuses; self-assessment, not compliance, certification or an audit.

**No register rows in the conversation** (a spreadsheet is mentioned but not attached, or "call it 80%"): still give the layout — the function table with formula and every cell `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`, gaps "all subcategories without a row are missing; owner [TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]", the self-assessment line — and ask once for the evidence register as `subcategory_id,status,evidence,owner` (ids as in NIST AI 100-1, e.g. `GOVERN 1.1`; template `assets/evidence-template.csv`). Without evidence the run stops (exit 2). Do not estimate coverage.

## Starting points
- **New** — starting a controls programme: fill `assets/evidence-template.csv` with what exists today; blank rows count as missing and the report gives the baseline coverage and the full gap list.
- **Existing** — bring the evidence register you maintain (and `obligations.csv` from `eu-ai-act-classifier`); the skill re-scores coverage, withholds credit from uncited claims, tracks the open obligations and applies your minimum-coverage gate.

## When to use
- ADLC govern stage: before a release review, an audit or a customer assurance questionnaire that asks for NIST AI RMF alignment.
- "Where are our gaps across GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE, and who owns them?"
- After `eu-ai-act-classifier`: pass its `obligations.csv` to see which open AI Act obligations lack supporting evidence.
- NOT for: AI Act tiering (`eu-ai-act-classifier`), risk registers and likelihood/impact scoring (`ai-governance-risk`), evaluating the AI system itself (`llm-eval-harness`, `red-team-suite`), certification or audit opinions.

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evidence` — `subcategory_id,status,evidence,owner` | yes | AI risk lead with control owners (copy `assets/evidence-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| owner blank on a row | — | control owner | `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]` |
| subcategory absent from `evidence` | — | — | counted as `missing` (a gap) |
| `min_coverage` — fraction 0-1 | no | AI risk lead | no gate; coverage reported only |
| `obligations` — classifier `obligations.csv` | no | `eu-ai-act-classifier` run | AI Act section omitted |

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Copy `assets/evidence-template.csv` (all 72 ids). Owners fill status, evidence (document id or link) and owner. Mark `not_applicable` only with a justification in `evidence`.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/map_controls.py` joins the evidence to `assets/nist-ai-rmf-1.0.csv` and computes coverage per `references/crosswalk-method.md`.
4. With `obligations`, it looks up each open obligation in `assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv` (the skill's own mapping) and reports supported, partial or none.
5. Exit 1 means coverage is below `min_coverage` or there are unknown ids. Fix the evidence; do not lower the threshold to pass.
6. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `controls.csv` — `subcategory_id, function, category, status, evidence, owner, gap, note`: 72 rows in catalogue order, plus `ERROR` rows for unknown ids.
- `coverage.json` — per-function and overall counts (implemented, partial, planned, not_applicable, missing, applicable) and coverage; gate; gaps; flags; input errors; AI Act obligation support.
- `controls-report.md` — **Summary**, **Coverage by function**, **Gaps** (with the AI Act sub-section when given), **Evidence register**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] All 72 subcategories present; counts per function are 19/18/22/13
- [ ] Coverage recomputes from controls.csv (`--verify` passes)
- [ ] Every gap has an owner or the AI risk lead TBD marker
- [ ] Claims without evidence and unjustified not_applicable rows are flagged
- [ ] The crosswalk is labelled the skill's own mapping wherever it is shown
- [ ] Limits stated: voluntary framework, self-assessed statuses, not compliance or an audit

## References
- `references/sources.md` — NIST AI 100-1, Playbook, crosswalk list; URLs and check date
- `references/crosswalk-method.md` — coverage formula, gap rules, crosswalk rules and limits
- `assets/nist-ai-rmf-1.0.csv` — 72 subcategories with function, category and paraphrase
- `assets/evidence-template.csv` — input template
- `assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv` — AI Act obligation → subcategory mapping (skill's own)
- `scripts/map_controls.py` — mapper and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-controls-mapping --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-controls-mapping`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`controls.csv`, `coverage.json`, `controls-report.md`). With `min_coverage`, the skill is a gate: evidence-backed coverage (claims with no evidence cited get no credit) below the minimum fails the run (exit 1) and the outputs are still written. Unknown subcategory ids also fail the run until they are fixed.

bodyMd:
# AI FinOps Chargeback (showback)

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-finops-chargeback --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-finops-chargeback`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`showback.csv`, `anomalies.csv`, `budget.csv`, `finops-report.md`). Every dollar figure in the report traces to the CSVs, and each output is re-verified against the inputs with `--verify`. With `strict=true` the run is a gate: a team forecast over budget exits 1, with complete outputs.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — you bring metered usage from the AI gateway, the dated price sheet and (optionally) team budgets; the skill allocates the spend, flags anomalies and forecasts each budget.
- Only for existing: chargeback allocates spend that has already been metered; pricing a workload before launch goes to `llm-cost-model`.

## When to use
- ADLC operate stage: monthly showback of AI spend to the teams and features that consume it, before Finance decides on chargeback.
- Unit economics: cost per 1k requests by feature and model, to target optimisation work.
- Budget tracking mid-month: run-rate forecast and variance per team, with a strict gate for alerts.
- Spend spike triage: which team-days broke the trailing-14-day pattern and which feature drove them.
- NOT for: pricing a planned workload before launch (`llm-cost-model`), GPU or self-hosting sizing (`infra-gpu-sizing`), provider invoice reconciliation or posting journal entries (Finance owns chargeback posting).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` — date, team, feature, model, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens[, cached_input_tokens] | yes | AI gateway / provider usage export, tagged by team and feature | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `prices` — model, input_per_1m, output_per_1m[, cached_input_per_1m], effective_from | yes | FinOps lead, from contract or vendor price page, dated | run stops (exit 2), asks once; never estimated |
| `budgets` — team, month, budget_usd | no | FinOps lead / budget owners | every budget reads `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead]`, status NO BUDGET |
| `as_of` — YYYY-MM-DD | no | run owner | latest usage date |
| `strict` — true/false | no | FinOps lead | false: over-budget reported, run exits 0 |

A usage row whose model has no price row, or no price in effect on its date, gets no cost: it is listed under Unpriced usage with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead]` and excluded from every total.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Export usage per day with team and feature tags; copy the layouts in `assets/`. Confirm `input_tokens` includes cached tokens.
3. Get the dated price sheet from the FinOps lead (one row per price change). Never fill a price from memory.
4. Run the agent. `scripts/chargeback.py` applies `references/method.md`.
5. Read Summary, then Budgets (OVER BUDGET rows first), Anomalies (send each to the team's engineering lead), Unpriced usage (FinOps lead adds price rows and re-runs).
6. Publish showback (team and team_feature rows). Chargeback posting is Finance's call once unpriced usage is priced and figures reconcile to the invoice.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `showback.csv` — `level, month, team, feature, model, requests, cost_usd, cost_per_1k_requests, share, mom_change_pct, input_tokens, output_tokens`; levels total, month, month_team, team, team_feature, model, detail.
- `anomalies.csv` — `date, team, cost_usd, trailing_mean_usd, trailing_sd_usd, threshold_usd, excess_usd, prior_days, top_feature`.
- `budget.csv` — `team, month, budget, actual, forecast, variance, status, basis, days_elapsed, days_in_month, unpriced_requests`.
- `finops-report.md` — **Summary**, **Spend by team**, **Unit economics**, **Anomalies**, **Budgets**, **Unpriced usage**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every price came from the supplied sheet; unpriced usage is TBD for the FinOps lead, never estimated
- [ ] Totals reconcile to the cent across levels (total = months = teams)
- [ ] Every $ figure in the report appears in a CSV (`numbers_trace_to` passes)
- [ ] The as-of month is flagged as partial; forecasts use the stated as-of date, never today
- [ ] Anomaly rule and forecast method are stated in Method; they are this skill's method, not a standard
- [ ] Fixture or fictional prices are never presented as real vendor prices

## References
- `references/method.md` — formulas, levels, worked example (the eval fixture, hand-checked), how showback feeds chargeback
- `references/sources.md` — FinOps Foundation showback / chargeback definitions, checked 2026-10-18
- `assets/usage-template.csv`, `assets/prices-template.csv`, `assets/budgets-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/chargeback.py` — calculator and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 strict over budget / 2 input)

bodyHtml:
AI Governance & Risk Review

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-governance-risk --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-governance-risk). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (risk-register.csv, register-diff.csv, model-card.md). Scores the canvas cannot support stay To be baselined · owner to be named; a High risk with no mapped control fails the run (exit 1) on purpose.

Starting points

  • New — a new AI use case: bring the filled use-case canvas; the register is scored only where the canvas supports it and everything else is TBD for the AI risk lead.
  • Existing — bring the updated canvas and last quarter's risk register; risk IDs stay stable, the canvas wins where it supports a value, reviewed scores, owners and still-valid controls carry forward (labelled for re-confirmation), and register-diff.csv lists every change, including rows that could not be carried.

When to use

  • Pre-launch risk review of an AI use case; building or refreshing the AI risk register; model documentation; regulatory mapping at summary level.
  • NOT for: legal opinions (state this; route to counsel), strategy/CoE (ai-strategy-coe), eval mechanics (llm-eval-harness).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Use-case description: purpose, users, decisions influenced, autonomy levelyesuser / design doc
Data: categories (PII, special categories, minors, financial, health, education records), sources, jurisdictionsyesuser
Model(s): provider/open-weights, version, fine-tuned?, hosting locationyesuser
Deployment context: internal / employee-facing / customer-facing / regulated decisionyesuser
Existing controls and policiesnouser
Existing risk register (e.g. last quarter's risk-register.csv)noAI risk lead; carried forward by category, changes in register-diff.csv
Applicable regulations the org already tracksnouser; otherwise summary mapping only

If the use case, data categories, or deployment context are missing, ask once.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Classify the use case. Determine the internal risk tier (low / medium / high) using references/risk-taxonomy.md §Tiering, and the summary EU AI Act tier using references/regulatory-mapping.md. State both with the criteria met.
  3. Identify risks. Walk the taxonomy (bias, privacy, hallucination, IP, security, misuse, operational, transparency). For each applicable risk: scenario, likelihood (1–5), impact (1–5), inherent score, in assets/risk-register.csv.
  4. Select controls from references/controls-catalog.md per risk; record control owner, status (in place / planned / gap), evidence, and residual score. Gaps become next steps with owner and date.
  5. Write the model card from assets/model-card.md: intended use, out-of-scope use, data, evaluation results (from llm-eval-harness where available), limitations, monitoring, contacts.
  6. Map to frameworks at summary level with references/regulatory-mapping.md: NIST AI RMF Govern/Map/Measure/Manage coverage table; EU AI Act tier and headline obligations; note other regimes the org names. Add the line: "Summary mapping for planning; legal review required for obligations."
  7. Decide. Launch recommendation: go / go with conditions / no-go, with the conditions listed as owner + date.
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

  • ai-risk-review-<use-case>.md: tiering, risk register table, controls, model card, framework mapping, decision, next steps.
  • risk-register.csv filled.
  • register-diff.csv — every carry-forward and change against the existing register (header only when none was given).

Self-check

  • [ ] Both internal tier and EU AI Act summary tier stated with criteria
  • [ ] Every risk has likelihood, impact, control, owner, residual score
  • [ ] Zero gaps without an owner and date
  • [ ] Model card has out-of-scope uses and limitations, not only intended use
  • [ ] Framework mapping is labeled summary-level; legal review line present
  • [ ] No fabricated regulatory citations; cite article/section only when provided by a source
  • [ ] Decision line is first

References

  • references/risk-taxonomy.md — risk categories, scenarios, tiering
  • references/controls-catalog.md — controls by risk with evidence expectations
  • references/regulatory-mapping.md — NIST AI RMF functions, EU AI Act tiers (summary)
  • scripts/risk_register.py — canvas + controls catalog (+ optional existing register) → risk-register.csv + register-diff.csv + model-card.md; exit 1 if a High risk has no control

Risk register covers bias, privacy (minors, education records), hallucination, security, transparency with likelihood/impact/controls/owners

NIST AI RMF coverage table and legal-review disclaimer line present
Decision line first: go with conditions or no-go, with owners and dates

# AI Governance & Risk Review

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-governance-risk --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-governance-risk`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`risk-register.csv`, `register-diff.csv`, `model-card.md`). Scores the canvas cannot support stay `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; a High risk with no mapped control fails the run (exit 1) on purpose.

## Starting points
- **New** — a new AI use case: bring the filled use-case canvas; the register is scored only where the canvas supports it and everything else is TBD for the AI risk lead.
- **Existing** — bring the updated canvas and last quarter's risk register; risk IDs stay stable, the canvas wins where it supports a value, reviewed scores, owners and still-valid controls carry forward (labelled for re-confirmation), and `register-diff.csv` lists every change, including rows that could not be carried.

## When to use
- Pre-launch risk review of an AI use case; building or refreshing the AI risk register; model documentation; regulatory mapping at summary level.
- NOT for: legal opinions (state this; route to counsel), strategy/CoE (`ai-strategy-coe`), eval mechanics (`llm-eval-harness`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Use-case description: purpose, users, decisions influenced, autonomy level | yes | user / design doc |
| Data: categories (PII, special categories, minors, financial, health, education records), sources, jurisdictions | yes | user |
| Model(s): provider/open-weights, version, fine-tuned?, hosting location | yes | user |
| Deployment context: internal / employee-facing / customer-facing / regulated decision | yes | user |
| Existing controls and policies | no | user |
| Existing risk register (e.g. last quarter's `risk-register.csv`) | no | AI risk lead; carried forward by category, changes in `register-diff.csv` |
| Applicable regulations the org already tracks | no | user; otherwise summary mapping only |

If the use case, data categories, or deployment context are missing, ask once.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. **Classify the use case.** Determine the internal risk tier (low / medium / high) using `references/risk-taxonomy.md` §Tiering, and the summary EU AI Act tier using `references/regulatory-mapping.md`. State both with the criteria met.
3. **Identify risks.** Walk the taxonomy (bias, privacy, hallucination, IP, security, misuse, operational, transparency). For each applicable risk: scenario, likelihood (1–5), impact (1–5), inherent score, in `assets/risk-register.csv`.
4. **Select controls** from `references/controls-catalog.md` per risk; record control owner, status (in place / planned / gap), evidence, and residual score. Gaps become next steps with owner and date.
5. **Write the model card** from `assets/model-card.md`: intended use, out-of-scope use, data, evaluation results (from `llm-eval-harness` where available), limitations, monitoring, contacts.
6. **Map to frameworks** at summary level with `references/regulatory-mapping.md`: NIST AI RMF Govern/Map/Measure/Manage coverage table; EU AI Act tier and headline obligations; note other regimes the org names. Add the line: "Summary mapping for planning; legal review required for obligations."
7. **Decide.** Launch recommendation: go / go with conditions / no-go, with the conditions listed as owner + date.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `ai-risk-review-<use-case>.md`: tiering, risk register table, controls, model card, framework mapping, decision, next steps.
- `risk-register.csv` filled.
- `register-diff.csv` — every carry-forward and change against the existing register (header only when none was given).

## Self-check
- [ ] Both internal tier and EU AI Act summary tier stated with criteria
- [ ] Every risk has likelihood, impact, control, owner, residual score
- [ ] Zero gaps without an owner and date
- [ ] Model card has out-of-scope uses and limitations, not only intended use
- [ ] Framework mapping is labeled summary-level; legal review line present
- [ ] No fabricated regulatory citations; cite article/section only when provided by a source
- [ ] Decision line is first

## References
- `references/risk-taxonomy.md` — risk categories, scenarios, tiering
- `references/controls-catalog.md` — controls by risk with evidence expectations
- `references/regulatory-mapping.md` — NIST AI RMF functions, EU AI Act tiers (summary)
- `scripts/risk_register.py` — canvas + controls catalog (+ optional existing register) → `risk-register.csv` + `register-diff.csv` + `model-card.md`; exit 1 if a High risk has no control

AI Incident Runbook

In a conversation: write the runbook now

The reply is the runbook: its first line is Severity: SEV<n> (provisional) — <rule ids that fired> — <the facts and unknowns that drove it>, never only a request for a CSV. Contain first; questions go after the actions.

  • The request describes the incident ("our assistant showed one member another member's claim details; started about an hour ago"), or says facts are attached but they are not in the conversation: write the runbook in this reply from the stated facts, in this order:
    1. Severity — classify with the skill's default matrix (references/severity-matrix.md) and say so; list every fired row. Missing users_affected, data_exposed, regulated_data are unknown, and unknown escalates (D02: exposure confirmed, regulated status unknown → SEV1; D03: exposure not ruled out, regulated data possible → SEV2; D12: users unknown → SEV3). Severity goes down only with evidence.
    2. Immediate actions — contain first, from assets/playbooks/<category>.md. For a data leak: disable the leaking path now (feature flag off, tool or connector revoked, retrieval source detached), preserve evidence (traces, logs, outputs) while restricting access to them, revoke and rotate any credentials that appeared. Timeline holds only the times the user gave (e.g. "started ~1 hour ago" as stated); every other time is To be baselined · owner: Incident commander.
    3. Containment and Recovery — the playbook's contain, eradicate, recover and verify steps.
    4. Communications — internal always; customer unless users_affected = 0; regulator track when regulated data is yes or unknown, flagged for Legal / privacy to confirm obligations and deadlines — no deadline is set or invented.
    5. Postmortem skeleton — fields and action items, including a regression eval case and the missing alert.
    6. Owners — incident commander, engineering lead, comms lead, legal/privacy, security lead: named only if the user named them, else To be baselined · owner: <role>.
    7. Facts I need — ask once, in one list: users affected, whether data was exposed and whether it is regulated, exact start and detection times, system name; until answered they stay unknown and escalate.
  • No incident facts at all ("we had an AI incident, give me the runbook"): ask once for category, start time, users affected, data exposed, regulated data (yes/no/unknown) and owners; do not guess a severity.
  • Asked to assume it's fine or keep severity low: decline in one line — unknown regulated status or exposure escalates. Show the severity the matrix gives (e.g. prompt injection with regulated status unknown → SEV2 via D03), keep the regulator track, and leave users, detection time and owners as TBD markers. A supplied matrix in which no row fires is rejected; ask for a baseline row rather than guessing a severity.

  • Existing — bring the incident facts and your team's own severity matrix; every row of your matrix is evaluated, the fired rules are listed, and a matrix with no baseline row fails the run instead of guessing.

  • A live AI incident: hallucination, data leak, prompt injection, outage, cost spike or harmful output.

  • NOT for: legal advice on notification duties (route to counsel), detection and SLO alerting (llm-observability), pre-launch risk review (ai-governance-risk), turning feedback into fixes (feedback-improvement-loop).

- **No incident facts at all** ("we had an AI incident, give me the runbook"): ask once for category, start time, users affected, data exposed, regulated data (yes/no/unknown) and owners; do not guess a severity.
- **Asked to assume it's fine or keep severity low**: decline in one line — unknown regulated status or exposure escalates. Show the severity the matrix gives (e.g. prompt injection with regulated status unknown → SEV2 via D03), keep the regulator track, and leave users, detection time and owners as TBD markers. A supplied matrix in which no row fires is rejected; ask for a baseline row rather than guessing a severity.

## Starting points
- **New** — no runbook or severity policy yet: bring the incident facts; the skill classifies with its documented default matrix (and says so) and assembles the runbook.
- **Existing** — bring the incident facts and your team's own severity matrix; every row of your matrix is evaluated, the fired rules are listed, and a matrix with no baseline row fails the run instead of guessing.

## When to use
- A live AI incident: hallucination, data leak, prompt injection, outage, cost spike or harmful output.
- Classifying severity consistently and showing why; producing the comms checklist and the postmortem skeleton.
- NOT for: legal advice on notification duties (route to counsel), detection and SLO alerting (`llm-observability`), pre-launch risk review (`ai-governance-risk`), turning feedback into fixes (`feedback-improvement-loop`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `incident` CSV: `category`, `started_at` | yes | incident commander |
| `users_affected`, `data_exposed`, `regulated_data` (yes/no/unknown) | no — missing = unknown, and unknown escalates | incident commander, privacy |
| `detected_at`, `detected_by`, `system_name`, `summary` | no | alert or report |
| `owner_<role>`: incident_commander, engineering_lead, comms_lead, legal_privacy, security_lead | no — missing = TBD with the accountable role | on-call rota |
| `matrix` CSV (rule_id, conditions, severity, reason) | no | your incident policy; default = the skill's documented matrix |

If `incident` is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. No time, name or count is invented.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Fill `assets/incident-template.csv` with what is known now; leave unknowns as `unknown`.
3. Run the skill. The script evaluates every matrix row (`references/severity-matrix.md`), takes the most severe, and lists every fired row as reasoning.
4. It loads `assets/playbooks/<category>.md` into Containment (contain, eradicate) and Recovery (recover, verify).
5. It builds the timeline from `started_at` / `detected_at` only; later events are TBD for the Incident commander.
6. Communications: internal always; customer unless `users_affected = 0`; regulator only when `regulated_data` is yes or unknown, with Legal / privacy confirming obligations.
7. Re-run as facts change (unknown → yes/no); severity can go down only with evidence.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `runbook.md`: Severity (fired rules, facts, unknowns), Immediate actions (+ Timeline), Containment, Recovery, Communications (internal, customer, regulator), Postmortem (fields and action items).
- `incident.json`: the same record, machine-readable.

## Self-check
- [ ] Severity shows every fired row and the matrix source (supplied or the skill's default)
- [ ] Unknown data/regulated status escalated, not assumed away
- [ ] Regulator track present only for regulated yes/unknown; no deadlines invented
- [ ] Timeline holds only supplied times; the rest TBD with an owner role
- [ ] Every owner named or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`
- [ ] Postmortem action items include a regression eval case and the missing alert

## References
- `references/severity-matrix.md` — the default matrix, method, comms rule
- `references/severity-matrix.default.csv` — machine copy of the default matrix
- `assets/playbooks/` — per-category playbooks (contain, eradicate, recover, verify)
- `assets/incident-template.csv` — input layout
- `scripts/runbook.py` — the classifier and runbook builder (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-incident-runbook --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-incident-runbook`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`runbook.md`, `incident.json`). A severity matrix in which no row fires fails the run (exit 1) on purpose.
