bodyHtml:
AI Postmortem (blameless, measured, owned)

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-postmortem --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-postmortem). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (postmortem.md, timings.json, actions.csv, eval-cases.csv). With strict=true the run is a gate: it exits 1 when a factor has no action or an action has no owner, and still writes every output so the gaps are visible.

Starting points

  • Existing — you bring the facts and timeline of an incident that happened (plus factors and actions when known); the skill measures the timings, checks the actions cover every factor and turns the failure into eval cases.
  • Only for existing: a postmortem always concerns an incident that has already happened; a live incident goes to ai-incident-runbook.

When to use

  • After an AI incident is mitigated: bad answers at scale, prompt-injection exploit, cost runaway, outage, harmful output, data leak.
  • Measuring time to detect, acknowledge, mitigate and resolve from the real timeline, and showing which milestones are missing.
  • Closing the loop: every contributing factor has an owned, dated action; failing inputs become regression evals.
  • NOT for: responding while the incident is live — severity, containment, comms (ai-incident-runbook); alerts and SLOs (llm-observability); scoring the eval set (llm-eval-harness); legal or HR determinations.

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
incident — key,value,source,notes: id, title, started_at (+ severity, system, customer_impact, detection_source, went_well)yesIncident commander; severity and start time from the ai-incident-runbook runrun stops (exit 2), asks once; optional keys become To be baselined · owner: Incident commander
timeline — timestamp,event,description,actor_roleyesincident channel, pager, deploy logrun stops (exit 2), asks once
factors — factor,category,evidencenopostmortem review meetingfactors TBD for the Incident commander; strict gate fails
actions — action,type,owner,due,factornopostmortem review meetingactions TBD for the Incident commander
strict — true/falsenoengineering leadfalse: gaps reported, run exits 0

Write actor_role as a role, never a person's name. Mark a failing user input in any description or evidence as input:"..." and the bad reply as output:"..." so it can become a regression case.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Copy assets/incident-template.csv, assets/timeline-template.csv, assets/factors-template.csv and assets/actions-template.csv. Carry started_at, detected_at and severity over from the ai-incident-runbook output.
  3. Pick each factor's category from assets/factor-taxonomy.csv. Describe systems and processes, not people.
  4. Run the skill. scripts/postmortem.py computes timings per references/method.md, flags missing and out-of-order milestones, links actions to factors and scans for blame phrasing (assets/blame-phrases.csv).
  5. Fix every flag in the inputs (rewrite blameful text, add owners, link uncovered factors) and re-run until the strict gate passes.
  6. Hand eval-cases.csv to the Eval lead: fill must_contain / must_not_contain, then feed it to llm-eval-harness.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • postmortem.md — Summary, Impact, Timeline, Timings, Contributing factors, What went well, Actions, Lessons for the eval set, Method (with the blameless language check).
  • timings.json — milestones, minutes per measure with basis, flags, coverage and gate result.
  • actions.csv — action, type, owner, due, factor, status (status open | in-progress | done | blocked: no owner | blocked: no due date).
  • eval-cases.csv — proposed regression cases in the llm-eval-harness golden-set columns.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every timing traces to two timeline timestamps; missing milestones are flagged, not estimated
  • [ ] An incident with no resolved event is reported OPEN
  • [ ] Every factor has at least one action; every action has an owner and a due date, or a TBD naming the Incident commander
  • [ ] Blame-phrase hits rewritten as system or process conditions
  • [ ] Eval cases use only inputs quoted in the timeline or factors; scoring left to the Eval lead
  • [ ] --verify passes on all four outputs
  • [ ] Limits stated: word-list blame scan, timeline accuracy, not a legal determination

References

  • references/method.md — timing definitions, ordering rules, coverage, eval-case extraction, limits
  • references/sources.md — blameless postmortem practice (Google SRE book ch. 15, SRE workbook ch. 10), checked 2026-10-18
  • assets/factor-taxonomy.csv — AI contributing-factor categories
  • assets/blame-phrases.csv — blame word list with rewrite hints
  • assets/incident-template.csv, assets/timeline-template.csv, assets/factors-template.csv, assets/actions-template.csv — input layouts
  • scripts/postmortem.py — builder and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

bodyMd:
# AI Postmortem (blameless, measured, owned)

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-postmortem --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-postmortem`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`postmortem.md`, `timings.json`, `actions.csv`, `eval-cases.csv`). With `strict=true` the run is a gate: it exits 1 when a factor has no action or an action has no owner, and still writes every output so the gaps are visible.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — you bring the facts and timeline of an incident that happened (plus factors and actions when known); the skill measures the timings, checks the actions cover every factor and turns the failure into eval cases.
- Only for existing: a postmortem always concerns an incident that has already happened; a live incident goes to `ai-incident-runbook`.

## When to use
- After an AI incident is mitigated: bad answers at scale, prompt-injection exploit, cost runaway, outage, harmful output, data leak.
- Measuring time to detect, acknowledge, mitigate and resolve from the real timeline, and showing which milestones are missing.
- Closing the loop: every contributing factor has an owned, dated action; failing inputs become regression evals.
- NOT for: responding while the incident is live — severity, containment, comms (`ai-incident-runbook`); alerts and SLOs (`llm-observability`); scoring the eval set (`llm-eval-harness`); legal or HR determinations.

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `incident` — `key,value,source,notes`: `id`, `title`, `started_at` (+ `severity`, `system`, `customer_impact`, `detection_source`, `went_well`) | yes | Incident commander; severity and start time from the `ai-incident-runbook` run | run stops (exit 2), asks once; optional keys become `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Incident commander]` |
| `timeline` — `timestamp,event,description,actor_role` | yes | incident channel, pager, deploy log | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `factors` — `factor,category,evidence` | no | postmortem review meeting | factors TBD for the Incident commander; strict gate fails |
| `actions` — `action,type,owner,due,factor` | no | postmortem review meeting | actions TBD for the Incident commander |
| `strict` — true/false | no | engineering lead | false: gaps reported, run exits 0 |

Write `actor_role` as a role, never a person's name. Mark a failing user input in any description or evidence as `input:"..."` and the bad reply as `output:"..."` so it can become a regression case.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Copy `assets/incident-template.csv`, `assets/timeline-template.csv`, `assets/factors-template.csv` and `assets/actions-template.csv`. Carry `started_at`, `detected_at` and severity over from the `ai-incident-runbook` output.
3. Pick each factor's category from `assets/factor-taxonomy.csv`. Describe systems and processes, not people.
4. Run the skill. `scripts/postmortem.py` computes timings per `references/method.md`, flags missing and out-of-order milestones, links actions to factors and scans for blame phrasing (`assets/blame-phrases.csv`).
5. Fix every flag in the inputs (rewrite blameful text, add owners, link uncovered factors) and re-run until the strict gate passes.
6. Hand `eval-cases.csv` to the Eval lead: fill `must_contain` / `must_not_contain`, then feed it to `llm-eval-harness`.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `postmortem.md` — **Summary**, **Impact**, **Timeline**, **Timings**, **Contributing factors**, **What went well**, **Actions**, **Lessons for the eval set**, **Method** (with the blameless language check).
- `timings.json` — milestones, minutes per measure with basis, flags, coverage and gate result.
- `actions.csv` — `action, type, owner, due, factor, status` (status `open | in-progress | done | blocked: no owner | blocked: no due date`).
- `eval-cases.csv` — proposed regression cases in the `llm-eval-harness` golden-set columns.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every timing traces to two timeline timestamps; missing milestones are flagged, not estimated
- [ ] An incident with no `resolved` event is reported OPEN
- [ ] Every factor has at least one action; every action has an owner and a due date, or a TBD naming the Incident commander
- [ ] Blame-phrase hits rewritten as system or process conditions
- [ ] Eval cases use only inputs quoted in the timeline or factors; scoring left to the Eval lead
- [ ] `--verify` passes on all four outputs
- [ ] Limits stated: word-list blame scan, timeline accuracy, not a legal determination

## References
- `references/method.md` — timing definitions, ordering rules, coverage, eval-case extraction, limits
- `references/sources.md` — blameless postmortem practice (Google SRE book ch. 15, SRE workbook ch. 10), checked 2026-10-18
- `assets/factor-taxonomy.csv` — AI contributing-factor categories
- `assets/blame-phrases.csv` — blame word list with rewrite hints
- `assets/incident-template.csv`, `assets/timeline-template.csv`, `assets/factors-template.csv`, `assets/actions-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/postmortem.py` — builder and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

bodyHtml:
AI Release Plan (staged rollout)

In a conversation: write the release plan now

The reply is the release plan: its first line is Readiness: READY / NOT READY / PENDING GATES — <the gates or facts that decided it>, never only a request for CSVs.

  • The request gives release facts (scores, risk tier, traffic — e.g. "offline evals 93%, red-team 98%, medium risk, ~48k requests a day"), or says facts and gates are attached but they are not in the conversation: write the plan in this reply, in this order:
    1. Readiness — gates come only from the owner; with none supplied, measured values are listed as "measured, gate threshold To be baselined · owner: Release manager" and readiness is PENDING GATES. Never propose default thresholds.
    2. Stages — offline eval → shadow (100 % mirrored, not served) → canary steps → GA. Canary steps by risk tier are the skill's policy (references/rollout-policy.md), say so: low 10, 50 %; medium 5, 25, 50 %; high 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 % (owner may override with canary_steps). Table: stage | traffic % | served | min hours | owner.
    3. Minimum durations — hours = ceil(min_observed_requests ÷ (daily_requests × traffic% ÷ 100 ÷ 24)), using the stated daily_requests; min_observed_requests is the owner's confidence choice, so show the formula and per-stage requests/hour (48,000/day at 5 % = 100/hour) and keep hours To be baselined · owner: Release manager until the owner sets it. Offline eval and GA have no duration.
    4. Gates — stage | metric | min | max | actual now | status (met / NOT MET / not measured); not measured never counts as met.
    5. Rollback — every shadow/canary/GA gate becomes a trigger; owner SRE on-call; rollback time as stated or TBD.
    6. Owners — Eval lead (offline eval), SRE on-call (shadow, rollback), Release manager (canary), Product owner (GA); any not named is To be baselined · owner: Release manager.
    7. What I need to finish — ask once for the gates (stage,metric,min,max for offline_eval, shadow, canary, ga), min_observed_requests, rollback_time_min and owner names.
  • A rollout under way (current stage plus live readings): decide the current stage — ROLL BACK if a gate is not met now, HOLD if a gate is not measured or too few requests were observed, else PROMOTE to the next step — with the Release manager as decision owner and the remaining rollback triggers kept.
  • No facts at all: ask once for system name, risk tier, measured metrics, daily requests and the gates; do not invent any.
  • Asked to use "standard" gates or mark ready despite a failed gate ("eval came in at 82% but mark us ready"): decline in one line — thresholds come only from the owner and a blocked first stage is NOT READY. Write the plan with the blocker (e.g. eval_pass_rate NOT MET) shown; never print the requested READY status or a made-up threshold.

Starting points

  • New — first rollout of a release: bring the release facts and the owner's gate thresholds; the skill builds offline eval → shadow → canary → GA, checks the first-stage gates now and sizes each stage.
  • Existing — a rollout already under way: add current_stage, the requests observed there and the live metric readings; the plan shows where you are and decides PROMOTE, HOLD or ROLL BACK for the current stage against the same gates.

When to use

  • A model, prompt, agent or RAG change is about to reach users and needs shadow → canary → GA with explicit gates.
  • "Are we ready?" — evaluate the owner's gates against the measured facts now.
  • NOT for: building the eval set or scoring it (llm-eval-harness), risk tiering (ai-governance-risk), pipeline wiring (ci-cd-vercel-github), live monitoring after GA (llm-observability).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
facts CSV key,value: system_name, risk_tier (low/medium/high)yesrelease owner; tier from ai-governance-risk
Measured metrics named by gates (e.g. eval_pass_rate, redteam_pass_rate, latency_p95_ms, error_rate)for gate statuseval run, red-team run, staging telemetry
daily_requests, min_observed_requestsfor durationstraffic forecast; owner's confidence target
rollback_time_min, owner_<role> (eval_lead, sre_oncall, release_manager, product_owner)noowner; missing → To be baselined · owner: Release manager
current_stage (stage id, e.g. canary_1), current_stage_observed_requestsonly for a rollout under wayrelease manager; live telemetry — metric facts are then the live readings
gates CSV stage,metric,min,max (stage ∈ offline_eval, shadow, canary, ga)yesrelease owner — the skill never supplies a threshold

If facts or gates is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. Missing optional facts stay TBD with an owner role; nothing is invented.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Copy assets/release-facts.csv and assets/release-gates.csv; the owner fills measured values and thresholds (with sources).
  3. Run the skill. The script builds the stage list from references/rollout-policy.md (canary steps by risk tier — the skill's policy, owner-overridable via canary_steps).
  4. It evaluates every gate against the facts now (references/gate-method.md): met / NOT MET / not measured; not measured never counts as met.
  5. It computes minimum shadow/canary durations: ceil(min_observed_requests ÷ (daily_requests × traffic% ÷ 24)) hours.
  6. It turns every live-stage gate into a rollback trigger and assigns an owner per step.
  7. Exit 1 if any offline_eval gate is not met or none was supplied; report the blockers, do not soften them. With current_stage set it also decides the current stage: ROLL BACK (a gate not met now; exit 1), HOLD (a gate not measured, no gate, or too few requests observed) or PROMOTE to the next stage (COMPLETE at GA).
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

  • release-plan.md: Readiness, Stages (traffic %, served, min hours, owner), Gates (threshold, actual now, status, source), Rollback (owner, time, triggers), Owners.
  • gates.json: the same plan, machine-readable (first_stage_ready, stages, gates, rollback_triggers, owners, current — null unless a rollout is under way).

Self-check

  • [ ] Every gate threshold came from the gates CSV; none defaulted
  • [ ] not measured gates are shown as such, never as met
  • [ ] Canary steps state their basis (tier policy or owner override)
  • [ ] Durations trace to daily_requests and min_observed_requests, or are TBD with an owner
  • [ ] Every rollback trigger maps to a gate; rollback owner named or TBD with role
  • [ ] Exit 1 when the first stage is blocked

References

  • references/rollout-policy.md — stage sequence, canary steps per risk tier (skill policy), owner per step
  • references/gate-method.md — gate statuses, duration formula, rollback triggers
  • assets/release-facts.csv, assets/release-gates.csv — input layouts
  • scripts/release_plan.py — the planner (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-release-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-release-plan). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (release-plan.md, gates.json). A first-stage gate that is not met fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the plan is still written so the blockers are visible.

bodyMd:
# AI Release Plan (staged rollout)

## In a conversation: write the release plan now
The reply **is the release plan**: its first line is `Readiness: READY / NOT READY / PENDING GATES — <the gates or facts that decided it>`, never only a request for CSVs.
- **The request gives release facts** (scores, risk tier, traffic — e.g. "offline evals 93%, red-team 98%, medium risk, ~48k requests a day"), or says facts and gates are attached but they are not in the conversation: write the plan **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **Readiness** — gates come only from the owner; with none supplied, measured values are listed as "measured, gate threshold `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]`" and readiness is PENDING GATES. Never propose default thresholds.
  2. **Stages** — offline eval → shadow (100 % mirrored, not served) → canary steps → GA. Canary steps by risk tier are **the skill's policy** (`references/rollout-policy.md`), say so: low 10, 50 %; **medium 5, 25, 50 %**; high 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 % (owner may override with `canary_steps`). Table: `stage | traffic % | served | min hours | owner`.
  3. **Minimum durations** — `hours = ceil(min_observed_requests ÷ (daily_requests × traffic% ÷ 100 ÷ 24))`, using the stated daily_requests; `min_observed_requests` is the owner's confidence choice, so show the formula and per-stage requests/hour (48,000/day at 5 % = 100/hour) and keep hours `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]` until the owner sets it. Offline eval and GA have no duration.
  4. **Gates** — `stage | metric | min | max | actual now | status (met / NOT MET / not measured)`; not measured never counts as met.
  5. **Rollback** — every shadow/canary/GA gate becomes a trigger; owner SRE on-call; rollback time as stated or TBD.
  6. **Owners** — Eval lead (offline eval), SRE on-call (shadow, rollback), Release manager (canary), Product owner (GA); any not named is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]`.
  7. **What I need to finish** — ask once for the gates (`stage,metric,min,max` for offline_eval, shadow, canary, ga), `min_observed_requests`, `rollback_time_min` and owner names.
- **A rollout under way** (current stage plus live readings): decide the current stage — ROLL BACK if a gate is not met now, HOLD if a gate is not measured or too few requests were observed, else PROMOTE to the next step — with the Release manager as decision owner and the remaining rollback triggers kept.
- **No facts at all**: ask once for system name, risk tier, measured metrics, daily requests and the gates; do not invent any.
- **Asked to use "standard" gates or mark ready despite a failed gate** ("eval came in at 82% but mark us ready"): decline in one line — thresholds come only from the owner and a blocked first stage is NOT READY. Write the plan with the blocker (e.g. eval_pass_rate NOT MET) shown; never print the requested READY status or a made-up threshold.

## Starting points
- **New** — first rollout of a release: bring the release facts and the owner's gate thresholds; the skill builds offline eval → shadow → canary → GA, checks the first-stage gates now and sizes each stage.
- **Existing** — a rollout already under way: add `current_stage`, the requests observed there and the live metric readings; the plan shows where you are and decides PROMOTE, HOLD or ROLL BACK for the current stage against the same gates.

## When to use
- A model, prompt, agent or RAG change is about to reach users and needs shadow → canary → GA with explicit gates.
- "Are we ready?" — evaluate the owner's gates against the measured facts now.
- NOT for: building the eval set or scoring it (`llm-eval-harness`), risk tiering (`ai-governance-risk`), pipeline wiring (`ci-cd-vercel-github`), live monitoring after GA (`llm-observability`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `facts` CSV `key,value`: `system_name`, `risk_tier` (low/medium/high) | yes | release owner; tier from `ai-governance-risk` |
| Measured metrics named by gates (e.g. `eval_pass_rate`, `redteam_pass_rate`, `latency_p95_ms`, `error_rate`) | for gate status | eval run, red-team run, staging telemetry |
| `daily_requests`, `min_observed_requests` | for durations | traffic forecast; owner's confidence target |
| `rollback_time_min`, `owner_<role>` (eval_lead, sre_oncall, release_manager, product_owner) | no | owner; missing → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]` |
| `current_stage` (stage id, e.g. `canary_1`), `current_stage_observed_requests` | only for a rollout under way | release manager; live telemetry — metric facts are then the live readings |
| `gates` CSV `stage,metric,min,max` (stage ∈ offline_eval, shadow, canary, ga) | yes | release owner — the skill never supplies a threshold |

If `facts` or `gates` is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. Missing optional facts stay TBD with an owner role; nothing is invented.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Copy `assets/release-facts.csv` and `assets/release-gates.csv`; the owner fills measured values and thresholds (with sources).
3. Run the skill. The script builds the stage list from `references/rollout-policy.md` (canary steps by risk tier — the skill's policy, owner-overridable via `canary_steps`).
4. It evaluates every gate against the facts now (`references/gate-method.md`): met / NOT MET / not measured; `not measured` never counts as met.
5. It computes minimum shadow/canary durations: `ceil(min_observed_requests ÷ (daily_requests × traffic% ÷ 24))` hours.
6. It turns every live-stage gate into a rollback trigger and assigns an owner per step.
7. Exit 1 if any `offline_eval` gate is not met or none was supplied; report the blockers, do not soften them.
   With `current_stage` set it also decides the current stage: ROLL BACK (a gate not met now; exit 1), HOLD (a gate not measured, no gate, or too few requests observed) or PROMOTE to the next stage (COMPLETE at GA).
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `release-plan.md`: Readiness, Stages (traffic %, served, min hours, owner), Gates (threshold, actual now, status, source), Rollback (owner, time, triggers), Owners.
- `gates.json`: the same plan, machine-readable (`first_stage_ready`, `stages`, `gates`, `rollback_triggers`, `owners`, `current` — null unless a rollout is under way).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every gate threshold came from the gates CSV; none defaulted
- [ ] `not measured` gates are shown as such, never as met
- [ ] Canary steps state their basis (tier policy or owner override)
- [ ] Durations trace to `daily_requests` and `min_observed_requests`, or are TBD with an owner
- [ ] Every rollback trigger maps to a gate; rollback owner named or TBD with role
- [ ] Exit 1 when the first stage is blocked

## References
- `references/rollout-policy.md` — stage sequence, canary steps per risk tier (skill policy), owner per step
- `references/gate-method.md` — gate statuses, duration formula, rollback triggers
- `assets/release-facts.csv`, `assets/release-gates.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/release_plan.py` — the planner (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-release-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-release-plan`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`release-plan.md`, `gates.json`). A first-stage gate that is not met fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the plan is still written so the blockers are visible.

name: ai-slo-definition
description: Use when the user needs service-level objectives for an AI feature — "define SLOs for our assistant", "what should our latency and availability targets be", "are we inside our error budget", "set up burn-rate alerts", "quality and cost per request as SLOs". Produces slos.csv, slo-spec.md (Summary, SLIs and objectives, Error budgets, Alerting policy, Method) and slo.json from a request log - availability, latency under threshold, quality pass rate and cost under threshold as SLIs, nearest-rank p50/p95/p99, error budget, budget consumed and multiwindow burn rates per the Google SRE workbook (14.4x / 6x / 1x for 30 days). Without targets it proposes objectives from observed data, each marked to be baselined by the Product owner. Exit 1 when an agreed SLO is breached. Not for live dashboards or trace schemas (llm-observability), distribution drift (drift-monitor) or monthly API cost forecasts (llm-cost-model).

bodyHtml:
AI SLO Definition

In a conversation: draft the SLO spec now

The reply is the SLO spec draft, never only a request for the log. No log rows are in the conversation, so no observed value is printed; every number the log would give is a marker.

  • The request names the feature and says logs exist ("a week of pilot logs", "here are two days of logs") but no rows are in the conversation: write the spec in this reply, in this order:
    1. Summary — line 1: Status: proposed — no objective is agreed until the Product owner signs it. Then how the objectives are set: scripts/slo.py is run on the pilot log without targets (python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input log=<pilot-log.csv> --input system="<feature>" --out <dir>), and each objective is proposed from the observed data.
    2. SLIs and objectives — table sli | good ÷ eligible | proposal rule | objective | threshold | status for the four SLIs: availability (status = ok ÷ every request); latency (ok requests with latency_ms <= threshold; failed requests count against availability only); quality (quality_pass = 1 ÷ labelled rows); cost (cost_usd <= threshold ÷ rows with a cost). Proposal rules from references/method.md: availability and quality take the highest ladder level not above the observed SLI (availability 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.99 / 0.995 / 0.999 / 0.9995 / 0.9999; quality 0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.98 / 0.99); latency threshold = observed nearest-rank p95 of ok requests rounded up to the next 100 ms at objective 0.95; cost threshold = observed p95 cost rounded up to the next 0.001 USD at objective 0.95. Every objective cell reads To be baselined · owner: Product owner and every status proposed; none is called agreed. Without quality_pass or cost_usd in the log, that SLI is "not measured" with its owner.
    3. Error budgets — error budget = 1 − objective; budget consumed = (1 − SLI) ÷ (1 − objective); above 1 is breached. Proposals are never gated; only agreed targets are.
    4. Alerting policy — Google SRE workbook multiwindow burn-rate alerts at a 30-day window: fast-burn page 14.4x over 1 h with a 5 m short window (2% of budget); slow-burn page 6x over 6 h / 30 m (5%); ticket 1x over 3 d / 6 h (10%). An alert fires when both windows burn at or above the threshold. The SLO window is To be baselined · owner: SRE lead until agreed; a pilot shorter than 3 days cannot show the ticket window.
    5. Method & limits — nearest-rank percentiles, the log must cover normal traffic, quality depends on labelling; then the next step: take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead, then re-run with the agreed targets file (sli,objective,threshold,window_days).
  • Agreed targets and a measurement are asked for ("measure against our targets", "errors spiked — check the SLOs and alerts"): give the same sections with the stated targets as objectives, the observed / consumed / burn columns as To be baselined · owner: SRE lead until the log is run, and state the gate: consumed above 1 on an agreed SLO is breached and the run exits 1 with every output written; a firing alert on an unbreached SLO is at-risk.
  • No feature and no log mentioned at all: ask once, in one list, for the request log (timestamp, latency_ms, status, optional quality_pass, cost_usd), any agreed targets, and the feature name. Do not invent latency, availability or cost figures.
  • Asked to "just set sensible SLOs" or to lower an objective so a breach passes: decline in one line — objectives come from observed data and the Product owner's agreement, not from typical industry numbers, and a breached objective is not lowered to pass the gate without the Product owner. Never print a suggested target number; show To be baselined · owner: Product owner and the proposal rules above.
  • Distribution drift ("have our confidence scores shifted since launch?"): that is drift-monitor; this skill measures SLIs against objectives.

Starting points

  • New — no SLOs yet: bring a pilot request log; every objective is proposed from the observed data and marked for the Product owner to agree.
  • Existing — bring the production request log and the targets already agreed; the skill measures each SLI against them, computes budget burn and flags breaches.

When to use

  • ADLC requirements stage: turn "it should be fast and reliable" into measurable SLIs, objectives and error budgets before build sign-off.
  • Drafting first objectives from a pilot or shadow log: the skill proposes them from observed data for the Product owner to accept or change.
  • Checking a release or a week of traffic against agreed targets, and wiring the burn-rate alert policy.
  • NOT for: dashboards, trace schemas and live monitoring (llm-observability); input or score drift (drift-monitor); monthly API spend forecasts (llm-cost-model); judging answer quality itself (llm-eval-harness produces the quality_pass labels).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
log — request log CSVyesplatform / API gateway logs (copy assets/log-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
targets — sli,objective,threshold,window_daysnoProduct owner + SRE lead (copy assets/targets-template.csv)objectives proposed from the data, each To be baselined · owner: Product owner; never presented as agreed
system — feature namenoProduct ownertitle reads "AI feature"

An SLI with an agreed target but no eligible rows in the log exits 2. Without quality_pass or cost_usd values, those SLIs are listed as not measured with a named owner.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Confirm the log covers normal traffic (ideally several days; the 6 h and 3 d alert windows need that much history).
  3. Run without targets first if none are agreed; take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead.
  4. Run with the agreed targets. scripts/slo.py applies references/method.md.
  5. Read Summary, then Error budgets (consumed > 1 is breached), then Alerting policy (which alerts fire now).
  6. On exit 1: open an incident or a reliability work item for each breached SLI; do not lower the objective to pass the gate without the Product owner.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • slos.csv — sli, objective, threshold, observed, budget_consumed, burn_rate, status, note (burn_rate = last 1 h; status met | at-risk | breached | proposed).
  • slo-spec.md — Summary, SLIs and objectives, Error budgets, Alerting policy (burn per window, thresholds, fires), Method.
  • slo.json — exact counts and fractions per SLI and window, verdict.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every observed value comes from the log; percentiles are nearest-rank
  • [ ] Every proposed objective carries To be baselined · owner: Product owner; none is called agreed
  • [ ] Burn-rate thresholds and windows match references/sources.md (SRE workbook, checked 2026-10-18)
  • [ ] A breached agreed SLO exits 1 with full outputs
  • [ ] Limits stated: sample log, short logs cannot show long windows, quality depends on labelling

References

  • references/method.md — SLI definitions, budget and burn formulas, proposal rules, hand-checked worked example
  • references/sources.md — Google SRE workbook burn-rate policy with URL and date checked
  • assets/targets-template.csv, assets/log-template.csv — input layouts
  • scripts/slo.py — calculator and --verify (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 breached / 2 input)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-slo-definition). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (slos.csv, slo-spec.md, slo.json). An agreed SLO with budget consumed above 1 fails the run (exit 1) on purpose, with every output still written. Both tabular outputs pass --verify, which recomputes budgets, alerts and statuses from the counts in slo.json.

# AI SLO Definition

## In a conversation: draft the SLO spec now
The reply **is the SLO spec draft**, never only a request for the log. No log rows are in the conversation, so no observed value is printed; every number the log would give is a marker.
- **The request names the feature and says logs exist** ("a week of pilot logs", "here are two days of logs") but no rows are in the conversation: write the spec **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **Summary** — line 1: `Status: proposed — no objective is agreed until the Product owner signs it.` Then how the objectives are set: `scripts/slo.py` is run on the pilot log **without targets** (`python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input log=<pilot-log.csv> --input system="<feature>" --out <dir>`), and each objective is proposed from the observed data.
  2. **SLIs and objectives** — table `sli | good ÷ eligible | proposal rule | objective | threshold | status` for the four SLIs: availability (`status = ok` ÷ every request); latency (ok requests with `latency_ms <= threshold`; failed requests count against availability only); quality (`quality_pass = 1` ÷ labelled rows); cost (`cost_usd <= threshold` ÷ rows with a cost). Proposal rules from `references/method.md`: availability and quality take the highest ladder level not above the observed SLI (availability `0.9 / 0.95 / 0.99 / 0.995 / 0.999 / 0.9995 / 0.9999`; quality `0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.98 / 0.99`); latency threshold = observed nearest-rank p95 of ok requests rounded up to the next 100 ms at objective 0.95; cost threshold = observed p95 cost rounded up to the next 0.001 USD at objective 0.95. Every objective cell reads `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and every status `proposed`; none is called agreed. Without `quality_pass` or `cost_usd` in the log, that SLI is "not measured" with its owner.
  3. **Error budgets** — error budget = 1 − objective; budget consumed = (1 − SLI) ÷ (1 − objective); above 1 is breached. Proposals are never gated; only agreed targets are.
  4. **Alerting policy** — Google SRE workbook multiwindow burn-rate alerts at a 30-day window: fast-burn page 14.4x over 1 h with a 5 m short window (2% of budget); slow-burn page 6x over 6 h / 30 m (5%); ticket 1x over 3 d / 6 h (10%). An alert fires when both windows burn at or above the threshold. The SLO window is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]` until agreed; a pilot shorter than 3 days cannot show the ticket window.
  5. **Method & limits** — nearest-rank percentiles, the log must cover normal traffic, quality depends on labelling; then the next step: take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead, then re-run with the agreed `targets` file (`sli,objective,threshold,window_days`).
- **Agreed targets and a measurement are asked for** ("measure against our targets", "errors spiked — check the SLOs and alerts"): give the same sections with the stated targets as objectives, the observed / consumed / burn columns as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]` until the log is run, and state the gate: consumed above 1 on an agreed SLO is breached and the run exits 1 with every output written; a firing alert on an unbreached SLO is at-risk.
- **No feature and no log mentioned at all**: ask once, in one list, for the request log (`timestamp, latency_ms, status`, optional `quality_pass`, `cost_usd`), any agreed targets, and the feature name. Do not invent latency, availability or cost figures.
- **Asked to "just set sensible SLOs" or to lower an objective so a breach passes**: decline in one line — objectives come from observed data and the Product owner's agreement, not from typical industry numbers, and a breached objective is not lowered to pass the gate without the Product owner. Never print a suggested target number; show `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and the proposal rules above.
- **Distribution drift** ("have our confidence scores shifted since launch?"): that is `drift-monitor`; this skill measures SLIs against objectives.

## Starting points
- **New** — no SLOs yet: bring a pilot request log; every objective is proposed from the observed data and marked for the Product owner to agree.
- **Existing** — bring the production request log and the targets already agreed; the skill measures each SLI against them, computes budget burn and flags breaches.

## When to use
- ADLC requirements stage: turn "it should be fast and reliable" into measurable SLIs, objectives and error budgets before build sign-off.
- Drafting first objectives from a pilot or shadow log: the skill proposes them from observed data for the Product owner to accept or change.
- Checking a release or a week of traffic against agreed targets, and wiring the burn-rate alert policy.
- NOT for: dashboards, trace schemas and live monitoring (`llm-observability`); input or score drift (`drift-monitor`); monthly API spend forecasts (`llm-cost-model`); judging answer quality itself (`llm-eval-harness` produces the `quality_pass` labels).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log` — request log CSV | yes | platform / API gateway logs (copy `assets/log-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `targets` — `sli,objective,threshold,window_days` | no | Product owner + SRE lead (copy `assets/targets-template.csv`) | objectives proposed from the data, each `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`; never presented as agreed |
| `system` — feature name | no | Product owner | title reads "AI feature" |

An SLI with an agreed target but no eligible rows in the log exits 2. Without `quality_pass` or `cost_usd` values, those SLIs are listed as not measured with a named owner.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Confirm the log covers normal traffic (ideally several days; the 6 h and 3 d alert windows need that much history).
3. Run without `targets` first if none are agreed; take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead.
4. Run with the agreed `targets`. `scripts/slo.py` applies `references/method.md`.
5. Read Summary, then Error budgets (consumed > 1 is breached), then Alerting policy (which alerts fire now).
6. On exit 1: open an incident or a reliability work item for each breached SLI; do not lower the objective to pass the gate without the Product owner.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `slos.csv` — `sli, objective, threshold, observed, budget_consumed, burn_rate, status, note` (burn_rate = last 1 h; status met | at-risk | breached | proposed).
- `slo-spec.md` — **Summary**, **SLIs and objectives**, **Error budgets**, **Alerting policy** (burn per window, thresholds, fires), **Method**.
- `slo.json` — exact counts and fractions per SLI and window, verdict.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every observed value comes from the log; percentiles are nearest-rank
- [ ] Every proposed objective carries `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`; none is called agreed
- [ ] Burn-rate thresholds and windows match `references/sources.md` (SRE workbook, checked 2026-10-18)
- [ ] A breached agreed SLO exits 1 with full outputs
- [ ] Limits stated: sample log, short logs cannot show long windows, quality depends on labelling

## References
- `references/method.md` — SLI definitions, budget and burn formulas, proposal rules, hand-checked worked example
- `references/sources.md` — Google SRE workbook burn-rate policy with URL and date checked
- `assets/targets-template.csv`, `assets/log-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/slo.py` — calculator and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 breached / 2 input)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-slo-definition`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`slos.csv`, `slo-spec.md`, `slo.json`). An agreed SLO with budget consumed above 1 fails the run (exit 1) on purpose, with every output still written. Both tabular outputs pass `--verify`, which recomputes budgets, alerts and statuses from the counts in `slo.json`.

card: AI maturity score, use-case portfolio and CoE design
name: ai-strategy-coe
description: Use when the user asks to design an enterprise AI strategy, stand up or assess an AI Center of Excellence (CoE), score an AI use-case portfolio, or build a 12-month AI roadmap. Produces a 5-level maturity assessment (data, platform, talent, governance, value), an operating-model recommendation (central / hub-and-spoke / federated), a scored use-case portfolio, a governance outline, and a quarter-by-quarter roadmap. Not for a single use case (use ai-use-case-canvas) or compliance-only reviews (use ai-governance-risk).

bodyHtml:
AI Strategy & CoE Design

In a conversation: write the strategy now

The reply is the deliverable (or one ask), never only a command. About 1,000 tokens; first line is the answer; tables, not prose.

Never

  • Never infer maturity from industry averages or invent benchmark figures; a dimension without evidence is To be baselined · owner to be named.
  • Never weight the formula, never rank a row missing any of V, F, D, R, never carry over an earlier score.
  • Never schedule scale before measurement exists.

Which reply

  1. No current-state evidence (e.g. "write us an AI strategy, we are a retailer"): ask once, then stop — no scores. Offer this table to fill: | Input | Your answer | rows: data platforms · cloud · existing AI/ML in production · AI team and skills · AI policy/governance · strategic priorities (12 months) · executive sponsor and budget envelope · candidate use cases.
  2. Operating-model question only: answer in tables (≤350 words). Apply references/operating-models.md: maturity 1–2 and talent in one team → Central CoE; maturity 2–3, 3+ business units, a platform exists → Hub-and-spoke; maturity 4+ with AI engineers in every BU → Federated. Give: | Model | Verdict | Why | (chosen + the two rejected); design decisions | Decision | Recommendation | — reporting line (where the data platform reports, never under one BU), funding (central for platform and lighthouses; chargeback once metered), intake (quarterly review + fast lane), risk gate (tiered: self-certify low, CoE medium, committee high), build vs buy/partner; precondition: 1–3 AI-capable people per spoke (talent per spoke) before the hub hands over; transition triggers (central → hub-and-spoke: 2+ spokes have trained builders and the platform has self-service onboarding and eval gates; hub-and-spoke → federated: value tracking at level 4, controls tested, spokes pass audits two quarters running).
  3. Full strategy from a description, in this order: (a) maturity table | Dimension | Score 1–5 | Evidence (from the user's words) | for all five — data, platform, talent, governance, value — score only what the user's facts support, else To be baselined · owner to be named; (b) "Overall: Level N (= minimum of the evidenced scores); constraining dimension: X"; (c) operating model chosen + two rejected with reasons; (d) portfolio — one row per idea the user counts (e.g. all 12), columns V | F | D | R | priority = V×F×D÷R | band; unnamed or unscored ideas keep their row with axes [TBD at scoring workshop] and band "unscored"; (e) governance minimum (intake gate, risk tiers, model inventory, review cadence); (f) roadmap | Quarter | Focus | Exit criterion | Owner | for Q1–Q4 from references/roadmap-skeleton.md (Q1 foundations + 1–2 lighthouses with baselines; Q4 operating-model transition decision); (g) ≤5-bullet executive summary.
  4. Use-case CSV attached but no maturity scorecard: first line asks once for the maturity scorecard (dimension, score_1_to_5, evidence, gap_to_next_level, owner; assets/maturity-scorecard.csv) — maturity.py cannot run without it; maturity stays "pending", not inferred. The ranked portfolio may follow.
  5. Files attached: name the commands — python3 -I scripts/score_portfolio.py use-cases.csv --out-dir out --org <org> [--previous previous-portfolio.csv] → portfolio.csv, unscored.csv, portfolio.md; python3 -I scripts/maturity.py maturity-scorecard.csv --out-dir out --org <org> --target 3 --default-owner "AI CoE lead" → maturity.md, roadmap.md — then show the computed result.

Portfolio procedure — compute row by row from the CSV; show the working table (scripts/score_portfolio.py)

  1. A row with any blank V/F/D/R → unscored (missing score(s): …), not ranked.
  2. score = V×F×D÷R (2 decimals). Sort by score desc, tie → lower id first. rank k = 1..n (n = ranked rows).
  3. quartile = ceil(k×4÷n) (n = 9: ranks 1–2 → Q1, 3–4 → Q2, 5–6 → Q3, 7–9 → Q4).
  4. Band, first match: Stop if V≤2 or F=1 or R=5; Now if quartile 1, R≤3, D≥3 and owner and baseline named (else Next, "no owner/baseline"); Next if quartile 1 with D≤2 or R>3, or quartile 2; else Later. Blank owner/baseline/evidence shows To be baselined · owner: AI CoE lead.
  5. With a previous portfolio.csv: movement = previous rank − rank now (up N / down N / same; new if absent before); band before → now (e.g. "UC-003 Now → Next"); list ids ranked before that are now unscored or no longer in the list. Computed from the two files only.

Working table: | rank | id | V | F | D | R | score | quartile | band | reason | prev rank/band | movement |.

Maturity procedure (scripts/maturity.py): a score without evidence is not a score → To be baselined · owner: <owner, else AI CoE lead>; overall = minimum of the evidenced scores, name the constraining dimension (level names 1 Ad hoc, 2 Emerging, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimizing); gap = below target (default 3) or unevidenced; one roadmap item per gap, with owner.

Starting points

  • New: a first list of scored AI ideas and a maturity self-assessment give a ranked portfolio, maturity gaps and a quarter roadmap.
  • Existing: add the portfolio.csv from your last review (previous_portfolio); the re-ranked portfolio shows each use case's rank and band movement, what is new and what dropped out or lost its scores.

When to use

  • "Build our AI strategy", "stand up an AI CoE", "where are we on AI maturity", "prioritize our AI backlog", "12-month AI roadmap".
  • Executive audience: CIO, CDO, CTO, board.
  • NOT for: qualifying one idea (ai-use-case-canvas), risk/compliance only (ai-governance-risk), agent design (agent-architecture).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Organization context (industry, size, regulatory posture)yesuser
Current-state evidence (data platforms, cloud, existing AI/ML, team)yesuser / documents
Candidate use-case list (even rough)nouser; skill elicits if missing
Executive sponsor and budget envelopenouser; mark To be baselined · owner to be named if absent
Strategic priorities for the next 12 monthsyesuser / annual plan

If organization context or current-state evidence is missing, ask once. Do not infer maturity from industry averages.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Assess maturity. Score each of the five dimensions 1–5 using references/maturity-model.md. Record evidence per score in assets/maturity-scorecard.csv. A score without evidence is To be baselined · owner to be named.
  3. Pick the operating model. Apply the decision table in references/operating-models.md. State the chosen model, the two rejected ones, and why. Maturity level and organizational breadth drive this, not preference.
  4. Score the portfolio. Score every candidate use case on value, feasibility, risk, data readiness (1–5 each) with references/use-case-scoring.md; fill assets/use-case-scoring.csv. Compute priority = value × feasibility × data readiness ÷ risk. Classify: Now / Next / Later / Stop.
  5. Define governance. Minimum: intake gate, risk tiering, model inventory, review cadence. Point deeper controls to ai-governance-risk.
  6. Build the roadmap. Use assets/roadmap.md with references/roadmap-skeleton.md. Q1 is foundations and 1–2 lighthouse use cases; never schedule scale before measurement exists.
  7. Write the executive summary (≤5 bullets): maturity headline, model choice, top-3 use cases, investment envelope or To be baselined · owner to be named, first 90-day commitments.
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

  • ai-strategy-<org>.md: exec summary, maturity table, operating model, portfolio table, governance, roadmap, risks, next steps (owner + date).
  • maturity-scorecard.csv and use-case-scoring.csv filled.
  • Saved to the working directory unless the user names a path.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every maturity score has an evidence line or a To be baselined · owner to be named marker
  • [ ] Operating model choice cites the decision criteria it satisfied
  • [ ] Portfolio table has every candidate scored on all four axes; no "high/med/low" without the numeric score
  • [ ] Roadmap quarters each have an exit criterion and an owner
  • [ ] No vendor named as a recommendation without a stated selection criterion
  • [ ] No invented benchmark figures; industry comparisons carry a source or are omitted
  • [ ] First line is the answer

References

  • references/maturity-model.md — 5-level model with criteria per dimension
  • references/operating-models.md — central / hub-and-spoke / federated, when to choose
  • references/use-case-scoring.md — rubric and formula
  • references/roadmap-skeleton.md — 12-month quarter plan with exit criteria
  • scripts/score_portfolio.py — scoring CSV → ranked portfolio.csv + unscored.csv + portfolio.md
  • scripts/maturity.py — scorecard CSV → maturity.md + roadmap.md skeleton (one item per gap)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (portfolio.csv, portfolio.md, maturity.md, roadmap.md); fill the operating-model and governance sections of the roadmap by hand from the references.

bodyMd:
# AI Strategy & CoE Design

## In a conversation: write the strategy now
The reply **is the deliverable** (or one ask), never only a command. About 1,000 tokens; first line is the answer; tables, not prose.

**Never**
- Never infer maturity from industry averages or invent benchmark figures; a dimension without evidence is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
- Never weight the formula, never rank a row missing any of V, F, D, R, never carry over an earlier score.
- Never schedule scale before measurement exists.

**Which reply**
1. **No current-state evidence** (e.g. "write us an AI strategy, we are a retailer"): ask once, then stop — no scores. Offer this table to fill: `| Input | Your answer |` rows: data platforms · cloud · existing AI/ML in production · AI team and skills · AI policy/governance · strategic priorities (12 months) · executive sponsor and budget envelope · candidate use cases.
2. **Operating-model question only**: answer in tables (≤350 words). Apply `references/operating-models.md`: maturity 1–2 and talent in one team → Central CoE; maturity 2–3, 3+ business units, a platform exists → **Hub-and-spoke**; maturity 4+ with AI engineers in every BU → Federated. Give: `| Model | Verdict | Why |` (chosen + the two rejected); **design decisions** `| Decision | Recommendation |` — reporting line (where the data platform reports, never under one BU), funding (central for platform and lighthouses; chargeback once metered), intake (quarterly review + fast lane), risk gate (tiered: self-certify low, CoE medium, committee high), build vs buy/partner; **precondition: 1–3 AI-capable people per spoke** (talent per spoke) before the hub hands over; **transition triggers** (central → hub-and-spoke: 2+ spokes have trained builders and the platform has self-service onboarding and eval gates; hub-and-spoke → federated: value tracking at level 4, controls tested, spokes pass audits two quarters running).
3. **Full strategy from a description**, in this order: (a) **maturity table** `| Dimension | Score 1–5 | Evidence (from the user's words) |` for all five — data, platform, talent, governance, value — score only what the user's facts support, else `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; (b) **"Overall: Level N (= minimum of the evidenced scores); constraining dimension: X"**; (c) operating model chosen + two rejected with reasons; (d) **portfolio** — one row per idea the user counts (e.g. all 12), columns `V | F | D | R | priority = V×F×D÷R | band`; unnamed or unscored ideas keep their row with axes `[TBD at scoring workshop]` and band "unscored"; (e) governance minimum (intake gate, risk tiers, model inventory, review cadence); (f) **roadmap** `| Quarter | Focus | Exit criterion | Owner |` for Q1–Q4 from `references/roadmap-skeleton.md` (Q1 foundations + 1–2 lighthouses with baselines; Q4 operating-model transition decision); (g) ≤5-bullet executive summary.
4. **Use-case CSV attached but no maturity scorecard**: first line asks once for the **maturity scorecard** (`dimension, score_1_to_5, evidence, gap_to_next_level, owner`; `assets/maturity-scorecard.csv`) — `maturity.py` cannot run without it; maturity stays "pending", not inferred. The ranked portfolio may follow.
5. **Files attached**: name the commands — `python3 -I scripts/score_portfolio.py use-cases.csv --out-dir out --org <org> [--previous previous-portfolio.csv]` → `portfolio.csv`, `unscored.csv`, `portfolio.md`; `python3 -I scripts/maturity.py maturity-scorecard.csv --out-dir out --org <org> --target 3 --default-owner "AI CoE lead"` → `maturity.md`, `roadmap.md` — then show the computed result.

**Portfolio procedure — compute row by row from the CSV; show the working table** (`scripts/score_portfolio.py`)
1. A row with any blank V/F/D/R → **unscored** (`missing score(s): …`), not ranked.
2. score = V×F×D÷R (2 decimals). Sort by score desc, tie → lower id first. rank k = 1..n (n = ranked rows).
3. quartile = ceil(k×4÷n) (n = 9: ranks 1–2 → Q1, 3–4 → Q2, 5–6 → Q3, 7–9 → Q4).
4. Band, first match: **Stop** if V≤2 or F=1 or R=5; **Now** if quartile 1, R≤3, D≥3 and owner and baseline named (else Next, "no owner/baseline"); **Next** if quartile 1 with D≤2 or R>3, or quartile 2; else **Later**. Blank owner/baseline/evidence shows `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI CoE lead]`.
5. With a previous portfolio.csv: movement = previous rank − rank now (`up N` / `down N` / `same`; `new` if absent before); band before → now (e.g. "UC-003 Now → Next"); list ids ranked before that are now unscored or **no longer in the list**. Computed from the two files only.
Working table: `| rank | id | V | F | D | R | score | quartile | band | reason | prev rank/band | movement |`.

**Maturity procedure** (`scripts/maturity.py`): a score without evidence is not a score → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <owner, else AI CoE lead>]`; overall = minimum of the evidenced scores, name the constraining dimension (level names 1 Ad hoc, 2 Emerging, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimizing); gap = below target (default 3) or unevidenced; **one roadmap item per gap**, with owner.

## Starting points
- **New:** a first list of scored AI ideas and a maturity self-assessment give a ranked portfolio, maturity gaps and a quarter roadmap.
- **Existing:** add the `portfolio.csv` from your last review (`previous_portfolio`); the re-ranked portfolio shows each use case's rank and band movement, what is new and what dropped out or lost its scores.

## When to use
- "Build our AI strategy", "stand up an AI CoE", "where are we on AI maturity", "prioritize our AI backlog", "12-month AI roadmap".
- Executive audience: CIO, CDO, CTO, board.
- NOT for: qualifying one idea (`ai-use-case-canvas`), risk/compliance only (`ai-governance-risk`), agent design (`agent-architecture`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Organization context (industry, size, regulatory posture) | yes | user |
| Current-state evidence (data platforms, cloud, existing AI/ML, team) | yes | user / documents |
| Candidate use-case list (even rough) | no | user; skill elicits if missing |
| Executive sponsor and budget envelope | no | user; mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` if absent |
| Strategic priorities for the next 12 months | yes | user / annual plan |

If organization context or current-state evidence is missing, ask once. Do not infer maturity from industry averages.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. **Assess maturity.** Score each of the five dimensions 1–5 using `references/maturity-model.md`. Record evidence per score in `assets/maturity-scorecard.csv`. A score without evidence is `[TO BE BASELINED]`.
3. **Pick the operating model.** Apply the decision table in `references/operating-models.md`. State the chosen model, the two rejected ones, and why. Maturity level and organizational breadth drive this, not preference.
4. **Score the portfolio.** Score every candidate use case on value, feasibility, risk, data readiness (1–5 each) with `references/use-case-scoring.md`; fill `assets/use-case-scoring.csv`. Compute priority = value × feasibility × data readiness ÷ risk. Classify: Now / Next / Later / Stop.
5. **Define governance.** Minimum: intake gate, risk tiering, model inventory, review cadence. Point deeper controls to `ai-governance-risk`.
6. **Build the roadmap.** Use `assets/roadmap.md` with `references/roadmap-skeleton.md`. Q1 is foundations and 1–2 lighthouse use cases; never schedule scale before measurement exists.
7. **Write the executive summary** (≤5 bullets): maturity headline, model choice, top-3 use cases, investment envelope or `[TO BE BASELINED]`, first 90-day commitments.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `ai-strategy-<org>.md`: exec summary, maturity table, operating model, portfolio table, governance, roadmap, risks, next steps (owner + date).
- `maturity-scorecard.csv` and `use-case-scoring.csv` filled.
- Saved to the working directory unless the user names a path.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every maturity score has an evidence line or a `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` marker
- [ ] Operating model choice cites the decision criteria it satisfied
- [ ] Portfolio table has every candidate scored on all four axes; no "high/med/low" without the numeric score
- [ ] Roadmap quarters each have an exit criterion and an owner
- [ ] No vendor named as a recommendation without a stated selection criterion
- [ ] No invented benchmark figures; industry comparisons carry a source or are omitted
- [ ] First line is the answer

## References
- `references/maturity-model.md` — 5-level model with criteria per dimension
- `references/operating-models.md` — central / hub-and-spoke / federated, when to choose
- `references/use-case-scoring.md` — rubric and formula
- `references/roadmap-skeleton.md` — 12-month quarter plan with exit criteria
- `scripts/score_portfolio.py` — scoring CSV → ranked `portfolio.csv` + `unscored.csv` + `portfolio.md`
- `scripts/maturity.py` — scorecard CSV → `maturity.md` + `roadmap.md` skeleton (one item per gap)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`portfolio.csv`, `portfolio.md`, `maturity.md`, `roadmap.md`); fill the operating-model and governance sections of the roadmap by hand from the references.

bodyHtml:
AI Threat Model (STRIDE + OWASP LLM Top 10 2025)

In a conversation: write the threat model now

  • The request names the architecture (components such as web app, orchestrator, hosted LLM, vector store, refund API), even when the CSVs are not in the conversation: build the threat model in this reply, in this order. Never reply with only a request for the CSVs.
    1. Components table in the assets/components-template.csv columns: id, name, kind, trust_zone, handles_pii, write_actions, internet_facing (kinds: user, external_api, app, llm, retriever, tool, agent, vector_store, data_store). Flows table: from, to, data, crosses_trust_boundary. Attributes the user did not state are To be baselined · owner: Solution architect; ask the user to confirm the two tables in one list.
    2. The command that produces the files: python3 -I scripts/threat_model.py via the runner (see "How to run" below), giving threats.csv, dfd.md, threat-report.md.
    3. Threats by severity (high first), one row each: threat_id (stable: <component>:<category> or <from>><to>:<category>) | element | category (STRIDE letter or OWASP 2025 id LLM01–LLM10) | threat | likelihood | impact | severity | mitigation ids | status | owner. Apply references/method.md: STRIDE per element (external entity S, R; process S, T, R, I, D, E; data store T, I, D; flow T, I, D); OWASP rules (LLM01 on llm/agent reachable from an untrusted origin; LLM02 where PII is handled; LLM05 on anything receiving model output; LLM06 where write_actions = yes; LLM07, LLM09, LLM10 on the llm; LLM08 on vector store and retriever). Likelihood = 1 + exposed + boundary; impact = 1 + PII + write (cap 3; D and LLM10 fixed at 2); severity high ≥ 6, medium 3–4, low ≤ 2.
    4. Mitigation ids only from assets/mitigations.csv: S M01; T M02, M07; R M03; I M04; D M05 (stores also M08); E M06, M07; LLM01 M20–M23; LLM02 M24, M25; LLM03 M26, M27; LLM04 M28, M27; LLM05 M29, M30; LLM06 M31–M33; LLM07 M34, M35; LLM08 M36, M28; LLM09 M37, M38; LLM10 M39, M40.
    5. Open high threats with owner: status comes only from a control register; with none, every threat is open and owned by To be baselined · owner: Security architect.
    6. Data flow: a mermaid flowchart, one subgraph per trust zone, boundary-crossing flows labelled.
    7. Method & limits: rule-based enumeration of the declared design; misses business-logic abuse and attack chains; not a penetration test or a security sign-off.
  • Components given, flows missing: still show the components table and the threats the components alone imply, and ask once for the flows CSV; do not guess flows.
  • No control register, or asked to "assume the usual controls are in place": decline in one line (a control counts only with a register row and evidence); no threat is marked mitigated or planned; every threat is open, owner To be baselined · owner: Security architect; offer assets/controls-template.csv for control owners to fill, then re-run.
  • Release gate ("fail if more than N high threats remain open"): report open high vs the limit — more than N fails (exit 1), equal passes; all outputs are still written.
  • Live jailbreak or prompt-leak testing of a running app: route to red-team-suite; offer this skill for the design-level threat model.

Starting points

  • New: components and flows of a design not yet built give every threat, all open and owned by the Security architect until controls exist.
  • Existing: add the control register you already keep (controls); each in-place or planned control closes or downgrades its threats, and only the residual open threats count toward the gate.

When to use

  • ADLC architecture stage: the component and data-flow design of an LLM app, RAG pipeline or agent is drafted and needs a security review before build.
  • Before a release review: re-run with the current control register to show residual (open) threats and gate on open highs.
  • After a design change (new tool, new data store, new vendor model): re-run; threat ids are stable, so the control register carries over.
  • NOT for: attacking a running app (red-team-suite), writing runtime input/output filters (guardrails-config), EU AI Act or NIST risk tiering (ai-governance-risk), or a penetration test or security sign-off.

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
components — id, name, kind, trust_zone, handles_pii, write_actions, internet_facingyessolution architect (copy assets/components-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
flows — from, to, data, crosses_trust_boundaryyessolution architect (copy assets/flows-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
controls — threat_id or mitigation_id, status, evidence, ownernosecurity architect / control owners (copy assets/controls-template.csv)every threat is open; owner To be baselined · owner: Security architect
max_open_high — integernoCISO / release ownerno gate; report says "no gate set"

Component ids are letters, digits and _. A flow whose ends sit in different trust zones is treated as crossing a boundary even if marked no (listed in dfd.md).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Build the components and flows CSVs from the architecture diagram; one row per component and per directed flow.
  3. Run the agent. scripts/threat_model.py applies STRIDE per element and the OWASP LLM 2025 rules in references/method.md, scores likelihood × impact, and attaches mitigation ids from assets/mitigations.csv.
  4. First run without controls: hand threats.csv to control owners; they record in_place / planned rows by threat_id or mitigation_id with evidence and owner.
  5. Re-run with the controls file and, for a release gate, max_open_high.
  6. Review the open high threats with the Security architect; add threats the rules cannot see (business-logic abuse, attack chains) by hand to the risk register.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • threats.csv — threat_id, element, element_type, category, threat, likelihood, impact, severity, mitigation, status, owner, evidence; sorted by severity then id. threat_id = <component>:<category> or <from>><to>:<category>.
  • dfd.md — mermaid flowchart: one subgraph per trust zone, boundary-crossing flows labelled and dashed red.
  • threat-report.md — Summary, Data flow, Threats by severity, Open high threats, Method & limits (with the mitigation catalogue used).

Self-check

  • [ ] Every component and flow from the architecture is in the inputs (unlisted elements are not analysed)
  • [ ] Every threat has a severity from the documented rule and at least one mitigation id
  • [ ] Status comes only from the control register; no control is assumed
  • [ ] Every owner is a named role or To be baselined · owner: Security architect
  • [ ] Limits stated: rule-based enumeration, not a penetration test or sign-off

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-threat-model --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-threat-model). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (threats.csv, dfd.md, threat-report.md). With max_open_high set, the run is a gate: more open high threats than the limit fails the run (exit 1) and all outputs are still written.

References

  • references/method.md — element mapping, OWASP rules, likelihood/impact/severity, status rules, limits
  • references/sources.md — OWASP 2025 list and STRIDE-per-element sources with dates checked
  • assets/owasp-llm-top10-2025.csv — LLM01–LLM10 ids, names, paraphrase, applicability, mitigation ids
  • assets/mitigations.csv — mitigation catalogue (id, mitigation, maps_to, applies_to)
  • scripts/threat_model.py — generator and --verify mode (argparse; stdlib)

bodyMd:
# AI Threat Model (STRIDE + OWASP LLM Top 10 2025)

## In a conversation: write the threat model now
- **The request names the architecture** (components such as web app, orchestrator, hosted LLM, vector store, refund API), even when the CSVs are not in the conversation: build the threat model **in this reply**, in this order. Never reply with only a request for the CSVs.
  1. **Components table** in the `assets/components-template.csv` columns: `id, name, kind, trust_zone, handles_pii, write_actions, internet_facing` (kinds: user, external_api, app, llm, retriever, tool, agent, vector_store, data_store). **Flows table**: `from, to, data, crosses_trust_boundary`. Attributes the user did not state are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Solution architect]`; ask the user to confirm the two tables in one list.
  2. The command that produces the files: `python3 -I scripts/threat_model.py` via the runner (see "How to run" below), giving `threats.csv`, `dfd.md`, `threat-report.md`.
  3. **Threats by severity** (high first), one row each: `threat_id` (stable: `<component>:<category>` or `<from>><to>:<category>`) | element | category (STRIDE letter or OWASP 2025 id LLM01–LLM10) | threat | likelihood | impact | severity | mitigation ids | status | owner. Apply `references/method.md`: STRIDE per element (external entity S, R; process S, T, R, I, D, E; data store T, I, D; flow T, I, D); OWASP rules (LLM01 on llm/agent reachable from an untrusted origin; LLM02 where PII is handled; LLM05 on anything receiving model output; LLM06 where write_actions = yes; LLM07, LLM09, LLM10 on the llm; LLM08 on vector store and retriever). Likelihood = 1 + exposed + boundary; impact = 1 + PII + write (cap 3; D and LLM10 fixed at 2); severity high ≥ 6, medium 3–4, low ≤ 2.
  4. **Mitigation ids** only from `assets/mitigations.csv`: S M01; T M02, M07; R M03; I M04; D M05 (stores also M08); E M06, M07; LLM01 M20–M23; LLM02 M24, M25; LLM03 M26, M27; LLM04 M28, M27; LLM05 M29, M30; LLM06 M31–M33; LLM07 M34, M35; LLM08 M36, M28; LLM09 M37, M38; LLM10 M39, M40.
  5. **Open high threats** with owner: status comes only from a control register; with none, every threat is `open` and owned by `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]`.
  6. **Data flow**: a mermaid flowchart, one subgraph per trust zone, boundary-crossing flows labelled.
  7. **Method & limits**: rule-based enumeration of the declared design; misses business-logic abuse and attack chains; not a penetration test or a security sign-off.
- **Components given, flows missing**: still show the components table and the threats the components alone imply, and ask once for the flows CSV; do not guess flows.
- **No control register, or asked to "assume the usual controls are in place"**: decline in one line (a control counts only with a register row and evidence); no threat is marked mitigated or planned; every threat is open, owner `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]`; offer `assets/controls-template.csv` for control owners to fill, then re-run.
- **Release gate** ("fail if more than N high threats remain open"): report open high vs the limit — more than N fails (exit 1), equal passes; all outputs are still written.
- **Live jailbreak or prompt-leak testing of a running app**: route to `red-team-suite`; offer this skill for the design-level threat model.

## Starting points
- **New:** components and flows of a design not yet built give every threat, all open and owned by the Security architect until controls exist.
- **Existing:** add the control register you already keep (`controls`); each in-place or planned control closes or downgrades its threats, and only the residual open threats count toward the gate.

## When to use
- ADLC architecture stage: the component and data-flow design of an LLM app, RAG pipeline or agent is drafted and needs a security review before build.
- Before a release review: re-run with the current control register to show residual (open) threats and gate on open highs.
- After a design change (new tool, new data store, new vendor model): re-run; threat ids are stable, so the control register carries over.
- NOT for: attacking a running app (`red-team-suite`), writing runtime input/output filters (`guardrails-config`), EU AI Act or NIST risk tiering (`ai-governance-risk`), or a penetration test or security sign-off.

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `components` — id, name, kind, trust_zone, handles_pii, write_actions, internet_facing | yes | solution architect (copy `assets/components-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `flows` — from, to, data, crosses_trust_boundary | yes | solution architect (copy `assets/flows-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `controls` — threat_id or mitigation_id, status, evidence, owner | no | security architect / control owners (copy `assets/controls-template.csv`) | every threat is `open`; owner `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]` |
| `max_open_high` — integer | no | CISO / release owner | no gate; report says "no gate set" |

Component ids are letters, digits and `_`. A flow whose ends sit in different trust zones is treated as crossing a boundary even if marked `no` (listed in `dfd.md`).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Build the components and flows CSVs from the architecture diagram; one row per component and per directed flow.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/threat_model.py` applies STRIDE per element and the OWASP LLM 2025 rules in `references/method.md`, scores likelihood × impact, and attaches mitigation ids from `assets/mitigations.csv`.
4. First run without controls: hand `threats.csv` to control owners; they record `in_place` / `planned` rows by `threat_id` or `mitigation_id` with evidence and owner.
5. Re-run with the controls file and, for a release gate, `max_open_high`.
6. Review the open high threats with the Security architect; add threats the rules cannot see (business-logic abuse, attack chains) by hand to the risk register.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `threats.csv` — `threat_id, element, element_type, category, threat, likelihood, impact, severity, mitigation, status, owner, evidence`; sorted by severity then id. `threat_id` = `<component>:<category>` or `<from>><to>:<category>`.
- `dfd.md` — mermaid flowchart: one subgraph per trust zone, boundary-crossing flows labelled and dashed red.
- `threat-report.md` — **Summary**, **Data flow**, **Threats by severity**, **Open high threats**, **Method & limits** (with the mitigation catalogue used).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every component and flow from the architecture is in the inputs (unlisted elements are not analysed)
- [ ] Every threat has a severity from the documented rule and at least one mitigation id
- [ ] Status comes only from the control register; no control is assumed
- [ ] Every owner is a named role or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]`
- [ ] Limits stated: rule-based enumeration, not a penetration test or sign-off

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-threat-model --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-threat-model`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`threats.csv`, `dfd.md`, `threat-report.md`). With `max_open_high` set, the run is a gate: more open high threats than the limit fails the run (exit 1) and all outputs are still written.

## References
- `references/method.md` — element mapping, OWASP rules, likelihood/impact/severity, status rules, limits
- `references/sources.md` — OWASP 2025 list and STRIDE-per-element sources with dates checked
- `assets/owasp-llm-top10-2025.csv` — LLM01–LLM10 ids, names, paraphrase, applicability, mitigation ids
- `assets/mitigations.csv` — mitigation catalogue (id, mitigation, maps_to, applies_to)
- `scripts/threat_model.py` — generator and `--verify` mode (argparse; stdlib)
