bodyHtml:
AI Transparency Notice (user notice, system card, Art. 50 checklist)

In a conversation: write the notice and checklist now

The reply is the transparency pack draft, never only a request for the facts CSV. Facts the user states fill the templates; every other fact is a marker, never typical wording.

  • The request names the system and its situation (e.g. "billing chatbot launching in the EU") but the facts CSV and classification.json are not in the conversation: write, in this reply, in this order:
    1. How it is produced — one line: the Product owner fills assets/facts-template.csv (each row with a source); optionally pass classification.json from eu-ai-act-classifier; run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input facts=<facts.csv> [--input classification=<classification.json>] --out <dir>.
    2. User notice — the sentences from assets/notice-sentences.csv, one per line, each tagged with the fact it traces to: "You are chatting with {system_name}. It is an AI system, not a person." / "{provider} runs it." / "It is here to {purpose}." / "It uses {data_sources}." / "It is not for {not_intended_for}." / "Keep in mind that it {known_limitations}." / "People stay in charge: {human_oversight}." / "Questions? Contact {contact}." / "Last updated: {last_updated}." — plus the synthetic, deep_fake, emotion, biometric sentences only when that yes/no fact is yes. Fill a placeholder only from a stated fact; otherwise To be baselined · owner: Product owner.
    3. Reading grade — Flesch-Kincaid grade against the ceiling (max_grade, default 8). Report it as [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run] while placeholders remain; above the ceiling the run exits 1 and the long facts are rewritten, not the notice.
    4. Art. 50 disclosure checklist — table duty | article | addressee | applies | provided | status | owner with the seven rows from assets/art50-duties.csv: interaction (Art. 50(1), Product owner), synthetic-content marking (Art. 50(2), Engineering lead), emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art. 50(3), Privacy officer), deep fake and public-interest text (Art. 50(4), Content lead), timing and accessibility (Art. 50(5), Product owner). applies follows the yes/no fact (unknown → to confirm); status is provided / partial / missing / to confirm / not applicable; Art. 50(5) is at most partial (placement and grade only).
    5. System card outline — Overview (with classification, else To be baselined · owner: Compliance lead), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log.
    6. Limits — this is not a legal determination and claims no compliance; exemptions are not assessed; counsel reviews the checklist before launch.
  • Only some facts are known ("we only know the name, provider and purpose — fill the rest with typical wording"): fill those three, mark every other fact To be baselined · owner: Product owner and the classification for the Compliance lead; say in one line that wording is not invented because each notice sentence must trace to a fact.
  • No system named at all: ask once, in one list, for the facts in assets/facts-template.csv (name, provider, purpose, data sources, oversight, limitations, not-intended-for, contact, the yes/no flags, notice placement) and the classifier output.
  • Asked to state that the system is compliant or to drop a checklist row: decline in one line — the checklist records evidence and owners, and compliance is a legal determination for counsel.

Starting points

  • New: the system's facts (and the classifier output) give the user notice, the system card and the Art. 50 checklist.
  • Existing: add the notice users see today (published_notice); notice-redline.md marks each sentence unchanged, changed, added or removed, and every removed sentence is a published claim the facts no longer support.

When to use

  • ADLC deploy stage: before users first see an AI assistant, chatbot or content generator.
  • "What do we tell users, and what does Article 50 expect us to disclose?" — notice plus a duty-by-duty checklist with evidence and owners.
  • Reviewer pack: a system card whose every row cites the source of the fact.
  • NOT for: deciding the EU AI Act risk tier (eu-ai-act-classifier), the risk register (ai-governance-risk), staged rollout (ai-release-plan), legal sign-off (route to counsel — this skill never claims compliance).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
facts — kv-csv key,value,source,notesyesProduct owner (copy assets/facts-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
classification — classification.jsonnooutput of ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifiersystem card classification line is To be baselined · owner: Compliance lead
max_grade — reading gradenoaccessibility or brand standard8
strict — true/falsenorelease ownerfalse: notice written with TBD markers, exit 0

Each missing fact is To be baselined · owner: Product owner in the card and notice. Yes/no facts (generates_synthetic_content, emotion_recognition, biometric_categorisation, interacts_directly, deep_fake, public_interest_text) accept only yes or no; anything else exits 2.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. The Product owner fills assets/facts-template.csv, writing each fact as a plain phrase that completes its template sentence, with a source for every row.
  3. Optionally run ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifier first and pass its classification.json.
  4. Run the agent. scripts/transparency_notice.py assembles the notice from assets/notice-sentences.csv, grades it (references/readability.md), writes the system card and evaluates assets/art50-duties.csv (references/method.md).
  5. Grade above max_grade → exit 1: rewrite the long facts, not the notice.
  6. Work every missing and to confirm checklist row with its owner. Treat partial on Art. 50(5) as a prompt for an accessibility review.
  7. Have counsel review the checklist before launch; run the self-check.

Output

  • notice.md — the user-facing notice (one sentence per line, ≤ 15 sentences).
  • system-card.md — Overview (with classification), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log (grade, checklist counts, facts not supplied).
  • disclosure-checklist.csv — duty, article, addressee, applies, provided, status, evidence, owner.
  • transparency.json — grade, max_grade, grade_ok, word_count, sentence_count, syllable_count, notice_sentences, notice_missing_facts, missing_facts, checklist counts, classification.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every notice sentence comes from a template and a fact; --verify re-grades notice.md to the same numbers
  • [ ] Grade within max_grade, or the run failed and says so
  • [ ] Every checklist row has an owner; nothing says "compliant"
  • [ ] Missing facts are TBD for the Product owner; missing classification is TBD for the Compliance lead
  • [ ] Limits stated: heuristic syllable count, exemptions not assessed, not a legal determination

References

  • references/sources.md — Article 50, 111(4), 113 text checked 2026-10-18; Flesch–Kincaid source
  • references/readability.md — grade formula, syllable heuristic and its limits
  • references/method.md — notice assembly, card rules, checklist rules
  • assets/facts-template.csv, assets/notice-sentences.csv, assets/art50-duties.csv — input layout, templates, duty catalog
  • scripts/transparency_notice.py — builder and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (notice.md, system-card.md, disclosure-checklist.csv, transparency.json). A notice above the reading-grade ceiling fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; every output is still written so the facts can be rewritten in plainer words.

bodyMd:
# AI Transparency Notice (user notice, system card, Art. 50 checklist)

## In a conversation: write the notice and checklist now
The reply **is the transparency pack draft**, never only a request for the facts CSV. Facts the user states fill the templates; every other fact is a marker, never typical wording.
- **The request names the system and its situation** (e.g. "billing chatbot launching in the EU") but the facts CSV and `classification.json` are not in the conversation: write, **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **How it is produced** — one line: the Product owner fills `assets/facts-template.csv` (each row with a source); optionally pass `classification.json` from `eu-ai-act-classifier`; run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input facts=<facts.csv> [--input classification=<classification.json>] --out <dir>`.
  2. **User notice** — the sentences from `assets/notice-sentences.csv`, one per line, each tagged with the fact it traces to: "You are chatting with {system_name}. It is an AI system, not a person." / "{provider} runs it." / "It is here to {purpose}." / "It uses {data_sources}." / "It is not for {not_intended_for}." / "Keep in mind that it {known_limitations}." / "People stay in charge: {human_oversight}." / "Questions? Contact {contact}." / "Last updated: {last_updated}." — plus the `synthetic`, `deep_fake`, `emotion`, `biometric` sentences only when that yes/no fact is yes. Fill a placeholder only from a stated fact; otherwise `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`.
  3. **Reading grade** — Flesch-Kincaid grade against the ceiling (`max_grade`, default 8). Report it as `[TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run]` while placeholders remain; above the ceiling the run exits 1 and the long facts are rewritten, not the notice.
  4. **Art. 50 disclosure checklist** — table `duty | article | addressee | applies | provided | status | owner` with the seven rows from `assets/art50-duties.csv`: interaction (Art. 50(1), Product owner), synthetic-content marking (Art. 50(2), Engineering lead), emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art. 50(3), Privacy officer), deep fake and public-interest text (Art. 50(4), Content lead), timing and accessibility (Art. 50(5), Product owner). `applies` follows the yes/no fact (unknown → `to confirm`); status is provided / partial / missing / to confirm / not applicable; Art. 50(5) is at most `partial` (placement and grade only).
  5. **System card outline** — Overview (with classification, else `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Compliance lead]`), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log.
  6. **Limits** — this is not a legal determination and claims no compliance; exemptions are not assessed; counsel reviews the checklist before launch.
- **Only some facts are known** ("we only know the name, provider and purpose — fill the rest with typical wording"): fill those three, mark every other fact `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and the classification for the Compliance lead; say in one line that wording is not invented because each notice sentence must trace to a fact.
- **No system named at all**: ask once, in one list, for the facts in `assets/facts-template.csv` (name, provider, purpose, data sources, oversight, limitations, not-intended-for, contact, the yes/no flags, notice placement) and the classifier output.
- **Asked to state that the system is compliant** or to drop a checklist row: decline in one line — the checklist records evidence and owners, and compliance is a legal determination for counsel.

## Starting points
- **New:** the system's facts (and the classifier output) give the user notice, the system card and the Art. 50 checklist.
- **Existing:** add the notice users see today (`published_notice`); notice-redline.md marks each sentence unchanged, changed, added or removed, and every removed sentence is a published claim the facts no longer support.

## When to use
- ADLC deploy stage: before users first see an AI assistant, chatbot or content generator.
- "What do we tell users, and what does Article 50 expect us to disclose?" — notice plus a duty-by-duty checklist with evidence and owners.
- Reviewer pack: a system card whose every row cites the source of the fact.
- NOT for: deciding the EU AI Act risk tier (`eu-ai-act-classifier`), the risk register (`ai-governance-risk`), staged rollout (`ai-release-plan`), legal sign-off (route to counsel — this skill never claims compliance).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `facts` — kv-csv `key,value,source,notes` | yes | Product owner (copy `assets/facts-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `classification` — `classification.json` | no | output of `ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifier` | system card classification line is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Compliance lead]` |
| `max_grade` — reading grade | no | accessibility or brand standard | 8 |
| `strict` — true/false | no | release owner | false: notice written with TBD markers, exit 0 |

Each missing fact is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` in the card and notice. Yes/no facts (`generates_synthetic_content`, `emotion_recognition`, `biometric_categorisation`, `interacts_directly`, `deep_fake`, `public_interest_text`) accept only yes or no; anything else exits 2.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. The Product owner fills `assets/facts-template.csv`, writing each fact as a plain phrase that completes its template sentence, with a source for every row.
3. Optionally run `ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifier` first and pass its `classification.json`.
4. Run the agent. `scripts/transparency_notice.py` assembles the notice from `assets/notice-sentences.csv`, grades it (`references/readability.md`), writes the system card and evaluates `assets/art50-duties.csv` (`references/method.md`).
5. Grade above `max_grade` → exit 1: rewrite the long facts, not the notice.
6. Work every `missing` and `to confirm` checklist row with its owner. Treat `partial` on Art. 50(5) as a prompt for an accessibility review.
7. Have counsel review the checklist before launch; run the self-check.

## Output
- `notice.md` — the user-facing notice (one sentence per line, ≤ 15 sentences).
- `system-card.md` — Overview (with classification), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log (grade, checklist counts, facts not supplied).
- `disclosure-checklist.csv` — `duty, article, addressee, applies, provided, status, evidence, owner`.
- `transparency.json` — `grade`, `max_grade`, `grade_ok`, `word_count`, `sentence_count`, `syllable_count`, `notice_sentences`, `notice_missing_facts`, `missing_facts`, checklist counts, classification.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every notice sentence comes from a template and a fact; `--verify` re-grades `notice.md` to the same numbers
- [ ] Grade within `max_grade`, or the run failed and says so
- [ ] Every checklist row has an owner; nothing says "compliant"
- [ ] Missing facts are TBD for the Product owner; missing classification is TBD for the Compliance lead
- [ ] Limits stated: heuristic syllable count, exemptions not assessed, not a legal determination

## References
- `references/sources.md` — Article 50, 111(4), 113 text checked 2026-10-18; Flesch–Kincaid source
- `references/readability.md` — grade formula, syllable heuristic and its limits
- `references/method.md` — notice assembly, card rules, checklist rules
- `assets/facts-template.csv`, `assets/notice-sentences.csv`, `assets/art50-duties.csv` — input layout, templates, duty catalog
- `scripts/transparency_notice.py` — builder and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`notice.md`, `system-card.md`, `disclosure-checklist.csv`, `transparency.json`). A notice above the reading-grade ceiling fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; every output is still written so the facts can be rewritten in plainer words.

card: One-page verdict: is this AI idea worth building
name: ai-use-case-canvas
description: Use when the user wants to qualify a single AI idea quickly — "is this a good AI use case", "use AI to <do X>", "fill the canvas for X", "should we build or buy this", "what would it take" — including testing whether the idea needs AI at all (a fixed threshold or approval rule such as "does an order over $10k need director approval" is a deterministic rule, verdict Stop or re-scope). Produces a one-page canvas: problem and user, current process and baseline, proposed AI capability, data readiness, feasibility, value hypothesis, risks and tier, build/buy/partner decision, next 30-day step. Do not use for portfolio-level strategy (ai-strategy-coe), designing an agent or its graph and tools once the idea is qualified (agent-architecture), retrieval design (rag-pipeline-design), or a full risk review (ai-governance-risk).

inputs.name: answers
inputs.from: answers.json: the canvas cells (problem_user, decision, current_process, capability, data, feasibility, value, risks), scores with evidence, build_buy factors, next_step (layout: evals/fixtures/answers.json)

inputs.name: previous
inputs.from: score.json from an earlier canvas of the same idea (re-review); decision.md then shows then-vs-now scores, verdict and decision

new.bring: your answers to the canvas questions about one AI idea

existing.bring: updated answers plus the scores from the idea's last review

bodyHtml:
AI Use-Case Canvas

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below (one answers.json; blanks are allowed and become owned To be baselined · owner to be named markers), then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-use-case-canvas --input answers=<file> --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-use-case-canvas). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (canvas.md, decision.md, score.json).

Starting points

  • New: your answers about one idea fill the canvas, score it and make the build, buy or partner call.
  • Existing: add the score.json from the idea's last canvas (previous); decision.md adds then-vs-now scores, priority, verdict and decision, so a re-review shows what moved and why.

When to use

  • First-pass qualification of one idea in under an hour; intake form for a CoE; pre-read for a sponsor conversation.
  • NOT for: ranking many ideas (ai-strategy-coe), designing the solution, legal/compliance sign-off.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
The idea in one or two sentences, and who raised ityesuser
The user of the output and the decision or task it affectsyesuser
Current process: steps, volume, time, error or cost signal (even rough)yesuser; unknowns marked To be baselined · owner to be named
Data involved: where it lives, owner, access, sensitivityyesuser
Constraints: budget envelope, timeline, vendor policynouser

If the user/decision or the data description is missing, ask once; otherwise fill the canvas with explicit unknowns rather than stalling.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Fill the canvas from assets/use-case-canvas.md following references/canvas-definition.md: every box has content or a labeled unknown with an owner.
  3. Score value, feasibility, data readiness, risk (1–5 each) using the rubric in ai-strategy-coe/references/use-case-scoring.md; compute priority = V × F × D ÷ R. Record the evidence per score.
  4. Decide build / buy / partner with references/build-buy-factors.md; state the two strongest factors behind the decision.
  5. Set the verdict: Proceed to design / Proceed after data readiness work / Park / Stop, plus the one 30-day step and its owner.
  6. Hand off: Proceed → agent-architecture or rag-pipeline-design; risk tier medium/high → ai-governance-risk before build.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • use-case-canvas-<name>.md: one page; verdict first; canvas table; scores; build/buy; next step.

Self-check

  • [ ] Verdict and next step are the first two lines
  • [ ] Baseline metric named, with value or To be baselined · owner to be named
  • [ ] Data box names owner, access path, and sensitivity
  • [ ] Scores have one evidence line each
  • [ ] Build/buy decision cites factors, not preference
  • [ ] Fits on one page (≤ 60 lines)
  • [ ] No vendor named without a selection criterion

References

  • references/canvas-definition.md — boxes, prompts, and quality tests
  • references/build-buy-factors.md — decision factors and patterns
  • scripts/canvas.py — answers.json → canvas.md (filled, scored, verdict), decision.md (build/buy/partner citing factors), score.json

bodyMd:
# AI Use-Case Canvas

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below (one `answers.json`; blanks are allowed and become owned `[TO BE BASELINED]` markers), then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-use-case-canvas --input answers=<file> --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-use-case-canvas`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`canvas.md`, `decision.md`, `score.json`).

## Starting points
- **New:** your answers about one idea fill the canvas, score it and make the build, buy or partner call.
- **Existing:** add the `score.json` from the idea's last canvas (`previous`); decision.md adds then-vs-now scores, priority, verdict and decision, so a re-review shows what moved and why.

## When to use
- First-pass qualification of one idea in under an hour; intake form for a CoE; pre-read for a sponsor conversation.
- NOT for: ranking many ideas (`ai-strategy-coe`), designing the solution, legal/compliance sign-off.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The idea in one or two sentences, and who raised it | yes | user |
| The user of the output and the decision or task it affects | yes | user |
| Current process: steps, volume, time, error or cost signal (even rough) | yes | user; unknowns marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` |
| Data involved: where it lives, owner, access, sensitivity | yes | user |
| Constraints: budget envelope, timeline, vendor policy | no | user |

If the user/decision or the data description is missing, ask once; otherwise fill the canvas with explicit unknowns rather than stalling.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. **Fill the canvas** from `assets/use-case-canvas.md` following `references/canvas-definition.md`: every box has content or a labeled unknown with an owner.
3. **Score** value, feasibility, data readiness, risk (1–5 each) using the rubric in `ai-strategy-coe/references/use-case-scoring.md`; compute priority = V × F × D ÷ R. Record the evidence per score.
4. **Decide build / buy / partner** with `references/build-buy-factors.md`; state the two strongest factors behind the decision.
5. **Set the verdict**: Proceed to design / Proceed after data readiness work / Park / Stop, plus the one 30-day step and its owner.
6. Hand off: Proceed → `agent-architecture` or `rag-pipeline-design`; risk tier medium/high → `ai-governance-risk` before build.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `use-case-canvas-<name>.md`: one page; verdict first; canvas table; scores; build/buy; next step.

## Self-check
- [ ] Verdict and next step are the first two lines
- [ ] Baseline metric named, with value or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Data box names owner, access path, and sensitivity
- [ ] Scores have one evidence line each
- [ ] Build/buy decision cites factors, not preference
- [ ] Fits on one page (≤ 60 lines)
- [ ] No vendor named without a selection criterion

## References
- `references/canvas-definition.md` — boxes, prompts, and quality tests
- `references/build-buy-factors.md` — decision factors and patterns
- `scripts/canvas.py` — answers.json → `canvas.md` (filled, scored, verdict), `decision.md` (build/buy/partner citing factors), `score.json`

bodyHtml:
AI Vendor Assessment (weighted scoring + third-party AI risk)

In a conversation: score the vendors now

The reply is the assessment (or its skeleton), never only a request for files. Replies are short (about 900 tokens): no preamble, tables over prose, risk shown as red flags and unanswered ids only (not 11 rows per option). The first three lines are always:

  1. Recommendation: <option> | no clear winner | pending — <reason>
  2. Run: python3 -I scripts/vendor_assess.py --options <options.csv> --criteria <criteria.csv> [--risk <risk.csv>] [--previous <scores.csv>] [--require-clear-winner] --out-dir out → scores.csv, sensitivity.csv, vendor-report.md (use the case's flags).
  3. Limits: a decision aid, not a contract or legal review; vendor claims are recorded, not verified; a missing score is never imputed.

Never

  • Never invent, propose or "sensibly" fill weights, even when asked ("use whatever weights make sense"). No criteria file → line 1 Recommendation: pending — criteria weights not provided; the run stops (exit 2), then decline in one sentence ("Weights must come from the decision owner; I will not invent them") and ask once: "Please send the criteria weights CSV criterion,weight,description signed off by the decision owner (sponsor)." Show the supplied scores and completeness only; no weighted score, rank or sensitivity.
  • Never impute a blank score: that option is complete = no, no weighted score, no rank, excluded from the recommendation; gap <criterion> To be baselined · owner: Procurement lead.
  • Never assume a risk answer ("assume the big vendors are compliant"): risk not assessed To be baselined · owner: Third-party risk manager; recommendation Conditional on a third-party risk review To be baselined · owner: Third-party risk manager.
  • Never treat unknown/blank/no row as a red flag (it is unanswered, owner Third-party risk manager); n/a is not applicable. Never use last year's scores in today's scores.

Procedure — compute from the supplied rows, writing every product out; never estimate

  1. Raw weights r_c and their sum R (weights normalised to 1.000: w_c = r_c ÷ R).
  2. Complete option = a 1-5 score on every criterion. Score outside 1-5, unknown criterion or duplicate row → stops (exit 2).
  3. Numerator N = Σ r_c × score_c, every term written; weighted score = N ÷ R (3 dp). Worked example (references/method.md): weights 40/25/20/15, scores 5,3,4,4 → N = 40×5 + 25×3 + 20×4 + 15×4 = 200 + 75 + 80 + 60 = 415; 415 ÷ 100 = 4.150. Match each score to its criterion by name, not by row order. Rank by score descending; equal scores share a rank.
  4. Sensitivity (2 runs per criterion: ×0.8, ×1.2 on that raw weight only). Let D = N_top − N_other for each other complete option. Under criterion c and factor f: D' = D + (f − 1) × r_c × (score_top,c − score_other,c); new sum R' = R + (f − 1) × r_c. The top is unchanged when every D' > 0 (top_changed = no); D' ≤ 0 → yes. Margin to the runner-up = min D' ÷ R'. Worked example (method.md): answer_quality 40 × 0.8 → R' = 92; Fabrikam 375/92 = 4.076 vs Tailspin 353/92 = 3.837; D' = 22, margin 0.239, top unchanged. Rank stability % = runs with no ÷ (2 × criteria) × 100 (state "n of N runs").
  5. Red flags — test every answer against its rule and write the test, e.g. TPR-02 90 > 30 → RED, TPR-02 30 > 30? no: TPR-01 eq:yes · TPR-02 retention days gt:30 · TPR-03 eq:no · TPR-04 eq:no · TPR-05 eq:no · TPR-06 eq:no · TPR-07 eq:no (in_progress not red) · TPR-08 change notice days lt:30 · TPR-09 incident hours gt:72 · TPR-10 eq:no · TPR-11 eq:no. unknown/blank/missing = unanswered, not red.
  6. Recommendation: clear winner = top complete option, not tied, with no red flags, first in every sensitivity run → Recommendation: <option> (weighted score x.xxx). Else **No clear winner.** Reasons: … (tie / "top-scoring X has red flags: TPR-nn" / "the top option changes under <criterion> <±20%>") and "Highest-scoring option without red flags: Y (score)". With --require-clear-winner and no clear winner, write "the run stops (exit 1); outputs still written"; otherwise exit 0. No risk file → conditional (see Never).
  7. Previous scores.csv: per option score then → now, change = now − then (signed, 3 dp), rank then → now, red flags raised/cleared; absent last time = new option; only in the previous file = no longer assessed.

Reply layout after the three lines

  1. Scores working table: option | N = Σ r×score (terms shown) | weighted score | rank | complete | red flags | unanswered.
  2. Sensitivity: one line per run criterion ±20%: R' | D' per rival | top | margin | top_changed, then Rank stability: x% (n of N runs).
  3. Third-party risk: per option, red-flag tests that fired, unanswered ids with owner.
  4. Recommendation (as step 6), Changes since last assessment (when previous), Method (weights normalised to 1.000, raw sum R).

No files in the conversation (vendors named, no scores/weights shown): line 1 Recommendation: pending — scores and weights not yet supplied, lines 2–3 as above, then these sections, each one line, then the ask:

  • Weighted scores: per option To be baselined · owner: Procurement lead; computed as Σ normalised weight × score (1-5) on complete options only — a missing score is never imputed.
  • ±20% sensitivity and rank stability: each criterion weight ×0.8 and ×1.2, renormalised; reports whether the winner holds and rank stability %.
  • Red flags (third-party AI risk questionnaire, 11 questions, assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv): training on customer data, retention > 30 days, residency, sub-processors, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001, model-change notice < 30 days, incident notice > 72 hours, IP indemnity, exit — per option To be baselined · owner: Third-party risk manager.
  • Ask once, one list: the scores CSV with a source per score (option,criterion,score,source); the criteria weights CSV from the decision owner (criterion,weight,description); the risk answers (option,question_id,answer,evidence).

Choosing an LLM on eval scores, token prices and latency: line 1 routes it to model-selection; offer this skill for vendor, contract and third-party risk comparison.

Starting points

  • New: a shortlist scored on your weighted criteria, with risk answers, gives the ranking, sensitivity and red flags before procurement.
  • Existing: add the scores.csv from the last assessment (previous), e.g. at renewal; the report adds each option's score and rank then and now, red flags raised or cleared, and options new or no longer assessed.

When to use

  • ADLC strategy stage: a shortlist of AI vendors, platforms or providers (and possibly an in-house build) must be compared on agreed criteria before procurement.
  • "Does the winner survive if we weight cost higher?" — the ±20% sensitivity answers it per criterion.
  • Third-party AI risk screen before contract: red flags on data use, retention, residency, assurance, change notice, incident SLA, indemnity and exit.
  • NOT for: choosing a model from eval scores, prices and latency (model-selection), forecasting token spend (llm-cost-model), legal contract review or drafting, or verifying vendor certificates (inspect the reports themselves).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
options — option, criterion, score 1–5, sourceyesevaluation team; one row per option × criterionrun stops (exit 2), asks once
criteria — criterion, weight, descriptionyesdecision owner (sponsor)run stops (exit 2), asks once

A blank score is missing: the option is marked incomplete, excluded from ranking and recommendation, and the gap is To be baselined · owner: Procurement lead. A score outside 1–5, an unknown criterion or a duplicate row stops the run (exit 2).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Agree criteria and weights with the decision owner before scoring; record a source for every score.
  3. Send vendors assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv; record answers (and n/a for a build option) in the risk CSV.
  4. Run the agent. scripts/vendor_assess.py normalises weights, scores complete options, runs ±20% sensitivity per criterion and applies the red-flag rules (references/method.md).
  5. If there is no clear winner, take the stated reasons to the decision owner (re-score, renegotiate terms, or re-weight) and re-run.
  6. Run the self-check.

Output

  • scores.csv — option, weighted_score, rank, complete, red_flags, missing_criteria, risk_unanswered (ranked complete options first, then incomplete ones).
  • sensitivity.csv — criterion, change, weight_before, weight_after, top_option, top_score, runner_up, margin, top_changed (two rows per criterion).
  • vendor-report.md — Summary, Scores (with score matrix), Sensitivity, Third-party risk, Recommendation, Method.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every score has a source; no score was imputed
  • [ ] Weights normalisation is stated
  • [ ] The recommendation is a complete option with no red flags that stays first under every ±20% change — or "no clear winner" with reasons
  • [ ] Unanswered risk questions and incomplete options name an owner
  • [ ] Limits stated: decision aid, not a legal or contract review; vendor claims not verified

References

  • references/method.md — scoring, ranking, sensitivity, red-flag and recommendation rules
  • references/sources.md — standards named in the questionnaire, with URLs and dates checked
  • assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv — 11 questions with answer types and red-flag rules
  • assets/options-template.csv, assets/criteria-template.csv, assets/risk-template.csv — input layouts

# AI Vendor Assessment (weighted scoring + third-party AI risk)

## In a conversation: score the vendors now
The reply **is the assessment** (or its skeleton), never only a request for files. Replies are short (about 900 tokens): no preamble, tables over prose, risk shown as red flags and unanswered ids only (not 11 rows per option). The first three lines are always:
1. `Recommendation: <option> | no clear winner | pending — <reason>`
2. `Run: python3 -I scripts/vendor_assess.py --options <options.csv> --criteria <criteria.csv> [--risk <risk.csv>] [--previous <scores.csv>] [--require-clear-winner] --out-dir out` → `scores.csv`, `sensitivity.csv`, `vendor-report.md` (use the case's flags).
3. `Limits: a decision aid, not a contract or legal review; vendor claims are recorded, not verified; a missing score is never imputed.`

**Never**
- Never invent, propose or "sensibly" fill weights, even when asked ("use whatever weights make sense"). No criteria file → line 1 `Recommendation: pending — criteria weights not provided; the run stops (exit 2)`, then decline in one sentence ("Weights must come from the decision owner; I will not invent them") and ask once: "Please send the criteria weights CSV `criterion,weight,description` signed off by the decision owner (sponsor)." Show the supplied scores and completeness only; no weighted score, rank or sensitivity.
- Never impute a blank score: that option is `complete = no`, no weighted score, no rank, excluded from the recommendation; gap `<criterion> [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Procurement lead]`.
- Never assume a risk answer ("assume the big vendors are compliant"): risk `not assessed [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager]`; recommendation `Conditional on a third-party risk review [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager].`
- Never treat `unknown`/blank/no row as a red flag (it is unanswered, owner Third-party risk manager); `n/a` is not applicable. Never use last year's scores in today's scores.

**Procedure — compute from the supplied rows, writing every product out; never estimate**
1. Raw weights r_c and their sum R (weights normalised to 1.000: w_c = r_c ÷ R).
2. Complete option = a 1-5 score on every criterion. Score outside 1-5, unknown criterion or duplicate row → **stops (exit 2)**.
3. Numerator N = Σ r_c × score_c, every term written; weighted score = N ÷ R (3 dp). Worked example (`references/method.md`): weights 40/25/20/15, scores 5,3,4,4 → N = 40×5 + 25×3 + 20×4 + 15×4 = 200 + 75 + 80 + 60 = 415; 415 ÷ 100 = **4.150**. Match each score to its criterion by name, not by row order. Rank by score descending; equal scores share a rank.
4. Sensitivity (2 runs per criterion: ×0.8, ×1.2 on that raw weight only). Let D = N_top − N_other for each other complete option. Under criterion c and factor f: D' = D + (f − 1) × r_c × (score_top,c − score_other,c); new sum R' = R + (f − 1) × r_c. The top is unchanged when every D' > 0 (`top_changed = no`); D' ≤ 0 → `yes`. Margin to the runner-up = min D' ÷ R'. Worked example (method.md): answer_quality 40 × 0.8 → R' = 92; Fabrikam 375/92 = 4.076 vs Tailspin 353/92 = 3.837; D' = 22, margin 0.239, top unchanged. Rank stability % = runs with `no` ÷ (2 × criteria) × 100 (state "n of N runs").
5. Red flags — test every answer against its rule and write the test, e.g. `TPR-02 90 > 30 → RED`, `TPR-02 30 > 30? no`: TPR-01 eq:yes · TPR-02 retention days gt:30 · TPR-03 eq:no · TPR-04 eq:no · TPR-05 eq:no · TPR-06 eq:no · TPR-07 eq:no (`in_progress` not red) · TPR-08 change notice days lt:30 · TPR-09 incident hours gt:72 · TPR-10 eq:no · TPR-11 eq:no. `unknown`/blank/missing = unanswered, not red.
6. Recommendation: clear winner = top complete option, not tied, with no red flags, first in every sensitivity run → `Recommendation: <option> (weighted score x.xxx)`. Else `**No clear winner.** Reasons: …` (tie / "top-scoring X has red flags: TPR-nn" / "the top option changes under <criterion> <±20%>") and "Highest-scoring option without red flags: Y (score)". With `--require-clear-winner` and no clear winner, write "the run **stops (exit 1)**; outputs still written"; otherwise exit 0. No risk file → conditional (see Never).
7. Previous `scores.csv`: per option score then → now, change = now − then (signed, 3 dp), rank then → now, red flags raised/cleared; absent last time = `new option`; only in the previous file = `no longer assessed`.

**Reply layout after the three lines**
1. **Scores** working table: `option | N = Σ r×score (terms shown) | weighted score | rank | complete | red flags | unanswered`.
2. **Sensitivity**: one line per run `criterion ±20%: R' | D' per rival | top | margin | top_changed`, then `Rank stability: x% (n of N runs)`.
3. **Third-party risk**: per option, red-flag tests that fired, unanswered ids with owner.
4. **Recommendation** (as step 6), **Changes since last assessment** (when `previous`), **Method** (weights normalised to 1.000, raw sum R).

**No files in the conversation** (vendors named, no scores/weights shown): line 1 `Recommendation: pending — scores and weights not yet supplied`, lines 2–3 as above, then these sections, each one line, then the ask:
- **Weighted scores**: per option `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Procurement lead]`; computed as Σ normalised weight × score (1-5) on complete options only — a missing score is never imputed.
- **±20% sensitivity and rank stability**: each criterion weight ×0.8 and ×1.2, renormalised; reports whether the winner holds and rank stability %.
- **Red flags (third-party AI risk questionnaire, 11 questions, `assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv`)**: training on customer data, retention > 30 days, residency, sub-processors, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001, model-change notice < 30 days, incident notice > 72 hours, IP indemnity, exit — per option `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager]`.
- Ask once, one list: the scores CSV with a source per score (`option,criterion,score,source`); the criteria weights CSV from the decision owner (`criterion,weight,description`); the risk answers (`option,question_id,answer,evidence`).

**Choosing an LLM on eval scores, token prices and latency**: line 1 routes it to `model-selection`; offer this skill for vendor, contract and third-party risk comparison.

## Starting points
- **New:** a shortlist scored on your weighted criteria, with risk answers, gives the ranking, sensitivity and red flags before procurement.
- **Existing:** add the `scores.csv` from the last assessment (`previous`), e.g. at renewal; the report adds each option's score and rank then and now, red flags raised or cleared, and options new or no longer assessed.

## When to use
- ADLC strategy stage: a shortlist of AI vendors, platforms or providers (and possibly an in-house build) must be compared on agreed criteria before procurement.
- "Does the winner survive if we weight cost higher?" — the ±20% sensitivity answers it per criterion.
- Third-party AI risk screen before contract: red flags on data use, retention, residency, assurance, change notice, incident SLA, indemnity and exit.
- NOT for: choosing a model from eval scores, prices and latency (`model-selection`), forecasting token spend (`llm-cost-model`), legal contract review or drafting, or verifying vendor certificates (inspect the reports themselves).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` — option, criterion, score 1–5, source | yes | evaluation team; one row per option × criterion | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `criteria` — criterion, weight, description | yes | decision owner (sponsor) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `risk` — option, question_id, answer, evidence | no | Third-party risk manager from vendor responses | risk "not assessed" `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager]`; recommendation is conditional |
| `questions` — questionnaire with thresholds | no | Third-party risk manager (copy the shipped file) | shipped defaults (30-day retention, 30-day change notice, 72-hour incident notice) |
| `require_clear_winner` — true/false | no | decision owner | false: "no clear winner" exits 0 |

A blank score is missing: the option is marked incomplete, excluded from ranking and recommendation, and the gap is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Procurement lead]`. A score outside 1–5, an unknown criterion or a duplicate row stops the run (exit 2).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Agree criteria and weights with the decision owner before scoring; record a source for every score.
3. Send vendors `assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv`; record answers (and `n/a` for a build option) in the risk CSV.
4. Run the agent. `scripts/vendor_assess.py` normalises weights, scores complete options, runs ±20% sensitivity per criterion and applies the red-flag rules (`references/method.md`).
5. If there is no clear winner, take the stated reasons to the decision owner (re-score, renegotiate terms, or re-weight) and re-run.
6. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `scores.csv` — `option, weighted_score, rank, complete, red_flags, missing_criteria, risk_unanswered` (ranked complete options first, then incomplete ones).
- `sensitivity.csv` — `criterion, change, weight_before, weight_after, top_option, top_score, runner_up, margin, top_changed` (two rows per criterion).
- `vendor-report.md` — **Summary**, **Scores** (with score matrix), **Sensitivity**, **Third-party risk**, **Recommendation**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every score has a source; no score was imputed
- [ ] Weights normalisation is stated
- [ ] The recommendation is a complete option with no red flags that stays first under every ±20% change — or "no clear winner" with reasons
- [ ] Unanswered risk questions and incomplete options name an owner
- [ ] Limits stated: decision aid, not a legal or contract review; vendor claims not verified

## References
- `references/method.md` — scoring, ranking, sensitivity, red-flag and recommendation rules
- `references/sources.md` — standards named in the questionnaire, with URLs and dates checked
- `assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv` — 11 questions with answer types and red-flag rules
- `assets/options-template.csv`, `assets/criteria-template.csv`, `assets/risk-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/vendor_assess.py` — scorer and `--verify` mode (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-vendor-assessment --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-vendor-assessment`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`scores.csv`, `sensitivity.csv`, `vendor-report.md`). "No clear winner" is a finding, not a failure (exit 0) unless `require_clear_winner=true`, which makes it a gate (exit 1, outputs still written).

card: How reliable your labels are, and which items disagree
name: annotation-agreement
description: Use when the user needs to know how consistently humans labelled data for AI evaluation or training — "measure inter-annotator agreement", "what's our Cohen's / Fleiss' kappa", "Krippendorff's alpha for these labels", "which items do annotators disagree on", "which labels do our guidelines need to clarify". Produces agreement.json, disputed-items.csv, label-agreement.csv and agreement-report.md from item_id,annotator,label rows - percent agreement, pairwise Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, nominal Krippendorff's alpha (handles missing ratings), per-label agreement, confusion pairs and low-agreement labels the guidelines do not define. Exit 1 when alpha is below the supplied minimum or no item has 2+ ratings (no score is faked). Not for scoring model outputs (llm-eval-harness), data quality (data-readiness-assessment) or building training sets (finetune-dataset-builder).

bodyHtml:
Annotation Agreement (inter-annotator reliability)

In a conversation: write the agreement assessment now

The reply is the agreement assessment draft, never only a request for the CSV. No label rows are in the conversation, so no alpha, kappa or count is printed; each is a marker until the run.

  • The request describes a labelling round (annotators, items, label set, purpose) but the labels are not in the conversation: write the report skeleton in this reply, in the order of agreement-report.md:
    1. Summary — gate verdict first: Gate: not set — the minimum alpha is the data owner's decision (ask them for it; never choose one), or the stated minimum against alpha [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run]. Line 2: how it is computed — export one row per rating as item_id, annotator, label and run scripts/agreement.py (python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input labels=<labels.csv> [--input guidelines=<guidelines.md>] [--input min_agreement=<alpha>] --out <dir>).
    2. Agreement — Krippendorff's alpha (nominal) is the headline; then percent agreement, pairwise Cohen's kappa per annotator pair and Fleiss' kappa (n/a with the reason when items have different numbers of ratings). State the interpretation bands as conventions, not tests: Krippendorff ≥ 0.800 commonly relied on, 0.667–0.800 tentative conclusions only, < 0.667 discard; Landis & Koch for kappa (< 0 poor, 0.00–0.20 slight, 0.21–0.40 fair, 0.41–0.60 moderate, 0.61–0.80 substantial, 0.81–1.00 almost perfect).
    3. Disputed items — table item_id | labels (label:count) | majority (or tie) | agreement, lowest first, to send to an adjudicator.
    4. Guideline gaps — per-label agreement (label | n | agreement | defined_in_guidelines); a low-agreement label is one below overall percent agreement; a gap is such a label the guidelines do not define, plus boundary rules for the top confusion pairs. Without guidelines: To be baselined · owner: Annotation lead.
    5. Method & limits — ratings must be independent; items with one rating are excluded and counted; nominal labels only; no confidence intervals; agreement measures consistency, not correctness.
  • Each item has only one annotator: say agreement cannot be computed without two or more independent ratings per item, report no score, and recommend double-labelling a sample.
  • No labelling round described at all: ask once for the labels export, the guidelines and the data owner's minimum alpha.
  • Asked to pick the threshold, declare labels defined without guidelines, or report a score anyway: decline in one line (the threshold is the data owner's; definitions come from written guidelines; no score without paired ratings) and show the marker.

Starting points

  • New: labels from a pilot round (and draft guidelines) give alpha, disputed items and the label boundaries to sharpen before labelling at scale.
  • Existing: add the agreement.json from the previous round (previous); the report adds alpha, percent agreement, disputed items and per-label agreement then vs now, and names labels whose agreement fell.

When to use

  • ADLC data stage: before human labels become an eval golden set, an LLM-as-judge calibration set or fine-tuning data.
  • Pilot labelling round: find disputed items and the label boundaries the guidelines must sharpen before labelling at scale.
  • Gate: labels may be used only when alpha meets the minimum the data owner set.
  • NOT for: scoring model outputs against labels (llm-eval-harness), data quality or PII scans (data-readiness-assessment, pii-data-inventory), building the training file (finetune-dataset-builder), ordinal or interval scales (nominal labels only).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
labels — item_id, annotator, labelyeslabelling tool export (one row per rating)run stops (exit 2), asks once
guidelines — MarkdownnoAnnotation leaddefined_in_guidelines and the gap list read To be baselined · owner: Annotation lead
min_agreement — alpha thresholdnoeval / data ownerno gate; the report says none was set

A blank label means "not rated" and is skipped. Two ratings of the same item by the same annotator stop the run (exit 2).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Confirm ratings were independent (annotators did not see each other's labels); agreement on shared work is inflated.
  3. Run the agent. scripts/agreement.py builds the coincidence matrix and computes alpha, Fleiss' kappa (equal ratings per item only), pairwise Cohen's kappa, per-label agreement and confusion pairs.
  4. Read Disputed items worst-first; send them to an adjudicator.
  5. Read Guideline gaps: define each low-agreement label the guidelines do not mention, and write a boundary rule for the top confusion pairs.
  6. Re-label a fresh sample after the guideline change and re-run; compare alpha.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • agreement.json — every statistic, per-item agreement, pairs, confusion pairs, gate result, settings for --verify.
  • disputed-items.csv — item_id, labels, majority, agreement (labels as label:count; majority is the plurality label or tie), lowest agreement first.
  • label-agreement.csv — label, n, agreement, defined_in_guidelines.
  • agreement-report.md — Summary (gate verdict first), Agreement, Disputed items, Guideline gaps, Method & limits.

Self-check

  • [ ] Alpha is reported with its band labelled as a convention (Krippendorff 0.667 / 0.800); kappas with Landis & Koch bands, also a convention
  • [ ] Fleiss' kappa is n/a (with the reason) when items have different numbers of ratings — alpha is the headline
  • [ ] Items with one rating are excluded and counted, not scored
  • [ ] Guideline gaps come from the supplied guidelines; without them the gap list is TBD for the Annotation lead
  • [ ] Limits stated: nominal only, no confidence intervals, agreement is not correctness

References

  • references/method.md — formulas, the worked examples the tests reproduce, per-label agreement definition
  • references/sources.md — Cohen 1960, Fleiss 1971, Krippendorff 2011, Landis & Koch 1977; verified URLs and dates
  • assets/labels-template.csv, assets/guidelines-template.md — input layouts
  • scripts/agreement.py — statistics and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/annotation-agreement). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (agreement.json, disputed-items.csv, label-agreement.csv, agreement-report.md). Alpha below min_agreement fails the run (exit 1) with every output written. If no item has two or more ratings the run exits 1 and reports no score. Each output passes --verify, which re-derives it from the labels and the settings recorded in agreement.json.

- **The request describes a labelling round** (annotators, items, label set, purpose) but the labels are not in the conversation: write the report skeleton **in this reply**, in the order of `agreement-report.md`:
  1. **Summary** — gate verdict first: `Gate: not set — the minimum alpha is the data owner's decision` (ask them for it; never choose one), or the stated minimum against `alpha [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run]`. Line 2: how it is computed — export one row per rating as `item_id, annotator, label` and run `scripts/agreement.py` (`python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input labels=<labels.csv> [--input guidelines=<guidelines.md>] [--input min_agreement=<alpha>] --out <dir>`).
  2. **Agreement** — Krippendorff's alpha (nominal) is the headline; then percent agreement, pairwise Cohen's kappa per annotator pair and Fleiss' kappa (n/a with the reason when items have different numbers of ratings). State the interpretation bands as **conventions, not tests**: Krippendorff ≥ 0.800 commonly relied on, 0.667–0.800 tentative conclusions only, < 0.667 discard; Landis & Koch for kappa (< 0 poor, 0.00–0.20 slight, 0.21–0.40 fair, 0.41–0.60 moderate, 0.61–0.80 substantial, 0.81–1.00 almost perfect).
  3. **Disputed items** — table `item_id | labels (label:count) | majority (or tie) | agreement`, lowest first, to send to an adjudicator.
  4. **Guideline gaps** — per-label agreement (`label | n | agreement | defined_in_guidelines`); a low-agreement label is one below overall percent agreement; a gap is such a label the guidelines do not define, plus boundary rules for the top confusion pairs. Without guidelines: `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]`.
  5. **Method & limits** — ratings must be independent; items with one rating are excluded and counted; nominal labels only; no confidence intervals; agreement measures consistency, not correctness.
- **Each item has only one annotator**: say agreement cannot be computed without two or more independent ratings per item, report no score, and recommend double-labelling a sample.
- **No labelling round described at all**: ask once for the labels export, the guidelines and the data owner's minimum alpha.
- **Asked to pick the threshold, declare labels defined without guidelines, or report a score anyway**: decline in one line (the threshold is the data owner's; definitions come from written guidelines; no score without paired ratings) and show the marker.

## Starting points
- **New:** labels from a pilot round (and draft guidelines) give alpha, disputed items and the label boundaries to sharpen before labelling at scale.
- **Existing:** add the `agreement.json` from the previous round (`previous`); the report adds alpha, percent agreement, disputed items and per-label agreement then vs now, and names labels whose agreement fell.

## When to use
- ADLC data stage: before human labels become an eval golden set, an LLM-as-judge calibration set or fine-tuning data.
- Pilot labelling round: find disputed items and the label boundaries the guidelines must sharpen before labelling at scale.
- Gate: labels may be used only when alpha meets the minimum the data owner set.
- NOT for: scoring model outputs against labels (`llm-eval-harness`), data quality or PII scans (`data-readiness-assessment`, `pii-data-inventory`), building the training file (`finetune-dataset-builder`), ordinal or interval scales (nominal labels only).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` — `item_id, annotator, label` | yes | labelling tool export (one row per rating) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `guidelines` — Markdown | no | Annotation lead | `defined_in_guidelines` and the gap list read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]` |
| `min_agreement` — alpha threshold | no | eval / data owner | no gate; the report says none was set |

A blank `label` means "not rated" and is skipped. Two ratings of the same item by the same annotator stop the run (exit 2).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Confirm ratings were independent (annotators did not see each other's labels); agreement on shared work is inflated.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/agreement.py` builds the coincidence matrix and computes alpha, Fleiss' kappa (equal ratings per item only), pairwise Cohen's kappa, per-label agreement and confusion pairs.
4. Read Disputed items worst-first; send them to an adjudicator.
5. Read Guideline gaps: define each low-agreement label the guidelines do not mention, and write a boundary rule for the top confusion pairs.
6. Re-label a fresh sample after the guideline change and re-run; compare alpha.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `agreement.json` — every statistic, per-item agreement, pairs, confusion pairs, gate result, settings for `--verify`.
- `disputed-items.csv` — `item_id, labels, majority, agreement` (labels as `label:count`; `majority` is the plurality label or `tie`), lowest agreement first.
- `label-agreement.csv` — `label, n, agreement, defined_in_guidelines`.
- `agreement-report.md` — **Summary** (gate verdict first), **Agreement**, **Disputed items**, **Guideline gaps**, **Method & limits**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Alpha is reported with its band labelled as a convention (Krippendorff 0.667 / 0.800); kappas with Landis & Koch bands, also a convention
- [ ] Fleiss' kappa is n/a (with the reason) when items have different numbers of ratings — alpha is the headline
- [ ] Items with one rating are excluded and counted, not scored
- [ ] Guideline gaps come from the supplied guidelines; without them the gap list is TBD for the Annotation lead
- [ ] Limits stated: nominal only, no confidence intervals, agreement is not correctness

## References
- `references/method.md` — formulas, the worked examples the tests reproduce, per-label agreement definition
- `references/sources.md` — Cohen 1960, Fleiss 1971, Krippendorff 2011, Landis & Koch 1977; verified URLs and dates
- `assets/labels-template.csv`, `assets/guidelines-template.md` — input layouts
- `scripts/agreement.py` — statistics and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/annotation-agreement`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`agreement.json`, `disputed-items.csv`, `label-agreement.csv`, `agreement-report.md`). Alpha below `min_agreement` fails the run (exit 1) with every output written. If no item has two or more ratings the run exits 1 and reports no score. Each output passes `--verify`, which re-derives it from the labels and the settings recorded in `agreement.json`.

bodyHtml:
Conversation Design (intents, fallback, hand-off, coverage)

In a conversation: route and report now

The reply is the coverage report (or one ask), never only a command. About 1,000 tokens, tables over prose. Line 1: Run: python3 -I scripts/conversation_design.py --intents <intents.csv> --utterances <utterances.csv> [--persona <persona.csv>] [--min-accuracy <x>] --out-dir out → routing.csv, intent-quality.csv, conversation-spec.md (use the case's flags). Line 2: the headline — Coverage a/b · Accuracy c/d = 0.xxx (or "not measured — no labels") · Gate: met (exit 0) | FAILED (exit 1) | none (exit 0).

Never

  • Never pick "sensible" persona values. Each of name, tone, reading_level, escalation_channel, disallowed_topics absent from the persona file is To be baselined · owner: Conversation designer — list each missing key by name (e.g. reading_level too), and say "not chosen: the Conversation designer's decision".
  • Never invent utterances or intents: no utterance file → ask once for the utterance sample (utterance[,expected_intent], assets/utterances-template.csv); the run stops (exit 2). Same for a missing intent catalog.
  • Never echo more than the first 80 characters of a user message (end with "…").
  • Never state accuracy without counting labelled rows from the file.

Procedure — row by row from the supplied CSVs (references/method.md)

  1. Tokenise: lower-case, [a-z0-9]+, drop tokens < 2 chars and stopwords (a an the and or but if of to in on at for from by with about as is are was were be been am do does did i me my we our you your it its this that these those there here can could would should will just so please hi hello hey), drop a trailing s on tokens > 3 chars not ending ss.
  2. One document per intent = description + all examples; idf(t) = ln((1+N)/(1+df)) + 1 over the N intent documents; vectors = count × idf, L2-normalised; utterance terms in no intent document are ignored. Score = cosine; best intent wins (tie → intent name). Best score < 0.25 → fallback (uncovered). Long messages sharing one or two common terms usually fall below 0.25.
  3. Coverage = utterances routed to an intent ÷ all utterances (blank-label rows count here).
  4. Labelled = rows with a non-blank expected_intent (fallback is a label). Accuracy = correct ÷ labelled, 3 decimals. Precision = correct ÷ routed-to-intent; recall = correct ÷ labelled-as-intent; zero denominator → n/a.
  5. Confusable: cosine of two intents' example sets ≥ 0.40 (shared example words such as "pay … bill" across two intents).
  6. Gate: --min-accuracy x and accuracy < x (or no labels) → "run exits 1; all outputs still written" (e.g. "0.870 is below 0.900"); accuracy ≥ x → "gate met (exit 0)"; no min_accuracy → "no gate (exit 0)". Unknown label, bad response_type, handoff not yes/no, duplicate intent, an intent named fallback, or a missing required file → stops (exit 2) with the line.

Reply layout after the two lines

  1. Working table, every utterance: | # | utterance (≤80 chars) | predicted | score≈ | expected | ✓ |, then the counts it gives.
  2. Per-intent | intent | examples | precision | recall | confusable_with | owner |.
  3. Gaps (each with the intent's owner): uncovered messages, recall/precision < 1.000, intents with < 5 examples, confusable pairs, missing persona keys.
  4. Fallback and hand-off: below 0.25 → rephrase prompt → re-route; second miss → the persona's escalation_channel (or its TBD); handoff=yes intents go straight there. Short mermaid flowchart.
  5. Method line: thresholds 0.25 route / 0.40 confusable; the router is lexical (TF-IDF) and sample-based, not a production NLU benchmark; hand-computed scores are approximate — routing.csv from the run is authoritative (--verify re-derives it).

No files in the conversation: give line 1, describe each metric above with its threshold, and ask once for the intent catalog and utterance sample.

Starting points

  • New: first-draft intents and unlabelled sample messages give a coverage figure, the messages nothing catches, thin and confusable intents, and the persona keys still to decide.
  • Existing: your live intent catalog, persona and labelled real messages give per-intent precision and recall, misroutes and an accuracy gate for edits to the catalog.

When to use

  • ADLC requirements stage: before building an assistant, to agree the intent catalog, response types, fallback and the human hand-off path.
  • "How much of what users actually say do our intents cover?" — route a sample of real messages and read coverage and gaps.
  • Regression check after editing intents: run with labelled utterances and a min_accuracy gate.
  • NOT for: prompt wording or system prompts (prompt-spec), grading LLM answers (llm-eval-harness), single- vs multi-agent design (agent-architecture), production NLU benchmarking (this router is lexical).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
intents — intent,description,examples,response_type,handoff,owneryesConversation designer (copy assets/intents-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
utterances — utterance[,expected_intent]yeschat logs, search logs, call-centre notes, sampled and de-identifiedrun stops (exit 2), asks once
persona — kv-csv name, tone, reading_level, escalation_channel, disallowed_topicsnoConversation designer / brand voice guideeach missing key is To be baselined · owner: Conversation designer
min_accuracy — 0–1noproduct ownerno gate; accuracy reported only

expected_intent may be an intent name, fallback (out of scope on purpose) or blank (unlabelled; counts toward coverage only). An unknown label, a bad response_type, a handoff other than yes/no, a duplicate intent or an intent named fallback stops the run (exit 2) with the line number.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Strip personal data from the utterance sample. Outputs echo at most 80 characters of each utterance, but the run reads all of it.
  3. Run the agent. scripts/conversation_design.py routes each utterance by TF-IDF cosine (references/method.md); below 0.25 it goes to fallback.
  4. With labels it computes accuracy, per-intent precision/recall and confusion pairs; it flags intent pairs whose example sets reach cosine 0.40.
  5. With min_accuracy, accuracy below it (or no labels to measure it) exits 1.
  6. Work the Gaps list with each intent's owner: add missed phrasings, split or merge confusable intents, confirm out-of-scope messages.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • routing.csv — utterance (≤ 80 chars), predicted_intent, score, expected_intent, correct, nearest_intent.
  • intent-quality.csv — intent, examples, precision, recall, confusable_with, response_type, handoff, routed, labelled, owner.
  • conversation-spec.md — Summary, Persona, Intents, Fallback and hand-off (mermaid flowchart), Coverage (uncovered utterances, confusion pairs), Gaps (each with an owner), Method.

Self-check

  • [ ] routing.csv re-derives exactly (--verify) and no output echoes more than 80 characters of an utterance (--leak-check)
  • [ ] Every gap names an owner; missing persona keys are TBD for the Conversation designer
  • [ ] The flowchart shows fallback and a path to a person
  • [ ] Threshold values (0.25 route, 0.40 confusable) are stated in the report
  • [ ] Limits stated: lexical router, sample-based, not a production NLU benchmark

References

  • references/method.md — tokenising, TF-IDF formula, thresholds, metrics, limits
  • assets/intents-template.csv, assets/utterances-template.csv, assets/persona-template.csv — input layouts
  • scripts/conversation_design.py — router, metrics, spec writer, --verify and --leak-check (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/conversation-design --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/conversation-design). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (routing.csv, intent-quality.csv, conversation-spec.md). Accuracy below a supplied min_accuracy fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the outputs are still written so the misses are visible.

5. Confusable: cosine of two intents' **example sets** ≥ **0.40** (shared example words such as "pay … bill" across two intents).
6. Gate: `--min-accuracy x` and accuracy < x (or no labels) → "**run exits 1; all outputs still written**" (e.g. "0.870 is below 0.900"); accuracy ≥ x → "gate met (exit 0)"; no min_accuracy → "no gate (exit 0)". Unknown label, bad response_type, handoff not yes/no, duplicate intent, an intent named `fallback`, or a missing required file → **stops (exit 2)** with the line.

**Reply layout after the two lines**
1. Working table, every utterance: `| # | utterance (≤80 chars) | predicted | score≈ | expected | ✓ |`, then the counts it gives.
2. Per-intent `| intent | examples | precision | recall | confusable_with | owner |`.
3. **Gaps** (each with the intent's owner): uncovered messages, recall/precision < 1.000, intents with < 5 examples, confusable pairs, missing persona keys.
4. **Fallback and hand-off**: below 0.25 → rephrase prompt → re-route; second miss → the persona's `escalation_channel` (or its TBD); `handoff=yes` intents go straight there. Short mermaid `flowchart`.
5. **Method** line: thresholds 0.25 route / 0.40 confusable; the router is **lexical (TF-IDF) and sample-based**, not a production NLU benchmark; hand-computed scores are approximate — `routing.csv` from the run is authoritative (`--verify` re-derives it).
No files in the conversation: give line 1, describe each metric above with its threshold, and ask once for the intent catalog and utterance sample.

## Starting points
- **New:** first-draft intents and unlabelled sample messages give a coverage figure, the messages nothing catches, thin and confusable intents, and the persona keys still to decide.
- **Existing:** your live intent catalog, persona and labelled real messages give per-intent precision and recall, misroutes and an accuracy gate for edits to the catalog.

## When to use
- ADLC requirements stage: before building an assistant, to agree the intent catalog, response types, fallback and the human hand-off path.
- "How much of what users actually say do our intents cover?" — route a sample of real messages and read coverage and gaps.
- Regression check after editing intents: run with labelled utterances and a `min_accuracy` gate.
- NOT for: prompt wording or system prompts (`prompt-spec`), grading LLM answers (`llm-eval-harness`), single- vs multi-agent design (`agent-architecture`), production NLU benchmarking (this router is lexical).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `intents` — `intent,description,examples,response_type,handoff,owner` | yes | Conversation designer (copy `assets/intents-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `utterances` — `utterance[,expected_intent]` | yes | chat logs, search logs, call-centre notes, sampled and de-identified | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `persona` — kv-csv `name, tone, reading_level, escalation_channel, disallowed_topics` | no | Conversation designer / brand voice guide | each missing key is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Conversation designer]` |
| `min_accuracy` — 0–1 | no | product owner | no gate; accuracy reported only |

`expected_intent` may be an intent name, `fallback` (out of scope on purpose) or blank (unlabelled; counts toward coverage only). An unknown label, a bad `response_type`, a `handoff` other than yes/no, a duplicate intent or an intent named `fallback` stops the run (exit 2) with the line number.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Strip personal data from the utterance sample. Outputs echo at most 80 characters of each utterance, but the run reads all of it.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/conversation_design.py` routes each utterance by TF-IDF cosine (`references/method.md`); below 0.25 it goes to `fallback`.
4. With labels it computes accuracy, per-intent precision/recall and confusion pairs; it flags intent pairs whose example sets reach cosine 0.40.
5. With `min_accuracy`, accuracy below it (or no labels to measure it) exits 1.
6. Work the Gaps list with each intent's owner: add missed phrasings, split or merge confusable intents, confirm out-of-scope messages.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `routing.csv` — `utterance` (≤ 80 chars), `predicted_intent`, `score`, `expected_intent`, `correct`, `nearest_intent`.
- `intent-quality.csv` — `intent, examples, precision, recall, confusable_with, response_type, handoff, routed, labelled, owner`.
- `conversation-spec.md` — **Summary**, **Persona**, **Intents**, **Fallback and hand-off** (mermaid flowchart), **Coverage** (uncovered utterances, confusion pairs), **Gaps** (each with an owner), **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] `routing.csv` re-derives exactly (`--verify`) and no output echoes more than 80 characters of an utterance (`--leak-check`)
- [ ] Every gap names an owner; missing persona keys are TBD for the Conversation designer
- [ ] The flowchart shows fallback and a path to a person
- [ ] Threshold values (0.25 route, 0.40 confusable) are stated in the report
- [ ] Limits stated: lexical router, sample-based, not a production NLU benchmark

## References
- `references/method.md` — tokenising, TF-IDF formula, thresholds, metrics, limits
- `assets/intents-template.csv`, `assets/utterances-template.csv`, `assets/persona-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/conversation_design.py` — router, metrics, spec writer, `--verify` and `--leak-check` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/conversation-design --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/conversation-design`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`routing.csv`, `intent-quality.csv`, `conversation-spec.md`). Accuracy below a supplied `min_accuracy` fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the outputs are still written so the misses are visible.

bodyHtml:
Data Contract Validator

In a conversation: validate the extract now

The reply is the contract report (or its skeleton): line 1 is Verdict: PASS | PASS WITH WARNINGS | FAIL | pending — <reason>, never only a request for files. Error-severity violations block use (the run exits 1); warnings do not.

  • The request carries the contract rules and the data (or a description of them): write the report in this reply in the script's order — Summary; Verdict with counts of error- and warn-severity violations; Violations table column, rule, severity, failing_rows, failing_rate, examples, owner, expectation (errors first; rules from references/rules.md: missing_column, extra_column, ragged_row, type, required, null_rate, unique, min/max, allowed, regex, freshness; at most 3 examples per violation, each ≤ 40 characters; blank owner = To be baselined · owner: Data owner); Profile (column, inferred_type, null_rate, distinct, min, max); Method. Name the run that produces the files: python3 -I scripts/validate_contract.py --contract … --data … [--freshness-column … --as-of … --max-age-days …] --out-dir ….
  • Files said to be attached, or the extract/contract named but not shown (e.g. "check this extract against the contract before RAG ingestion"): lay out every section above now with each value To be baselined · owner: Data owner, state the gate rule (any error-severity violation → FAIL, exit 1, outputs still written; examples truncated, at most 3 per violation), and ask once, in one list, for: the contract (CSV per assets/contract-template.csv, or ODCS v3 YAML), the extract CSV, and for freshness the column, load (as-of) date and max age. Never invent rules, thresholds or owners.
  • No contract yet / onboarding a feed: the run drafts contract-draft.csv from the first extract (types, required, unique keys, enums, observed null limits, all at warn severity, owners left to the Data owner); the report marks the contract DRAFT and says the pass is by construction until the owner signs it off.
  • ODCS YAML contract: map the supported subset (references/odcs-subset.md: primaryKey, pattern, minimum/maximum, validValues, format email, nullValues percent, duplicateValues); list anything else (e.g. missingValues) as not evaluated, never silently passed.
  • "Use today's date and a sensible max age" for freshness: decline in one line (freshness must be measured from the load date and the owner's SLA); freshness reads not checked: as_of and max_age_days To be baselined · owner: Data owner; today's date is never used and no max age is proposed.
  • "Which columns hold personal data / need masking?": line 1 routes it to pii-data-inventory; offer this skill for contract conformance afterwards.

Starting points

  • New: with only a first extract, the run drafts contract-draft.csv from it (types, required, keys, code lists, null limits, observed ranges in notes, all at warn severity with no owner invented) and checks the extract against the draft; the report marks the contract DRAFT until the Data owner signs it off.
  • Existing: your agreed contract (CSV or ODCS YAML) and the latest extract give every breach with its owner and the error-severity gate.

When to use

  • ADLC data stage: before an extract is loaded into a vector store, a fine-tune set or an evaluation set.
  • A recurring feed into an AI system needs a pass/fail gate on schema, types, nulls, keys, ranges, code lists and freshness.
  • A data owner has a contract (CSV, or an ODCS v3 YAML file) and wants every breach listed with its owner.
  • NOT for: finding personal data (pii-data-inventory), overall readiness scoring (data-readiness-assessment), building or cleaning training data (finetune-dataset-builder), cross-table or drift checks, fixing the data (this skill reports; it never edits the source).

InputRequiredSourceIf missing

Contract types: string, integer, number, boolean, date, datetime, email, enum. min/max are numbers, dates or (for text types) character lengths. allowed is pipe-separated. Blank severity = error; blank owner = To be baselined · owner: Data owner. YAML: the subset in references/odcs-subset.md is parsed with the repo's YAML subset parser; anything outside it is listed as not evaluated, never silently passed.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Get the contract from the data owner; if none exists, start from assets/contract-template.csv and have the owner sign off each row (severity and owner especially).
  3. If the extract may hold personal data, run pii-data-inventory first; examples here are truncated but still real values.
  4. Run the agent. scripts/validate_contract.py checks every rule in references/rules.md and profiles every column.
  5. Read the Verdict. FAIL (exit 1): send each error row to its owner; fix at source and re-run — never edit the outputs.
  6. Review warnings and extra_column rows with the Data owner: add the column to the contract or drop it from the feed.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • violations.csv — column, rule, severity, failing_rows, failing_rate, examples, owner, expectation; errors first.
  • profile.csv — column, inferred_type, null_rate, distinct, min, max (min/max for numeric and date-like columns only).
  • contract-report.md — Summary, Verdict, Violations, Profile, Method.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every violation names an owner or To be baselined · owner: Data owner
  • [ ] No more than 3 examples per violation, each ≤ 40 characters; no text values in the profile
  • [ ] Freshness used the supplied as-of date, or is marked TBD — never today's date
  • [ ] YAML terms outside the subset are listed as not evaluated
  • [ ] Each output passes --verify; an error-severity violation exits 1
  • [ ] Limits stated: one extract, not a statistical guarantee

References

  • references/rules.md — rules, denominators, type parsing, sensitivity handling, limits
  • references/odcs-subset.md — ODCS v3 YAML mapping and what is not evaluated
  • references/sources.md — ODCS sources checked 2026-10-18
