2. **Plan.** Stage table (from `references/pipeline-stages.md`): stage → trigger → job → required check name → secrets. For fixes: failing step → root cause hypothesis → minimal change. Post; wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Build.** Read the repo first (flavour, deploy target, existing workflows — table above). Copy/merge `assets/workflows/ci.yml`, and `preview.yml`/`prod.yml` only when Vercel is the deploy target; never overwrite a customised workflow — diff and merge, or hand the team `ci-additions.yml`. Confirm every `npm run <script>` exists. Fill the env/secret matrix from `references/env-promotion.md`; list `gh secret set` commands (values never in chat).
4. **Branch protection.** Required checks = `ci / lint-typecheck-test`, `ci / rls-lint`, `preview / e2e`. Commands in `project-bootstrap/references/branch-rules.md`.
5. **Test.** Validate YAML (`python3 -c "import yaml"`-free: open each file; check `on:`/`jobs:`), run `act` if available or push a `chore/ci` branch and watch the run; confirm check names match protection. *(gate: build→test)*
6. **Prod path.** Walk `references/env-promotion.md`: GitHub Environments `staging` and `production` (required reviewers on production), tag → migrate staging → migrate prod → deploy → smoke → release. Dry-run with a `v0.0.0-rc` tag against staging only if the user approves.
7. **Rollback.** Install `references/rollback.md` as `docs/runbooks/rollback.md`; confirm the previous deployment is promotable (`vercel rollback` or Vercel "Instant Rollback") and the migration revert path exists.
8. **Verify.** One PR shows green `ci` + `preview` and a comment with the preview URL; one tag (rc) runs `prod.yml` to the staging gate. *(gate: test→verify)*
9. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Workflows | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `preview.yml`, `prod.yml` |
| Env/secret matrix | `docs/ci-cd.md` §Environments (from `references/env-promotion.md`) |
| Rollback runbook | `docs/runbooks/rollback.md` |
| Branch-protection commands | chat |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every stage has a required-check name that matches branch protection
- [ ] Secrets only via GitHub secrets / Vercel env; none echoed in logs (`::add-mask::` where derived)
- [ ] `concurrency` set on every workflow; prod never cancels in progress
- [ ] Prod deploy only from tag on `main`; verified by `git merge-base`
- [ ] Migrations run before deploy, staging before prod, with the production Environment gate
- [ ] Smoke hits `/api/health` and `/api/health/deep` after deploy
- [ ] Rollback runbook tested once (previous deployment promoted)

## References
- `references/pipeline-stages.md` — stages, jobs, check names, caching, timeouts
- `references/env-promotion.md` — environment matrix, secrets, promotion flow, Vercel settings
- `references/rollback.md` — code and migration rollback procedures, decision table
- `references/troubleshooting.md` — common failures and fixes
- `assets/workflows/ci.yml`, `assets/workflows/preview.yml`, `assets/workflows/prod.yml`
- `scripts/install_ci.py` — read-before-write installer: detects flavour and deploy target, writes absent workflows (Vercel deploy workflows only for Vercel targets), keeps existing ones, proposes missing standard jobs as `<name>-additions.yml`, validates `on:`/`jobs:`; atomic, exit 1 only on conflict

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/ci-cd-vercel-github --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/ci-cd-vercel-github`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. A kept (customised) workflow that lacks a standard job gives `gate: NEEDS-MERGE` (exit 0) and `.github/<name>-additions.yml` to merge by hand — branch protection depends on those check names, so do not call CI done until the Standard-jobs table is all `present`. name: code-review-runner
description: Use when a diff, branch or PR needs a first-pass review before a human or model reads it — "review this diff", "anything blocking in this PR", "check this change before merge", "did I leave secrets or debug prints in". bodyHtml:
code-review-runner

Wraps code-review from mattpocock/skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). Upstream reviews a change on two separate axes — Standards and Spec — with a Fowler smell baseline as judgement calls. This skill makes the deterministic part of the Standards axis executable and hands the upstream instructions to the optional narrative step by path (../../../vendor/code-review/SKILL.md), never by copy.

In a conversation: review the change now

Never

  • Never BLOCK for a warning or info finding: the verdict is BLOCK only if at least one finding has severity blocking; otherwise PASS (warnings and info are listed under Non-blocking). console.log is CR-DEBUG = warning; an owner-less TODO is CR-TODO = info (unless team rules override).
  • Never flag removed (-) or context ( ) lines, and never flag CR-DEBUG inside a test file (__tests__/, tests/, *.test.ts, test_*.py, …).
  • Never print a full secret: evidence keeps the first 4 characters + [redacted] (e.g. AKIA[redacted]).
  • Never "just approve": a blocking finding fails the gate (exit 1) regardless of deadline.

Procedure (from scripts/review.py; work line by line through the supplied diff)

  1. Parse: per file, status (added if --- /dev/null, else modified), hunks, added lines with new-file line numbers — the @@ … +N start is line N; each context or + line advances the counter, - lines do not.
  2. Detect on added lines only — blocking: CR-SECRET (key/token literals, password|secret|token|api_key = "<literal ≥8>", high-entropy literal ≥ 20 chars at ≥ 4.0 bits/char), CR-EVAL (eval(/exec(/new Function(), CR-TLS (verify=False, rejectUnauthorized: false, CERT_NONE, curl -k…), CR-SQL-CONCAT (SQL keyword text built with +, f-string, ${}, %, .format(); warning: CR-SWALLOW (except: pass, empty catch {}), CR-DEBUG (non-test files: console.log/debug/trace, debugger, print( in .py, pdb, System.out.println); info: CR-TODO (TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK not followed by (name), @name, [ABC-12], (#12)), CR-DUP (same ≥3-line added block twice); warning: CR-NO-TESTS when source code files changed and no test file changed.
  3. Team rules (rules CSV) after the built-ins: a built-in rule_id with empty pattern overrides its severity (off disables) — e.g. CR-TODO,,warning makes the TODO a warning, CR-NO-TESTS,,blocking only bites if no test changed; other rows are custom regex rules on added lines (filtered by file_glob).
  4. Sort blocking → warning → info, then file, line; number F01, F02 …. Counts per severity.
  5. Verdict: BLOCK if blocking count > 0 (script exits 1, outputs still written, --gate review.json fails); else PASS (exit 0).

Reply layout: first a working table — one row per added line that hits a detector (file:line, text, rule, severity) and the test check (source files changed, test files changed) — then Verdict: **PASS** or Verdict: **BLOCK** — "N blocking, N warning, N info.", then the review.md sections: Summary (files (source/test), hunks, lines added / removed, size vs 400, risky paths), Blocking, Non-blocking, Tests ("Test verdict: tests changed" / "MISSING" / "no source change", listing source and test files), Files. Each finding row: id, file:line, rule, severity, finding, evidence, fix.

  • Name the run: python3 -I scripts/review.py --diff <change.patch> [--rules <rules.csv>] --json review.json --md review.md, then python3 -I scripts/review.py --gate review.json; outputs review.json and review.md (and review-two-axis.md only with narrative=true).
  • The request says a diff, PR, team rules or spec is here but its text is not in the conversation: still write the review skeleton now — the five sections with their headings, the detector checklist above that will run on the added lines, the Tests line, and Verdict: To be baselined · owner: author, from the diff. With team rules: state they are applied after the built-ins (custom regex rules; a built-in id with empty pattern overrides its severity, e.g. CR-TODO raised to warning or CR-NO-TESTS made blocking) and record each override. With a narrative request: lay out the two-axis review (Standards from the findings, Spec from the issue/spec, kept separate, then Summary) per assets/two-axis-review-template.md and the upstream method. End with one line asking for the unified diff (git diff <base>...HEAD > change.patch). Never print a PASS verdict or invent findings for code you have not seen.
  • Nothing to review ("review my PR" with no diff): ask once for the unified diff (and, optionally, the team rules CSV and the spec). Do not review an imagined change.
  • Asked to "just approve it" or skip the review to merge today: decline in one line — approval without the review is not given, and a blocking finding (secret, eval, disabled TLS, SQL built by concatenation) fails the gate regardless of deadline. Run or lay out the review as above; offer the fastest defensible path: fix the blocking rows, re-run, merge on PASS.

Starting points

  • New — a diff that adds new files is reviewed on its added lines: standards findings, test verdict, verdict.
  • Existing — a change to code that already exists is reviewed together with your team's own rules file (custom regex rules and severity overrides), so the verdict follows the team's bar, not only the built-in one.

When to use

  • Before merge: a quick, repeatable pass that catches the mechanical defects first.
  • In CI: review.py --gate review.json as a required check.
  • NOT for: threat modelling and authz reasoning (security-review), stack-specific conventions (nextjs-enterprise-conventions), fixing what it finds (safe-fix).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
diffyesUnified diff, three-dot against the merge base. Only added lines are scanned.
rulesnoTeam rules CSV (assets/rules-template.csv): rule_id,pattern,severity,message,file_glob. A built-in id with empty pattern overrides its severity (off disables).
specnoIssue or spec text for the Spec axis of the narrative step. Without it the Spec axis reports "no spec available".
narrativenotrue runs the LLM step that writes the two-axis review.

Procedure

  1. Parse the diff (scripts/review.py): files, status, hunks, added lines with new-file line numbers, removed-line counts.
  2. Stats: files, hunks, +/-, size label (--large-change, default 400 changed lines), source vs test files, risky paths (auth, migrations, config, CI, env).
  3. Detect on added lines: CR-SECRET, CR-EVAL, CR-TLS, CR-SQL-CONCAT (blocking); CR-SWALLOW, CR-DEBUG, CR-NO-TESTS (warning); CR-TODO, CR-DUP (info). See references/review-rules.md.
  4. Apply team rules from the rules CSV; sort findings blocking → info, number F01….
  5. Write review.json and review.md; exit 1 if anything is blocking.
  6. Gate: review.py --gate review.json is the output check that fails the run on blocking findings.
  7. Optional: with narrative=true the LLM fills assets/two-axis-review-template.md — Standards (from the findings) and Spec (from spec) kept separate, per the upstream method.

Output

  • review.json — stats, files, tests verdict, counts, verdict (PASS/BLOCK), findings {id, rule, severity, file, line, evidence, message, fix}; secrets redacted in evidence.
  • review.md — Summary, Blocking, Non-blocking, Tests, Files.
  • review-two-axis.md (only with narrative=true).

Self-check

  • [ ] Every finding has file:line, rule and severity; evidence never shows a full secret
  • [ ] Only added lines were scanned; context and removed lines produce no findings
  • [ ] Blocking findings fail the run through the gate check
  • [ ] The Tests section states whether tests changed alongside source
  • [ ] The Spec axis is not claimed by the script; it is the narrative step's job and needs a spec

References

  • references/review-rules.md — detector rules, severities, false-positive notes, overrides
  • assets/rules-template.csv — team rules layout
  • assets/two-axis-review-template.md — narrative template for the optional LLM step
  • scripts/review.py — parser, detectors, renderer and gate (argparse; stdlib)
  • Upstream method: vendor/code-review/SKILL.md

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/code-review-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/code-review-runner). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The script always writes both outputs; the gate check on review.json then fails the run (exit 1) when any blocking finding remains, so a blocking diff is reported, never waved through.

1. Parse: per file, status (added if `--- /dev/null`, else modified), hunks, added lines with new-file line numbers — the `@@ … +N` start is line N; each context or `+` line advances the counter, `-` lines do not.
2. Detect on added lines only — blocking: CR-SECRET (key/token literals, `password|secret|token|api_key = "<literal ≥8>"`, high-entropy literal ≥ 20 chars at ≥ 4.0 bits/char), CR-EVAL (`eval(`/`exec(`/`new Function(`), CR-TLS (`verify=False`, `rejectUnauthorized: false`, `CERT_NONE`, `curl -k`…), CR-SQL-CONCAT (SQL keyword text built with `+`, f-string, `${}`, `%`, `.format(`); warning: CR-SWALLOW (`except: pass`, empty `catch {}`), CR-DEBUG (non-test files: `console.log/debug/trace`, `debugger`, `print(` in .py, `pdb`, `System.out.println`); info: CR-TODO (TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK not followed by `(name)`, `@name`, `[ABC-12]`, `(#12)`), CR-DUP (same ≥3-line added block twice); warning: CR-NO-TESTS when source code files changed and **no** test file changed.
3. Team rules (`rules` CSV) after the built-ins: a built-in `rule_id` with empty pattern overrides its severity (`off` disables) — e.g. `CR-TODO,,warning` makes the TODO a warning, `CR-NO-TESTS,,blocking` only bites if no test changed; other rows are custom regex rules on added lines (filtered by `file_glob`).
4. Sort blocking → warning → info, then file, line; number F01, F02 …. Counts per severity.
5. Verdict: BLOCK if blocking count > 0 (script exits 1, outputs still written, `--gate review.json` fails); else PASS (exit 0).

**Reply layout**: first a working table — one row per added line that hits a detector (file:line, text, rule, severity) and the test check (source files changed, test files changed) — then `Verdict: **PASS**` or `Verdict: **BLOCK**` — "N blocking, N warning, N info.", then the `review.md` sections: **Summary** (files (source/test), hunks, lines added / removed, size vs 400, risky paths), **Blocking**, **Non-blocking**, **Tests** ("Test verdict: tests changed" / "MISSING" / "no source change", listing source and test files), **Files**. Each finding row: id, `file:line`, rule, severity, finding, evidence, fix.
- Name the run: `python3 -I scripts/review.py --diff <change.patch> [--rules <rules.csv>] --json review.json --md review.md`, then `python3 -I scripts/review.py --gate review.json`; outputs `review.json` and `review.md` (and `review-two-axis.md` only with `narrative=true`).
- **The request says a diff, PR, team rules or spec is here but its text is not in the conversation**: still write the review skeleton now — the five sections with their headings, the detector checklist above that will run on the added lines, the Tests line, and `Verdict: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: author, from the diff]`. With team rules: state they are applied after the built-ins (custom regex rules; a built-in id with empty pattern overrides its severity, e.g. CR-TODO raised to warning or CR-NO-TESTS made blocking) and record each override. With a narrative request: lay out the two-axis review (Standards from the findings, Spec from the issue/spec, kept separate, then Summary) per `assets/two-axis-review-template.md` and the upstream method. End with one line asking for the unified diff (`git diff <base>...HEAD > change.patch`). Never print a PASS verdict or invent findings for code you have not seen.
- **Nothing to review** ("review my PR" with no diff): ask once for the unified diff (and, optionally, the team rules CSV and the spec). Do not review an imagined change.
- **Asked to "just approve it" or skip the review to merge today**: decline in one line — approval without the review is not given, and a blocking finding (secret, eval, disabled TLS, SQL built by concatenation) fails the gate regardless of deadline. Run or lay out the review as above; offer the fastest defensible path: fix the blocking rows, re-run, merge on PASS.

## Starting points
- **New** — a diff that adds new files is reviewed on its added lines: standards findings, test verdict, verdict.
- **Existing** — a change to code that already exists is reviewed together with your team's own rules file (custom regex rules and severity overrides), so the verdict follows the team's bar, not only the built-in one.

## When to use
- Before merge: a quick, repeatable pass that catches the mechanical defects first.
- In CI: `review.py --gate review.json` as a required check.
- NOT for: threat modelling and authz reasoning (`security-review`), stack-specific conventions (`nextjs-enterprise-conventions`), fixing what it finds (`safe-fix`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `diff` | yes | Unified diff, three-dot against the merge base. Only added lines are scanned. |
| `rules` | no | Team rules CSV (`assets/rules-template.csv`): `rule_id,pattern,severity,message,file_glob`. A built-in id with empty pattern overrides its severity (`off` disables). |
| `spec` | no | Issue or spec text for the Spec axis of the narrative step. Without it the Spec axis reports "no spec available". |
| `narrative` | no | `true` runs the LLM step that writes the two-axis review. |

## Procedure
1. **Parse the diff** (`scripts/review.py`): files, status, hunks, added lines with new-file line numbers, removed-line counts.
2. **Stats**: files, hunks, +/-, size label (`--large-change`, default 400 changed lines), source vs test files, risky paths (auth, migrations, config, CI, env).
3. **Detect** on added lines: CR-SECRET, CR-EVAL, CR-TLS, CR-SQL-CONCAT (blocking); CR-SWALLOW, CR-DEBUG, CR-NO-TESTS (warning); CR-TODO, CR-DUP (info). See `references/review-rules.md`.
4. **Apply team rules** from the rules CSV; sort findings blocking → info, number F01….
5. **Write** `review.json` and `review.md`; exit 1 if anything is blocking.
6. **Gate**: `review.py --gate review.json` is the output check that fails the run on blocking findings.
7. Optional: with `narrative=true` the LLM fills `assets/two-axis-review-template.md` — Standards (from the findings) and Spec (from `spec`) kept separate, per the upstream method.

## Output
- `review.json` — stats, files, tests verdict, counts, verdict (PASS/BLOCK), findings `{id, rule, severity, file, line, evidence, message, fix}`; secrets redacted in evidence.
- `review.md` — Summary, Blocking, Non-blocking, Tests, Files.
- `review-two-axis.md` (only with `narrative=true`).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every finding has file:line, rule and severity; evidence never shows a full secret
- [ ] Only added lines were scanned; context and removed lines produce no findings
- [ ] Blocking findings fail the run through the gate check
- [ ] The Tests section states whether tests changed alongside source
- [ ] The Spec axis is not claimed by the script; it is the narrative step's job and needs a spec

## References
- `references/review-rules.md` — detector rules, severities, false-positive notes, overrides
- `assets/rules-template.csv` — team rules layout
- `assets/two-axis-review-template.md` — narrative template for the optional LLM step
- `scripts/review.py` — parser, detectors, renderer and gate (argparse; stdlib)
- Upstream method: `vendor/code-review/SKILL.md`

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/code-review-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/code-review-runner`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The script always writes both outputs; the gate check on `review.json` then fails the run (exit 1) when any blocking finding remains, so a blocking diff is reported, never waved through.

bodyHtml:
domain-modeling-runner

Wraps domain-modeling from mattpocock/skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). Upstream is a conversational discipline — challenge terms against the glossary, sharpen fuzzy language, stress-test relationships with scenarios, record hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs. This skill makes the checkable part deterministic (structure, identifiers, cardinalities, glossary gaps, invariants) and passes the upstream instructions and its glossary/ADR formats to the optional review step by path (../../../vendor/domain-modeling/SKILL.md), never by copy.

In a conversation: write the model now

  • Entities, relationships and glossary are stated in the conversation (CSV text or plain sentences): write model.md in this reply in this order — Diagram (Mermaid erDiagram with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases 1 to 0+ for 1:N, 1 to 1, 0+ to 0+), Entities, Relationships, Invariants (a checklist to confirm: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs), Glossary (**Term**: definition, _Avoid_: synonyms; supplied definitions kept word for word; any entity without one gets To be baselined · owner: Domain expert), Open questions (every error and warning, owned by the domain expert). An N:M relationship is drawn through its join entity (e.g. Enrollment between Student and Course).
  • Validate before drawing: errors E1–E6 — relationship endpoint not a defined entity, entity without identifier, cardinality not 1:1/1:N/N:M (e.g. many), N:M without join: <Entity>, duplicate attribute, bad required value; warnings W1–W3 — orphan entity, term without definition, glossary term that is not an entity. Any error means the run fails: say so on line 1, leave invalid relationships out of the diagram, and list each error under Open questions. Never add an undefined entity (e.g. an Instructor that has no entity rows) to make a relationship valid.
  • Existing model plus revised files: compare and list what is added, removed or changed (entities, attributes, required, type changes); every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.
  • The request says files are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: still write every section now from whatever the request states, with each entity, attribute, cardinality or definition not given shown as To be baselined · owner to be named naming the file it comes from (entities CSV, relationships CSV, glossary CSV, baseline model.json). With a review request, also lay out the modeling review per assets/modeling-review-template.md — Challenged terms, Edge-case scenarios, Invariants to confirm, ADR candidates — per the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for files.
  • Relationships entirely missing (entities only, "draw the ER diagram"): ask once for the relationships (from,to,cardinality,name[,notes]) instead of guessing how entities relate; definitions and cardinalities are never invented.

Starting points

  • New — entities, relationships and glossary become a validated model: Mermaid ER diagram, invariants, glossary, open questions.
  • Existing — add baseline (the model.json of today's model): the proposed model is validated the same way and compared with it — what is added, removed or changed — and every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.

When to use

  • Before schema, API or event design: get entities, keys and cardinalities agreed.
  • When terms drift ("account" vs "customer"): build the glossary and see which terms lack a definition.
  • NOT for: SQL migrations and RLS (supabase-schema-rls), tenancy audits (multi-tenant-saas-patterns), product requirements (product-spec-prd).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
entitiesyesOne row per attribute: entity,attribute,type,required,notes. Mark the identifier with an id / <entity>_id name or PK in notes; FK in notes marks a foreign key.
relationshipsyesfrom,to,cardinality,name[,notes]; cardinality 1:1, 1:N, N:M; N:M needs join: <Entity> in notes.
glossarynoterm,definition[,avoid]. Entities without a definition get To be baselined · owner: Domain expert.
titlenoBounded-context name (default "Domain model").
narrativenotrue runs the LLM modeling review.

Procedure

  1. Read the CSVs (scripts/model.py); missing columns or files → exit 2 naming them.
  2. Validate (errors E1–E6): undefined relationship endpoints, entities without identifier, bad cardinality, N:M without join, duplicate attributes, bad required values. Warn (W1–W3): orphan entities (join entities count as linked), terms without definitions, glossary terms that are not entities.
  3. Render the diagram: Mermaid erDiagram with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases (1 to 0+ for 1:N, 1 to 1, 0+ to 0+). Invalid relationships are left out of the diagram.
  4. Derive invariants: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs — as a checklist to confirm, not as facts.
  5. Glossary in the upstream GLOSSARY format (**Term**: definition, _Avoid_: synonyms).
  6. Open questions: every error and warning, owned by the domain expert.
  7. Optional: with narrative=true the LLM fills assets/modeling-review-template.md.

Output

  • model.md — Diagram, Entities, Relationships, Invariants, Glossary, Open questions.
  • model.json — entities, relationships, glossary, invariants, errors, warnings; model.py --check fails on errors or undefined endpoints.
  • modeling-review.md (only with narrative=true).

Self-check

  • [ ] Every relationship endpoint is a defined entity; every entity has an identifier
  • [ ] Every N:M names its join; every cardinality is 1:1, 1:N or N:M
  • [ ] The Mermaid block parses; invalid relationships are not drawn
  • [ ] No definition was invented: missing ones carry To be baselined · owner: Domain expert
  • [ ] Invariants are presented as a checklist to confirm

References

  • references/modeling-rules.md — validation rules, Mermaid mapping, invariant derivation

- **Entities, relationships and glossary are stated in the conversation** (CSV text or plain sentences): write `model.md` **in this reply** in this order — Diagram (Mermaid `erDiagram` with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases `1 to 0+` for 1:N, `1 to 1`, `0+ to 0+`), Entities, Relationships, Invariants (a checklist to confirm: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs), Glossary (`**Term**:` definition, `_Avoid_:` synonyms; supplied definitions kept word for word; any entity without one gets `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`), Open questions (every error and warning, owned by the domain expert). An N:M relationship is drawn through its join entity (e.g. Enrollment between Student and Course).
- **Validate before drawing**: errors E1–E6 — relationship endpoint not a defined entity, entity without identifier, cardinality not `1:1`/`1:N`/`N:M` (e.g. `many`), N:M without `join: <Entity>`, duplicate attribute, bad `required` value; warnings W1–W3 — orphan entity, term without definition, glossary term that is not an entity. Any error means the run fails: say so on line 1, leave invalid relationships out of the diagram, and list each error under Open questions. Never add an undefined entity (e.g. an Instructor that has no entity rows) to make a relationship valid.
- **Existing model plus revised files**: compare and list what is added, removed or changed (entities, attributes, `required`, type changes); every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.
- **The request says files are attached but their contents are not in the conversation**: still write every section now from whatever the request states, with each entity, attribute, cardinality or definition not given shown as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the file it comes from (entities CSV, relationships CSV, glossary CSV, baseline `model.json`). With a review request, also lay out the modeling review per `assets/modeling-review-template.md` — Challenged terms, Edge-case scenarios, Invariants to confirm, ADR candidates — per the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for files.
- **Relationships entirely missing** (entities only, "draw the ER diagram"): ask once for the relationships (`from,to,cardinality,name[,notes]`) instead of guessing how entities relate; definitions and cardinalities are never invented.

## Starting points
- **New** — entities, relationships and glossary become a validated model: Mermaid ER diagram, invariants, glossary, open questions.
- **Existing** — add `baseline` (the `model.json` of today's model): the proposed model is validated the same way and compared with it — what is added, removed or changed — and every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.

## When to use
- Before schema, API or event design: get entities, keys and cardinalities agreed.
- When terms drift ("account" vs "customer"): build the glossary and see which terms lack a definition.
- NOT for: SQL migrations and RLS (`supabase-schema-rls`), tenancy audits (`multi-tenant-saas-patterns`), product requirements (`product-spec-prd`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `entities` | yes | One row per attribute: `entity,attribute,type,required,notes`. Mark the identifier with an `id` / `<entity>_id` name or `PK` in notes; `FK` in notes marks a foreign key. |
| `relationships` | yes | `from,to,cardinality,name[,notes]`; cardinality `1:1`, `1:N`, `N:M`; N:M needs `join: <Entity>` in notes. |
| `glossary` | no | `term,definition[,avoid]`. Entities without a definition get `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`. |
| `title` | no | Bounded-context name (default "Domain model"). |
| `narrative` | no | `true` runs the LLM modeling review. |

## Procedure
1. **Read** the CSVs (`scripts/model.py`); missing columns or files → exit 2 naming them.
2. **Validate** (errors E1–E6): undefined relationship endpoints, entities without identifier, bad cardinality, N:M without join, duplicate attributes, bad `required` values. **Warn** (W1–W3): orphan entities (join entities count as linked), terms without definitions, glossary terms that are not entities.
3. **Render the diagram**: Mermaid `erDiagram` with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases (`1 to 0+` for 1:N, `1 to 1`, `0+ to 0+`). Invalid relationships are left out of the diagram.
4. **Derive invariants**: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs — as a checklist to confirm, not as facts.
5. **Glossary** in the upstream GLOSSARY format (`**Term**:` definition, `_Avoid_:` synonyms).
6. **Open questions**: every error and warning, owned by the domain expert.
7. Optional: with `narrative=true` the LLM fills `assets/modeling-review-template.md`.

## Output
- `model.md` — Diagram, Entities, Relationships, Invariants, Glossary, Open questions.
- `model.json` — entities, relationships, glossary, invariants, errors, warnings; `model.py --check` fails on errors or undefined endpoints.
- `modeling-review.md` (only with `narrative=true`).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every relationship endpoint is a defined entity; every entity has an identifier
- [ ] Every N:M names its join; every cardinality is 1:1, 1:N or N:M
- [ ] The Mermaid block parses; invalid relationships are not drawn
- [ ] No definition was invented: missing ones carry `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`
- [ ] Invariants are presented as a checklist to confirm

## References
- `references/modeling-rules.md` — validation rules, Mermaid mapping, invariant derivation
- `assets/entities-template.csv`, `assets/relationships-template.csv`, `assets/glossary-template.csv` — input layouts
- `assets/modeling-review-template.md` — narrative template for the optional LLM step
- `scripts/model.py` — validator, renderer and contract check (argparse; stdlib)
- Upstream method: `vendor/domain-modeling/` (SKILL.md, GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md, ADR-FORMAT.md)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/domain-modeling-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/domain-modeling-runner`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Validation errors fail the run (exit 1) but both outputs are still written, so the gaps are listed under Open questions.

multi-tenant-saas-patterns

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/multi-tenant-saas-patterns --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/multi-tenant-saas-patterns). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The audit step exits 1 when a non-exempt table lacks tenant_id, RLS or a tenant-leading index; hand the findings and policies.sql to supabase-schema-rls for the migration.

Starting points

  • New — your first migration is audited for tenant_id, RLS, policies and a tenant-leading index, and RLS policies are generated from the starter RBAC matrix.
  • Existing — your whole migrations folder is replayed in order (columns and keys added later by alter table, tables dropped later), each table that still exists is audited, your own RBAC matrix is cross-checked against those tables, and policies are generated from it.

When to use

  • "Add organisations/workspaces", "who can do what", "plans and limits", "feature flags per customer", "audit trail", "invite users", "switch tenant".
  • Before the first migration of a multi-tenant app; before adding billing.
  • NOT for: writing the SQL (supabase-schema-rls does that from this design), security verification (security-review), single-tenant apps.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Tenant concept (org / workspace / account) and whether users belong to manyyesuser — ask once
Roles needed and the actions that matter (≤ 20 actions)yesdocs/SPEC.md / user
Plans / tiers and the limits/features that differyes if billinguser
Compliance needs for audit (retention, immutability, export)nouser; default 1 year, append-only
Existing schemayes if presentrepo

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md (Multi-tenant, Auth rows) and ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Plan. Decide the four models with the user using references/tenant-model.md decision table: tenancy shape, membership, claims, invitation. Post a one-page design summary; wait for "go". (gate: plan→approve)
  3. Tenant model. Produce the table list (tenants, tenant_members, invitations), JWT claim strategy (app_metadata.tenant_id, role; refresh on switch), tenant-switch flow, and the requireUser() contract.
  4. RBAC matrix. Fill assets/rbac-matrix.csv (role × action → allow/deny/own) following references/rbac.md; define enforcement points: RLS (data), requireRole() (actions), UI (hide only). Each action maps to a policy and a service check.
  5. Plans and feature flags. From references/plans-and-flags.md: plans, tenant_subscriptions, tenant_features (overrides), entitlements resolution order, limit checks in services (not UI), flag naming feature.<name>.
  6. Audit log. From references/audit-log.md: audit_log table (append-only, RLS read by admin, no update/delete), app.audit_row() trigger, application-level events for non-row actions, retention and export.
  7. Hand off to build. Produce the migration task list for supabase-schema-rls and the service/action list for nextjs-enterprise-conventions; include negative tests for test-strategy-tdd. (gate: build via those skills → test)
  8. Verify. Walk the checklist: every tenant table has tenant_id + RLS; every RBAC action has an enforcement point; every limit is checked in a service; every sensitive action is audited. (gate: verify)

# multi-tenant-saas-patterns

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/multi-tenant-saas-patterns --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/multi-tenant-saas-patterns`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The audit step exits 1 when a non-exempt table lacks tenant_id, RLS or a tenant-leading index; hand the findings and `policies.sql` to supabase-schema-rls for the migration.

## Starting points
- **New** — your first migration is audited for tenant_id, RLS, policies and a tenant-leading index, and RLS policies are generated from the starter RBAC matrix.
- **Existing** — your whole migrations folder is replayed in order (columns and keys added later by `alter table`, tables dropped later), each table that still exists is audited, your own RBAC matrix is cross-checked against those tables, and policies are generated from it.

## When to use
- "Add organisations/workspaces", "who can do what", "plans and limits", "feature flags per customer", "audit trail", "invite users", "switch tenant".
- Before the first migration of a multi-tenant app; before adding billing.
- NOT for: writing the SQL (`supabase-schema-rls` does that from this design), security verification (`security-review`), single-tenant apps.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tenant concept (org / workspace / account) and whether users belong to many | yes | user — ask once |
| Roles needed and the actions that matter (≤ 20 actions) | yes | `docs/SPEC.md` / user |
| Plans / tiers and the limits/features that differ | yes if billing | user |
| Compliance needs for audit (retention, immutability, export) | no | user; default 1 year, append-only |
| Existing schema | yes if present | repo |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` (Multi-tenant, Auth rows) and `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. **Plan.** Decide the four models with the user using `references/tenant-model.md` decision table: tenancy shape, membership, claims, invitation. Post a one-page design summary; wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Tenant model.** Produce the table list (tenants, tenant_members, invitations), JWT claim strategy (`app_metadata.tenant_id`, `role`; refresh on switch), tenant-switch flow, and the `requireUser()` contract.
4. **RBAC matrix.** Fill `assets/rbac-matrix.csv` (role × action → allow/deny/own) following `references/rbac.md`; define enforcement points: RLS (data), `requireRole()` (actions), UI (hide only). Each action maps to a policy and a service check.
5. **Plans and feature flags.** From `references/plans-and-flags.md`: `plans`, `tenant_subscriptions`, `tenant_features` (overrides), `entitlements` resolution order, limit checks in services (not UI), flag naming `feature.<name>`.
6. **Audit log.** From `references/audit-log.md`: `audit_log` table (append-only, RLS read by admin, no update/delete), `app.audit_row()` trigger, application-level events for non-row actions, retention and export.
7. **Hand off to build.** Produce the migration task list for `supabase-schema-rls` and the service/action list for `nextjs-enterprise-conventions`; include negative tests for `test-strategy-tdd`. *(gate: build via those skills → test)*
8. **Verify.** Walk the checklist: every tenant table has `tenant_id` + RLS; every RBAC action has an enforcement point; every limit is checked in a service; every sensitive action is audited. *(gate: verify)*
9. Record decisions as ADRs (`project-bootstrap/assets/adr-template.md`); update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Design doc | `docs/tenancy.md` (tenant model, claims, flows) |
| RBAC matrix | `docs/rbac-matrix.csv` (from `assets/rbac-matrix.csv`) |
| Plans/flags design | `docs/tenancy.md` §Plans |
| Audit design | `docs/tenancy.md` §Audit |
| ADRs | `docs/adr/NNNN-tenancy.md`, `NNNN-rbac.md` |
| Build task list | for `supabase-schema-rls` / `nextjs-enterprise-conventions` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Tenant id comes only from the JWT (`app_metadata`), never from client input
- [ ] Role change or tenant switch forces a token refresh; stale-claim window stated
- [ ] RBAC matrix: every action has RLS + service enforcement; UI is hide-only
- [ ] Limits enforced in services with a `Result` error code (`PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED`)
- [ ] Audit log append-only; actor, tenant, entity, action, before/after, requestId
- [ ] Cross-tenant unique constraints scoped by `tenant_id`
- [ ] Deleting a tenant: cascade plan + export + retention stated

## References
- `references/tenant-model.md` — tenancy shapes, membership, claims, invitation and switch flows, deletion
- `references/rbac.md` — role design, matrix method, enforcement points, testing
- `references/plans-and-flags.md` — plans, entitlements, overrides, flag lifecycle
- `references/audit-log.md` — schema, trigger, app events, retention, access
- `assets/rbac-matrix.csv` — starter matrix
- `assets/tenancy-schema.sql` — reference DDL for the core tables (hand to supabase-schema-rls)
- `scripts/tenancy_audit.py` — migrations → tenant_id / RLS / leading-index audit (exit 1 on findings); `scripts/rbac_to_sql.py` — matrix → policies.sql

card: Next.js code checked against enterprise conventions
name: nextjs-enterprise-conventions
description: Use whenever writing, adding or reviewing Next.js (App Router) / React / TypeScript code in this stack — "add a form page under app/… with a server action", "build this page/component/route handler", "review this component", "make this follow our conventions", or a component that queries Supabase inside useEffect or console.logs data. Enforces server/client component rules, data-access layering (lib/db, server/services, server/actions), zod at boundaries, the typed Result<T,E> error pattern, structured logging, folder and naming conventions from shared/stack-conventions.md, and Vercel's react/next best-practice skills when installed. Produces compliant code plus a conventions checklist result (rule → pass/fail → file:line). Do not use for planning a multi-file feature before coding (spec-to-plan), fixing a reported bug with a repro (safe-fix), schema (supabase-schema-rls) or security audits (security-review).

bodyHtml:
nextjs-enterprise-conventions

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/nextjs-enterprise-conventions --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/nextjs-enterprise-conventions). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The lint step exits 1 on any high-severity finding, so a non-compliant repo fails the run by design; fix the findings in code, then re-run.

Starting points

  • New — a new repo is linted against every convention; any high-severity finding fails the gate.
  • Existing — add baseline (the findings.csv of an earlier run): each finding is marked known or new, the gate fails only on new high-severity findings, known debt stays listed, and baseline items no longer found are reported as resolved.

When to use

  • Any new or modified file under app/, components/, lib/, server/.
  • "Review this component", "is this the right place for this query", "add a server action", "add a page".
  • Invoked by spec-to-plan tasks and safe-fix when the diff touches Next.js code.
  • NOT for: schema/RLS (supabase-schema-rls), security audit (security-review), tests design (test-strategy-tdd).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
The task or diffyesuser / plan
Repo (CLAUDE.md, lib/, server/, existing patterns)yesrepo
Next.js major version (package.json)yesrepo

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md and ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md. Read package.json for the Next.js version and existing lib/result.ts, lib/logger.ts, lib/env.ts — reuse, never duplicate.
  2. Plan. For a new feature slice, list files by layer (validator → service → action/route → component → page) with the server/client decision per component. For a review, list the files and the rule IDs you will check. Wait for "go" on anything touching >3 files. (gate: plan→approve)
  3. Framework rules. If the upstream skills vercel-react-best-practices and vercel-composition-patterns are installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke them for this step; otherwise follow references/framework-rules.md (server/client boundaries, caching, data fetching, server actions, routing).
  4. Layering and errors. Apply references/layering.md (what lives where, import direction) and references/error-result-pattern.md (Result<T,E>, error codes, no throws across the boundary).
  5. Logging. Apply references/logging.md: lib/logger only, correlation id from headers, no PII, no console.log.
  6. Build. Write code in minimal diffs. Each server action: zod parse → auth/tenant check → service call → Result → typed response. Each component: server by default; "use client" only for interactivity, with the reason in a comment.
  7. Test. Unit for validators/services; component tests for client components with logic; e2e for the page path. Run lint, typecheck, full unit suite. (gate: build→test)
  8. Verify. Walk references/conventions-checklist.md; report as a table (rule → pass/fail/n.a. → file:line). Fix fails before returning. (gate: test→verify)
  9. Update docs/HANDOFF.md.

Output

ArtifactForm
Codeminimal diffs in the layered locations
Conventions tablechat: rule → status → location
Teststests/unit/**, tests/e2e/**

Self-check

  • [ ] No Supabase call outside lib/db / server/services
  • [ ] Every server action and route handler parses input with zod and checks auth before work
  • [ ] Services return Result<T,E>; no throw crosses server→client; errors have stable codes
  • [ ] "use client" only where needed, with reason; no secrets or server-only imports in client files
  • [ ] Logs structured via lib/logger, with requestId; no console.log, no PII
  • [ ] Names and folders match shared/stack-conventions.md
  • [ ] lint + typecheck + unit green; e2e for touched pages

References

  • references/framework-rules.md — server/client components, caching, fetching, actions, routing (fallback for Vercel skills)
  • references/layering.md — folder/layer rules, import direction, naming
  • references/error-result-pattern.md — Result<T,E>, error codes, boundary mapping
  • references/logging.md — log schema, correlation id, redaction
  • references/conventions-checklist.md — rule table used in verify

# nextjs-enterprise-conventions

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/nextjs-enterprise-conventions --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/nextjs-enterprise-conventions`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The lint step exits 1 on any high-severity finding, so a non-compliant repo fails the run by design; fix the findings in code, then re-run.

## Starting points
- **New** — a new repo is linted against every convention; any high-severity finding fails the gate.
- **Existing** — add `baseline` (the `findings.csv` of an earlier run): each finding is marked known or new, the gate fails only on new high-severity findings, known debt stays listed, and baseline items no longer found are reported as resolved.

## When to use
- Any new or modified file under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `server/`.
- "Review this component", "is this the right place for this query", "add a server action", "add a page".
- Invoked by `spec-to-plan` tasks and `safe-fix` when the diff touches Next.js code.
- NOT for: schema/RLS (`supabase-schema-rls`), security audit (`security-review`), tests design (`test-strategy-tdd`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The task or diff | yes | user / plan |
| Repo (`CLAUDE.md`, `lib/`, `server/`, existing patterns) | yes | repo |
| Next.js major version (`package.json`) | yes | repo |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` and `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`. Read `package.json` for the Next.js version and existing `lib/result.ts`, `lib/logger.ts`, `lib/env.ts` — reuse, never duplicate.
2. **Plan.** For a new feature slice, list files by layer (validator → service → action/route → component → page) with the server/client decision per component. For a review, list the files and the rule IDs you will check. Wait for "go" on anything touching >3 files. *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Framework rules.** If the upstream skills `vercel-react-best-practices` and `vercel-composition-patterns` are installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke them for this step; otherwise follow `references/framework-rules.md` (server/client boundaries, caching, data fetching, server actions, routing).
4. **Layering and errors.** Apply `references/layering.md` (what lives where, import direction) and `references/error-result-pattern.md` (`Result<T,E>`, error codes, no throws across the boundary).
5. **Logging.** Apply `references/logging.md`: `lib/logger` only, correlation id from headers, no PII, no `console.log`.
6. **Build.** Write code in minimal diffs. Each server action: zod parse → auth/tenant check → service call → `Result` → typed response. Each component: server by default; `"use client"` only for interactivity, with the reason in a comment.
7. **Test.** Unit for validators/services; component tests for client components with logic; e2e for the page path. Run lint, typecheck, full unit suite. *(gate: build→test)*
8. **Verify.** Walk `references/conventions-checklist.md`; report as a table (rule → pass/fail/n.a. → file:line). Fix fails before returning. *(gate: test→verify)*
9. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Form |
|---|---|
| Code | minimal diffs in the layered locations |
| Conventions table | chat: rule → status → location |
| Tests | `tests/unit/**`, `tests/e2e/**` |

## Self-check
- [ ] No Supabase call outside `lib/db` / `server/services`
- [ ] Every server action and route handler parses input with zod and checks auth before work
- [ ] Services return `Result<T,E>`; no `throw` crosses server→client; errors have stable codes
- [ ] `"use client"` only where needed, with reason; no secrets or server-only imports in client files
- [ ] Logs structured via `lib/logger`, with `requestId`; no `console.log`, no PII
- [ ] Names and folders match `shared/stack-conventions.md`
- [ ] lint + typecheck + unit green; e2e for touched pages

## References
- `references/framework-rules.md` — server/client components, caching, fetching, actions, routing (fallback for Vercel skills)
- `references/layering.md` — folder/layer rules, import direction, naming
- `references/error-result-pattern.md` — `Result<T,E>`, error codes, boundary mapping
- `references/logging.md` — log schema, correlation id, redaction
- `references/conventions-checklist.md` — rule table used in verify
- `assets/result.ts`, `assets/server-action.example.ts`, `assets/service.example.ts` — starters
- `scripts/lint_conventions.py` — offline linter for NX1–NX5 (Supabase in components, console.log, zod at actions, service-role exposure, raw SQL); exit 1 on high findings

bodyHtml:
observability-setup

In a conversation: plan the setup now

  • The request asks for observability on this stack: answer in this reply, in order: (1) one list of questions, asked once — critical user journeys (≤5), error-tracking vendor (Sentry default) and DSN availability, notification channel — each with your default, then carry on with the defaults; (2) the plan table — component → file → add/change → why — covering logger, request context, error tracking, health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard, with a line that nothing changes until "go"; (3) logging: lib/logger.ts + lib/logger/context.ts (JSON fields ts, level, msg, service, env, requestId; redaction of email, token, password, authorization, cookie, key; requestId set in middleware.ts), console.* replaced in minimal diffs, ESLint no-console: error; (4) health: app/api/health/route.ts (liveness, no dependencies) and app/api/health/deep/route.ts (bearer-protected, ≤ 3 s timeout per dependency, 503 when one is down), with tests for both; (5) an alert table — alert → threshold → window → severity tier → runbook → owner → channel — and an SLO table per journey with an error-budget policy; (6) verification on preview: force a synthetic failure (deep health 503) and confirm the alert fires end to end, and confirm a test error reaches the tracker tagged with requestId. Thresholds and SLO targets the user has not given are To be baselined · owner to be named. Never reply with only a request for the repo.
  • Part of it already exists (e.g. "we already have Sentry"): open with an inventory of what is there (Sentry server/client/edge configs, global-error.tsx, tags, source maps) and state that it is kept as is; add only what was asked (e.g. health routes and alert rules); add requestId as a Sentry tag only if it is missing, as a minimal diff; touch the logger only if console.* calls are found.
  • Bare "add observability": ask once, in one list, for the critical journeys and the alert channel; meanwhile show the plan skeleton with every SLO target and alert threshold as To be baselined · owner to be named. Never invent SLO numbers.
  • Asked to replace an existing logger or config outright: decline the overwrite in one line (it loses the team's wiring) and propose the standard file beside it as a .proposed twin for a manual merge.

Starting points

  • New — point target at an empty folder: logger, health routes, alert rules, SLO doc and .env.example are written (TypeScript by default).
  • Existing — point target at your repo. Read before write: the language flavour is detected first (tsconfig.json or any .ts/.tsx under app|lib|components → TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript) and every file is emitted as .ts or .js to match — a JavaScript Next.js app gets lib/logger.js and route.js, never a .ts file. A file you already have, in either extension, is never overwritten and never gets a conflicting sibling (route.ts beside route.js is a Next.js routing conflict): an existing health route is reported exists, kept with a static gap table (exports GET? force-dynamic? no-store? liveness free of dependency calls?), another existing file in the same flavour gets a .proposed twin to merge, one in the other flavour is kept and pointed at the asset. Env vars are appended to .env.example only for files written in this run; every console.* call in your source is listed. A repo that already has every piece exits 0 with just the gap table; a repo that already holds a conflicting pair (route.js and route.ts) writes nothing, says why in the report, and exits 1.

When to use

  • First production release; after an incident with "we had no idea"; before an SLA commitment.
  • Adding a new service/edge function/job that has no logs or health signal.
  • NOT for: a specific bug (safe-fix), pipeline alerts (ci-cd-vercel-github).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Critical user journeys (≤5)yesdocs/SPEC.md / user — ask once
Error-tracking vendor decision (Sentry default) and DSN availabilityyesuser
Log sink (Vercel Log Drain target)nouser; default: vendor's drain
On-call / notification channelyesuser — ask once
Existing lib/logger.ts, health routesyesrepo

Missing facts do not stop the plan: use the stated defaults, mark thresholds and SLO targets To be baselined · owner to be named and ask once at the start. Never invent SLO numbers.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md (Logging, Errors rows) and ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md. Inventory what exists: language flavour (tsconfig.json / .ts source vs jsconfig.json / .js only), logger, Sentry, health routes in either extension, deploy platform (Vercel or AWS workflows), Next special files. Every file you add takes the repo's extension; never place a .ts route or module beside an existing .js one.
  2. Plan. Table of components to add/change: logger, request context, error tracking (server + client + edge), health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard, runbook links. Post; wait for "go". (gate: plan→approve)
  3. Logging. Install assets/logger.ts (or assets/logger.js in a JavaScript repo) as lib/logger.{ts,js} (+ lib/logger/context.{ts,js} AsyncLocalStorage) per references/log-schema.md; wire requestId in middleware.ts; ESLint no-console: error. Replace existing console.* in minimal diffs.
  4. Error tracking. Follow references/error-tracking.md: server, client, edge configs; requestId/tenantId tags; PII scrubbing; source maps in CI; error.tsx reporting.
  5. Health. Add assets/health-route.ts (or .js) as app/api/health/route.{ts,js} (liveness, no deps) and app/api/health/deep/route.{ts,js} (DB, auth, storage, queue; bearer-protected) per references/health-endpoints.md. If a health route already exists in either extension, keep it, verify it exports GET, and list what it is missing versus the standard (see the reference's brownfield table) instead of adding a sibling.
  6. Alerts + SLOs. From references/alerts-and-slos.md, fill assets/alert-rules.yaml for the chosen vendor and the SLO table for the critical journeys. Every alert has a runbook link and an owner.
  7. Test. Unit test logger redaction; integration test both health routes (200 / 503 on simulated DB failure); trigger a test error and confirm it appears in the tracker with requestId. Full unit suite green. (gate: build→test)
  8. Verify. Deploy to preview; curl both health routes; confirm Log Drain delivers JSON; confirm an alert fires on a synthetic failure (health 503). (gate: test→verify)
  9. Write docs/observability.md (schema, endpoints, alerts, dashboards, how to find a request by id). Update docs/HANDOFF.md.

Output

ArtifactPath
Loggerlib/logger.{ts,js}, lib/logger/context.{ts,js} (extension follows the repo)
Error trackingsentry.{server,client,edge}.config.ts (or vendor equivalent), app/global-error.tsx
Healthapp/api/health/route.{ts,js}, app/api/health/deep/route.{ts,js}
Alerts / SLOsops/alerts.yaml, docs/observability.md
Dashboard specdocs/observability.md §Dashboards

Self-check

  • [ ] Every log line has ts, level, msg, service, env; request-scoped lines have requestId
  • [ ] Redaction list covers email, token, password, authorization, cookie, key
  • [ ] Health liveness has zero dependencies; deep check is auth-protected and times out ≤ 3 s per dependency
  • [ ] Every added file matches the repo's flavour (.js in a JavaScript repo); no route or module exists in two extensions
  • [ ] Every alert: threshold, window, severity, runbook, owner, notification channel
  • [ ] SLOs defined for each critical journey with an error-budget policy
  • [ ] Synthetic failure produced an alert end-to-end
  • [ ] No PII reached the error tracker (checked a real event)

References

  • references/log-schema.md — fields, levels, redaction, request context
  • references/error-tracking.md — Sentry (default) wiring for server/client/edge, scrubbing, source maps
  • references/health-endpoints.md — liveness vs readiness vs deep; response contract
  • references/alerts-and-slos.md — alert catalogue, SLO starter, error-budget policy, dashboard panels
  • assets/logger.ts, assets/logger-context.ts, assets/health-route.ts, assets/health-deep-route.ts (+ the .js twins assets/logger.js, assets/logger-context.js, assets/health-route.js, assets/health-deep-route.js, functionally identical), assets/alert-rules.yaml
  • scripts/install.py — detects the flavour, installs the matching assets without overwriting or creating .ts/.js siblings (exists, kept + gap table for health routes, .proposed twins otherwise), appends env vars for written files to .env.example
  • scripts/check_siblings.py — fails when any route or module exists in two source extensions (used by the eval checks)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/observability-setup --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/observability-setup). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Existing files are never overwritten and never get a .ts/.js sibling: a health route that exists is kept and gap-checked, a differing file in the same flavour gets a .proposed twin listed in the report for a manual merge, and an existing conflicting pair aborts the run (exit 1, nothing written).

# observability-setup

## In a conversation: plan the setup now
- **The request asks for observability on this stack**: answer **in this reply**, in order: (1) one list of questions, asked once — critical user journeys (≤5), error-tracking vendor (Sentry default) and DSN availability, notification channel — each with your default, then carry on with the defaults; (2) the plan table — component → file → add/change → why — covering logger, request context, error tracking, health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard, with a line that nothing changes until "go"; (3) logging: `lib/logger.ts` + `lib/logger/context.ts` (JSON fields `ts, level, msg, service, env, requestId`; redaction of email, token, password, authorization, cookie, key; `requestId` set in `middleware.ts`), `console.*` replaced in minimal diffs, ESLint `no-console: error`; (4) health: `app/api/health/route.ts` (liveness, no dependencies) and `app/api/health/deep/route.ts` (bearer-protected, ≤ 3 s timeout per dependency, 503 when one is down), with tests for both; (5) an alert table — alert → threshold → window → severity tier → runbook → owner → channel — and an SLO table per journey with an error-budget policy; (6) verification on preview: force a synthetic failure (deep health 503) and confirm the alert fires end to end, and confirm a test error reaches the tracker tagged with `requestId`. Thresholds and SLO targets the user has not given are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never reply with only a request for the repo.
- **Part of it already exists** (e.g. "we already have Sentry"): open with an inventory of what is there (Sentry server/client/edge configs, `global-error.tsx`, tags, source maps) and state that it is kept as is; add only what was asked (e.g. health routes and alert rules); add `requestId` as a Sentry tag only if it is missing, as a minimal diff; touch the logger only if `console.*` calls are found.
- **Bare "add observability"**: ask once, in one list, for the critical journeys and the alert channel; meanwhile show the plan skeleton with every SLO target and alert threshold as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never invent SLO numbers.
- **Asked to replace an existing logger or config outright**: decline the overwrite in one line (it loses the team's wiring) and propose the standard file beside it as a `.proposed` twin for a manual merge.

## Starting points
- **New** — point `target` at an empty folder: logger, health routes, alert rules, SLO doc and `.env.example` are written (TypeScript by default).
- **Existing** — point `target` at your repo. **Read before write:** the language flavour is detected first (`tsconfig.json` or any `.ts/.tsx` under `app|lib|components` → TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript) and every file is emitted as `.ts` or `.js` to match — a JavaScript Next.js app gets `lib/logger.js` and `route.js`, never a `.ts` file. A file you already have, **in either extension**, is never overwritten and never gets a conflicting sibling (`route.ts` beside `route.js` is a Next.js routing conflict): an existing health route is reported `exists, kept` with a static gap table (exports `GET`? `force-dynamic`? `no-store`? liveness free of dependency calls?), another existing file in the same flavour gets a `.proposed` twin to merge, one in the other flavour is kept and pointed at the asset. Env vars are appended to `.env.example` only for files written in this run; every `console.*` call in your source is listed. A repo that already has every piece exits 0 with just the gap table; a repo that already holds a conflicting pair (`route.js` **and** `route.ts`) writes nothing, says why in the report, and exits 1.

## When to use
- First production release; after an incident with "we had no idea"; before an SLA commitment.
- Adding a new service/edge function/job that has no logs or health signal.
- NOT for: a specific bug (`safe-fix`), pipeline alerts (`ci-cd-vercel-github`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Critical user journeys (≤5) | yes | `docs/SPEC.md` / user — ask once |
| Error-tracking vendor decision (Sentry default) and DSN availability | yes | user |
| Log sink (Vercel Log Drain target) | no | user; default: vendor's drain |
| On-call / notification channel | yes | user — ask once |
| Existing `lib/logger.ts`, health routes | yes | repo |

Missing facts do not stop the plan: use the stated defaults, mark thresholds and SLO targets `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and ask once at the start. Never invent SLO numbers.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` (Logging, Errors rows) and `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`. Inventory what exists: language flavour (`tsconfig.json` / `.ts` source vs `jsconfig.json` / `.js` only), logger, Sentry, health routes in either extension, deploy platform (Vercel or AWS workflows), Next special files. Every file you add takes the repo's extension; never place a `.ts` route or module beside an existing `.js` one.
2. **Plan.** Table of components to add/change: logger, request context, error tracking (server + client + edge), health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard, runbook links. Post; wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Logging.** Install `assets/logger.ts` (or `assets/logger.js` in a JavaScript repo) as `lib/logger.{ts,js}` (+ `lib/logger/context.{ts,js}` AsyncLocalStorage) per `references/log-schema.md`; wire `requestId` in `middleware.ts`; ESLint `no-console: error`. Replace existing `console.*` in minimal diffs.
4. **Error tracking.** Follow `references/error-tracking.md`: server, client, edge configs; `requestId`/`tenantId` tags; PII scrubbing; source maps in CI; `error.tsx` reporting.
5. **Health.** Add `assets/health-route.ts` (or `.js`) as `app/api/health/route.{ts,js}` (liveness, no deps) and `app/api/health/deep/route.{ts,js}` (DB, auth, storage, queue; bearer-protected) per `references/health-endpoints.md`. If a health route already exists in either extension, keep it, verify it exports `GET`, and list what it is missing versus the standard (see the reference's brownfield table) instead of adding a sibling.
6. **Alerts + SLOs.** From `references/alerts-and-slos.md`, fill `assets/alert-rules.yaml` for the chosen vendor and the SLO table for the critical journeys. Every alert has a runbook link and an owner.
7. **Test.** Unit test logger redaction; integration test both health routes (200 / 503 on simulated DB failure); trigger a test error and confirm it appears in the tracker with `requestId`. Full unit suite green. *(gate: build→test)*
8. **Verify.** Deploy to preview; curl both health routes; confirm Log Drain delivers JSON; confirm an alert fires on a synthetic failure (health 503). *(gate: test→verify)*
9. Write `docs/observability.md` (schema, endpoints, alerts, dashboards, how to find a request by id). Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Logger | `lib/logger.{ts,js}`, `lib/logger/context.{ts,js}` (extension follows the repo) |
| Error tracking | `sentry.{server,client,edge}.config.ts` (or vendor equivalent), `app/global-error.tsx` |
| Health | `app/api/health/route.{ts,js}`, `app/api/health/deep/route.{ts,js}` |
| Alerts / SLOs | `ops/alerts.yaml`, `docs/observability.md` |
| Dashboard spec | `docs/observability.md` §Dashboards |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every log line has `ts, level, msg, service, env`; request-scoped lines have `requestId`
- [ ] Redaction list covers email, token, password, authorization, cookie, key
- [ ] Health liveness has zero dependencies; deep check is auth-protected and times out ≤ 3 s per dependency
- [ ] Every added file matches the repo's flavour (`.js` in a JavaScript repo); no route or module exists in two extensions
- [ ] Every alert: threshold, window, severity, runbook, owner, notification channel
- [ ] SLOs defined for each critical journey with an error-budget policy
- [ ] Synthetic failure produced an alert end-to-end
- [ ] No PII reached the error tracker (checked a real event)

## References
- `references/log-schema.md` — fields, levels, redaction, request context
- `references/error-tracking.md` — Sentry (default) wiring for server/client/edge, scrubbing, source maps
- `references/health-endpoints.md` — liveness vs readiness vs deep; response contract
- `references/alerts-and-slos.md` — alert catalogue, SLO starter, error-budget policy, dashboard panels
- `assets/logger.ts`, `assets/logger-context.ts`, `assets/health-route.ts`, `assets/health-deep-route.ts` (+ the `.js` twins `assets/logger.js`, `assets/logger-context.js`, `assets/health-route.js`, `assets/health-deep-route.js`, functionally identical), `assets/alert-rules.yaml`
- `scripts/install.py` — detects the flavour, installs the matching assets without overwriting or creating `.ts`/`.js` siblings (`exists, kept` + gap table for health routes, `.proposed` twins otherwise), appends env vars for written files to `.env.example`
- `scripts/check_siblings.py` — fails when any route or module exists in two source extensions (used by the eval checks)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/observability-setup --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/observability-setup`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Existing files are never overwritten and never get a `.ts`/`.js` sibling: a health route that exists is kept and gap-checked, a differing file in the same flavour gets a `.proposed` twin listed in the report for a manual merge, and an existing conflicting pair aborts the run (exit 1, nothing written).

bodyHtml:
perf-review-runner

The review a senior performance engineer does on the source before a traffic spike: ten checkable patterns that make a Next.js + Supabase app slow under load, each reported as file:line with a severity and a fix. Static only — nothing runs, nothing is measured.

In a conversation: review the code now

Never

  • Never report a PASS, a finding count or a "no N+1s" verdict for code that is not in the conversation. Review only pasted or attached source; for the rest, lay out the checklist and ask for the files.
  • Never invent a latency, a query count or a "p95" — this review measures nothing. Numbers come from observability-setup dashboards, not from here.
  • Never rate select("*"), an unbounded list read or an N+1 as medium because "the table is small today": they are high and fail the gate; the baseline is the only way to carry them as known debt.
  • Never flag useMemo-wrapped sort/filter (PF6), a for await loop (PF2), a .single()/.range()/.limit() chain (PF4), a head: true count (PF3/PF4) or a heavy import in a non-page component (PF8): those are the clean forms.

Procedure (from scripts/perf_review.py; work file by file through the supplied code)

  1. Classify each file: client ("use client") or server; app/**/page|layout (page), app/**/route.ts (handler), other.
  2. Loops and callbacks: a Supabase .from(/.rpc( or fetch( inside a for/while body or a .map/.forEach/.flatMap callback → PF1 high. Any other await inside a for/while body (not for await) → PF2 medium.
  3. Every Supabase chain .from(…).select(…)…: a select list containing * → PF3 high; a read (no insert/update/delete/upsert, no head: true) with none of .limit(/.range(/.single(/.maybeSingle(/.eq("id", …) → PF4 high.
  4. Client files: a useEffect whose callback calls fetch/.from/.rpc → PF5 medium; in a PascalCase component body, .sort(/.filter( on a destructured prop or props.x outside useMemo/useCallback/useEffect → PF6 medium.
  5. .tsx/.jsx: <img → PF7 medium. Pages: a static import … from one of the heavy client libraries (recharts, chart.js, three, monaco, mapbox-gl, leaflet, pdfjs, xlsx, quill, tiptap, ag-grid, moment, lodash, …) → PF8 medium; a server page where every fetch passes cache: "no-store" → PF9 medium per fetch.
  6. Route handlers: readFileSync/readdirSync inside an exported GET|POST|… body → PF10 medium (module-scope reads are fine).
  7. Sort by file, line, rule. Gate: FAIL if any high finding is new; PASS otherwise. With a baseline, match on rule + file + snippet (lines may move): matched → known, else new; unmatched baseline rows → resolved.

Reply layout: the Summary table (rule, name, severity, count), then Findings (rule, file:line, severity, status, snippet, fix from references/perf-rules.md), then the gate line Gate: PASS / Gate: FAIL (high-severity findings), then the limits line (static, nothing measured).

  • Name the run: python3 -I scripts/perf_review.py --target <repo> [--baseline <findings.csv>] --findings findings.csv --report report.md.
  • The request names a repo, branch or file but its code is not in the conversation: write the review skeleton — Summary table with the ten rules and counts To be baselined · owner: author, from the repo, the per-rule checklist above, and the gate line unfilled. End with one line asking for the repo path (and the earlier findings.csv if debt was recorded). Never guess findings.
  • Asked to downgrade or "sign off" with highs open: decline in one line; offer the defensible paths — fix the high rows now (named columns, .range, .in()/embedded select), or record them as a baseline so only new highs gate.

Starting points

  • New — a repo is reviewed against all ten rules; any high finding (N+1, select("*"), unbounded read) fails the gate.
  • Existing — add baseline (the findings.csv of an earlier run): each finding is marked known or new, the gate fails only on new high findings, known debt stays listed and baseline items no longer found are reported as resolved.

When to use

  • Before a launch, campaign, term start or any expected traffic multiple; before scaling the Supabase plan "just in case".
  • "Why is this page slow", "find the N+1s", "check our queries", "are we bundling the chart library into every page".
  • In CI as a required check: exit 1 on new high findings.
  • NOT for: stack conventions, layering and where code lives (nextjs-enterprise-conventions), measuring latency, errors or query time in production (observability-setup), schema and indexes (supabase-schema-rls), applying the fixes (safe-fix).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
targetyesNext.js repo root (app/, components/, lib/, server/)runner exits 2 and writes needs_input.json
baselinenofindings.csv from an earlier run (recorded debt)every finding is new; any high finding fails the gate

Procedure

  1. Scan (scripts/perf_review.py): every .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs under target, skipping node_modules, .next, out, dist, build, coverage, tests.
  2. Detect PF1–PF10 per file as in the conversation procedure; rules, rationale and fixes in references/perf-rules.md.
  3. Baseline (optional): mark known/new, list resolved.
  4. Write findings.csv and report.md; print one line per finding and the summary line.
  5. Gate: exit 1 when any new high-severity finding remains; 0 otherwise.

Output

ArtifactForm
findings.csvrule,file,line,snippet,severity,status — sorted by file, line, rule
report.mdSummary (per-rule counts), Findings table, Baseline (when given), Rules with fix hints

Self-check

  • [ ] Every finding has rule, file:line, severity and a snippet copied from the source
  • [ ] PF1/PF3/PF4 are high; PF2/PF5–PF10 are medium; nothing else is invented
  • [ ] A clean repo yields zero findings and Gate: PASS; the same input twice yields byte-identical outputs
  • [ ] With a baseline, known debt is listed but does not gate; resolved rows are named
  • [ ] The report states that nothing was executed or measured

References

  • references/perf-rules.md — PF1–PF10: id, what is matched, rationale, fix, known false positives and limits
  • scripts/perf_review.py — scanner, baseline matcher, report writer and gate (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/perf-review-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/perf-review-runner). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The review step exits 1 on any new high-severity finding, so a repo with an N+1, select("*") or unbounded list read fails the run by design; fix the findings in code (or record them in a baseline as known debt), then re-run.

Flags PF1 (high) on the order_items query inside the for loop: up to 200 queries per page view, so query count scales with the list
Proposes one query: an embedded select (select("id, total, order_items(sku, qty)")) or .in("order_id", ids) on order_items, then join in memory

Flags PF2 await-in-loop (medium) on the awaits: tenants are processed one after another, so total time is the sum of all tenants
Fix: map tenants to promises and await Promise.all (or Promise.allSettled), optionally in bounded batches if the upstream rate-limits
Notes that if the order is intentional, keep the loop with a comment and record it in the baseline; PF2 is medium and does not fail the gate by itself

All four are medium, so the gate passes; proposes a server page that fetches stock and passes props, useMemo for the filter, next/image, and next/dynamic for the export feature
