bodyHtml:
Interview Prep (truth-locked)

In a conversation: prepare the candidate now

  • The request names the round, the interviewers and the JD / story bank (even if the files are "attached" and their contents are not in the conversation): build the prep pack in this reply, in this order: (1) traceability table — JD competency (C1–C10 from references/competency-map.md, ranked by JD emphasis) → story ID → fit STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP; (2) STAR+R stories, each ≤120 words and citing [SB-nn] or [MR-Lnn]; (3) likely questions for this round type, each mapped to a story ID or GAP; (4) for hiring-manager, CIO/CEO or executive rounds, a 90-day plan on the Days 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 skeleton with an owner per item, built only from JD facts, unknowns To be baselined · owner to be named; (5) questions to ask, grouped by interviewer title (e.g., business VP, peer directors, principal architect; CIO-specific questions for a CIO round); (6) gaps and how to handle each honestly. Where story content is not visible, keep the user's SB ids and mark the content To be baselined · owner: user, source SB-nn; never invent it. Never reply with only a request for files. Chat reply ≤50 words outside the pack.
  • Asked to make up a story ("make up a SOX remediation story"): decline in one line, naming the TRUTH LOCK rule — every story must trace to the story bank or résumé, and an invented story fails the first follow-up question. Show the competency (SOX/audit → C7 Risk, security and compliance) as GAP in the traceability table, then offer (a) to interview the user for a true adjacent example, or (b) an honest "closest experience and how I would approach it" answer outline.
  • No story bank and no master résumé: ask once for the story bank (or the résumé, to build one by interviewing the user). Do not fill stories from memory and do not run a mock round on invented stories.

Starting points

  • New — the JD's competencies are mapped to your story bank (gaps stay gaps — nothing is invented), with the round's likely questions, questions to ask and a 90-day plan skeleton.
  • Existing — add your debrief from the last round: stories you already told are marked, competencies where every story is spent and JD competencies not shown yet are listed, and the questions already asked are kept for consistent follow-ups.

When to use

  • "I have a panel interview Thursday", "grill me for the CIO round", "map my stories to this JD", "draft my 90-day plan", "what should I ask them".
  • Mock-interview mode: user asks to be questioned and scored.
  • NOT for: résumé rewriting (resume-tailor), post-interview thank-you notes (outreach-and-followup), offer decisions (offer-evaluator).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Story bank (STAR+R entries with stable IDs)yesuser file; format in assets/story-bank.example.md
Master résuméyes (if story bank is thin)user file; same format as resume-tailor
JD textyesuser paste
Round type and interviewers (titles)yesuser
Company context (public: strategy, recent news, tech stack)nouser or web search, each fact sourced
Interview date and format (virtual/onsite, length, case prompt)nouser

Story bank named but its contents not visible: build the pack anyway with the SB ids and To be baselined · owner to be named story content. No story bank and no résumé: ask once; offer to build it from the master résumé by interviewing the user (one question per bullet). Never fill it from memory.

TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)

  1. Every story, number, title and outcome traces to a story-bank ID [SB-nn] or résumé line [MR-Lnn].
  2. Allowed: reframe a story for a different competency, tighten, pick which details to lead with, add a Reflection sentence the user confirms.
  3. Not allowed: invent a story, add a metric, change the user's role in the story, upgrade "contributed" to "led".
  4. If the JD needs a competency with no story, say so and offer: (a) interview the user for a true example, or (b) prepare an honest "here is the closest experience and how I would approach it" answer.
  5. Output includes a traceability table: competency → story ID → fit (STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Map JD responsibilities to the competencies in references/competency-map.md. Rank by JD emphasis.
  3. For each competency, select the best story from the story bank. Rewrite it in STAR+R per references/star-r-format.md (≤120 words spoken, ~90 seconds). Cite the ID.
  4. Pull the question bank for the round type from references/question-bank.md. Pair each likely question with a story ID or a GAP note.
  5. If the round is hiring manager, CIO/CEO or board-style: draft the 90-day plan from assets/90-day-plan.md using only JD facts and sourced company facts. Mark unknowns To be baselined · owner to be named.
  6. Select 6–8 questions to ask from references/questions-to-ask.md, tuned to interviewer title.
  7. Mock mode: ask one question at a time, score the answer against the STAR+R rubric (structure, specificity, scale, result, reflection; 1–5 each), give one fix, move on. Do not score stories not in the bank.
  8. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

Output

Markdown file prep-<company>-<round>.md:

  1. Competency → story traceability table
  2. STAR+R stories (ranked by JD emphasis)
  3. Likely questions for this round with story mapping
  4. 90-day plan draft (if applicable)
  5. Questions to ask (by interviewer)
  6. Gaps and how to handle them honestly

Self-check

  • [ ] Every story cites [SB-nn] or [MR-Lnn]; traceability table complete
  • [ ] No metric or role claim beyond the source; Reflection lines confirmed by user or marked [confirm]
  • [ ] Each story ≤120 words; Result contains a number where the source has one
  • [ ] Question bank matches the round type; interviewer titles respected
  • [ ] 90-day plan uses only JD and sourced facts; unknowns carry an owner
  • [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

References

  • scripts/prep.py — JD competencies → story map (GAP when no story), prep pack by round type, questions to ask, 90-day plan skeleton (stdlib, offline)
  • references/competency-map.md — exec IT competencies, behavioral indicators, JD phrases
  • references/star-r-format.md — STAR+R structure, timing, scoring rubric
  • references/question-bank.md — questions by round type
  • references/questions-to-ask.md — questions to ask by interviewer
  • assets/story-bank.example.md — EXAMPLE story bank (fictional)
  • assets/90-day-plan.md — plan skeleton

bodyMd:
# Interview Prep (truth-locked)

## In a conversation: prepare the candidate now
- **The request names the round, the interviewers and the JD / story bank** (even if the files are "attached" and their contents are not in the conversation): build the prep pack in this reply, in this order: (1) traceability table — JD competency (C1–C10 from `references/competency-map.md`, ranked by JD emphasis) → story ID → fit STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP; (2) STAR+R stories, each ≤120 words and citing `[SB-nn]` or `[MR-Lnn]`; (3) likely questions for this round type, each mapped to a story ID or GAP; (4) for hiring-manager, CIO/CEO or executive rounds, a 90-day plan on the Days 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 skeleton with an owner per item, built only from JD facts, unknowns `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; (5) questions to ask, grouped by interviewer title (e.g., business VP, peer directors, principal architect; CIO-specific questions for a CIO round); (6) gaps and how to handle each honestly. Where story content is not visible, keep the user's SB ids and mark the content `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user, source SB-nn]`; never invent it. Never reply with only a request for files. Chat reply ≤50 words outside the pack.
- **Asked to make up a story** ("make up a SOX remediation story"): decline in one line, naming the **TRUTH LOCK** rule — every story must trace to the story bank or résumé, and an invented story fails the first follow-up question. Show the competency (SOX/audit → C7 Risk, security and compliance) as **GAP** in the traceability table, then offer (a) to interview the user for a true adjacent example, or (b) an honest "closest experience and how I would approach it" answer outline.
- **No story bank and no master résumé**: ask once for the story bank (or the résumé, to build one by interviewing the user). Do not fill stories from memory and do not run a mock round on invented stories.

## Starting points
- **New** — the JD's competencies are mapped to your story bank (gaps stay gaps — nothing is invented), with the round's likely questions, questions to ask and a 90-day plan skeleton.
- **Existing** — add your debrief from the last round: stories you already told are marked, competencies where every story is spent and JD competencies not shown yet are listed, and the questions already asked are kept for consistent follow-ups.

## When to use
- "I have a panel interview Thursday", "grill me for the CIO round", "map my stories to this JD", "draft my 90-day plan", "what should I ask them".
- Mock-interview mode: user asks to be questioned and scored.
- NOT for: résumé rewriting (`resume-tailor`), post-interview thank-you notes (`outreach-and-followup`), offer decisions (`offer-evaluator`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Story bank (STAR+R entries with stable IDs) | yes | user file; format in `assets/story-bank.example.md` |
| Master résumé | yes (if story bank is thin) | user file; same format as `resume-tailor` |
| JD text | yes | user paste |
| Round type and interviewers (titles) | yes | user |
| Company context (public: strategy, recent news, tech stack) | no | user or web search, each fact sourced |
| Interview date and format (virtual/onsite, length, case prompt) | no | user |

Story bank named but its contents not visible: build the pack anyway with the SB ids and `[TO BE BASELINED]` story content. No story bank and no résumé: ask once; offer to build it from the master résumé by interviewing the user (one question per bullet). Never fill it from memory.

## TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)
1. Every story, number, title and outcome traces to a story-bank ID `[SB-nn]` or résumé line `[MR-Lnn]`.
2. Allowed: reframe a story for a different competency, tighten, pick which details to lead with, add a Reflection sentence the user confirms.
3. Not allowed: invent a story, add a metric, change the user's role in the story, upgrade "contributed" to "led".
4. If the JD needs a competency with no story, say so and offer: (a) interview the user for a true example, or (b) prepare an honest "here is the closest experience and how I would approach it" answer.
5. Output includes a traceability table: competency → story ID → fit (STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Map JD responsibilities to the competencies in `references/competency-map.md`. Rank by JD emphasis.
3. For each competency, select the best story from the story bank. Rewrite it in STAR+R per `references/star-r-format.md` (≤120 words spoken, ~90 seconds). Cite the ID.
4. Pull the question bank for the round type from `references/question-bank.md`. Pair each likely question with a story ID or a GAP note.
5. If the round is hiring manager, CIO/CEO or board-style: draft the 90-day plan from `assets/90-day-plan.md` using only JD facts and sourced company facts. Mark unknowns `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
6. Select 6–8 questions to ask from `references/questions-to-ask.md`, tuned to interviewer title.
7. Mock mode: ask one question at a time, score the answer against the STAR+R rubric (structure, specificity, scale, result, reflection; 1–5 each), give one fix, move on. Do not score stories not in the bank.
8. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

## Output
Markdown file `prep-<company>-<round>.md`:
1. Competency → story traceability table
2. STAR+R stories (ranked by JD emphasis)
3. Likely questions for this round with story mapping
4. 90-day plan draft (if applicable)
5. Questions to ask (by interviewer)
6. Gaps and how to handle them honestly

## Self-check
- [ ] Every story cites `[SB-nn]` or `[MR-Lnn]`; traceability table complete
- [ ] No metric or role claim beyond the source; Reflection lines confirmed by user or marked `[confirm]`
- [ ] Each story ≤120 words; Result contains a number where the source has one
- [ ] Question bank matches the round type; interviewer titles respected
- [ ] 90-day plan uses only JD and sourced facts; unknowns carry an owner
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

## References
- `scripts/prep.py` — JD competencies → story map (GAP when no story), prep pack by round type, questions to ask, 90-day plan skeleton (stdlib, offline)
- `references/competency-map.md` — exec IT competencies, behavioral indicators, JD phrases
- `references/star-r-format.md` — STAR+R structure, timing, scoring rubric
- `references/question-bank.md` — questions by round type
- `references/questions-to-ask.md` — questions to ask by interviewer
- `assets/story-bank.example.md` — EXAMPLE story bank (fictional)
- `assets/90-day-plan.md` — plan skeleton

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/interview-prep --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/interview-prep`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

Produces a weighted fit score (must-haves 60%, nice-to-haves 25%, culture/logistics 15%, red flags subtract), a gap table, and a go/no-go call for senior director / VP / executive IT roles. bodyHtml:
JD Fit Scorer

In a conversation: score the role now

  • The JD and the profile (keyword file or résumé) are both supplied (even if "pasted" or "attached" and only partly visible): score in this reply, in this order: (1) first line is the verdict — GO / LEAN GO / LEAN NO / NO-GO — <score>/100 — <reason>; (2) bucket table with weights must-haves 60 / nice-to-haves 25 / culture-logistics 15, items, MATCH / PARTIAL / GAP counts and the math (bucket = weight × Σcredit ÷ items, MATCH 1.0, PARTIAL 0.5, total minus red-flag penalties); (3) gap table — every MATCH or PARTIAL cites the profile line it rests on, every GAP has a mitigation or "accept gap"; (4) red flags with penalties, or "none detected"; (5) next action. Requirements or profile lines not visible in the conversation are To be baselined · owner to be named, and the verdict line says which inputs it still depends on. Never reply with only a request for files.
  • A hard constraint is breached (active clearance required but the profile says none; travel above the profile's max + 15 points; location, comp floor): check these before any score. The verdict is NO-GO regardless of the keyword score; name each constraint hit explicitly with the JD text and the profile line; suggest logging the role in the tracker as Passed with the reason (application-tracker).
  • Asked to change how strict matching is ("only count exact matches", "be strict"): raise the match threshold (the share of a requirement's words the profile must carry; default 0.5, e.g. 0.9 for near-exact) and rescore — weaker overlaps become GAP, not PARTIAL. The verdict still comes from the same weights and rules; say in the verdict line which threshold was used.
  • No profile or résumé supplied: ask once for the profile keyword file or master résumé. Do not score from memory, from the user's job title or from earlier conversation, and do not state any experience the user has not supplied.

Starting points

  • New — write a short profile from the template (skills plus your limits: location, travel, comp floor, clearance) and the JD is scored against it: must-have / nice-to-have / culture fit, red flags, a go/no-go verdict.
  • Existing — add the résumé you already have: its lines are read as evidence and each matched requirement cites the résumé line id, so a profile with only your limits is enough.

When to use

  • User pastes a JD, posting URL text, or recruiter summary and asks "should I apply?", "how well do I fit?", "score this", or "rank these roles".
  • User wants a gap list before tailoring a résumé.
  • NOT for: rewriting the résumé (use resume-tailor), evaluating an offer (use offer-evaluator), or logging the application (use application-tracker).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
JD full text (title, responsibilities, requirements, location, comp if listed)yesuser paste or file
Profile keyword file or master résuméyesassets/profile-keywords.example.txt format; user supplies the real one
Hard constraints (location, travel, remote, comp floor, clearance)nouser; defaults in references/scoring-rubric.md
Target level (Sr Director / VP / CxO)nouser; default Sr Director

If the JD or the profile is missing, ask once. Do not score from memory or from a job title alone.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Parse the JD into three buckets: must-haves (required, "must", years, certifications, degree, clearance), nice-to-haves (preferred, "plus", "ideally"), culture/logistics (location, remote policy, travel, reporting line, team size, comp band, industry).
  3. Normalize each requirement to a short keyword phrase (≤6 words). Collapse duplicates.
  4. Match each requirement against the profile keyword file. Mark MATCH, PARTIAL (adjacent skill or older than 7 years), or GAP. Cite the profile line for every MATCH/PARTIAL; a match with no citation is a GAP.
  5. Scan the JD against references/red-flag-catalog.md. Record each hit with its penalty.
  6. Score using references/scoring-rubric.md. Optional: run scripts/score.py (--jd jd.txt --profile profile.txt) for the deterministic keyword pass, then apply judgement to PARTIALs.
  7. Apply the go/no-go thresholds in references/go-no-go.md. Hard-constraint violations force NO-GO regardless of score.
  8. Produce the output below. Run the self-check.

Output

Markdown, first line is the verdict. Save as fit-<company>-<role>.md if a file is requested.

GO / LEAN GO / LEAN NO / NO-GO — <score>/100 — <one-sentence reason>

| Bucket | Weight | Items | Matched | Partial | Gap | Bucket score |
| Red flags | — | <n> hits | penalty −<n> |

Gap table: | Requirement | Bucket | Status | Evidence (profile line) | Mitigation |
Red flags: | Flag | Penalty | JD text |
Next action: apply via … / tailor résumé / ask recruiter X before applying / pass

Self-check

  • [ ] Every MATCH/PARTIAL cites a profile line; none inferred from job titles alone
  • [ ] Weights sum to 100 before penalties; math shown
  • [ ] Hard constraints checked before the score is reported
  • [ ] Gap table includes a mitigation or "accept gap" for every GAP
  • [ ] Verdict is the first line; reply ≤50 words outside the artifact
  • [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; profile comes from the supplied file only

References

  • references/scoring-rubric.md — weights, status values, bucket math
  • references/red-flag-catalog.md — penalties and detection phrases
  • references/go-no-go.md — thresholds and hard-constraint overrides
  • scripts/score.py — offline keyword pass (stdlib only)
  • assets/profile-keywords.example.txt — profile file format (EXAMPLE, fictional)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/jd-fit-scorer --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain career/jd-fit-scorer). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

bodyMd:
# JD Fit Scorer

## In a conversation: score the role now
- **The JD and the profile (keyword file or résumé) are both supplied** (even if "pasted" or "attached" and only partly visible): score in this reply, in this order: (1) first line is the verdict — `GO / LEAN GO / LEAN NO / NO-GO — <score>/100 — <reason>`; (2) bucket table with weights must-haves 60 / nice-to-haves 25 / culture-logistics 15, items, MATCH / PARTIAL / GAP counts and the math (`bucket = weight × Σcredit ÷ items`, MATCH 1.0, PARTIAL 0.5, total minus red-flag penalties); (3) gap table — every MATCH or PARTIAL cites the profile line it rests on, every GAP has a mitigation or "accept gap"; (4) red flags with penalties, or "none detected"; (5) next action. Requirements or profile lines not visible in the conversation are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, and the verdict line says which inputs it still depends on. Never reply with only a request for files.
- **A hard constraint is breached** (active clearance required but the profile says none; travel above the profile's max + 15 points; location, comp floor): check these before any score. The verdict is **NO-GO** regardless of the keyword score; name each constraint hit explicitly with the JD text and the profile line; suggest logging the role in the tracker as Passed with the reason (`application-tracker`).
- **Asked to change how strict matching is** ("only count exact matches", "be strict"): raise the match threshold (the share of a requirement's words the profile must carry; default 0.5, e.g. 0.9 for near-exact) and rescore — weaker overlaps become GAP, not PARTIAL. The verdict still comes from the same weights and rules; say in the verdict line which threshold was used.
- **No profile or résumé supplied**: ask once for the profile keyword file or master résumé. Do not score from memory, from the user's job title or from earlier conversation, and do not state any experience the user has not supplied.

## Starting points
- **New** — write a short profile from the template (skills plus your limits: location, travel, comp floor, clearance) and the JD is scored against it: must-have / nice-to-have / culture fit, red flags, a go/no-go verdict.
- **Existing** — add the résumé you already have: its lines are read as evidence and each matched requirement cites the résumé line id, so a profile with only your limits is enough.

## When to use
- User pastes a JD, posting URL text, or recruiter summary and asks "should I apply?", "how well do I fit?", "score this", or "rank these roles".
- User wants a gap list before tailoring a résumé.
- NOT for: rewriting the résumé (use `resume-tailor`), evaluating an offer (use `offer-evaluator`), or logging the application (use `application-tracker`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| JD full text (title, responsibilities, requirements, location, comp if listed) | yes | user paste or file |
| Profile keyword file or master résumé | yes | `assets/profile-keywords.example.txt` format; user supplies the real one |
| Hard constraints (location, travel, remote, comp floor, clearance) | no | user; defaults in `references/scoring-rubric.md` |
| Target level (Sr Director / VP / CxO) | no | user; default Sr Director |

If the JD or the profile is missing, ask once. Do not score from memory or from a job title alone.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Parse the JD into three buckets: **must-haves** (required, "must", years, certifications, degree, clearance), **nice-to-haves** (preferred, "plus", "ideally"), **culture/logistics** (location, remote policy, travel, reporting line, team size, comp band, industry).
3. Normalize each requirement to a short keyword phrase (≤6 words). Collapse duplicates.
4. Match each requirement against the profile keyword file. Mark `MATCH`, `PARTIAL` (adjacent skill or older than 7 years), or `GAP`. Cite the profile line for every MATCH/PARTIAL; a match with no citation is a GAP.
5. Scan the JD against `references/red-flag-catalog.md`. Record each hit with its penalty.
6. Score using `references/scoring-rubric.md`. Optional: run `scripts/score.py` (`--jd jd.txt --profile profile.txt`) for the deterministic keyword pass, then apply judgement to PARTIALs.
7. Apply the go/no-go thresholds in `references/go-no-go.md`. Hard-constraint violations force NO-GO regardless of score.
8. Produce the output below. Run the self-check.

## Output
Markdown, first line is the verdict. Save as `fit-<company>-<role>.md` if a file is requested.

```
GO / LEAN GO / LEAN NO / NO-GO — <score>/100 — <one-sentence reason>

| Bucket | Weight | Items | Matched | Partial | Gap | Bucket score |
| Red flags | — | <n> hits | penalty −<n> |

Gap table: | Requirement | Bucket | Status | Evidence (profile line) | Mitigation |
Red flags: | Flag | Penalty | JD text |
Next action: apply via … / tailor résumé / ask recruiter X before applying / pass
```

## Self-check
- [ ] Every MATCH/PARTIAL cites a profile line; none inferred from job titles alone
- [ ] Weights sum to 100 before penalties; math shown
- [ ] Hard constraints checked before the score is reported
- [ ] Gap table includes a mitigation or "accept gap" for every GAP
- [ ] Verdict is the first line; reply ≤50 words outside the artifact
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; profile comes from the supplied file only

## References
- `references/scoring-rubric.md` — weights, status values, bucket math
- `references/red-flag-catalog.md` — penalties and detection phrases
- `references/go-no-go.md` — thresholds and hard-constraint overrides
- `scripts/score.py` — offline keyword pass (stdlib only)
- `assets/profile-keywords.example.txt` — profile file format (EXAMPLE, fictional)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/jd-fit-scorer --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/jd-fit-scorer`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

Produces a total-compensation table, a COL-adjusted comparison, a negotiation-lever plan, and a weighted decision matrix for senior director / VP / executive IT roles. Uses only figures the user supplies (offer letter, current comp, COL indices); no hardcoded market or COL data.

bodyHtml:
Offer Evaluator

In a conversation: evaluate the offer now

  • The offer figures are in the request: evaluate in this reply, in this order: (1) recommendation line first (accept / negotiate X then accept / decline) with the deciding number; (2) total-comp table per option — base, target bonus, sign-on, equity per year (grant ÷ vesting years), relocation, year-1 cash, annual recurring, annualized total over the horizon, COL-adjusted recurring; (3) COL basis — the user's indices quoted with their source and date (e.g., "Columbus 100, Austin 108 — user's calculator, Oct 2026"); (4) negotiation plan with 2–3 levers, each with ask, justification, fallback and order; (5) decision matrix with weights summing to 100 and each option's weight × score arithmetic and total shown — score from the stated facts only; a criterion with no facts is scored To be baselined · owner: user (never a made-up default), the arithmetic is shown for every scored criterion, and the totals are labelled "partial — N of M criteria scored" until the user supplies the rest; (6) risks and open items with owners. Components not given are To be baselined · owner: user.
  • COL index missing or the user asks you to "figure out" cost of living: never supply, estimate or recall an index. Still produce the nominal total-comp table from the figures supplied (rows for every component; values not given are To be baselined · owner: user), show the COL-adjusted column as To be baselined · owner: user, and ask for each location's index with its source and date.
  • Negotiation plan only: sequence it per references/negotiation-levers.md: thank and ask for a call → lead with the biggest lever stated as a number (base, L1, citing the disclosed band and its midpoint) → hold sign-on (L2, citing the forfeited bonus amount) as the bridge → bundle non-cash items → one justified counter → close with written confirmation and a revised letter. Ask the user for their probability of a yes on each lever rather than assuming it, and point to outreach-and-followup (negotiation-open) for the message draft.
  • No offer details at all ("is this offer good?"): ask once, in one list, for the offer components, the current package and the locations; do not estimate a bonus, equity value or market rate.

Starting points

  • New — the offers alone (e.g. between roles, no current package): year-1 cash, recurring and annualized totals, COL-adjusted only with indices you supply.
  • Existing — include your current package as the Current row: every offer is also shown as the change against what you have today, recurring and COL-adjusted.

When to use

  • "Is this offer good?", "compare offer A vs B vs my current job", "adjust for moving to Austin", "what should I negotiate?", "help me decide".
  • NOT for: writing the negotiation email (outreach-and-followup → negotiation open), interview prep, or tracking status (application-tracker).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource

Missing offer components → show them as To be baselined · owner: user in the table and ask once at the end; only when no offer details are given at all, ask before drafting. Never estimate a bonus, equity value, or COL index. Mark unknown components To be baselined · owner: user.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Fill assets/offer-comparison.csv with one row per option (current job included). Equity: use the user's stated value and vesting; show annualized value over the user's planning horizon only.
  3. Run scripts/compare.py with --file offer-comparison.csv --horizon 4 --col "Columbus OH=100,Austin TX=108" --base-location "Columbus OH" (indices supplied by the user). The script computes year-1 cash, annualized total comp, and COL-adjusted figures per references/total-comp.md and references/col-adjustment.md.
  4. Build the negotiation plan from references/negotiation-levers.md: rank levers by expected value × likelihood, pick 2–3, state the ask and the fallback.
  5. Score each option in the decision matrix (references/decision-matrix.md) using user weights. Show the arithmetic.
  6. State the recommendation first, then the table, then risks (likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner).
  7. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words; the artifact carries the detail.

Output

  1. Recommendation line (accept / negotiate X then accept / decline) with the deciding number
  2. Total-comp table (per option: base, bonus, sign-on, equity/yr, benefits value, total yr-1, annualized, COL-adjusted)

bodyMd:
# Offer Evaluator

## In a conversation: evaluate the offer now
- **The offer figures are in the request**: evaluate in this reply, in this order: (1) recommendation line first (accept / negotiate X then accept / decline) with the deciding number; (2) total-comp table per option — base, target bonus, sign-on, equity per year (grant ÷ vesting years), relocation, year-1 cash, annual recurring, annualized total over the horizon, COL-adjusted recurring; (3) COL basis — the user's indices quoted with their source and date (e.g., "Columbus 100, Austin 108 — user's calculator, Oct 2026"); (4) negotiation plan with 2–3 levers, each with ask, justification, fallback and order; (5) decision matrix with weights summing to 100 and each option's weight × score arithmetic and total shown — score from the stated facts only; a criterion with no facts is scored `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]` (never a made-up default), the arithmetic is shown for every scored criterion, and the totals are labelled "partial — N of M criteria scored" until the user supplies the rest; (6) risks and open items with owners. Components not given are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]`.
- **COL index missing or the user asks you to "figure out" cost of living**: never supply, estimate or recall an index. Still produce the nominal total-comp table from the figures supplied (rows for every component; values not given are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]`), show the COL-adjusted column as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]`, and ask for each location's index with its source and date.
- **Negotiation plan only**: sequence it per `references/negotiation-levers.md`: thank and ask for a call → lead with the biggest lever stated as a number (base, L1, citing the disclosed band and its midpoint) → hold sign-on (L2, citing the forfeited bonus amount) as the bridge → bundle non-cash items → one justified counter → close with written confirmation and a revised letter. Ask the user for their probability of a yes on each lever rather than assuming it, and point to `outreach-and-followup` (negotiation-open) for the message draft.
- **No offer details at all** ("is this offer good?"): ask once, in one list, for the offer components, the current package and the locations; do not estimate a bonus, equity value or market rate.

## Starting points
- **New** — the offers alone (e.g. between roles, no current package): year-1 cash, recurring and annualized totals, COL-adjusted only with indices you supply.
- **Existing** — include your current package as the `Current` row: every offer is also shown as the change against what you have today, recurring and COL-adjusted.

## When to use
- "Is this offer good?", "compare offer A vs B vs my current job", "adjust for moving to Austin", "what should I negotiate?", "help me decide".
- NOT for: writing the negotiation email (`outreach-and-followup` → negotiation open), interview prep, or tracking status (`application-tracker`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Offer components (base, target bonus %, sign-on, equity grant and vesting, benefits, 401k match, PTO, relocation, start date) | yes | offer letter / user |
| Current package, same components | yes for comparison | user |
| Cost-of-living index for each location, with source and date | no — without it the COL-adjusted column is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]` | user supplies (e.g., a COL calculator result); the skill never assumes one |
| Role facts: title, reporting line, team size, budget, remote/travel | no — unknowns marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]` | JD / interviews |
| User's decision weights (or accept defaults in `references/decision-matrix.md`) | no | user |
| Market comp reference (survey, pay-transparency bands) with source | no | user |

Missing offer components → show them as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]` in the table and ask once at the end; only when no offer details are given at all, ask before drafting. Never estimate a bonus, equity value, or COL index. Mark unknown components `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]`.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Fill `assets/offer-comparison.csv` with one row per option (current job included). Equity: use the user's stated value and vesting; show annualized value over the user's planning horizon only.
3. Run `scripts/compare.py` with `--file offer-comparison.csv --horizon 4 --col "Columbus OH=100,Austin TX=108" --base-location "Columbus OH"` (indices supplied by the user). The script computes year-1 cash, annualized total comp, and COL-adjusted figures per `references/total-comp.md` and `references/col-adjustment.md`.
4. Build the negotiation plan from `references/negotiation-levers.md`: rank levers by expected value × likelihood, pick 2–3, state the ask and the fallback.
5. Score each option in the decision matrix (`references/decision-matrix.md`) using user weights. Show the arithmetic.
6. State the recommendation first, then the table, then risks (likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner).
7. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words; the artifact carries the detail.

## Output
Markdown `offer-eval-<company>.md`:
1. Recommendation line (accept / negotiate X then accept / decline) with the deciding number
2. Total-comp table (per option: base, bonus, sign-on, equity/yr, benefits value, total yr-1, annualized, COL-adjusted)
3. Negotiation plan: lever, ask, justification, fallback, order
4. Decision matrix with weights and scores
5. Risks and open items (`[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`)

## Self-check
- [ ] Every figure traces to the offer letter, the user, or a cited source; nothing estimated silently
- [ ] COL indices carry a source and date supplied by the user
- [ ] Equity valued only on user-stated price/value and vesting; horizon stated
- [ ] Decision matrix weights sum to 100; scores shown with arithmetic
- [ ] Recommendation is the first line; risks have owners
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

## References
- `references/total-comp.md` — components, valuation rules
- `references/col-adjustment.md` — index method, what to adjust and what not to
- `references/negotiation-levers.md` — levers, typical ranges to *ask the user about*, sequencing
- `references/decision-matrix.md` — criteria, default weights, scoring scale
- `assets/offer-comparison.csv` — input layout
- `scripts/compare.py` — comparison calculator (stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/offer-evaluator --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/offer-evaluator`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

Outreach and Follow-up

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/outreach-and-followup --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain career/outreach-and-followup). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

Starting points

  • New — a first message: the type's variants filled only from your facts, every missing slot listed, and the follow-up cadence dated; the model polishes it, or with draft_only the filled skeleton is final.
  • Existing — add the thread so far: the touches you already sent are counted, only the follow-ups still due are dated (or the stop rule is reported), a reply is flagged, and facts you already used are marked so the next touch adds something new.

When to use

  • "Write a note to X asking for a referral", "reply to this recruiter", "thank-you after my panel", "it's been 10 days, nudge them", "decline this politely", "open the comp conversation".
  • "When should I follow up?" → cadence table.
  • NOT for: résumé content (resume-tailor), interview answers (interview-prep), offer math (offer-evaluator), logging the touch (application-tracker, but remind the user to log it).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Message type (one of six)yesuser
Recipient: name, title, relationship, channel (LinkedIn / email / text)yesuser
Role and companyyesuser
Context: last contact date, what was said, interview details, deadlineyes for follow-upsuser or tracker row
Facts to cite (1–2 outcomes from master résumé / story bank, with IDs)nouser file
Goal of this message (one sentence)yesuser; ask once if missing

No recipient name or context → ask once. Never guess names, dates, titles, or what was discussed.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Identify message type and load its rules from references/message-types.md (goal, length, tone, must-include, must-avoid).
  3. Draft 2–3 variants that differ in strategy, not tone (e.g., "Direct ask" vs "Soft ask via advice"; "Hold firm" vs "Open the door"). Label each with the goal it serves and the trade-off.
  4. Pull structure from assets/message-templates.md; fill only from supplied facts. Any <placeholder> left unfilled is listed for the user.
  5. Add a subject line for email. Keep LinkedIn connection notes ≤300 characters; InMail ≤150 words; email ≤180 words; thank-you ≤120 words.
  6. Attach the cadence row from references/cadence.md: next touch date, channel, stop rule.
  7. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact; drafts are the artifact.

Subject: …
<body>

…

Cadence: next touch <date / +N business days> via <channel>; stop after <n> touches or on <event>.
Log: add a row to tracker.csv (stage, touch date, next action).

Self-check

  • [ ] Variants differ in strategy, each labelled with what it prioritizes and trades off
  • [ ] Length limits respected; one ask per message; no banned words; no flattery
  • [ ] Cadence row present with a stop rule
  • [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

# Outreach and Follow-up

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/outreach-and-followup --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/outreach-and-followup`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## Starting points
- **New** — a first message: the type's variants filled only from your facts, every missing slot listed, and the follow-up cadence dated; the model polishes it, or with `draft_only` the filled skeleton is final.
- **Existing** — add the thread so far: the touches you already sent are counted, only the follow-ups still due are dated (or the stop rule is reported), a reply is flagged, and facts you already used are marked so the next touch adds something new.

## When to use
- "Write a note to X asking for a referral", "reply to this recruiter", "thank-you after my panel", "it's been 10 days, nudge them", "decline this politely", "open the comp conversation".
- "When should I follow up?" → cadence table.
- NOT for: résumé content (`resume-tailor`), interview answers (`interview-prep`), offer math (`offer-evaluator`), logging the touch (`application-tracker`, but remind the user to log it).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Message type (one of six) | yes | user |
| Recipient: name, title, relationship, channel (LinkedIn / email / text) | yes | user |
| Role and company | yes | user |
| Context: last contact date, what was said, interview details, deadline | yes for follow-ups | user or tracker row |
| Facts to cite (1–2 outcomes from master résumé / story bank, with IDs) | no | user file |
| Goal of this message (one sentence) | yes | user; ask once if missing |

No recipient name or context → ask once. Never guess names, dates, titles, or what was discussed.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Identify message type and load its rules from `references/message-types.md` (goal, length, tone, must-include, must-avoid).
3. Draft 2–3 variants that differ in **strategy**, not tone (e.g., "Direct ask" vs "Soft ask via advice"; "Hold firm" vs "Open the door"). Label each with the goal it serves and the trade-off.
4. Pull structure from `assets/message-templates.md`; fill only from supplied facts. Any `<placeholder>` left unfilled is listed for the user.
5. Add a subject line for email. Keep LinkedIn connection notes ≤300 characters; InMail ≤150 words; email ≤180 words; thank-you ≤120 words.
6. Attach the cadence row from `references/cadence.md`: next touch date, channel, stop rule.
7. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact; drafts are the artifact.

## Output
```
Type: <message type> | Channel: <x> | Goal: <one line>

### Variant A — <strategy label>  (prioritizes …; trades off …)
Subject: …
<body>

### Variant B — <strategy label>
…

Cadence: next touch <date / +N business days> via <channel>; stop after <n> touches or on <event>.
Log: add a row to tracker.csv (stage, touch date, next action).
Unfilled placeholders: <list or "none">
```

## Self-check
- [ ] No name, date, title, or interview detail that the user did not supply
- [ ] Any résumé fact cited carries its `[MR-…]` / `[SB-…]` ID
- [ ] Variants differ in strategy, each labelled with what it prioritizes and trades off
- [ ] Length limits respected; one ask per message; no banned words; no flattery
- [ ] Cadence row present with a stop rule
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

## References
- `scripts/fill.py` — fills the type's variants from context.json only (unfilled slots become owned markers) and dates the cadence in business days (stdlib, offline)
- `assets/message-final-template.md` — the llm step polishes into this; every fact and id from message.md is kept
- `references/message-types.md` — rules per type
- `references/cadence.md` — timing, channels, stop rules, escalation ladder
- `assets/message-templates.md` — skeletons with placeholders

bodyHtml:
Résumé Tailor (truth-locked)

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/resume-tailor --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain career/resume-tailor). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

Starting points

  • New — the JD's keywords are mapped to your master résumé (gaps go to you, never into the résumé); the model writes the tailored résumé, or with draft_only it is assembled from verbatim master lines; either way every bullet must trace to a master line.
  • Existing — add a résumé you already tailored: it is kept word for word, every bullet is traced against the master, and the supported JD keywords it does not cite yet are added as verbatim, cited bullets under "Additions for this JD".

When to use

  • "Tailor my résumé for this JD", "make this ATS-friendly", "rewrite my summary for a VP role", "which keywords am I missing".
  • After jd-fit-scorer returns GO / LEAN GO.
  • NOT for: scoring fit (use jd-fit-scorer), cover letters or recruiter messages (use outreach-and-followup), interview stories (use interview-prep).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Master résumé (full, untailored, with line numbers or stable bullet IDs)yesuser file; format in assets/master-resume.example.md
JD full textyesuser paste
Target title and levelnoJD; default Sr Director
Fit output from jd-fit-scorernoprior step; speeds keyword mapping
Page limit and format (2-page, ATS plain, LinkedIn)nouser; default 2-page ATS plain

If the master résumé is missing, stop and ask for it. Do not build from memory, LinkedIn recollection, or prior conversations.

TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)

  1. The master résumé is the only source of facts: employers, titles, dates, team sizes, budgets, metrics, technologies, awards.
  2. Every tailored bullet carries a source reference [MR-L<line>] or [MR-<bullet-id>].
  3. Allowed transformations: reorder, reword, merge two source bullets, drop detail, change emphasis, swap synonyms for JD keywords when the master résumé supports the underlying fact.
  4. Not allowed: new metrics, inflated numbers, new technologies, new scope, new titles, implied certifications, "led" where the source says "contributed to".
  5. If the user asks to add a claim with no source line, refuse that claim, explain why in one sentence, and offer two options: (a) add the fact to the master résumé first with their confirmation it is true, or (b) phrase the adjacent true fact instead. Continue with the rest of the tailoring.
  6. The output must include a traceability table. A bullet with no source row is a defect; remove it before returning.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Number the master résumé lines if not already numbered (MR-L1…). Do not alter content.
  3. Build the ATS keyword map per references/ats-keyword-mapping.md: JD keyword → exact/synonym → master résumé evidence line → placement (summary, core competencies, bullet, skills).
  4. Flag JD keywords with no evidence as UNSUPPORTED. These go in the gap note to the user, never into the résumé.
  5. Rewrite the executive summary (≤4 lines) using only supported keywords; structure per references/executive-resume-structure.md.
  6. Rewrite bullets with the formula in references/bullet-formula.md. Prioritize the 8–12 bullets most relevant to the JD's must-haves; demote the rest. Patterns (not facts) are in assets/bullet-bank.md.
  7. Produce the before/after diff per references/diff-format.md.
  8. Produce the traceability table: tailored bullet → [MR-Lxx] → transformation type.
  9. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

Output

Markdown file resume-<company>-<role>.md containing, in order:

  1. Keyword map table (JD keyword | status | evidence | placement)
  2. Tailored résumé (ATS plain: no tables, no columns, no graphics, standard headings)
  3. Before/after diff
  4. Traceability table
  5. Unsupported-claims note (what the JD wants that the master résumé cannot support, and what to do about it)

Self-check

  • [ ] Every tailored bullet has a [MR-…] source and appears in the traceability table
  • [ ] No number, employer, title, date, or technology appears that is absent from the master résumé
  • [ ] Any user-requested unsupported claim was refused with an explanation and alternatives
  • [ ] Summary ≤4 lines; bullets ≤2 lines each; action verb first; metric present where the source has one
  • [ ] ATS plain formatting: standard section names, no tables inside the résumé body, dates as Mon YYYY – Mon YYYY
  • [ ] Banned words from writing-style.md absent (leverage, synergy, robust, seamless, cutting-edge)
  • [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; everything comes from the supplied master résumé

References

  • scripts/tailor.py — JD keyword → master-line evidence map, gap list, verbatim candidate bullets (stdlib, offline)
  • scripts/check_traceability.py — the TRUTH LOCK gate: exit 1 on an uncited bullet, an unknown id, or a number absent from its cited lines
  • assets/tailored-resume-template.md — the llm step fills this; every bullet ends with [MR-Lnn]
  • references/ats-keyword-mapping.md — mapping method, synonym rules, density limits
  • references/bullet-formula.md — action + scope + metric + outcome, exec verbs, anti-patterns
  • references/executive-resume-structure.md — section order, length, what to cut at exec level
  • references/diff-format.md — before/after and traceability table layouts
  • assets/master-resume.example.md — EXAMPLE master résumé format (fictional)
  • assets/bullet-bank.md — reusable bullet patterns (no facts)

bodyMd:
# Résumé Tailor (truth-locked)

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/resume-tailor --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/resume-tailor`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## Starting points
- **New** — the JD's keywords are mapped to your master résumé (gaps go to you, never into the résumé); the model writes the tailored résumé, or with `draft_only` it is assembled from verbatim master lines; either way every bullet must trace to a master line.
- **Existing** — add a résumé you already tailored: it is kept word for word, every bullet is traced against the master, and the supported JD keywords it does not cite yet are added as verbatim, cited bullets under "Additions for this JD".

## When to use
- "Tailor my résumé for this JD", "make this ATS-friendly", "rewrite my summary for a VP role", "which keywords am I missing".
- After `jd-fit-scorer` returns GO / LEAN GO.
- NOT for: scoring fit (use `jd-fit-scorer`), cover letters or recruiter messages (use `outreach-and-followup`), interview stories (use `interview-prep`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Master résumé (full, untailored, with line numbers or stable bullet IDs) | yes | user file; format in `assets/master-resume.example.md` |
| JD full text | yes | user paste |
| Target title and level | no | JD; default Sr Director |
| Fit output from `jd-fit-scorer` | no | prior step; speeds keyword mapping |
| Page limit and format (2-page, ATS plain, LinkedIn) | no | user; default 2-page ATS plain |

If the master résumé is missing, stop and ask for it. Do not build from memory, LinkedIn recollection, or prior conversations.

## TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)
1. The master résumé is the only source of facts: employers, titles, dates, team sizes, budgets, metrics, technologies, awards.
2. Every tailored bullet carries a source reference `[MR-L<line>]` or `[MR-<bullet-id>]`.
3. Allowed transformations: reorder, reword, merge two source bullets, drop detail, change emphasis, swap synonyms for JD keywords **when the master résumé supports the underlying fact**.
4. Not allowed: new metrics, inflated numbers, new technologies, new scope, new titles, implied certifications, "led" where the source says "contributed to".
5. If the user asks to add a claim with no source line, refuse that claim, explain why in one sentence, and offer two options: (a) add the fact to the master résumé first with their confirmation it is true, or (b) phrase the adjacent true fact instead. Continue with the rest of the tailoring.
6. The output must include a traceability table. A bullet with no source row is a defect; remove it before returning.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Number the master résumé lines if not already numbered (`MR-L1`…). Do not alter content.
3. Build the ATS keyword map per `references/ats-keyword-mapping.md`: JD keyword → exact/synonym → master résumé evidence line → placement (summary, core competencies, bullet, skills).
4. Flag JD keywords with no evidence as **UNSUPPORTED**. These go in the gap note to the user, never into the résumé.
5. Rewrite the executive summary (≤4 lines) using only supported keywords; structure per `references/executive-resume-structure.md`.
6. Rewrite bullets with the formula in `references/bullet-formula.md`. Prioritize the 8–12 bullets most relevant to the JD's must-haves; demote the rest. Patterns (not facts) are in `assets/bullet-bank.md`.
7. Produce the before/after diff per `references/diff-format.md`.
8. Produce the traceability table: tailored bullet → `[MR-Lxx]` → transformation type.
9. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

## Output
Markdown file `resume-<company>-<role>.md` containing, in order:
1. Keyword map table (JD keyword | status | evidence | placement)
2. Tailored résumé (ATS plain: no tables, no columns, no graphics, standard headings)
3. Before/after diff
4. Traceability table
5. Unsupported-claims note (what the JD wants that the master résumé cannot support, and what to do about it)

## Self-check
- [ ] Every tailored bullet has a `[MR-…]` source and appears in the traceability table
- [ ] No number, employer, title, date, or technology appears that is absent from the master résumé
- [ ] Any user-requested unsupported claim was refused with an explanation and alternatives
- [ ] Summary ≤4 lines; bullets ≤2 lines each; action verb first; metric present where the source has one
- [ ] ATS plain formatting: standard section names, no tables inside the résumé body, dates as `Mon YYYY – Mon YYYY`
- [ ] Banned words from `writing-style.md` absent (leverage, synergy, robust, seamless, cutting-edge)
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; everything comes from the supplied master résumé

## References
- `scripts/tailor.py` — JD keyword → master-line evidence map, gap list, verbatim candidate bullets (stdlib, offline)
- `scripts/check_traceability.py` — the TRUTH LOCK gate: exit 1 on an uncited bullet, an unknown id, or a number absent from its cited lines
- `assets/tailored-resume-template.md` — the llm step fills this; every bullet ends with `[MR-Lnn]`
- `references/ats-keyword-mapping.md` — mapping method, synonym rules, density limits
- `references/bullet-formula.md` — action + scope + metric + outcome, exec verbs, anti-patterns
- `references/executive-resume-structure.md` — section order, length, what to cut at exec level
- `references/diff-format.md` — before/after and traceability table layouts
- `assets/master-resume.example.md` — EXAMPLE master résumé format (fictional)
- `assets/bullet-bank.md` — reusable bullet patterns (no facts)

card: Account plan: stakeholders, pipeline and next moves
name: account-plan
description: Use when the user asks to build or refresh a quarterly or annual account plan, account strategy, or account review for an existing or target client — including weighting the account's pipeline (win probabilities, deal values the CRM lacks) or setting the account target. Produces a one-page-first account plan — account snapshot, relationship and stakeholder map with coverage gaps, white-space map (our services × their business units/platforms), pipeline table, risks to the account, and 90-day plays with owners and dates — with every revenue, pipeline, or stakeholder fact sourced to the user's inputs or marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]. Do not use for pre-pitch research on a new logo (client-research-brief) or for a single-pursuit battle card (competitive-positioning).

bodyHtml:
account-plan

In a conversation: write the plan now

The reply is the plan: its first line is Posture: <Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter> — <the facts that drove it>, never a question or a request for files. Questions for missing facts go at the end.

  • The request carries account facts (engagements, end dates, pipeline, stakeholders, events such as a sponsor leaving), or says the CRM export, stakeholder list, catalog or prior plan are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the full account plan in this reply from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order, page 1 standing alone:
    1. Posture on line 1 (Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter) with the two or three facts that drove it (e.g. sponsor departure, nearest engagement end date).
    2. Snapshot — revenue, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles; each cell sourced ("CRM export, <date>") or To be baselined · owner to be named. Weighted pipeline only when the CRM supplies probabilities, and say so.
    3. Top risks and 90-day plays (3–6), each with owner, date and success measure: at least one coverage play (e.g. the successor to a departing sponsor) and one renewal/defense play for the nearest engagement end.
    4. Detail: stakeholder map (role, influence, disposition — unknown stays unknown —, our owner, last contact) with departures flagged as exposure and coverage gaps computed; white-space matrix (our services × their units) using current / qualified / hypothesis / no fit / unknown, each hypothesis citing its signal and confirming action; pipeline table; risk register; change log vs the prior plan on a refresh (achieved, carried, dropped and why). Mark every value the request does not give To be baselined · owner to be named naming the source it will come from, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
  • No account facts at all ("write an account plan for X"): ask once, in one list, for account facts (engagements, revenue, stakeholders, pipeline), our service catalog and the quarter. Do not estimate current spend, wallet share or stakeholder dispositions. Offer the Enter posture template with every cell marked To be baselined · owner to be named if the account is a target with no history.
  • Asked to invent win probabilities or a target ("assign 60% / 30%", "put the target at what we usually aim for"): say in one line that probabilities and targets are not invented, because leadership will treat them as forecast. Show the unweighted pipeline only; offer to add probabilities if the user records them in the CRM as their own sales judgment, labelled as such. Show the target as To be baselined · owner to be named until the user confirms the official target and its source, and report gap-to-target as a marker until target and weighting are confirmed. Never print the requested percentages or target figure as plan values.

Starting points

  • New — stakeholders, pipeline and service coverage become a 90-day plan: stakeholder map, white space, pipeline, risks and plays with owned TBDs.
  • Existing — add last quarter's plays and pipeline: the refresh says which plays were done, carried over (with last quarter's owner to confirm), dropped or closed by events, which plays are new, and how each opportunity moved since the last plan.

When to use

  • "Build the Q<n> account plan for <client>."
  • "Refresh the account strategy — we just lost the renewal / won the assessment."
  • "Prepare the quarterly account review for leadership."
  • NOT for: new-logo research (client-research-brief), one pursuit (competitive-positioning, proposal-writer).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Account facts: current engagements (scope, value, end dates), revenue history, contract vehicles, team on the accountyesuser / CRM export / prior plan
Stakeholder list with titles, our relationship owner, last contactyes (any subset; rest TBD)user / CRM
Client business context: strategy, initiatives, org changes, budget cycle (from client-research-brief or user)nobrief / user
Pipeline: opportunities, stage, value, close date, next stepyes or "none"CRM / user
Our service catalog (for white space)yesfile / user
Prior plan (for refresh)nofile
Quarter and planning horizonyesuser

If the request carries no account facts at all, ask once. Individual facts missing from a request that has some (catalog, revenue, a stakeholder's last contact) do not stop the draft: they are marked To be baselined · owner to be named. Never estimate the client's spend with us or wallet share from memory.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Snapshot: fill the account snapshot table (assets/account-plan-template.md §1) from inputs only: revenue by period, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles, NPS/health signals if provided. Each cell sourced (CRM export date, prior plan version, user statement) or marked.
  2. Stakeholder map per references/account-planning-method.md §2: for each stakeholder — role, influence (decision / influencer / gatekeeper / user), disposition toward us (advocate / neutral / skeptic / unknown), our relationship owner, last meaningful contact, next contact plan. Compute coverage gaps: decision-makers with no owner or no contact in 90 days; business units with no relationship. Unknown disposition is unknown, never assumed neutral.
  3. White-space map (§3): matrix of our service lines × the client's business units or platforms. Cells: current (sourced engagement), qualified (pipeline), hypothesis (signal from brief or discovery with the signal cited), no fit (reason), unknown. Hypotheses carry the confirming action. Count the cells; the plan's growth plays come from hypothesis cells with the strongest signals.
  4. Pipeline table: each opportunity with stage (use the user's stage names), value (from CRM or marked), close date, win probability only if the user's CRM supplies it (no invented probabilities), next step with owner and date, and the blocker if any. Reconcile the sum with the snapshot.
  5. Decision point — account posture. Per §4: Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter, from the facts (renewal exposure, relationship coverage, competitive threat, white-space signal strength). State the posture on line 1 and the two or three facts that drove it.
  6. Risks to the account (§5): renewal risk, stakeholder departure, competitive entry, delivery issues, budget cut, concentration risk; each with likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner.
  7. 90-day plays: 3–6 plays, each with objective, actions, owner, date, success measure, and which white-space cell or risk it addresses. Plays without an owner are not plays. Include at least one relationship play (coverage gap) and one delivery-quality play if any engagement is active.
  8. Targets only from the user: if a revenue target exists, show gap-to-target = target − (booked + weighted pipeline, if probabilities are supplied) and the plays that close it. If no target, To be baselined · owner to be named.
  9. One-page view first, detail behind. Refresh mode: diff against the prior plan (what changed, what was achieved, what was dropped and why).
  10. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: account-plan-<client>-<quarter>.md per assets/account-plan-template.md
  • Page 1: posture and bottom line · snapshot · top risks · 90-day plays. Following pages: stakeholder map and gaps · white-space matrix · pipeline · risk register · change log (refresh)

Self-check

  • [ ] Posture stated on line 1 with the driving facts
  • [ ] Every revenue, pipeline, and target figure sourced or To be baselined · owner to be named
  • [ ] No invented win probabilities; weighted pipeline only if the CRM supplies probabilities
  • [ ] Stakeholder dispositions sourced; unknowns marked unknown
  • [ ] Coverage gaps computed and addressed by at least one play
  • [ ] White-space hypotheses cite a signal and a confirming action
  • [ ] Every play has owner, date, success measure
  • [ ] Risks have likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner
  • [ ] Internal document; no content copied into client-facing material without review

References

  • references/account-planning-method.md — snapshot, stakeholder mapping, white-space logic, posture decision, risk patterns, play design, review cadence
  • assets/account-plan-template.md — plan template (one page first)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/account-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/account-plan). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

bodyMd:
# account-plan

## In a conversation: write the plan now
The reply **is the plan**: its first line is `Posture: <Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter> — <the facts that drove it>`, never a question or a request for files. Questions for missing facts go at the end.
- **The request carries account facts** (engagements, end dates, pipeline, stakeholders, events such as a sponsor leaving), or says the CRM export, stakeholder list, catalog or prior plan are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the full account plan **in this reply** from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order, page 1 standing alone:
  1. **Posture on line 1** (Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter) with the two or three facts that drove it (e.g. sponsor departure, nearest engagement end date).
  2. **Snapshot** — revenue, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles; each cell sourced ("CRM export, <date>") or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Weighted pipeline only when the CRM supplies probabilities, and say so.
  3. **Top risks** and **90-day plays** (3–6), each with owner, date and success measure: at least one coverage play (e.g. the successor to a departing sponsor) and one renewal/defense play for the nearest engagement end.
  4. Detail: **stakeholder map** (role, influence, disposition — unknown stays `unknown` —, our owner, last contact) with departures flagged as exposure and **coverage gaps** computed; **white-space matrix** (our services × their units) using `current / qualified / hypothesis / no fit / unknown`, each hypothesis citing its signal and confirming action; **pipeline table**; **risk register**; **change log vs the prior plan** on a refresh (achieved, carried, dropped and why).
  Mark every value the request does not give `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the source it will come from, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
- **No account facts at all** ("write an account plan for X"): ask once, in one list, for account facts (engagements, revenue, stakeholders, pipeline), our service catalog and the quarter. Do not estimate current spend, wallet share or stakeholder dispositions. Offer the **Enter** posture template with every cell marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` if the account is a target with no history.
- **Asked to invent win probabilities or a target** ("assign 60% / 30%", "put the target at what we usually aim for"): say in one line that probabilities and targets are not invented, because leadership will treat them as forecast. Show the **unweighted** pipeline only; offer to add probabilities if the user records them in the CRM as their own sales judgment, labelled as such. Show the target as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` until the user confirms the official target and its source, and report gap-to-target as a marker until target and weighting are confirmed. Never print the requested percentages or target figure as plan values.

## Starting points
- **New** — stakeholders, pipeline and service coverage become a 90-day plan: stakeholder map, white space, pipeline, risks and plays with owned TBDs.
- **Existing** — add last quarter's plays and pipeline: the refresh says which plays were done, carried over (with last quarter's owner to confirm), dropped or closed by events, which plays are new, and how each opportunity moved since the last plan.

## When to use
- "Build the Q<n> account plan for <client>."
- "Refresh the account strategy — we just lost the renewal / won the assessment."
- "Prepare the quarterly account review for leadership."
- NOT for: new-logo research (`client-research-brief`), one pursuit (`competitive-positioning`, `proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Account facts: current engagements (scope, value, end dates), revenue history, contract vehicles, team on the account | yes | user / CRM export / prior plan |
| Stakeholder list with titles, our relationship owner, last contact | yes (any subset; rest TBD) | user / CRM |
| Client business context: strategy, initiatives, org changes, budget cycle (from `client-research-brief` or user) | no | brief / user |
| Pipeline: opportunities, stage, value, close date, next step | yes or "none" | CRM / user |
| Our service catalog (for white space) | yes | file / user |
| Prior plan (for refresh) | no | file |
| Quarter and planning horizon | yes | user |

If the request carries no account facts at all, ask once. Individual facts missing from a request that has some (catalog, revenue, a stakeholder's last contact) do not stop the draft: they are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never estimate the client's spend with us or wallet share from memory.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Snapshot**: fill the account snapshot table (`assets/account-plan-template.md` §1) from inputs only: revenue by period, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles, NPS/health signals if provided. Each cell sourced (CRM export date, prior plan version, user statement) or marked.
2. **Stakeholder map** per `references/account-planning-method.md` §2: for each stakeholder — role, influence (decision / influencer / gatekeeper / user), disposition toward us (advocate / neutral / skeptic / unknown), our relationship owner, last meaningful contact, next contact plan. Compute coverage gaps: decision-makers with no owner or no contact in 90 days; business units with no relationship. Unknown disposition is `unknown`, never assumed neutral.
3. **White-space map** (§3): matrix of our service lines × the client's business units or platforms. Cells: `current` (sourced engagement), `qualified` (pipeline), `hypothesis` (signal from brief or discovery with the signal cited), `no fit` (reason), `unknown`. Hypotheses carry the confirming action. Count the cells; the plan's growth plays come from `hypothesis` cells with the strongest signals.
4. **Pipeline table**: each opportunity with stage (use the user's stage names), value (from CRM or marked), close date, win probability only if the user's CRM supplies it (no invented probabilities), next step with owner and date, and the blocker if any. Reconcile the sum with the snapshot.
5. **Decision point — account posture.** Per §4: Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter, from the facts (renewal exposure, relationship coverage, competitive threat, white-space signal strength). State the posture on line 1 and the two or three facts that drove it.
6. **Risks to the account** (§5): renewal risk, stakeholder departure, competitive entry, delivery issues, budget cut, concentration risk; each with likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner.
7. **90-day plays**: 3–6 plays, each with objective, actions, owner, date, success measure, and which white-space cell or risk it addresses. Plays without an owner are not plays. Include at least one relationship play (coverage gap) and one delivery-quality play if any engagement is active.
8. **Targets** only from the user: if a revenue target exists, show gap-to-target = target − (booked + weighted pipeline, if probabilities are supplied) and the plays that close it. If no target, `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
9. **One-page view first**, detail behind. Refresh mode: diff against the prior plan (what changed, what was achieved, what was dropped and why).
10. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `account-plan-<client>-<quarter>.md` per `assets/account-plan-template.md`
- Page 1: posture and bottom line · snapshot · top risks · 90-day plays. Following pages: stakeholder map and gaps · white-space matrix · pipeline · risk register · change log (refresh)

## Self-check
- [ ] Posture stated on line 1 with the driving facts
- [ ] Every revenue, pipeline, and target figure sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] No invented win probabilities; weighted pipeline only if the CRM supplies probabilities
- [ ] Stakeholder dispositions sourced; unknowns marked unknown
- [ ] Coverage gaps computed and addressed by at least one play
- [ ] White-space hypotheses cite a signal and a confirming action
- [ ] Every play has owner, date, success measure
- [ ] Risks have likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner
- [ ] Internal document; no content copied into client-facing material without review

## References
- `references/account-planning-method.md` — snapshot, stakeholder mapping, white-space logic, posture decision, risk patterns, play design, review cadence
- `assets/account-plan-template.md` — plan template (one page first)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/account-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/account-plan`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.
