bodyHtml:
client-research-brief

In a conversation: write the brief now

  • The request names the company and the purpose (the angle is optional — when it is missing, the brief is still written and the angle shows To be baselined · owner to be named; with or without a notes file — if the notes are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation, work from what the request states): write the brief in this reply, applying the skeleton script's classification by hand (sort each note item — filing link, job posting, announcement — into its section and number it as a source [S1]…). Never reply with only a request for the file. In template order (assets/brief-template.md):
    1. Bottom line — three facts the reader must walk in knowing, each with its source.
    2. Snapshot — each cell sourced or To be baselined · owner to be named.
    3. Financial signals — each number cites the filing and its section/page (e.g. "10-K, Item 7, p. __"); figures not quoted in the request stay To be baselined · owner to be named naming the filing section to read.
    4. Technology signals table — signal, source and tier, confidence (High / Med / Low per the playbook), and the confirming question for the call.
    5. Leadership — public-record facts only (title, since, prior employer, quoted priorities); no personality inference.
    6. Recent news (≤6, dated) · Likely initiatives labelled Hypothesis, each with the signal and its tier and the confirming question · Risks and landmines · Questions for the call.
    7. Sources — every URL or document with date accessed and tier. Keep the reply to about one page (≈700 words) so the Sources list is always complete.
  • Company or purpose missing or ambiguous ("a brief on Apex"): ask once which company (legal name, HQ country, ticker if listed) and the purpose and date of the meeting. Do not produce a brief for a guessed company and do not invent a notes file or sources.
  • Asked to fill revenue, IT spend or other figures that no source gives (private company, "use what you think it is"): say in one line that private-company figures are not estimated without a cited public source. Show those cells as To be baselined · owner to be named — never print an estimate anywhere, and never cite aggregator revenue estimates. Use only the user's notes as sources, rate a fact resting on a single signal Low, and give the specific discovery question that would baseline each figure (e.g. "What is the annual run cost of your WMS and integration estate?").

Starting points

  • New — your notes and links are sorted into the brief's sections with every source numbered; the model step writes the brief, or with draft_only the brief is your notes verbatim, each item cited, the so-what left as owned markers.
  • Existing — add previous (the last brief on this client): material already in it is carried, new material is marked NEW, and sources it cited that your notes no longer carry are listed to re-check or drop.

When to use

  • "Research <company> before the pitch on <date>."
  • "What is <account> likely to be spending on in the next 12 months?"
  • "Build a brief on the new CIO at <company>."
  • NOT for: competitor analysis (competitive-positioning), quarterly account strategy (account-plan), call synthesis (discovery-interview).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Company legal/common name, HQ countryyesuser
Purpose: pitch / discovery / proposal / exec meeting, and dateyesuser
Our angle: the service line or initiative we are positioningyesuser
Notes/links file (notes.md or .txt: URLs, pasted excerpts, prior-contact notes)nofile
Named stakeholders to profilenouser
Network access available? (yes/no)yesenvironment

If company name or purpose is missing, ask once. A missing notes file or angle does not stop the brief: unsourced cells are marked To be baselined · owner to be named. Never guess which company is meant when names collide (ask "Acme Corp (NYSE: ACM) or Acme Ltd (UK)?").

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Scope the brief to the purpose. A discovery brief emphasizes initiatives and pains; a proposal brief emphasizes procurement, incumbents, and financial capacity; an exec-meeting brief emphasizes the individual and their public positions. Use references/research-method.md §1 to pick the emphasis weights.
  2. Build the source plan from references/research-method.md §2 (source tiers: filings > investor materials > regulator/press releases > reputable press > job postings > vendor case studies > social). Decide which tiers are reachable: if no network, only the notes file and user-provided excerpts count as sources; everything else is To be baselined · owner to be named.
  3. Run the skeleton script when a notes file exists: python3 -I scripts/brief_skeleton.py --notes notes.md --company "<name>" --out brief.md. It classifies links and excerpts into the brief sections and lists what is still empty. Then fill each section by reading the sources (the script does not fetch).
  4. Extract tech-stack signals using references/tech-signal-playbook.md: job postings (platform names, team sizes), engineering blogs, case studies by vendors, conference talks, open-source repos, status pages, DNS/MX hints if provided. Record each signal with confidence (High / Med / Low) per the playbook rubric; never upgrade confidence without a second independent source.
  5. Decision point — financial capacity. If public: pull revenue, operating margin trend, capex/opex guidance, and any stated cost-out or transformation program from the latest annual/quarterly filing (cite the document and page). If private: state ownership (PE / founder / family), last funding or acquisition event if public, and mark capacity To be baselined · owner to be named. Do not estimate revenue for a private company.
  6. Profile leadership limited to the roles that matter for our angle (CIO/CTO/CDO, the business sponsor, CFO, CISO where security gates apply). Tenure, prior employer, public statements, and what they have changed since arrival. Public-record facts only; no inference about personality or politics.
  7. Derive likely initiatives as hypotheses, not facts: each row cites the signal(s) behind it and states what question on the call would confirm it. Feed these to discovery-interview.
  8. Write the brief on assets/brief-template.md. One page. Bottom line first: the three facts the reader must walk in knowing. Sources appendix lists every URL/document with the date accessed.
  9. Run the self-check. Delete any sentence you cannot trace to a source line or to the user's notes.

Output

  • File: client-brief-<company-slug>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md
  • Sections (template order): Bottom line · Snapshot · Financial signals · Technology signals (table with confidence) · Leadership · Recent news (≤6 items, dated) · Likely initiatives and hypotheses · Risks and landmines · Questions for the call · Sources
  • Length: ≤ 1 page body plus sources. If longer, move detail to an appendix.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every number carries a source (document + page/section, or URL + date)
  • [ ] No revenue, headcount, or spend estimate for a private company unless from a cited public source
  • [ ] Tech signals carry a confidence rating; no "they use X" at Low confidence
  • [ ] Leadership section contains only public-record facts; no personal characterizations
  • [ ] Likely initiatives are labeled hypotheses with the confirming question
  • [ ] No content from other clients or from the author's own history
  • [ ] Bottom line is three facts, first lines of the document

References

  • references/research-method.md — emphasis by purpose, source tiers, financial-signal extraction, writing rules
  • references/tech-signal-playbook.md — where tech-stack signals live and how to rate confidence
  • assets/brief-template.md — one-page brief template
  • scripts/brief_skeleton.py — notes/links file → brief skeleton with empty-section report (no network)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/client-research-brief --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/client-research-brief). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

  3. **Financial signals** — each number cites the filing and its section/page (e.g. "10-K, Item 7, p. __"); figures not quoted in the request stay `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the filing section to read.
  4. **Technology signals table** — signal, source and tier, confidence (High / Med / Low per the playbook), and the confirming question for the call.
  5. **Leadership** — public-record facts only (title, since, prior employer, quoted priorities); no personality inference.
  6. **Recent news** (≤6, dated) · **Likely initiatives** labelled *Hypothesis*, each with the signal and its tier and the confirming question · **Risks and landmines** · **Questions for the call**.
  7. **Sources** — every URL or document with date accessed and tier.
  Keep the reply to about one page (≈700 words) so the Sources list is always complete.
- **Company or purpose missing or ambiguous** ("a brief on Apex"): ask once which company (legal name, HQ country, ticker if listed) and the purpose and date of the meeting. Do not produce a brief for a guessed company and do not invent a notes file or sources.
- **Asked to fill revenue, IT spend or other figures that no source gives** (private company, "use what you think it is"): say in one line that private-company figures are not estimated without a cited public source. Show those cells as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` — never print an estimate anywhere, and never cite aggregator revenue estimates. Use only the user's notes as sources, rate a fact resting on a single signal **Low**, and give the specific discovery question that would baseline each figure (e.g. "What is the annual run cost of your WMS and integration estate?").

## Starting points
- **New** — your notes and links are sorted into the brief's sections with every source numbered; the model step writes the brief, or with `draft_only` the brief is your notes verbatim, each item cited, the so-what left as owned markers.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (the last brief on this client): material already in it is carried, new material is marked NEW, and sources it cited that your notes no longer carry are listed to re-check or drop.

## When to use
- "Research <company> before the pitch on <date>."
- "What is <account> likely to be spending on in the next 12 months?"
- "Build a brief on the new CIO at <company>."
- NOT for: competitor analysis (`competitive-positioning`), quarterly account strategy (`account-plan`), call synthesis (`discovery-interview`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Company legal/common name, HQ country | yes | user |
| Purpose: pitch / discovery / proposal / exec meeting, and date | yes | user |
| Our angle: the service line or initiative we are positioning | yes | user |
| Notes/links file (`notes.md` or `.txt`: URLs, pasted excerpts, prior-contact notes) | no | file |
| Named stakeholders to profile | no | user |
| Network access available? (yes/no) | yes | environment |

If company name or purpose is missing, ask once. A missing notes file or angle does not stop the brief: unsourced cells are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never guess which company is meant when names collide (ask "Acme Corp (NYSE: ACM) or Acme Ltd (UK)?").

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Scope the brief to the purpose.** A discovery brief emphasizes initiatives and pains; a proposal brief emphasizes procurement, incumbents, and financial capacity; an exec-meeting brief emphasizes the individual and their public positions. Use `references/research-method.md` §1 to pick the emphasis weights.
2. **Build the source plan** from `references/research-method.md` §2 (source tiers: filings > investor materials > regulator/press releases > reputable press > job postings > vendor case studies > social). Decide which tiers are reachable: if no network, only the notes file and user-provided excerpts count as sources; everything else is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
3. **Run the skeleton script** when a notes file exists: `python3 -I scripts/brief_skeleton.py --notes notes.md --company "<name>" --out brief.md`. It classifies links and excerpts into the brief sections and lists what is still empty. Then fill each section by reading the sources (the script does not fetch).
4. **Extract tech-stack signals** using `references/tech-signal-playbook.md`: job postings (platform names, team sizes), engineering blogs, case studies by vendors, conference talks, open-source repos, status pages, DNS/MX hints if provided. Record each signal with confidence (High / Med / Low) per the playbook rubric; never upgrade confidence without a second independent source.
5. **Decision point — financial capacity.** If public: pull revenue, operating margin trend, capex/opex guidance, and any stated cost-out or transformation program from the latest annual/quarterly filing (cite the document and page). If private: state ownership (PE / founder / family), last funding or acquisition event if public, and mark capacity `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Do not estimate revenue for a private company.
6. **Profile leadership** limited to the roles that matter for our angle (CIO/CTO/CDO, the business sponsor, CFO, CISO where security gates apply). Tenure, prior employer, public statements, and what they have changed since arrival. Public-record facts only; no inference about personality or politics.
7. **Derive likely initiatives** as hypotheses, not facts: each row cites the signal(s) behind it and states what question on the call would confirm it. Feed these to `discovery-interview`.
8. **Write the brief** on `assets/brief-template.md`. One page. Bottom line first: the three facts the reader must walk in knowing. Sources appendix lists every URL/document with the date accessed.
9. Run the self-check. Delete any sentence you cannot trace to a source line or to the user's notes.

## Output
- File: `client-brief-<company-slug>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections (template order): Bottom line · Snapshot · Financial signals · Technology signals (table with confidence) · Leadership · Recent news (≤6 items, dated) · Likely initiatives and hypotheses · Risks and landmines · Questions for the call · Sources
- Length: ≤ 1 page body plus sources. If longer, move detail to an appendix.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every number carries a source (document + page/section, or URL + date)
- [ ] No revenue, headcount, or spend estimate for a private company unless from a cited public source
- [ ] Tech signals carry a confidence rating; no "they use X" at Low confidence
- [ ] Leadership section contains only public-record facts; no personal characterizations
- [ ] Likely initiatives are labeled hypotheses with the confirming question
- [ ] No content from other clients or from the author's own history
- [ ] Bottom line is three facts, first lines of the document

## References
- `references/research-method.md` — emphasis by purpose, source tiers, financial-signal extraction, writing rules
- `references/tech-signal-playbook.md` — where tech-stack signals live and how to rate confidence
- `assets/brief-template.md` — one-page brief template

In a conversation: write the battle card now

    2. Alternative profile — the class (e.g. incumbent services provider); class patterns labelled Hypothesis (class pattern) until evidenced.
    3. Evidence table — claim, source, confidence: a client quote given in the request is High; RFP wording that mirrors the alternative is cited by clause, or To be baselined · owner to be named if not quoted.
    4. Criteria scorecard — criteria from the RFP (or To be baselined · owner to be named), us vs them, each neutralize / reframe / concede; at least one criterion conceded.
    5. Wedge — where we win and the client stated a concern (cite the quote); if no intersection, say so.
    6. Landmines · Objection handling as acknowledge → reframe → proof (cleared references only) → ask-back · Ghost lines that never name the alternative · Evaluation criteria to seed · Intelligence gaps with owners.
  • Alternative or pursuit context unknown ("make a battle card for the Northgate deal"): ask once, in one list, who or what we compete against and the pursuit context (client priorities, decision criteria, decision owner). In the same reply, so it is usable, sketch the card against status quo and an incumbent-type provider, every row labelled hypothesis, with no competitor facts asserted.

Offer the compliant alternative: a neutral discovery or clarification question that surfaces the client's own view of incumbent performance and cost.

Starting points

  • New — capabilities, their claims and stakeholder concerns become a battle card: wedge, landmines, objection grid, ghost lines and intelligence gaps, evidence-rated.
  • Existing — add the claims behind your last card: the refresh lists claims that are new, withdrawn or re-rated and any wedge the new evidence has closed, so the team stops leading with it.

When to use

  • "How do we beat the incumbent at <client>?"
  • "Build a battle card against <competitor type> for this pursuit."
  • "The client's platform vendor is bidding services too — what is our angle?"
  • NOT for: researching the client (client-research-brief), writing the proposal (proposal-writer), rehearsing objections live (orals-prep uses this output).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Pursuit context: client, initiative, decision criteria known, decision owneryesdiscovery synthesis / user
Alternative(s) we face: named competitor, incumbent, vendor services arm, in-house build, status quoyesuser
Evidence about the alternative: public materials, client statements, RFP wording, prior encountersno (but confidence drops without it)files / user
Our cleared proof points and capability catalogyesfile / user

Missing evidence, proof points or decision criteria do not stop the card: they are marked To be baselined · owner to be named or Hypothesis. If the alternative is unknown, ask once; if still unknown, build the card against "status quo" and "an incumbent-type provider" as labeled hypotheses.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

Each class has predictable strengths, weaknesses, and selling motions; use them as hypotheses, labeled as such, until evidence confirms.
  2. Build the evidence table for the alternative: every strength/weakness claim carries a source (public material, client quote, RFP wording that mirrors their language, prior encounter) and a confidence rating. No evidence → Hypothesis (class pattern); it never becomes a "fact" in any client-facing document.
  3. Map the client's decision criteria (stated in RFP/discovery; else To be baselined · owner to be named) and score us vs the alternative on each, honestly, using the scoring in §3 of the method. Where we lose on a criterion, decide: neutralize (close the gap), reframe (change the criterion's weight in the client's mind), or concede (do not fight it; move the battle).
  4. Decision point — the wedge. Identify the one or two criteria where we win and the client cares (from discovery). If no such intersection exists, say so: the recommendation is to reshape the opportunity (phase, scope, partner) or to qualify out. Do not manufacture a wedge.

Where we lose on a criterion, decide: neutralize (close the gap), reframe (change the criterion's weight in the client's mind), or concede (do not fight it; move the battle).
4. **Decision point — the wedge.** Identify the one or two criteria where we win and the client cares (from discovery). If no such intersection exists, say so: the recommendation is to reshape the opportunity (phase, scope, partner) or to qualify out. Do not manufacture a wedge.
5. **Landmines**: what we must not say or do (attacking the incumbent by name, disparaging the platform the client already bought, promising what their contract forbids, referencing other clients without clearance). Add client-specific sensitivities from discovery.
6. **Objection handling** with `references/objection-handling.md`: for each likely objection (the alternative's strengths restated as client concerns), write acknowledge → reframe → proof → ask-back. Proof only from cleared references.
7. **Ghost lines** for `proposal-writer`: the alternative's weakness stated as a general risk the client should evaluate, followed by how we remove it. No names.
8. **Evaluation criteria we want adopted**: three to five criteria phrased neutrally that favor our wedge; these go into clarification questions, discovery follow-ups, and the proposal's approach section.
9. **Write the battle card** on `assets/battle-card-template.md`. One page; internal only; marked so. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `battle-card-<client>-vs-<alternative>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` (internal, not for client distribution)
- Sections: Bottom line (win/lose assessment and wedge in two sentences) · Alternative profile (class, evidence table with confidence) · Criteria scorecard (us vs them with neutralize/reframe/concede) · Wedge · Landmines · Objection handling · Ghost lines · Evaluation criteria to seed · Intelligence gaps (what we need to learn, owner)

## Self-check
- [ ] Every claim about the alternative has a source and confidence, or is labeled hypothesis
- [ ] Scorecard is honest: at least one criterion where we lose is acknowledged
- [ ] Wedge sits at the intersection of "we win" and "client cares (sourced)"; or the card says there is none
- [ ] No competitor named in ghost lines or any content intended for client-facing use
- [ ] Objection proofs are cleared references only
- [ ] Landmines include client-specific sensitivities
- [ ] Card marked internal; no other-client specifics beyond cleared proof; no author history

## References
- `references/competitive-method.md` — alternative classes, evidence standards, criteria scoring, wedge logic, win/loss patterns
- `references/objection-handling.md` — objection patterns by alternative class with response structure
- `assets/battle-card-template.md` — one-page battle card

bodyHtml:
discovery-interview

In a conversation: produce the pack now

The reply is the pack or the synthesis, never only a request for files. About 1,000 tokens, tables.

Never

  • Never put a figure, budget, decision owner or date in the reply that the notes do not state — even when asked to fill it "from what clients usually do" or "so I can use it in the proposal". Say in one line: "Not in the notes — it must be baselined." Mark it To be baselined · owner to be named.
  • Never ask a question that opens with a technology or vendor comparison; never write a question list before the vertical is known.

Which reply

  1. Vertical or mode missing (e.g. "help me with the discovery call for Northwind"): ask once, one list — mode (prep or synthesize), vertical (EdTech, Retail, Manufacturing, Travel), opportunity context (attendees, trigger) — and stop. Never invent attendees, triggers or pains.
  2. Prep (vertical and call described), in this order:
    • Hypotheses | H# | Suspected pain | Owner | Confirms if | Kills if | Questions | (3–5).
    • Question plan: 12–18 questions (a 45-minute call: 36 min of questions ÷ 3 min = 12) from references/question-banks/<vertical>.md, ordered situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision → constraints (at least one per stage), table | # | Stage | Question | Persona | H# |.
    • Five closes: decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure.
    • Time budget table with an explicit row "Client's questions — 20% (9 of 45 min)" plus opening, question stages and closes.
    • Branches: "If they say X, go to Y" (3 rows).
  3. Synthesize call notes, in this order:
    • Line 1: the qualification call — PURSUE / PURSUE-WITH-CONDITIONS / PARK and the 2–3 facts that drove it.
    • Pain matrix | Pain | Evidence ("verbatim quote") | Pain score | Impact | Urgency | Owner | — Impact without a stated figure scores 2 or lower and shows To be baselined · owner to be named; Urgency names the forcing event as the notes state it (e.g. "before the S/4 go-live, next year — no date stated"), never an invented date.
    • Gaps list | Missing fact | Likely client holder | Our owner | — one row for every number asked for but not given (e.g. annual cost of the manual reconciliation → plant controller / VP Ops; Engagement lead).
    • Five closes, each quoted verbatim or TBD — owner: Engagement lead; hypothesis register; follow-up note ≤120 words.
  4. Files or structured inputs given (vertical, personas, minutes, notes): name the commands and outputs, then show the result: python3 -I scripts/build_pack.py --vertical <v> --personas "<p1,p2>" --minutes <m> --banks references/question-banks --client <c> --out discovery-pack.md --five-closes five-closes.md --pain-matrix pain-matrix.csv (time budget: 20% reserved for the client's questions, 10 min closes, 3 min opening, 3 min per question round-robin across stages; five closes all open; pain matrix header only), then with notes python3 -I scripts/synthesize.py notes.md --pain-matrix pain-matrix.csv --five-closes five-closes.md --client <c> (every pain row's evidence is the verbatim line; impact/urgency H only when the line holds a figure or a date/renewal word, else TBD; each close quoted or TBD — owner: Engagement lead; nothing inferred). Thin notes → closes not in the notes stay TBD with that owner.

Starting points

  • New — before the call: a timed question plan for the attendees' personas from the vertical's question bank, with the five closes all open and an empty pain matrix.
  • Existing — after the call: your notes or transcript are synthesised into the pain matrix and the five closes; anything the notes do not say stays an owned TBD.

When to use

  • "Prep me for the discovery call with <client> on <topic>."
  • "Here are my notes from the workshop — synthesize them."
  • "What should I ask a <vertical> CIO about <platform/initiative>?"
  • NOT for: company background before a pitch (client-research-brief), RFP question lists (rfp-compliance-matrix), or pitch rehearsal (orals-prep).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Client name, vertical (EdTech / Retail / Manufacturing / Travel / other)yesuser
Opportunity context: initiative, platform(s), trigger eventyesuser / brief
Attendee list with titles (or "unknown")nouser
Mode: prep (before call) or synthesize (after call)yesuser
Raw notes / transcript (synthesize mode only)yes in synthesizefile
Time available for the call (minutes)no — default 45user

If a required input is missing, ask once. Do not invent the vertical, attendees, or the client's pain.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first. Both apply to every output here.

Mode A — prep

  1. Classify the opportunity: vertical, buyer persona (CIO / CDO / VP Apps / COO / Head of Supply Chain / Provost / CFO), and initiative type (modernization, migration, AI, integration, cost-out, compliance). If the vertical is outside the four banks, use references/question-banks/retail.md as the structural base and say so.
  2. Write 3–5 hypotheses before writing questions (references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md §1). Each hypothesis states a suspected pain, who owns it, and what evidence would confirm or kill it. Questions exist to test hypotheses, not to fill time.
  3. Load the vertical bank from references/question-banks/<vertical>.md. Select 12–18 questions using the time budget rule: ~3 minutes per open question, reserve 20% for their questions. Tag each selected question with the hypothesis it tests (H1…H5) and the persona it is aimed at.
  4. Order questions using the funnel in references/discovery-method.md §2: situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision process → constraints. Never open with a technology question.
  5. Add the five non-negotiable closes from references/discovery-method.md §4 (decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure). These are asked on every call.
  6. Produce the prep pack (see Output). Include an "If they say X, go to Y" branch table for the 3 most likely pivots.

Mode B — synthesize

  1. Read the notes once end-to-end before extracting anything. Note what was not said (no numbers, no owner named, no timeline).
  2. Extract every pain statement verbatim into the pain/impact/urgency matrix using the scoring rubric in references/discovery-method.md §3. A pain with no stated impact scores Impact = To be baselined · owner to be named, never a guessed number.
  3. Update the hypothesis register: confirmed / killed / untested, with the quote that decides it.
  4. Build the gaps list: every fact the proposal or estimate will need that the call did not produce (volumes, counts, contract dates, team size, budget range). Assign an owner on our side to chase each gap and the client-side person who likely holds it.
  5. Decision point — qualify: apply the qualification gate in references/discovery-method.md §5. Output one of PURSUE / PURSUE-WITH-CONDITIONS / PARK with the two or three facts that drove it. Do not soften a PARK.
  6. Draft the follow-up note (≤120 words, client-facing): what we heard, what we will bring next, the two or three things we need from them, by when.

Both modes

  1. Run the self-check. Strip anything that looks like a figure you did not hear or read.

## Starting points
- **New** — before the call: a timed question plan for the attendees' personas from the vertical's question bank, with the five closes all open and an empty pain matrix.
- **Existing** — after the call: your notes or transcript are synthesised into the pain matrix and the five closes; anything the notes do not say stays an owned TBD.

## When to use
- "Prep me for the discovery call with <client> on <topic>."
- "Here are my notes from the workshop — synthesize them."
- "What should I ask a <vertical> CIO about <platform/initiative>?"
- NOT for: company background before a pitch (`client-research-brief`), RFP question lists (`rfp-compliance-matrix`), or pitch rehearsal (`orals-prep`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Client name, vertical (EdTech / Retail / Manufacturing / Travel / other) | yes | user |
| Opportunity context: initiative, platform(s), trigger event | yes | user / brief |
| Attendee list with titles (or "unknown") | no | user |
| Mode: `prep` (before call) or `synthesize` (after call) | yes | user |
| Raw notes / transcript (synthesize mode only) | yes in synthesize | file |
| Time available for the call (minutes) | no — default 45 | user |

If a required input is missing, ask once. Do not invent the vertical, attendees, or the client's pain.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. Both apply to every output here.

### Mode A — prep
1. Classify the opportunity: vertical, buyer persona (CIO / CDO / VP Apps / COO / Head of Supply Chain / Provost / CFO), and initiative type (modernization, migration, AI, integration, cost-out, compliance). If the vertical is outside the four banks, use `references/question-banks/retail.md` as the structural base and say so.
2. Write 3–5 **hypotheses** before writing questions (`references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md` §1). Each hypothesis states a suspected pain, who owns it, and what evidence would confirm or kill it. Questions exist to test hypotheses, not to fill time.
3. Load the vertical bank from `references/question-banks/<vertical>.md`. Select 12–18 questions using the time budget rule: ~3 minutes per open question, reserve 20% for their questions. Tag each selected question with the hypothesis it tests (H1…H5) and the persona it is aimed at.
4. Order questions using the funnel in `references/discovery-method.md` §2: situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision process → constraints. Never open with a technology question.
5. Add the five **non-negotiable closes** from `references/discovery-method.md` §4 (decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure). These are asked on every call.
6. Produce the prep pack (see Output). Include an "If they say X, go to Y" branch table for the 3 most likely pivots.

### Mode B — synthesize
1. Read the notes once end-to-end before extracting anything. Note what was *not* said (no numbers, no owner named, no timeline).
2. Extract every pain statement verbatim into the pain/impact/urgency matrix using the scoring rubric in `references/discovery-method.md` §3. A pain with no stated impact scores Impact = `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, never a guessed number.
3. Update the hypothesis register: confirmed / killed / untested, with the quote that decides it.
4. Build the **gaps list**: every fact the proposal or estimate will need that the call did not produce (volumes, counts, contract dates, team size, budget range). Assign an owner on our side to chase each gap and the client-side person who likely holds it.
5. Decision point — qualify: apply the qualification gate in `references/discovery-method.md` §5. Output one of `PURSUE / PURSUE-WITH-CONDITIONS / PARK` with the two or three facts that drove it. Do not soften a PARK.
6. Draft the follow-up note (≤120 words, client-facing): what we heard, what we will bring next, the two or three things we need from them, by when.

### Both modes
7. Run the self-check. Strip anything that looks like a figure you did not hear or read.

## Output
| Mode | File | Format |
|---|---|---|
| prep | `discovery-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` | Sections: Hypotheses (table) · Question plan (table: #, question, persona, hypothesis, time) · Branches · Closes · Pre-reads to send |
| synthesize | `discovery-synthesis-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` | Sections: Bottom line (qualification call) · Pain/Impact/Urgency matrix · Hypothesis register · Gaps list (table with owners) · Follow-up note · Parked items |

Template: `assets/discovery-pack-template.md`.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every question maps to a hypothesis; no orphan questions
- [ ] No number in the synthesis that is not a verbatim quote or marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Five closes present (prep) or answered/gapped (synthesize)
- [ ] Qualification call stated on line 1 of the synthesis
- [ ] Gaps list has an owner for every row
- [ ] Follow-up note contains no internal commentary and no other-client references
- [ ] Tables for questions, matrix, hypotheses, gaps

## References
- `references/discovery-method.md` — funnel, scoring rubric, closes, qualification gate
- `references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md` — hypothesis writing, listening-for-absence, synthesis patterns
- `references/question-banks/edtech.md`, `references/question-banks/retail.md`, `references/question-banks/manufacturing.md`, `references/question-banks/travel.md` — vertical banks
- `assets/discovery-pack-template.md` — output template

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/discovery-interview --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/discovery-interview`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

card: Effort and price at P50 / P80 / P90
name: effort-estimator
description: Use when the user asks to size, estimate, or price a services engagement — "give me the price for <client>", "give me P50/P80/P90, staffing and price", "run the estimate on this WBS and rate card", "re-estimate and show what changed", or sizing a platform migration (e.g. "size the MuleSoft-to-Apigee migration") from interface counts by complexity band an assessment already produced. bodyHtml:
effort-estimator

In a conversation: build the estimate now

The reply is the estimate, about 1,000 tokens: compact tables (WBS ≤ 12 rows), one line per point, no preamble — all seven parts must fit, so never spend the reply on one part. Never claim a Monte Carlo figure you did not compute: P50/P80/P90 come from the estimate.py run (quote them exactly when its output is in the conversation, else [from estimate.py run — owner: Estimation lead]); never write only a command.

  • The request carries scope counts (e.g. "118 interfaces: 60 simple, 40 medium, 18 complex"), even when it says the actuals, WBS or rate card are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the estimate in this reply, in this order. Never reply with only a request for files.
    1. WBS in the assets/wbs-template.csv columns (task_id, phase, work_package, task, role, driver_group, count, unit_o, unit_m, unit_p, …, basis, predecessors, notes): parametric rows per band (count × unit effort, basis PAR, citing the prior actuals as the unit source), plus explicit PM, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare and KT packages. Unit efforts not in the conversation are To be baselined · owner to be named naming the attached actuals as source.
    2. Model: the exact command — python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md — and a results table P50 / P80 / P90 effort and cost with contingency = P80 − P50 as its own column; figures not yet computed read To be baselined · owner: Estimation lead, from the estimate.py run.
    3. Confidence quoted per references/estimation-method.md §4, and why: fixed price, inventory known → P80; fixed price, inventory unconfirmed → P90 or assessment first; T&M → P50 with P80 as NTE.
    4. Staffing table by role and phase with onshore/offshore split, allocations between 20% and 100%, leverage ratio.
    5. Price and margin: price only from the supplied rate card (effort × bill rate), margin at P50 and at P80; rates not visible are To be baselined · owner to be named, never typical rates.
    6. Assumptions: every count and unit effort as a row with its source.
    7. Memo in the assets/estimate-summary-template.md sections: Bottom line, Basis of estimate (basis mix ANA/PAR/JUD %), Assumptions, Exclusions, Risks to the estimate and de-risking, Sensitivity, Staffing, Price-to-win.
  • WBS given (or said to be attached), no rate card ("here is the WBS, give me the price"): ask once for the rate card with its columns (role, grade, location, cost_rate, bill_rate, currency, valid_until), and in the same reply produce the effort-only output: | | P50 | P80 | P90 | Contingency (P80 − P50) | effort row (from the WBS run, or [from estimate.py run] when the WBS content is not visible), the staffing table by role and phase, and a price row that reads exactly Price: To be baselined · owner to be named — no rate card supplied; no rates assumed.
  • No WBS and no scope ("give me the price for Acme"): ask once for the WBS (assets/wbs-template.csv) — estimate.py cannot run without it — and the rate card; invent no tasks.
  • WBS and rate card attached: line 1 the command — python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rates.csv --iterations 20000 --seed 7 --out estimate.md --memo estimate-memo.md --client <client> [--previous estimate-previous.json] [--draft-only] (+ --json → estimate.json) — then P50/P80/P90 with contingency = P80 − P50, staffing, price and margin, and the memo in the template sections (Bottom line, Basis of estimate, Assumptions, Risks). draft_only / "no LLM": the memo is written from the run's figures, labelled as a draft, every figure tracing to estimate.md.
  • Re-estimate with a previous estimate.json: a change table | Item | Previous | Now | Change | for P80 effort, each phase (a phase absent before is "new"), and price at P80 — previous values copied exactly from the file, current values from this run — and the memo repeats that table.
  • No scope or WBS at all: ask once, in one list, for the scope counts, phases, commercial model and rate card; say no counts, unit efforts or rates will be invented.
  • Asked to use an "industry-standard" unit effort or quote fixed price at P50: decline in one line (there is no sourced industry standard; a P50 fixed price carries no contingency, so it loses money half the time). Do not supply an industry figure. Use the user's own figure (e.g. 3 days per interface) only if they confirm it as their assumption, labelled JUD, with the anchor source To be baselined · owner to be named. Flag that JUD > 30% of effort makes the estimate low-confidence and recommend an assessment phase or per-unit pricing with a count band. Do not stop at asking — show, in this reply: | Unit effort | 3 days/interface — user's figure, basis JUD | anchor source To be baselined · owner to be named |; Basis mix: JUD 100% > 30% → low confidence → recommend an assessment phase, or per-unit pricing with a count band; | | P50 | P80 | Contingency (P80 − P50) | side by side; and the recommendation P80/P90 fixed or T&M with a P80 NTE.

Starting points

  • New — your WBS (and rate card) is modelled: P10–P90 effort, phases, variance contributors, staffing, cost and price; the model step writes the memo, or with draft_only the memo is written from the run's figures, every number traceable.
  • Existing — add previous (the earlier run's estimate.json): the re-estimate shows what changed — totals, each phase and price at P80, previous → now — in the report and the memo.

When to use

  • "Size the <initiative> engagement."
  • "Give me P50/P80 for this WBS."
  • "What team do we need and what is the onshore/offshore split?"
  • "Does this price hold margin?"
  • NOT for: benefits and ROI (value-case-builder), interface-level complexity scoring (integration-migration-assessor feeds this skill), narrative (proposal-writer).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Scope definition: deliverables, counts (interfaces, components, sites, users), phasesyesdiscovery synthesis / architecture doc / assessor output
Rate card CSV (role, location, cost rate, bill rate, currency)yes for cost/price; else effort-onlyuser file (assets/rate-card.example.csv shows the layout)
Constraints: deadline, team-size cap, onshore/offshore policy, client-side availabilitynouser
Target margin or price-to-win (if known)nouser
Prior actuals for similar work (if any)nouser file

If scope counts are missing, ask once; otherwise estimate per unit and mark counts To be baselined · owner to be named so the total scales. If the rate card is missing, produce effort and staffing only; never invent rates.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Decompose to a WBS per references/estimation-method.md §1: phases → work packages → tasks sized 2–15 person-days. Each task carries a driver (count × unit effort) or a fixed effort, a role mix, and a dependency. Keep management, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, and knowledge transfer as explicit packages; they are the most frequently omitted.
  2. Assign 3-point estimates (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic) per task using the calibration rules in §2. Pessimistic is the "things go wrong but not catastrophic" case, typically 1.5–3× most-likely. Record the basis for each: analogy (prior actual), parametric (count × unit), or expert judgment. Expert judgment on >30% of effort is a flag in the output.
  3. Run the model: python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md. Outputs P50/P80/P90 effort and cost, per-phase distribution, staffing table, and a sensitivity list (tasks contributing most variance). Without --rates, the script outputs effort only. Rates match on role AND location (add a WBS location column when a role is priced onshore and offshore); a mixed-currency card needs --currency and sourced --fx CUR=rate, otherwise the script stops. The script does not compute duration; the memo derives it from the critical path and staffing plan or marks it To be baselined · owner: Estimation lead.
  4. Decision point — confidence level to quote. Per §4: fixed-price → P80 minimum, P90 for migrations with unknown inventories; T&M → P50 as the estimate with P80 as the not-to-exceed; assessments → fixed at P80 with a short duration. State which was used and why.
  5. Build the staffing pyramid per references/staffing-and-rates.md: roles, grades, allocation by phase, onshore/offshore split against policy and client constraints, ramp-up and ramp-down, leverage ratio. Check span of control and that no role is allocated above 100% or below a useful minimum (20%).
  6. Cost and margin: cost = effort × cost rate; price = effort × bill rate or target-margin markup; contingency = (P80 − P50) shown explicitly, not buried in rates. Compare with price-to-win if given; if the gap exceeds 15%, list scope or mix levers rather than cutting the estimate.
  7. Write the estimate memo on assets/estimate-summary-template.md: bottom line (P80 effort, duration, team, price or "price pending rate card"), basis of estimate, assumptions (every count and rate), exclusions, risks to the estimate, sensitivity.
  8. Run the self-check.

Self-check

  • [ ] WBS includes PM, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, KT packages
  • [ ] Every task has basis (analogy / parametric / judgment); judgment share reported
  • [ ] Confidence level chosen and justified against the commercial model
  • [ ] Contingency shown explicitly as P80 − P50
  • [ ] Rates only from the supplied rate card; no rates if none supplied
  • [ ] Every count is an assumption row with To be baselined · owner to be named where unconfirmed
  • [ ] Staffing allocations between 20% and 100%; leverage ratio stated
  • [ ] Totals reconcile across WBS, model output, and memo

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/effort-estimator --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/effort-estimator). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

bodyMd:
# effort-estimator

## In a conversation: build the estimate now
The reply **is the estimate**, about 1,000 tokens: compact tables (WBS ≤ 12 rows), one line per point, no preamble — all seven parts must fit, so never spend the reply on one part. Never claim a Monte Carlo figure you did not compute: P50/P80/P90 come from the `estimate.py` run (quote them exactly when its output is in the conversation, else `[from estimate.py run — owner: Estimation lead]`); never write only a command.
- **The request carries scope counts** (e.g. "118 interfaces: 60 simple, 40 medium, 18 complex"), even when it says the actuals, WBS or rate card are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the estimate **in this reply**, in this order. Never reply with only a request for files.
  1. **WBS** in the `assets/wbs-template.csv` columns (`task_id, phase, work_package, task, role, driver_group, count, unit_o, unit_m, unit_p, …, basis, predecessors, notes`): parametric rows per band (count × unit effort, basis `PAR`, citing the prior actuals as the unit source), plus explicit PM, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare and KT packages. Unit efforts not in the conversation are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the attached actuals as source.
  2. **Model**: the exact command — `python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md` — and a results table P50 / P80 / P90 effort and cost with **contingency = P80 − P50** as its own column; figures not yet computed read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead, from the estimate.py run]`.
  3. **Confidence quoted** per `references/estimation-method.md` §4, and why: fixed price, inventory known → P80; fixed price, inventory unconfirmed → P90 or assessment first; T&M → P50 with P80 as NTE.
  4. **Staffing table** by role and phase with onshore/offshore split, allocations between 20% and 100%, leverage ratio.
  5. **Price and margin**: price only from the supplied rate card (effort × bill rate), margin at P50 and at P80; rates not visible are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, never typical rates.
  6. **Assumptions**: every count and unit effort as a row with its source.
  7. **Memo** in the `assets/estimate-summary-template.md` sections: Bottom line, Basis of estimate (basis mix ANA/PAR/JUD %), Assumptions, Exclusions, Risks to the estimate and de-risking, Sensitivity, Staffing, Price-to-win.
- **WBS given (or said to be attached), no rate card** ("here is the WBS, give me the price"): ask once for the rate card with its columns (`role, grade, location, cost_rate, bill_rate, currency, valid_until`), and in the same reply produce the **effort-only output**: `| | P50 | P80 | P90 | Contingency (P80 − P50) |` effort row (from the WBS run, or `[from estimate.py run]` when the WBS content is not visible), the staffing table by role and phase, and a price row that reads exactly **`Price: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] — no rate card supplied; no rates assumed`**.
- **No WBS and no scope** ("give me the price for Acme"): ask once for the WBS (`assets/wbs-template.csv`) — `estimate.py` cannot run without it — and the rate card; invent no tasks.
- **WBS and rate card attached**: line 1 the command — `python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rates.csv --iterations 20000 --seed 7 --out estimate.md --memo estimate-memo.md --client <client> [--previous estimate-previous.json] [--draft-only]` (+ `--json` → `estimate.json`) — then P50/P80/P90 with contingency = P80 − P50, staffing, price and margin, and the memo in the template sections (Bottom line, Basis of estimate, Assumptions, Risks). `draft_only` / "no LLM": the memo is written from the run's figures, **labelled as a draft**, every figure tracing to `estimate.md`.
- **Re-estimate with a previous `estimate.json`**: a change table `| Item | Previous | Now | Change |` for P80 effort, each phase (a phase absent before is "new"), and price at P80 — previous values copied exactly from the file, current values from this run — and the memo repeats that table.
- **No scope or WBS at all**: ask once, in one list, for the scope counts, phases, commercial model and rate card; say no counts, unit efforts or rates will be invented.
- **Asked to use an "industry-standard" unit effort or quote fixed price at P50**: decline in one line (there is no sourced industry standard; a P50 fixed price carries no contingency, so it loses money half the time). Do not supply an industry figure. Use the user's own figure (e.g. 3 days per interface) only if they confirm it as their assumption, labelled `JUD`, with the anchor source `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Flag that `JUD` > 30% of effort makes the estimate low-confidence and recommend an assessment phase or per-unit pricing with a count band. Do not stop at asking — show, in this reply: `| Unit effort | 3 days/interface — user's figure, basis JUD | anchor source [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] |`; `Basis mix: JUD 100% > 30% → low confidence → recommend an assessment phase, or per-unit pricing with a count band`; `| | P50 | P80 | Contingency (P80 − P50) |` side by side; and the recommendation P80/P90 fixed or T&M with a P80 NTE.

## Starting points
- **New** — your WBS (and rate card) is modelled: P10–P90 effort, phases, variance contributors, staffing, cost and price; the model step writes the memo, or with `draft_only` the memo is written from the run's figures, every number traceable.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (the earlier run's `estimate.json`): the re-estimate shows what changed — totals, each phase and price at P80, previous → now — in the report and the memo.

## When to use
- "Size the <initiative> engagement."
- "Give me P50/P80 for this WBS."
- "What team do we need and what is the onshore/offshore split?"
- "Does this price hold margin?"
- NOT for: benefits and ROI (`value-case-builder`), interface-level complexity scoring (`integration-migration-assessor` feeds this skill), narrative (`proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Scope definition: deliverables, counts (interfaces, components, sites, users), phases | yes | discovery synthesis / architecture doc / assessor output |
| Rate card CSV (role, location, cost rate, bill rate, currency) | yes for cost/price; else effort-only | user file (`assets/rate-card.example.csv` shows the layout) |
| Constraints: deadline, team-size cap, onshore/offshore policy, client-side availability | no | user |
| Target margin or price-to-win (if known) | no | user |
| Prior actuals for similar work (if any) | no | user file |

If scope counts are missing, ask once; otherwise estimate per unit and mark counts `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` so the total scales. If the rate card is missing, produce effort and staffing only; never invent rates.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Decompose to a WBS** per `references/estimation-method.md` §1: phases → work packages → tasks sized 2–15 person-days. Each task carries a driver (count × unit effort) or a fixed effort, a role mix, and a dependency. Keep management, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, and knowledge transfer as explicit packages; they are the most frequently omitted.
2. **Assign 3-point estimates** (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic) per task using the calibration rules in §2. Pessimistic is the "things go wrong but not catastrophic" case, typically 1.5–3× most-likely. Record the basis for each: analogy (prior actual), parametric (count × unit), or expert judgment. Expert judgment on >30% of effort is a flag in the output.
3. **Run the model**: `python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md`. Outputs P50/P80/P90 effort and cost, per-phase distribution, staffing table, and a sensitivity list (tasks contributing most variance). Without `--rates`, the script outputs effort only. Rates match on role AND location (add a WBS `location` column when a role is priced onshore and offshore); a mixed-currency card needs `--currency` and sourced `--fx CUR=rate`, otherwise the script stops. The script does not compute duration; the memo derives it from the critical path and staffing plan or marks it `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead]`.
4. **Decision point — confidence level to quote.** Per §4: fixed-price → P80 minimum, P90 for migrations with unknown inventories; T&M → P50 as the estimate with P80 as the not-to-exceed; assessments → fixed at P80 with a short duration. State which was used and why.
5. **Build the staffing pyramid** per `references/staffing-and-rates.md`: roles, grades, allocation by phase, onshore/offshore split against policy and client constraints, ramp-up and ramp-down, leverage ratio. Check span of control and that no role is allocated above 100% or below a useful minimum (20%).
6. **Cost and margin**: cost = effort × cost rate; price = effort × bill rate or target-margin markup; contingency = (P80 − P50) shown explicitly, not buried in rates. Compare with price-to-win if given; if the gap exceeds 15%, list scope or mix levers rather than cutting the estimate.
7. **Write the estimate memo** on `assets/estimate-summary-template.md`: bottom line (P80 effort, duration, team, price or "price pending rate card"), basis of estimate, assumptions (every count and rate), exclusions, risks to the estimate, sensitivity.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File |
|---|---|
| WBS with 3-point estimates | `wbs-<client>-<initiative>.csv` (layout: `assets/wbs-template.csv`) |
| Model output | `estimate-<client>-<initiative>.md` (from script) |
| Estimate memo | `estimate-memo-<client>-<initiative>.md` (template: `assets/estimate-summary-template.md`) |

## Self-check
- [ ] WBS includes PM, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, KT packages
- [ ] Every task has basis (analogy / parametric / judgment); judgment share reported
- [ ] Confidence level chosen and justified against the commercial model
- [ ] Contingency shown explicitly as P80 − P50
- [ ] Rates only from the supplied rate card; no rates if none supplied
- [ ] Every count is an assumption row with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` where unconfirmed
- [ ] Staffing allocations between 20% and 100%; leverage ratio stated
- [ ] Totals reconcile across WBS, model output, and memo

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/effort-estimator --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/effort-estimator`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## References
- `references/estimation-method.md` — WBS rules, 3-point calibration, PERT/Monte Carlo, confidence selection, sensitivity
- `references/staffing-and-rates.md` — pyramid design, onshore/offshore, leverage, margin sanity, rate-card contract
- `assets/wbs-template.csv` — WBS input layout
- `assets/rate-card.example.csv` — rate-card layout with EXAMPLE placeholder rows (replace with real rates; never ship)
- `assets/estimate-summary-template.md` — memo template
- `scripts/estimate.py` — PERT + Monte Carlo, staffing table, cost roll-up

bodyHtml:
exec-deck-redline

In a conversation: redline now

  • The request carries the audience, the decision and the slot — including when the deck and source documents are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: produce the redline in this reply. Never reply with only a request for the file. In this order:
    1. Storyline as found in ≤6 bullets, preserved; no new narrative (where slide text is not in the conversation, mark each bullet [confirm against slide n] rather than inventing content).
    2. Decision test — what the audience must believe after slide 1 and approve by the last slide.
    3. Rubric score before and after (assets/redline-rubric.md).
    4. Redline table — every slide gets a verdict [KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]; each [SHARPEN] row has the full rewritten title (an assertion, ≤12 words) and body.
    5. Numbers check against the named sources (e.g. the estimate memo, the discovery synthesis); every unsourced number, role or date becomes To be baselined · owner to be named.
    6. Time fit — about one body slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck (30 minutes → ~15 body slides); overflow to the appendix and a parked list with destinations.
    7. Executive summary slide — the decision, three reasons (numbers or markers), next steps with owners and dates.
    8. Speaker notes ≤60 words per kept or sharpened slide, aligned to slide content · Open items with owners.
  • No decision, audience or slot ("tidy up these slides"): ask once, in one list, for the audience, the decision the deck must obtain and the time slot. Do not begin slide rewrites without the decision test. Offer a density-only pass (titles, one point per slide, tables for lists) as the fallback if the user has no decision in mind, labelled "density-only — not a decision redline".
  • Asked to put an invented savings figure, go-live date or assumed sponsor on a slide: say in one line that the redline marks unknowns rather than inventing figures, roles or dates, because the CFO will hold the team to them. Keep the slide (e.g. the business-case slide stays in the storyline as [SHARPEN]/[TBD], not cut) and show: savings To be baselined · owner to be named with a note naming the source that would confirm it (the value case); go-live To be baselined · owner to be named tied to the estimate's critical path, not a chosen quarter; sponsor To be baselined · owner to be named, no assumed name or role. Never print the requested figure, quarter or person anywhere.

Starting points

  • Existing — your deck is read slide by slide into a ledger with every unsourced figure listed; the model step writes the redline (storyline kept, [KEEP]/[SHARPEN]/[CUT]/[ADD]/[TBD]), or with draft_only a mechanical redline flags unsourced figures, label titles and dense slides; the verdicts are applied back to the ledger.
  • Only for existing: a redline always starts from a deck that already exists; to build a deck from nothing, start with proposal-writer or value-case-builder.

When to use

  • "Redline this steering-committee deck."
  • "Sharpen these slides for the CIO — keep the story."
  • "Review the board pack before Friday."
  • NOT for: building a new deck (produce content with the domain skill, then this skill for the pass), documents (proposal-writer, sow-drafter).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
The deck (PPTX, PDF, or slide text export)yesfile
Audience and the decision the deck must obtainyesuser
Time slot (minutes)yesuser
Source documents behind the numbers (if any)nofiles
Constraints: template, slide limit, mandated sectionsnouser

If the audience or the decision is missing, ask once; a deck without a decision cannot be sharpened, only tidied. Missing source documents or slot constraints do not stop the redline: unsourced numbers are marked To be baselined · owner to be named.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md (redline convention) and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first. The user's standing instruction applies: stay close to the original storyline and sharpen it; do not replace the narrative; no invented dollar figures, roles, or dates.

  1. Read the whole deck before touching any slide. Write the storyline as it stands in ≤6 bullets (situation → complication → decision asked → options → recommendation → next steps, or whatever the author used). If the storyline is coherent, it stays. If it has a gap (e.g., no decision slide), that is an [ADD], not a rewrite.
  2. Set the decision test. From the audience and decision input: what must the reader believe after slide 1, and what must they approve by the last slide? Every slide is judged against this.
  3. Score the deck with assets/redline-rubric.md (storyline, titles, evidence, so-what, density, numbers discipline, time fit). Record the score before and after; the after score is the self-check.
  4. Redline slide by slide per references/redline-method.md:
    • [KEEP] unchanged.
    • [SHARPEN] rewrite the title as an assertion; cut to the one point; convert prose to a table or a single chart spec; state the "so what" in the first line of the body. Provide the rewritten text in full.
    • [CUT] with reason (duplicates, no decision relevance, appendix material) and where the content moves.
    • [ADD] only for storyline gaps; state source for any content added.
    • [TBD] for every number, role, date without a source in the provided materials: To be baselined · owner to be named.
  5. Decision point — time fit. Count body slides vs time slot using the rule in the method (§4): roughly one slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck, less for discussion. Over the limit → move to appendix, do not shrink fonts.
  6. Write speaker notes for every kept/sharpened body slide: ≤60 words, the spoken point, the number to say, the transition. Notes never contain content absent from the slide or the sources.
  7. Produce the executive summary slide if missing (one slide: decision asked, three reasons with numbers or [TBD], next steps with owners and dates). Place it as slide 2 (after title) or 1 if there is no title slide.
  8. Deliver: redline table, rewritten slide text in order, speaker notes, parked list (content cut with destination), and the before/after rubric score. If the user supplied a PPTX and asks for the file edited, apply changes with the pptx tooling available in the session; otherwise deliver text ready to paste.
  9. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: deck-redline-<client-or-topic>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md
  • Sections: Storyline as found (≤6 bullets) · Decision test · Rubric score before/after · Redline table (slide #, original title, verdict, reason, new title, body change summary) · Rewritten slides (full text, in order) · Speaker notes · Parked content · Open items ([TBD] list with owners)

Self-check

  • [ ] Storyline preserved; changes are sharpening, not replacement
  • [ ] Every title is an assertion with a number or consequence
  • [ ] Every number, role, date has a source or To be baselined · owner to be named
  • [ ] No slide carries more than one point; 3+ items are tables
  • [ ] Slide count fits the time slot; overflow in appendix
  • [ ] Speaker notes ≤60 words, aligned to slide content
  • [ ] Executive summary slide present with decision, reasons, next steps
  • [ ] No banned words; no author or other-client references

References

  • references/redline-method.md — storyline preservation, title assertions, slide patterns, density rules, time fit, speaker-note rules
  • assets/redline-rubric.md — scoring rubric and redline table layout
  • assets/storyline-checklist.md — storyline integrity checklist by deck type

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/exec-deck-redline --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/exec-deck-redline). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

bodyMd:
# exec-deck-redline

## In a conversation: redline now
- **The request carries the audience, the decision and the slot** — including when the deck and source documents are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: produce the redline **in this reply**. Never reply with only a request for the file. In this order:
  1. **Storyline as found** in ≤6 bullets, preserved; no new narrative (where slide text is not in the conversation, mark each bullet `[confirm against slide n]` rather than inventing content).
  2. **Decision test** — what the audience must believe after slide 1 and approve by the last slide.
  3. **Rubric score before and after** (`assets/redline-rubric.md`).
  4. **Redline table** — every slide gets a verdict `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]`; each `[SHARPEN]` row has the full rewritten title (an assertion, ≤12 words) and body.
  5. **Numbers check** against the named sources (e.g. the estimate memo, the discovery synthesis); every unsourced number, role or date becomes `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
  6. **Time fit** — about one body slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck (30 minutes → ~15 body slides); overflow to the appendix and a **parked list** with destinations.
  7. **Executive summary slide** — the decision, three reasons (numbers or markers), next steps with owners and dates.
  8. **Speaker notes** ≤60 words per kept or sharpened slide, aligned to slide content · **Open items** with owners.
- **No decision, audience or slot** ("tidy up these slides"): ask once, in one list, for the audience, the decision the deck must obtain and the time slot. Do not begin slide rewrites without the decision test. Offer a **density-only pass** (titles, one point per slide, tables for lists) as the fallback if the user has no decision in mind, labelled "density-only — not a decision redline".
- **Asked to put an invented savings figure, go-live date or assumed sponsor on a slide**: say in one line that the redline marks unknowns rather than inventing figures, roles or dates, because the CFO will hold the team to them. Keep the slide (e.g. the business-case slide stays in the storyline as `[SHARPEN]`/`[TBD]`, not cut) and show: savings `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` with a note naming the source that would confirm it (the value case); go-live `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` tied to the estimate's critical path, not a chosen quarter; sponsor `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, no assumed name or role. Never print the requested figure, quarter or person anywhere.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — your deck is read slide by slide into a ledger with every unsourced figure listed; the model step writes the redline (storyline kept, [KEEP]/[SHARPEN]/[CUT]/[ADD]/[TBD]), or with `draft_only` a mechanical redline flags unsourced figures, label titles and dense slides; the verdicts are applied back to the ledger.
- Only for existing: a redline always starts from a deck that already exists; to build a deck from nothing, start with proposal-writer or value-case-builder.

## When to use
- "Redline this steering-committee deck."
- "Sharpen these slides for the CIO — keep the story."
- "Review the board pack before Friday."
- NOT for: building a new deck (produce content with the domain skill, then this skill for the pass), documents (`proposal-writer`, `sow-drafter`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The deck (PPTX, PDF, or slide text export) | yes | file |
| Audience and the decision the deck must obtain | yes | user |
| Time slot (minutes) | yes | user |
| Source documents behind the numbers (if any) | no | files |
| Constraints: template, slide limit, mandated sections | no | user |

If the audience or the decision is missing, ask once; a deck without a decision cannot be sharpened, only tidied. Missing source documents or slot constraints do not stop the redline: unsourced numbers are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` (redline convention) and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. The user's standing instruction applies: stay close to the original storyline and sharpen it; do not replace the narrative; no invented dollar figures, roles, or dates.

1. **Read the whole deck before touching any slide.** Write the storyline as it stands in ≤6 bullets (situation → complication → decision asked → options → recommendation → next steps, or whatever the author used). If the storyline is coherent, it stays. If it has a gap (e.g., no decision slide), that is an `[ADD]`, not a rewrite.
2. **Set the decision test.** From the audience and decision input: what must the reader believe after slide 1, and what must they approve by the last slide? Every slide is judged against this.
3. **Score the deck** with `assets/redline-rubric.md` (storyline, titles, evidence, so-what, density, numbers discipline, time fit). Record the score before and after; the after score is the self-check.
4. **Redline slide by slide** per `references/redline-method.md`:
   - `[KEEP]` unchanged.
   - `[SHARPEN]` rewrite the title as an assertion; cut to the one point; convert prose to a table or a single chart spec; state the "so what" in the first line of the body. Provide the rewritten text in full.
   - `[CUT]` with reason (duplicates, no decision relevance, appendix material) and where the content moves.
   - `[ADD]` only for storyline gaps; state source for any content added.
   - `[TBD]` for every number, role, date without a source in the provided materials: `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
5. **Decision point — time fit.** Count body slides vs time slot using the rule in the method (§4): roughly one slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck, less for discussion. Over the limit → move to appendix, do not shrink fonts.
6. **Write speaker notes** for every kept/sharpened body slide: ≤60 words, the spoken point, the number to say, the transition. Notes never contain content absent from the slide or the sources.
7. **Produce the executive summary slide** if missing (one slide: decision asked, three reasons with numbers or `[TBD]`, next steps with owners and dates). Place it as slide 2 (after title) or 1 if there is no title slide.
8. **Deliver**: redline table, rewritten slide text in order, speaker notes, parked list (content cut with destination), and the before/after rubric score. If the user supplied a PPTX and asks for the file edited, apply changes with the pptx tooling available in the session; otherwise deliver text ready to paste.
9. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `deck-redline-<client-or-topic>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections: Storyline as found (≤6 bullets) · Decision test · Rubric score before/after · Redline table (slide #, original title, verdict, reason, new title, body change summary) · Rewritten slides (full text, in order) · Speaker notes · Parked content · Open items (`[TBD]` list with owners)

## Self-check
- [ ] Storyline preserved; changes are sharpening, not replacement
- [ ] Every title is an assertion with a number or consequence
- [ ] Every number, role, date has a source or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] No slide carries more than one point; 3+ items are tables
- [ ] Slide count fits the time slot; overflow in appendix
- [ ] Speaker notes ≤60 words, aligned to slide content
- [ ] Executive summary slide present with decision, reasons, next steps
- [ ] No banned words; no author or other-client references

## References
- `references/redline-method.md` — storyline preservation, title assertions, slide patterns, density rules, time fit, speaker-note rules
- `assets/redline-rubric.md` — scoring rubric and redline table layout
- `assets/storyline-checklist.md` — storyline integrity checklist by deck type

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/exec-deck-redline --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/exec-deck-redline`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

integration-migration-assessor

In a conversation: assess now

  • The request carries the inventory (or its contents): produce the readout in this reply. Report the share of unknown factors and whether the assessment is provisional; list retirement candidates with owners to confirm before effort is discussed; a band distribution table with outliers explained; a wave plan (wave 0 foundation, a representative wave 1, balanced middle waves, dependencies enforced, cutovers outside the client's freeze windows, entry/exit criteria); TCO lines that cite the client's contract for licence cost, with migration cost To be baselined · owner to be named until the effort estimate exists; handoffs to effort-estimator and solution-architecture-doc.
  • No inventory, only a count: ask once for the inventory and offer the collection template (assets/inventory-columns.md) and the minimum viable column set for a provisional assessment. Never synthesize an inventory or a band distribution from a count.
  • Asked to use list prices, treat blanks as simple, or give a ballpark savings figure: say in one line why not (blank factors scored simple are the main cause of overrun; vendor list prices from memory are not the client's contract). Score blanks as unknown (mid-band, flagged); show licence cost and savings as To be baselined · owner to be named naming the client contract as the source; state the TCO direction qualitatively at most; give next steps with owners.

Starting points

  • Existing — the inventory of your current estate is scored, banded and planned into waves, the TCO is built only from the rate inputs you supply, and the readout is written by the model step or, with draft_only, assembled from the two summaries with every figure copied verbatim.
  • Only for existing: an assessment always scores an integration estate that already runs; there is nothing to assess from scratch.

When to use

  • "Assess <client>'s MuleSoft/Boomi/ESB/Informatica estate for migration to <target>."
  • "Score this interface inventory and give me waves."
  • "Build the TCO comparison for staying vs migrating."
  • NOT for: drawing the target architecture (solution-architecture-doc), P50/P80 effort (effort-estimator), full business case with non-platform benefits (value-case-builder).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Interface inventory CSV (one row per interface/API/flow; columns per assets/inventory-columns.md)yesclient export / discovery / platform admin console export
Source and target platforms (or "target to be selected")yesuser
Current platform cost facts: licence, infrastructure, support/run team, contract endno — TCO is To be baselined · owner to be named without themclient / user
Constraints: freeze windows, contract end dates, dependent programs (ERP upgrade), compliancenodiscovery
Prior migration actuals (unit effort per band) if anynouser

If the inventory is missing, ask once; offer assets/inventory-columns.md as the collection template. Never synthesize an inventory.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Validate the inventory: run python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --validate. It reports missing columns, blank factor cells, and duplicates. Blank factor cells score as "unknown" (mid-band with a flag), never as "simple". Report the unknown share; above 25% the assessment is provisional and says so.
  2. Score complexity with python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --out scored.csv --waves 4. Factors and weights per references/complexity-scoring.md (pattern, transformation logic, protocol/connector availability on target, endpoints, data volume, error handling and orchestration, security, test coverage, documentation, business criticality). Review the band distribution (Simple / Medium / Complex / Very complex) against what discovery said; investigate outliers.
  3. Decision point — migration approach per band. Apply references/migration-factory-method.md §2: Simple → automated/tool-assisted conversion with templated tests; Medium → factory with pattern templates; Complex → design-led with refactor; Very complex → candidates for redesign, retirement, or re-platform outside the factory. Retirement candidates (unused, duplicate, superseded) are identified first; they are the cheapest migration.
  4. Assign waves (script output, then adjust): wave 0 foundation; wave 1 representative simples; middle waves balance complexity and resolve dependencies; final wave long-tail and decommission. Respect freeze windows and dependent programs from constraints. Each wave gets entry/exit criteria and a rollback approach from §4 of the method.
  5. Build the TCO/ROI layout on assets/tco-model-spec.md (CSV layout spec) and assets/tco-model.md (markdown table layout): current run-rate (licence, infra, people, support, incidents) vs target run-rate, one-time migration cost (from effort-estimator, or To be baselined · owner to be named), timing of savings (only after decommission), 3–5-year view, payback, sensitivity on the two biggest drivers. Every figure sourced to a client document or marked. Licence savings are not realized until the source platform is decommissioned; model that date explicitly.
  6. Risk register for the migration: dual-run cost, connector gaps on target, skills, endpoint changes during migration, data drift, cutover windows, vendor cooperation; each with likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner.
  7. Write the assessment readout on assets/assessment-readout-template.md: bottom line (inventory size, band mix, approach, waves, TCO direction with confidence, decision asked), evidence, scoring results, wave plan, TCO layout, risks, next steps. Feed interface counts and bands to effort-estimator and the wave plan to solution-architecture-doc.
  8. Run the self-check.
