bodyMd:
# solution-architecture-doc

## In a conversation: write the document now
- **The request carries facts** (systems, interfaces, constraints, NFRs, dates, audience): write the architecture document **in this reply**. Do not ask for a file or JSON first, and never answer with only questions. Use what is given; mark each missing fact `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`; end with the few questions that would close those gaps.
- **The request carries no client facts at all**: ask once, in one list, for current-state facts, drivers and constraints, NFR expectations and the audience. Do not draw a current state from assumptions. You may offer a generic pattern catalogue, labelled "not client-specific".
- **Asked to invent NFR numbers or to "just pick" products**: say in one line why not (unsourced targets and undecided products become contractual and credibility risk). Show each target as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` with its measurement method and the discovery question that would set it; show products as role placeholders with `proposed` ADRs naming the client decision owner; offer the scored options table as the way to decide.

The document, in this order (CIO depth: 6–10 pages, the bottom line stands alone; ARB depth adds component, deployment and security views):
1. **Bottom line** — the target state in one paragraph, the top 3 decisions, the waves, the biggest risk, what is still open.
2. **Drivers and constraints** — each with its source.
3. **Current state** (context + container, Mermaid) from evidence only; every box source-tagged; unknown integrations dashed and listed as gaps.
4. **Options and recommendation** — at least two options scored on weighted criteria (show the arithmetic); the choice is ADR-001.
5. **Target state** (context + container, Mermaid C4) — undecided products as placeholders.
6. **Integration map** — interfaces grouped by pattern, with protocol, data, volume/SLA (sourced or marked) and wave.
7. **NFRs** — target, measurement method, source, design response; constraints such as data residency become NFRs.
8. **Security and data**, **operability and environments**.
9. **Migration waves** — goal, scope, entry and exit criteria, rollback, aligned to the stated dates.
10. **Decision log** (ADRs with owner and status), **risks** (likelihood × impact, owner, mitigation), **open items** with owners, **sources**.

## Starting points
- **New** — the target design becomes a decision-ready architecture document: bottom line, drivers, C4 context, container and deployment diagrams, integration map, migration waves (entry, exit, rollback), NFRs, security, scored options with ADRs, risks, decision log, open items and sources.
- **Existing** — add `current` (the estate as it runs today, same layout): the document gains a change view — containers kept, added, retired or re-platformed, integrations added, retired or re-patterned — and a decision-log row for every retirement and re-platform.

## When to use
- "Produce the target architecture for <client>'s <initiative>."
- "Draw the C4 context and container views for the proposal."
- "Write the NFRs and decision log for this design."
- "Review this architecture document before it goes to the client."
- NOT for: effort (`effort-estimator`), interface scoring and TCO (`integration-migration-assessor`), proposal prose (`proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Current-state facts: systems, platforms, integration inventory, environments, hosting | yes | discovery synthesis / assessor output / client docs |
| Drivers and constraints: objectives, compliance regimes, vendor decisions already made, budget shape, dates | yes | discovery synthesis / RFP |
| Stated NFR expectations (volumes, latency, availability, RPO/RTO, security) or "none stated" | yes | client docs / user |
| Audience: CIO deck-level vs architecture-review-board level | yes | user |
| Existing draft (review mode) | yes in review | file |

Missing facts never stop the draft: write what is evidenced, mark the rest `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, and ask for it at the end. Never draw a current-state diagram from assumptions.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Fix the audience and depth** per `references/architecture-method.md` §1. CIO-level: context view + container view + decisions + waves, 6–10 pages. ARB-level: add component views for the critical containers, full NFR table, deployment view, security view.
2. **Draw the current state first** (context + container) from evidence only. Every box carries a source tag (document, slide, interview). Unknown integrations are drawn dashed with a `?` label and listed as gaps. This diagram is the baseline the client will correct; invite correction explicitly.
3. **Decision point — architecture options.** Identify the 2–3 options that the drivers permit (e.g., strangler migration vs big-bang; single API gateway vs federated; event backbone vs point-to-point API). Score each against the weighted criteria in §3 of the method (fit to drivers, risk, cost shape, time to value, operability, lock-in). Record the chosen option as ADR-001 using `assets/adr-template.md`; the others become the "alternatives considered" section. Never present a single option as inevitable.
4. **Draw the target state** (context, container; component for critical containers at ARB depth) with the Mermaid C4 templates in `assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md`. Name every container with technology placeholders only where a product decision is still open; mark those `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
5. **Build the integration map**: table of interfaces (source, target, pattern, protocol, data, volume, SLA, owner, wave) from the assessor output or the inventory; group by pattern (sync API, async event, batch file, managed-file transfer). Volumes and SLAs come from sources or are marked.
6. **Write the NFRs** with `assets/nfr-checklist.md`: every applicable NFR gets a measurable target, a measurement method, a source for the target (client statement, regulation, SLA), and a design response. "High availability" is not an NFR; "99.9% monthly, measured at the gateway, excluding planned windows ≤4h/month" is.
7. **Log every significant decision** as an ADR (context, options, decision, consequences, status, owner, date). Significant = changes cost, risk, vendor lock-in, or operating model. Decisions the client must make are ADRs in `proposed` status with the client owner named.
8. **Plan migration waves** per §5 of the method: wave criteria (risk, dependency, business value, freeze windows), per-wave scope, entry/exit criteria, rollback approach, parallel-run strategy. Wave membership for interfaces comes from the assessor's wave assignment when it exists.
9. **Security, data, and operability views** at the depth the audience needs: identity and access model, data classification and residency, secrets, observability, environments and promotion path, DR.
10. **Review mode**: read the draft fully; check each section against the review rubric in `references/architecture-review-rubric.md`; produce `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]` findings with rewritten content; deliver the clean version.
11. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `architecture.md` (Mermaid blocks inline, for Git and Confluence) and `architecture.html` (the same document, printable, diagrams inline; Print → Save as PDF)
- `diagrams/context.svg`, `diagrams/container.svg`, `diagrams/deployment.svg` (C4 pictures for slides) and `architecture.drawio` (every view, editable in diagrams.net / Confluence)
- `adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md` per decision, with the weighted option scores; `nfr.csv`
- Sections: Bottom line (target state in one paragraph + top 3 decisions) · Drivers and constraints · Current state (diagrams + gaps) · Options and recommendation (scored table) · Target state (diagrams) · Integration map · NFRs · Security and data · Operability and environments · Migration waves · Decision log (ADR index) · Risks · Open items with owners
- Appendices: `adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md` per decision (template `assets/adr-template.md`)

## Self-check
- [ ] Current-state boxes each carry a source; unknowns dashed and listed as gaps
- [ ] ≥2 options scored on stated criteria before the recommendation
- [ ] Every NFR has target, measurement method, source, design response
- [ ] Every significant decision has an ADR with owner and status
- [ ] Every volume, SLA, count sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Waves have entry/exit criteria and rollback
- [ ] Product names appear only where decided; otherwise placeholders marked
- [ ] Diagrams render (valid Mermaid); each has a one-line caption stating what it shows
- [ ] No other-client architecture details, no author history

## References
- `references/architecture-method.md` — depth by audience, current-state evidence rules, option scoring, wave planning, views
- `references/architecture-review-rubric.md` — review criteria and scoring for existing documents
- `assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md` — Mermaid C4 context/container/component/deployment templates
- `assets/nfr-checklist.md` — NFR categories with target patterns and measurement methods
- `assets/adr-template.md` — ADR template

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. When you can run commands, put the facts into `components.json` (layout: `evals/fixtures/northwind-order-hub.json`) and run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/solution-architecture-doc --input components=<file> --input client=<name> --out <dir>`; report `run.json` and hand over the deliverables it writes (below) instead of re-typing them.
When you cannot run commands, **write the document yourself** following the Procedure — never answer a request that already carries facts with only a question. Draft from what is given, mark every gap `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, and ask for the missing facts at the end.

bodyHtml:
sow-drafter

In a conversation: draft the SOW now

  • The request carries the approved proposal, the estimate and the commercial model — including when the proposal and estimate are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: draft the SOW in this reply on assets/sow-template.md from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
    1. Scope — numbered S-nn statements (verb + object + boundary, with appendix references) and mirrored O-nn out-of-scope items where ambiguity is likely.
    2. Deliverables and acceptance — table with ID, format, objective acceptance criteria, method, review window, approver (client role), milestone; plus a deemed-acceptance clause.
    3. Milestones and payment tied to accepted deliverables per the stated model (e.g. fixed price per wave → one milestone per wave on acceptance); amounts from the proposal pricing or To be baselined · owner to be named.
    4. Assumptions — every estimate quantity as an assumption with basis, consequence if false, change-control trigger = Y, and who confirms by when.
    5. Client dependencies with due dates and a delay-consequence clause.
    6. Governance and RACI with exactly one A per row; change-control procedure with a minor-change threshold.
    7. Legal flags — topics (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance) referenced to the MSA clause and marked "confirm with counsel", not drafted.
    8. Separately, internal (not shipped): proposal → SOW traceability table and scope-ambiguity register. Mark every value the request does not give To be baselined · owner to be named naming its source, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
  • No proposal, or no commercial model ("turn this proposal into an SOW"): ask once, in one list, for the commercial model (fixed / T&M / milestone / run-rate) and the estimate file (and the proposal if absent). Say in one line that acceptance-payment linkage depends on the model. Do not draft the commercial section on an assumed model; you may offer to draft scope and deliverables meanwhile.
  • Asked for subjective acceptance or an unsourced price ("to the client's reasonable satisfaction", "put roughly what we discussed on the call"): say in one line that subjective acceptance invites disputes over sign-off and payment. Rewrite the criteria as objective, testable ones per references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md. Show the total as To be baselined · owner to be named with a note that it must come from the estimate/proposal pricing — never print the discussed figure anywhere. Offer a deemed-acceptance clause (accepted unless written rejection with reasons within the review window) as the flexibility mechanism instead.

Starting points

  • New — the approved proposal becomes a SOW on the template: scope in and out, deliverables with acceptance criteria, milestones, team, every assumption carried, the change-control clause verbatim.
  • Existing — add existing_sow (the client's paper or an earlier version): it is reconciled against the proposal — deliverables missing or added, subjective acceptance criteria, assumptions not carried, clauses absent — in sow-reconciliation.md, next to the SOW drafted from the proposal.

When to use

  • "Turn the approved proposal into an SOW."
  • "Redline this SOW — the scope is too loose."
  • "Write acceptance criteria for these deliverables."
  • NOT for: proposal narrative (proposal-writer), estimate (effort-estimator), MSA/legal clauses (flag for counsel).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Approved proposal (final version)yesfile
Estimate output: phases, effort, team, milestonesyesfile
Commercial model decided: fixed / T&M / milestone / run-rateyesuser
Governing agreement (MSA) reference and any mandated SOW templatenouser / file
Client-side named roles for RACInouser
Existing SOW draft (redline mode)yes in redlinefile

If the proposal or commercial model is missing, ask once. A missing estimate figure, MSA reference or client role name does not stop the draft: it is marked To be baselined · owner to be named. An SOW without a decided commercial model cannot define acceptance and payment linkage.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first. Redline convention applies in redline mode.

  1. Extract the scope baseline from the proposal: objectives, phases, deliverables, team, timeline, assumptions, risks. Build a traceability table: proposal section → SOW clause. Anything in the proposal that is not scope, deliverable, assumption, or commercial term (marketing language, win themes) is dropped from the SOW.
  2. Write scope as numbered statements per references/sow-method.md §2: each in-scope item is a verb + object + boundary ("Migrate the 42 interfaces listed in Appendix A from platform X to platform Y, including unit and integration test"). Mirror every in-scope item with an explicit out-of-scope statement where ambiguity is likely. Run the scope-ambiguity scan (§3) and register each ambiguity with its resolution.
  3. Define deliverables with acceptance criteria using references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md. Each deliverable: ID, description, format, acceptance criteria (objective, testable), acceptance method (review / test / demonstration), review window (days), deemed-acceptance rule, approver (client role).
  4. Decision point — commercial linkage. Per references/sow-method.md §5: fixed-price → milestones tied to accepted deliverables; T&M → monthly invoicing against approved timesheets with a not-to-exceed; milestone → payment on acceptance with a percentage schedule; run-rate → service levels with credits. Amounts come from the estimate/proposal pricing or are To be baselined · owner to be named. Never place a number without a source.
  5. Convert every assumption into a change-control trigger: assumption → basis → what happens if false (effort, schedule, price) → who confirms by when. Client dependencies get a due date and a consequence clause ("delay of client dependency D3 by more than 5 business days shifts dependent milestones day for day").
  6. Governance and RACI: forums, cadence, decision rights, escalation path, and a RACI across the deliverables with one A per row. Client roles named if supplied, else role titles with To be baselined · owner to be named.
  7. Change-control procedure: request → impact assessment (effort, schedule, price, risk) → approval authority and threshold → documentation. Include a minor-change threshold to avoid paperwork for trivial items.
  8. Legal flags: list every clause that counsel must confirm against the MSA (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance). Do not draft these; reference the MSA or mark for counsel.
  9. Redline mode: read the draft fully; score each clause against the ambiguity scan and acceptance patterns; produce [KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD] with rewritten text; deliver the clean version.
  10. Run the self-check.

bodyMd:
# sow-drafter

## In a conversation: draft the SOW now
- **The request carries the approved proposal, the estimate and the commercial model** — including when the proposal and estimate are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: draft the SOW **in this reply** on `assets/sow-template.md` from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
  1. **Scope** — numbered `S-nn` statements (verb + object + boundary, with appendix references) and mirrored `O-nn` out-of-scope items where ambiguity is likely.
  2. **Deliverables and acceptance** — table with ID, format, objective acceptance criteria, method, review window, approver (client role), milestone; plus a **deemed-acceptance clause**.
  3. **Milestones and payment** tied to accepted deliverables per the stated model (e.g. fixed price per wave → one milestone per wave on acceptance); amounts from the proposal pricing or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
  4. **Assumptions** — every estimate quantity as an assumption with basis, consequence if false, change-control trigger = Y, and who confirms by when.
  5. **Client dependencies** with due dates and a delay-consequence clause.
  6. **Governance and RACI** with exactly one A per row; **change-control procedure** with a minor-change threshold.
  7. **Legal flags** — topics (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance) referenced to the MSA clause and marked "confirm with counsel", not drafted.
  8. Separately, internal (not shipped): **proposal → SOW traceability table** and **scope-ambiguity register**.
  Mark every value the request does not give `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming its source, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
- **No proposal, or no commercial model** ("turn this proposal into an SOW"): ask once, in one list, for the commercial model (fixed / T&M / milestone / run-rate) and the estimate file (and the proposal if absent). Say in one line that acceptance-payment linkage depends on the model. Do not draft the commercial section on an assumed model; you may offer to draft scope and deliverables meanwhile.
- **Asked for subjective acceptance or an unsourced price** ("to the client's reasonable satisfaction", "put roughly what we discussed on the call"): say in one line that subjective acceptance invites disputes over sign-off and payment. Rewrite the criteria as objective, testable ones per `references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md`. Show the total as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` with a note that it must come from the estimate/proposal pricing — never print the discussed figure anywhere. Offer a **deemed-acceptance clause** (accepted unless written rejection with reasons within the review window) as the flexibility mechanism instead.

## Starting points
- **New** — the approved proposal becomes a SOW on the template: scope in and out, deliverables with acceptance criteria, milestones, team, every assumption carried, the change-control clause verbatim.
- **Existing** — add `existing_sow` (the client's paper or an earlier version): it is reconciled against the proposal — deliverables missing or added, subjective acceptance criteria, assumptions not carried, clauses absent — in `sow-reconciliation.md`, next to the SOW drafted from the proposal.

## When to use
- "Turn the approved proposal into an SOW."
- "Redline this SOW — the scope is too loose."
- "Write acceptance criteria for these deliverables."
- NOT for: proposal narrative (`proposal-writer`), estimate (`effort-estimator`), MSA/legal clauses (flag for counsel).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Approved proposal (final version) | yes | file |
| Estimate output: phases, effort, team, milestones | yes | file |
| Commercial model decided: fixed / T&M / milestone / run-rate | yes | user |
| Governing agreement (MSA) reference and any mandated SOW template | no | user / file |
| Client-side named roles for RACI | no | user |
| Existing SOW draft (redline mode) | yes in redline | file |

If the proposal or commercial model is missing, ask once. A missing estimate figure, MSA reference or client role name does not stop the draft: it is marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. An SOW without a decided commercial model cannot define acceptance and payment linkage.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. Redline convention applies in redline mode.

1. **Extract the scope baseline** from the proposal: objectives, phases, deliverables, team, timeline, assumptions, risks. Build a traceability table: proposal section → SOW clause. Anything in the proposal that is not scope, deliverable, assumption, or commercial term (marketing language, win themes) is dropped from the SOW.
2. **Write scope as numbered statements** per `references/sow-method.md` §2: each in-scope item is a verb + object + boundary ("Migrate the 42 interfaces listed in Appendix A from platform X to platform Y, including unit and integration test"). Mirror every in-scope item with an explicit out-of-scope statement where ambiguity is likely. Run the scope-ambiguity scan (§3) and register each ambiguity with its resolution.
3. **Define deliverables with acceptance criteria** using `references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md`. Each deliverable: ID, description, format, acceptance criteria (objective, testable), acceptance method (review / test / demonstration), review window (days), deemed-acceptance rule, approver (client role).
4. **Decision point — commercial linkage.** Per `references/sow-method.md` §5: fixed-price → milestones tied to accepted deliverables; T&M → monthly invoicing against approved timesheets with a not-to-exceed; milestone → payment on acceptance with a percentage schedule; run-rate → service levels with credits. Amounts come from the estimate/proposal pricing or are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never place a number without a source.
5. **Convert every assumption into a change-control trigger**: assumption → basis → what happens if false (effort, schedule, price) → who confirms by when. Client dependencies get a due date and a consequence clause ("delay of client dependency D3 by more than 5 business days shifts dependent milestones day for day").
6. **Governance and RACI**: forums, cadence, decision rights, escalation path, and a RACI across the deliverables with one A per row. Client roles named if supplied, else role titles with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
7. **Change-control procedure**: request → impact assessment (effort, schedule, price, risk) → approval authority and threshold → documentation. Include a minor-change threshold to avoid paperwork for trivial items.
8. **Legal flags**: list every clause that counsel must confirm against the MSA (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance). Do not draft these; reference the MSA or mark for counsel.
9. **Redline mode**: read the draft fully; score each clause against the ambiguity scan and acceptance patterns; produce `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]` with rewritten text; deliver the clean version.
10. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `sow-<client>-<initiative>-v0.1.md` (or `-redline-<date>.md` in redline mode)
- Template: `assets/sow-template.md`
- Companion: `assets/assumptions-checklist.md` completed as Appendix C
- Internal (not shipped): proposal→SOW traceability table; scope-ambiguity register; legal-flags list

## Self-check
- [ ] Every in-scope item is numbered, bounded, and has a matching out-of-scope statement where ambiguity exists
- [ ] Every deliverable has objective acceptance criteria, method, review window, approver, deemed-acceptance rule
- [ ] Every assumption states consequence if false and is a change-control trigger
- [ ] Client dependencies have due dates and delay consequences
- [ ] Payment schedule links to accepted deliverables/milestones; all amounts sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] RACI has exactly one A per deliverable
- [ ] Legal clauses referenced to MSA or flagged for counsel; none drafted here
- [ ] No proposal marketing language, no other-client references, no author history

## References
- `references/sow-method.md` — scope statements, ambiguity scan, commercial linkage, change control, governance
- `references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md` — patterns by deliverable type with examples
- `assets/sow-template.md` — SOW template
- `assets/assumptions-checklist.md` — assumptions and dependencies checklist by engagement type

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/sow-drafter --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/sow-drafter`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

value-case-builder

In a conversation: build the case now

  • The request carries baselines (volumes, costs, rates from client sources): write the value case in this reply. A benefits tree tracing each lever to the client's statements and cost drivers; baselines cited with confidence (H/M/L); unbaselined benefits kept out of the headline and listed; targets as low/base/high with mechanisms and ramps tied to delivery milestones; costs including delivery (at the estimate's P80), run, dual-run and decommission timing; NPV only at a discount rate the client's finance supplied, on their fiscal year; sensitivity on the top three assumptions with break-even values; a benefits-realization plan with client owners (unowned benefits flagged); a double-counting check.
  • The request says files are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: still build the whole case now from the facts the request states (who said what, which sources exist, the discount rate, the fiscal year). Lay out every section in full — benefits tree, baselines table, targets, costs, NPV, sensitivity, realization plan, double-counting check — with each value the request does not give shown as To be baselined · owner to be named naming the attached source it will come from. Never reply with only a request for the files.
  • No client baselines: ask once for scope, outcomes, at least one baseline fact and the audience. If none are available, say on line 1 that this is not a business case yet, give a hypothesis map (benefits tree with every baseline To be baselined · owner to be named) and the specific data requests with their likely holders.
  • Asked to use an industry benchmark or put a big multiple on page one: decline in one line (a CFO-grade case is built from the client's baselines and mechanisms; an unsourced multiple will not survive finance review). Show the headline as To be baselined · owner to be named — never print the requested multiple or percentage anywhere, not even beside that marker — list the unbaselined benefits, and offer the path to a defensible number: data requests with owners and a short baselining phase. A benchmark the user supplies with a source is recorded at confidence L and kept out of the headline.

Starting points

  • New — sourced benefits and costs become a CFO-grade value case: yearly cash flows, NPV, payback, P80 cost and sensitivity, with unbaselined rows kept out of the headline.
  • Existing — add previous (the earlier case's value-model.json): the refresh shows how benefits, costs, net, NPV, P80 cost and payback moved, and which benefits were added, removed, re-estimated or newly baselined.

When to use

  • "Build the business case for <initiative>."
  • "What is the ROI on this program, and how confident are we?"
  • "Review the client's draft business case before the steering committee."
  • NOT for: platform TCO alone (integration-migration-assessor), effort and price (effort-estimator), the proposal narrative (proposal-writer).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Initiative scope and outcomes (objectives, success measures)yesdiscovery synthesis / proposal
Baseline facts: current cost, volumes, cycle times, headcount on the process, error/incident rates, revenue leversyes (any subset; rest is TBD)client documents / statements
Cost of the initiative: one-time (from effort-estimator) and run (from TCO or client)yes or To be baselined · owner to be namedestimate memo / TCO
Finance conventions: currency, horizon (3/5 yr), discount rate, capex/opex treatment, fiscal yearno — defaults stated as assumptionsclient finance / user
Audience: CFO-grade vs sponsor-levelyesuser

If scope and at least one baseline fact are missing, ask once. A value case with no client baseline is a hypothesis map, and the output says so on line 1.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Build the benefits tree per references/value-method.md §1: strategic driver → value lever → operational metric → financial value. Each leaf must trace to an outcome the client stated. Classify each benefit: hard (cash, cost avoided with a named budget line), soft-quantifiable (productivity hours with a conversion rule), strategic (unquantified; listed, not summed).
  2. Baseline every metric: value, source (document/page or client role and date), confidence (H/M/L). No source → To be baselined · owner to be named and the metric is excluded from the headline number until baselined. Do not borrow benchmarks from memory; if the user supplies an external benchmark, cite it and rate confidence L.
  3. Set improvement targets as ranges (low / base / high) with the mechanism that produces them (automation of step X removes Y hours; decommission removes licence line Z). A target without a mechanism is not admissible. Ramp realization over time per §3 (benefits rarely start at 100% on go-live).
  4. Model costs: one-time (delivery at P80 from the estimate memo, licences, change management, decommission), run (new platform, support, subscriptions), and the cost of delay for the status quo if evidenced. Cite sources; mark unknowns.
  5. Decision point — headline metric. With the finance conventions in hand choose: simple payback and multi-year net (sponsor-level) or NPV/IRR (CFO-grade). State the discount rate as an assumption with owner. Never present NPV if the discount rate is not from the client's finance team; use undiscounted net and say so.
  6. Compute and lay out on assets/value-model-spec.md (CSV layout) and assets/value-case-template.md (markdown). Any output depending on a To be baselined · owner to be named input is itself marked, not computed from a placeholder.
  7. Sensitivity: identify the three assumptions with the largest effect on 3-year net; show ±20% (or the realistic range) and the break-even value of each. If the case flips sign within the realistic range, say so on line 1.
  8. Benefits-realization plan: each benefit with a KPI, baseline, target, measurement method, owner (client), review cadence, and the realization start date tied to a delivery milestone. Benefits without a client owner are listed as unowned risks.
  9. Risks to the case: adoption, dependency on other programs, data quality, timing of decommission, double counting (check overlap between levers).
  10. Review mode: apply the rubric in references/value-case-review-rubric.md, redline per convention, deliver clean version.
  11. Run the self-check.

Output

ArtifactFile
Value model (CSV layout)value-model-<client>-<initiative>.csv per assets/value-model-spec.md
Value case documentvalue-case-<client>-<initiative>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md per assets/value-case-template.md

Sections: Bottom line (headline metric with confidence and what is unbaselined) · Benefits tree · Baselines and sources · Targets and mechanisms · Costs · Model (yearly table, payback, net) · Sensitivity · Benefits-realization plan · Risks · Assumptions register · Decision asked

Self-check

  • [ ] Every benefit traces to a client-stated outcome and has a mechanism
  • [ ] Every baseline has source and confidence or is To be baselined · owner to be named
  • [ ] Headline number excludes unbaselined benefits; the exclusion is stated

  • [ ] Costs include run and decommission timing; delivery cost cites the estimate memo
  • [ ] Sensitivity on top three assumptions with break-even values
  • [ ] Every benefit has a client owner or is flagged unowned

bodyMd:
# value-case-builder

## In a conversation: build the case now
- **The request carries baselines** (volumes, costs, rates from client sources): write the value case **in this reply**. A benefits tree tracing each lever to the client's statements and cost drivers; baselines cited with confidence (H/M/L); unbaselined benefits kept out of the headline and listed; targets as low/base/high with mechanisms and ramps tied to delivery milestones; costs including delivery (at the estimate's P80), run, dual-run and decommission timing; NPV only at a discount rate the client's finance supplied, on their fiscal year; sensitivity on the top three assumptions with break-even values; a benefits-realization plan with client owners (unowned benefits flagged); a double-counting check.
- **The request says files are attached but their contents are not in the conversation**: still build the whole case now from the facts the request states (who said what, which sources exist, the discount rate, the fiscal year). Lay out every section in full — benefits tree, baselines table, targets, costs, NPV, sensitivity, realization plan, double-counting check — with each value the request does not give shown as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the attached source it will come from. Never reply with only a request for the files.
- **No client baselines**: ask once for scope, outcomes, at least one baseline fact and the audience. If none are available, say on line 1 that this is not a business case yet, give a hypothesis map (benefits tree with every baseline `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`) and the specific data requests with their likely holders.
- **Asked to use an industry benchmark or put a big multiple on page one**: decline in one line (a CFO-grade case is built from the client's baselines and mechanisms; an unsourced multiple will not survive finance review). Show the headline as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` — never print the requested multiple or percentage anywhere, not even beside that marker — list the unbaselined benefits, and offer the path to a defensible number: data requests with owners and a short baselining phase. A benchmark the user supplies with a source is recorded at confidence L and kept out of the headline.

## Starting points
- **New** — sourced benefits and costs become a CFO-grade value case: yearly cash flows, NPV, payback, P80 cost and sensitivity, with unbaselined rows kept out of the headline.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (the earlier case's `value-model.json`): the refresh shows how benefits, costs, net, NPV, P80 cost and payback moved, and which benefits were added, removed, re-estimated or newly baselined.

## When to use
- "Build the business case for <initiative>."
- "What is the ROI on this program, and how confident are we?"
- "Review the client's draft business case before the steering committee."
- NOT for: platform TCO alone (`integration-migration-assessor`), effort and price (`effort-estimator`), the proposal narrative (`proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Initiative scope and outcomes (objectives, success measures) | yes | discovery synthesis / proposal |
| Baseline facts: current cost, volumes, cycle times, headcount on the process, error/incident rates, revenue levers | yes (any subset; rest is TBD) | client documents / statements |
| Cost of the initiative: one-time (from `effort-estimator`) and run (from TCO or client) | yes or `[TO BE BASELINED]` | estimate memo / TCO |
| Finance conventions: currency, horizon (3/5 yr), discount rate, capex/opex treatment, fiscal year | no — defaults stated as assumptions | client finance / user |
| Audience: CFO-grade vs sponsor-level | yes | user |

If scope and at least one baseline fact are missing, ask once. A value case with no client baseline is a hypothesis map, and the output says so on line 1.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Build the benefits tree** per `references/value-method.md` §1: strategic driver → value lever → operational metric → financial value. Each leaf must trace to an outcome the client stated. Classify each benefit: hard (cash, cost avoided with a named budget line), soft-quantifiable (productivity hours with a conversion rule), strategic (unquantified; listed, not summed).
2. **Baseline every metric**: value, source (document/page or client role and date), confidence (H/M/L). No source → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and the metric is excluded from the headline number until baselined. Do not borrow benchmarks from memory; if the user supplies an external benchmark, cite it and rate confidence L.
3. **Set improvement targets** as ranges (low / base / high) with the mechanism that produces them (automation of step X removes Y hours; decommission removes licence line Z). A target without a mechanism is not admissible. Ramp realization over time per §3 (benefits rarely start at 100% on go-live).
4. **Model costs**: one-time (delivery at P80 from the estimate memo, licences, change management, decommission), run (new platform, support, subscriptions), and the cost of delay for the status quo if evidenced. Cite sources; mark unknowns.
5. **Decision point — headline metric.** With the finance conventions in hand choose: simple payback and multi-year net (sponsor-level) or NPV/IRR (CFO-grade). State the discount rate as an assumption with owner. Never present NPV if the discount rate is not from the client's finance team; use undiscounted net and say so.
6. **Compute and lay out** on `assets/value-model-spec.md` (CSV layout) and `assets/value-case-template.md` (markdown). Any output depending on a `[TO BE BASELINED]` input is itself marked, not computed from a placeholder.
7. **Sensitivity**: identify the three assumptions with the largest effect on 3-year net; show ±20% (or the realistic range) and the break-even value of each. If the case flips sign within the realistic range, say so on line 1.
8. **Benefits-realization plan**: each benefit with a KPI, baseline, target, measurement method, owner (client), review cadence, and the realization start date tied to a delivery milestone. Benefits without a client owner are listed as unowned risks.
9. **Risks to the case**: adoption, dependency on other programs, data quality, timing of decommission, double counting (check overlap between levers).
10. Review mode: apply the rubric in `references/value-case-review-rubric.md`, redline per convention, deliver clean version.
11. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File |
|---|---|
| Value model (CSV layout) | `value-model-<client>-<initiative>.csv` per `assets/value-model-spec.md` |
| Value case document | `value-case-<client>-<initiative>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` per `assets/value-case-template.md` |

Sections: Bottom line (headline metric with confidence and what is unbaselined) · Benefits tree · Baselines and sources · Targets and mechanisms · Costs · Model (yearly table, payback, net) · Sensitivity · Benefits-realization plan · Risks · Assumptions register · Decision asked

## Self-check
- [ ] Every benefit traces to a client-stated outcome and has a mechanism
- [ ] Every baseline has source and confidence or is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Headline number excludes unbaselined benefits; the exclusion is stated
- [ ] Strategic benefits listed, not summed
- [ ] Costs include run and decommission timing; delivery cost cites the estimate memo
- [ ] Sensitivity on top three assumptions with break-even values
- [ ] Every benefit has a client owner or is flagged unowned
- [ ] No double counting across levers; no benchmarks from memory

## References
- `references/value-method.md` — benefits tree, classification, baselining, targets and ramps, finance conventions, double-counting checks
- `references/value-case-review-rubric.md` — review criteria for an existing business case
- `assets/value-model-spec.md` — CSV layout specification
- `assets/value-case-template.md` — markdown document template

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/value-case-builder --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/value-case-builder`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.
